title: inline 'if/else' erroneously causes st.write()
body:
# Summary

When calling a function that appears within an inline 'if/else' statement, the output of the function is erroneously displayed on the website via a st.write().

# Steps to reproduce

Code snippet, simplest case:

```
# 'foo' appears on the website
import streamlit as st
'foo' if True else 'goo'
```

Perhaps the above is expected? If so, what about the below:

Code snippet, realistic case:

```
# 'None' appears on the website
import streamlit as st
def foo(i):
    # Do stuff here, such as st.write(f'{i}')
    # No return value
foo(i=1) if True else foo(i=2)
```

## Expected behavior:

At least in the second case, above, I would expect that 'None' does not appear on the website. The return value (or lack thereof) of the function should not be considered an expression to be displayed on the website.

## Actual behavior:

As noted in the code comment, in the latter case, the text 'None' appears on the website (i.e, the 'return' value of the function foo()).

I'm pretty confident this counts as a glitch.

# Debug info

- Streamlit version: 0.75.0
- Python version: 3.8.5
- Using Conda? PipEnv? PyEnv? Pex? Docker with raw Python installation
- OS version: Ubuntu 20.04
- Browser version: Chrome, Version 88.0.4324.104 (Official Build) (64-bit)

comments.text:
Hey @user, thanks for reporting this!

(TL; DR - I think what the desired behavior should be here turns out to be surprisingly tricky, but in the meantime [you can turn magic commands off](https://docs.streamlit.io/en/latest/api.html#magic-commands))

The behavior is a bit surprising and unintuitive, but I'm not entirely sure if it can be classified as a bug. Streamlit has a [magic commands](https://docs.streamlit.io/en/latest/api.html#magic-commands) feature that essentially transforms standalone expressions into calls to `st.write()`.

There's a subtle difference between `if`/`else` statements written on separate lines and Python's one-liner conditional expression. The latter, as its name suggests, is indeed an expression, which is why writing things like 

```python
x = f() if some_condition else g()
```
works.

It's also why the behavior you're seeing occurs since semantically conditional expressions always evaluate to some value while `if`/`else` statements may not. I think that having 
```python
'foo' if True else 'goo'
```
write `'foo'` to the app is what one would want magic commands to do, but it's a bit harder to say what the behavior should be when functions are called in conditional expressions since they _technically_ evaluate to some value, but a person's intention when calling a function in a conditional expression may be purely to trigger side effects while ignoring the return value. At the same time, I can see an argument for wanting the behavior to be to be to convert the expression to a call to `st.write()` in the case that the function being called is pure and the user cares only about its return value.

Maybe @user may have some input on this?

+1 on @user's answer. 

Having `st.write` print `None` when the function has no return value does seem like an unintended consequence of one liner conditional statements / function calls and magic commands 

As a workaround, you can consider turning off magic commands and if that is not an option then returning an empty string might also be an option. 

```python
def foo():
    # some computation
    return ''
```

@user If the workarounds are not an adequate fix for now, please let us know. Thanks!
Clsoing, as mentioned above, this is expected behavior with magic.

title: When "upload_file_request_handler.py" returns 400 error, we can see session ID.
body:
# Summary

We make application on Microsoft Azure App Service with streamlit.
When we conducted a test of uploading file with `st.file_uploader`,  it returned 400 error and **session ID** as string.
We checked your codes and noticed that we have 400 error, `streamlit/lib/streamlit/server/upload_file_request_handler.py`  returns error code 400, reason and session ID on line 126-128.
This problem may lead to security incidents like XSS.
Please check it.

# Steps to reproduce

Code snippet:

```
import streamlit as st

uploaded_file = st.file_uploader("uploading Excel files", type="xlsx", key="xlsx_up")
if uploaded_file is not None:
     st.write("Success")

```
How the error occurred cannot be provided due to confidentiality,

## Expected behavior:

When we have 400 error, streamlit will return only error code and error reason without session ID.

## Actual behavior:

When we have 400 error, streamlit returns error code and error reason with session ID
Screenshots cannot be uploaded due to confidentiality.

## Is this a regression?

That is, did this use to work the way you expected in the past?
yes / no
⇒no

# Debug info

- Streamlit version: (get it with `$ streamlit version`)
⇒0.74.1
- Python version: (get it with `$ python --version`)
⇒3.7
- Using Conda? PipEnv? PyEnv? Pex?
⇒Pip
- OS version:
⇒Linux

comments.text:
Thanks for raising this!

In the ideal world we should only be returning that error if a session ID is invalid in which case it should not matter what the `session_id` is since it should not be usable for any connection with the server. We should definitely pull out the `widget_id` out of the check and separate that so that we are not potentially exposing a valid `session_id`. Once that is done, I think it should be fine showing an invalid `session_id` but would love to get your thoughts!

Thank you for your comment.
We can understand what you think about this issue.

We got a capture that shows the problem. 
We send POST message to our uploading functions using streamlit on Azure App service with invalid session ID and an script to get Cookie.
Application returned original invalid session ID and script without escaped method.
This script will be used to attack application or get information in the system.
I think streamlit should escape invalid scripts for avoid attack from someone.

Thank you for your consideration.

title: `streamlit config show` newlines are not printing correctly
body:
### Steps to reproduce

```
streamlit config show
```

**Expected behavior:**

Sections that use newlines for meaningful formatting (e.g. to make up lists) should have their newlines honored. For example, `browser.serverAddress` should look like this:
```
# Internet address where users should point their browsers in order to connect to the app. Can be IP address or DNS name and path.
#
# This is used to:
# - Set the correct URL for CORS and XSRF protection purposes.
# - Show the URL on the terminal
# - Open the browser
# - Tell the browser where to connect to the server when in liveSave mode.
#
# Default: 'localhost'
serverAddress = "localhost"
```

**Actual behavior:**

The section above looks like this in reality:
```
# Internet address where users should point their browsers in order to connect to the app. Can be IP address or DNS name and path.
# This is used to: - Set the correct URL for CORS and XSRF protection purposes. - Show the URL on the terminal - Open the browser - Tell the browser where to connect to the server when in liveSave mode.
# Default: 'localhost'
serverAddress = "localhost"
```

### Is this a regression?

no

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 0.76.0

### Additional information

I'm pretty sure I wrote the code that is doing the wrong thing :)
Should be somewhere around `config.py` at `_clean_paragraphs()`.

title: Can't connect to app from iOS device using Basic Authentication
body:
### Summary

I launched streamlit app by using ngrok.  Almost device (like windows, mac, Android) can access to the app through ngrok link, but iOS device (iPhone & iPad) cannot access it.  ( Freeze with text "Please wait ...".  )

### Steps to reproduce

1. Run `streamlit hello`
2. Access to ngrok link from iOS device

**Expected behavior:**

Access the hello-example in the browser on iOS device.

**Actual behavior:**

Freeze with text "Please wait ...". 
[image]

### Is this a regression?

no

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 0.69.1
- Python version: 3.8.5
- Using Conda
- OS version: iPadOS 14.4 , Windows 10 (server)
- Browser version: chrome, safari

### Additional information

I tried to setup `config.toml` like below, but it doesn't work.
```config.toml
[server]
enableCORS = false
enableXsrfProtection = false
```
If I don't set `enableXsrfProtection = false`, enableCORS is overwrited into true.

comments.text: @user Thanks for messaging us. I just tried it locally and had no problem using both HTTP and HTTPS url (no config changes). Your version of Streamlit is rather old. Can you try updating and verifying if it is still an issue? Thanks!
@user Thank you for replying. I have tried it again after updating Streamlit for 0.79.0, but this problem still happened.

Sorry, I forgot one important information.
If ngrok runs with "-auth" option, this problem happens.  This problem dose not happen without auth options. Thank you.

Thanks for the response @user That was really helpful. I see the issue when using the auth feature. This implements a Basic Authentication method on the http website.

Safari unfortunately does _not_ forward the basic auth to the web socket connection. This can be confirmed that Safari doesn't work, but it works on Chrome on macOS.

Reading https://stackoverflow.com/a/4361358 it seems that this may be more intentional in an attempt to deprecate Basic Authentication being very insecure. There _might_ be a solution where we make a pretend request, observe the Auth Header sent, decode it, and connect to the web socket properly. Given the pain of the implementation for a very specific situation and the motivation of trying to discourage Basic Authentication, this is probably low in priority. I'll leave this issue open in case we see more use cases pop up.

Hit the same problem here with both chrome and safari on iPadOS, stream lit 0.8.0 behind reverse proxy on nginx with basic auth. Works like a charm on macOS, on Windows, and on android. Seems that iPadOS network stack is the problem — even With chrome.

is there a workaround please? Some of my users use iPads and iPhones.
Thanks for any idea!

@user You might have better luck asking others on [forums](https://discuss.streamlit.io) for opinions. For what it's worth, Chrome on iPadOS uses Apple's rendering engine, so it's not its own browser like Chrome is on macOS. It mimics a lot of Safari's functionality.
Thanks @user , I suspected something like this. Will try my luck on the forum. Do you think iOS will be more amicable if I use https?
I unfortunately don't know for sure @user

title: Custom components - send data after creation
body:
### Problem

We need to send data to our custom component after created.

Why?
There is a websocket connection in our streamlit app which can send some changing information in our custom component without rerun the whole app.

### Solution

**MVP** 

We can send data losslessly to our custom component after created

**Possible additions:**

Custom components instance can be represented with a python class.

**Preferred solution:**

Fist PR:
https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/2836

Our current code backward compatible way:
https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/compare/develop...FloWide:custom_components_send_with_merge?diff=split&expand=1

This change enables at custom component creation to add a class to "wrap" components result with a 'send' function.

title: Time or event (websocket/redis) callbacks
body:
### Problem

I want to create outside trigger event changes (like timeout, websocket connection, redis subscribed channel, other streamlit app) without owning the report thread, and without blocking user interactions (buttons, checkboxes etc.) and with streamlit's low code mindset

### Solution

**Preferred solution:**

We created a solution here:
https://github.com/FloWide/streamlit_callbacks

with simple usages:
```
from streamlit.callbacks.callbacks import later, rerun
import streamlit as st
from datetime import datetime

st.write(datetime.now())

later(2.0, rerun) # After 2 sec calls a rerun
```

```
import streamlit.callbacks.websocket as ws
import streamlit as st

print_message = st.empty()
def msg_handler(msg):
  print_message.write(f"Arrived message from ws: {msg}")
  
ws.on_message('ws://localhost:10000', msg_handler)
```

More examples at `README.md`

title: The file uploader reports "400 session invalid" when streamlit is wrapped in swarm docker container if REPLICAS > 1
body:
### Summary

The file uploader reports "400 session invalid" when streamlit is wrapped swarm docker container if REPLICAS > 1 . If we set REPLICAS = 1, no error will be reported.

It seems that streamlit is using traditional "passing session id" method to verfiy the identiy of the user. But it is not suitable for the distrubited system with REPLICAS > 1 because session id could not be shared between different nodes. UploadedFile = st.file_uploader("test", type=['png', 'jpeg', 'jpg'])

title: Comment out config options in `streamlit config show` if they are set to their default values
body:
NOTE: we'll need to verify that this is indeed what we want the behavior to be before doing any work on this.

Consider the following sequence of actions a user might take
1. Populate a `config.toml` file by running `streamlit config show > ~/.streamlit/config.toml`
2. In the file, change the `server.port` config option to something other than 8501 (the default), let's say it's changed to 8502
3. Start up streamlit: `streamlit run my_app.py`
4. See the following message being logged and wonder why the port change apparently didn't take effect (note the server will be serving on http://localhost:8502)
```
  You can now view your Streamlit app in your browser.

  Local URL: http://localhost:8501
  Network URL: http://192.168.0.19:8501
```

The cause of this confusing behavior is that `streamlit config show` prints the current values of config options when run, but this can cause weird interactions with config options with default values when using the command to initially populate a `config.toml` file.

In the example above, the default value for `server.port` is 8501, and the default value for `browser.serverPort` is to match the value of `server.port`. `streamlit config show` prints the following
```toml
[server]
# The port where the server will listen for browser connections.
# Default: 8501
port = 8501

[browser]
# Port where users should point their browsers in order to connect to the app.
# This is used to: - Set the correct URL for CORS and XSRF protection purposes. - Show the URL on the terminal - Open the browser
# Default: whatever value is set in server.port.
serverPort = 8501
```
When the user uses the output of the command to initially populate a config file, then later changes `server.port`, the value of `browser.serverPort` is still explicitly set to 8501 within the config file, resulting in confusion. Most likely, the desired behavior was to have `browser.serverPort` use the default value instead of unintentionally fixing it in `config.toml`

If we instead print something like
```toml
[server]
# The port where the server will listen for browser connections.
# Default: 8501
# port = 8501

[browser]
# Port where users should point their browsers in order to connect to the app.
# This is used to: - Set the correct URL for CORS and XSRF protection purposes. - Show the URL on the terminal - Open the browser
# Default: whatever value is set in server.port.
# serverPort = 8501
```
there's no chance that some options are accidentally fixed within a config file when the intention was to use the default.

title: Recognize user on multiple tab / multiple session - login process
body:
### Problem

Currently there are no method to recognize users if they use streamlit on multiple tabs / multiple sessions.

### Solution

**Preferred solution:** 

We found an acceptable solution for a login process.
https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/compare/develop...FloWide:browser_id

On this branch, the streamlit sets an unique cookie (`_user` -> uuid) for the browser at first http get. This cookie is visible for the websocket connection too, where we save it as an `user_id`. This id is reachable from the `report_context`.

The login process is based on this id. On a successful login, streamlit app can cache login information for this user id, and if the app meets again this id, from the cached information can get the logined user data.

title: Change health check endpoint name
body:
### Problem

In Google Cloud Run, 404 error occurs after 1 minute.
Streamlit use healthz url for health check.
However, healthz is reserved url in GCP.
https://cloud.google.com/run/docs/issues#ah

### Solution

Configure health check url in configuration file or cli option.
ex) streamlit run --health-check-url=health-check

### Additional context

Currently, I walkaround with this tweak.
entrypoint: find ${VIRTUAL_ENV}/lib/python3.6/site-packages/streamlit -type f \( -iname \*.py -o -iname \*.js \) -print0 | xargs -0 sed -i 's/healthz/health-check/g' && streamlit run app.py

The syntax for `docker run` may be different in Windows than in Linux.
Do you use `powershell` or `cmd` under Windows?

yes it's correctly mounted as I have to press R each time to reload even if the reload on save is checked , I use git bash or ubuntu wsl terminal on windows. the R works fine if I updated the app.py , I have to rerun docker each time I update any other file that is deeply imported

I can confirm that **Rerun** does _not_ work out of the box on Windows 10 if you run streamlit in a **Docker** container.
I assume that the file watcher does not work.
I added a config file in `.streamlit/config.toml` and added the following line:

```toml
[server]
fileWatcherType = "poll"
```

After this change to `poll` mode, the "Rerun" also worked when running Streamlit in a Docker container on Windows 10.

Thanks for looking into this @user!

I'm guessing you're editing your script source files from an editor running in windows, @user? If that's the case, then I believe this isn't something that we can handle on our end, as the root cause of this is that Docker for Windows doesn't notify containers of files in mounted volumes that are changed from Windows. See [this thread](https://forums.docker.com/t/file-system-watch-does-not-work-with-mounted-volumes/12038) on the docker forums. Aside from switching your `fileWatcherType` to "poll", the thread that I linked also has a few packages and workarounds that can help with this.

I'm going to close this issue since as far as I can tell, this isn't something solvable from within streamlit and is currently fixable by adjusting some settings in `.streamlit/config.toml`. Feel free to reopen this issue if I'm mistaken here!

~My understanding is that, after sending a ping, the client needs to receive the pong within `pingInterval` duration or it will consider the connection to have been lost. So this change could result in Streamlit becoming less stable for high-latency connections.~

Whoops, I was thinking this was about the client ping interval. Tornado has its own `websocket_ping_interval`, and a separate `websocket_ping_timeout` value.

I set Tornado's `websocket_ping_interval` to 1s, and then simulated a client connection with 5000ms of latency and very low upload/download speeds, and didn't see any issues.

title: Unrecognized RootContainer in deltaPath
body:
### Summary

I've put my app into production at [https://binancepremiums.com](https://binancepremiums.com)

It seems that every few hours, the app stops working and only shows a Streamlit error

```Unrecognized RootContainer in deltaPath```

[image]

I deployed the app on heroku and don't think that's causing the problems (no errors there). When I restart the Heroku dyno (i.e restart the streamlit server), it seems to work for a while.

This could definitely be user error, but it's important for me to find out what the cause is.

May or may not be related: the memory consumption of the app steadily increases over time (drops are when I reset the app). Anecdotally it seems that the aforementioned error is more likely to happen when memory consumption is relatively high (but there mightn't be a causal link there). 

[image]

## Background

Below is a skeleton of my app. I pull data from the binance API every 5 minutes and want to display the updated table (don't need any old data). Maybe I'm using some common antipattern?

```python
import time
import streamlit as st
from streamlit import caching
from binance import Client
client = Client()

@st.cache(ttl=310, allow_output_mutation=True)
def get_data(timestamp=None)
    client.get(...)
    return df
    
table = st.empty()

while True:
     # update every 5 mins
     caching.clear_cache()  # not sure if needed
     timestamp = dt.utcnow()
     table.dataframe(get_data(timestamp))

```

comments.text: Hey @user Thanks for your report. I'm curious if our latest release helps? After each script run, we run Python's garbage collection, which should hopefully alleviate stress on memory.

Hi,

I bumped to 0.82 and deployed it. It seems to have helped a little, but the memory still steadily grows over time. I've attached the Heroku memory profile.

Some context: the server was set to restart every hour (my fix to the memory issue), hence the sawtooth profile initially. After bumping the version (tagged 5ca2beba), the gradient of the sawtooth seems to be shallower, so memory is building up more slowly.

I disabled the hourly reset to see what would happen – sadly, still builds up  memory (I manually reset it after 3pm UTC to avoid a crash).

[image]

Best,
Robret

Thanks @user for the memory report. We'll have to investigate more fully what could be the problem here.

For now, here's what I know and perhaps that can help in debugging.

1. The error message tends to associate with unable to find the place for a placeholder (in this case, it's the `st.empty`.
2. Also, the use of the infinite loop, while legal, is not in the recommended strategy of the Streamlit (in fact, auto refreshing has never been a good use case for Streamlit, but one we are considering).
3. You _might_ fare better if you use `st.experimental_rerun` and just adding a time constraint (and removing the need for `st.empty`)

Hi @user, thanks for this info!

> Also, the use of the infinite loop, while legal, is not in the recommended strategy

Do let me know if there is a better design pattern – I had a quick look in the forums but it was mostly while loops. 

> auto refreshing has never been a good use case for Streamlit

I would have thought that the majority of users would like to present dynamic data? In any case, I definitely cast my vote for this feature 🚀 

For other users experiencing this, I suggest you automatically restart your app every so often. This can be done on Heroku by scheduling an API request to restart the server.
Closing this issue since it did not have any activity or upvotes for > 3 years. Please open a new issue or respond here in case this issue still exists.

title: When I create the image docker and try it to run localy I recive "Streamlit requires raw Python (.py) files, but the provided file has no extension.\nFor more information, please see https://docs.streamlit.io"
body:
### Summary
I built the images docker and when I try to run locally I receive the next error  "Streamlit requires raw Python (.py) files, but the provided file has no extension.\nFor more information, please see https://docs.streamlit.io" 

### Steps to reproduce
Build images and run
```
docker build --tag bug-app .

docker run -p 8501:8501 bug-app
```

### Packages 
I used config.toml and credentials.toml as Mark recommend it 
https://github.com/MarcSkovMadsen/awesome-streamlit/tree/master/.streamlit

I know abhinand5 added this pull request to the code https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/2115 in case the people don't use .py extensions. However, this is not the case. I have app.py file in my folder.

### Debug info
- streamlit==0.81.1
- Python version: 3.7.10
- Ubuntu 18.04

### Fix 
I fixed it changing the docker file
```
FROM python:3.7
COPY . /app
WORKDIR /app
RUN pip install -r requirements.txt
EXPOSE 8501
RUN mkdir ~/.streamlit
RUN cp config.toml ~/.streamlit/config.toml
RUN cp credentials.toml ~/.streamlit/credentials.toml
RUN apt-get update ##[edited]
RUN apt-get install ffmpeg libsm6 libxext6  -y
WORKDIR /app
ENTRYPOINT ["streamlit", "run"]
CMD [ "app.py"]
```
to 
```
FROM python:3.7
COPY . /app
WORKDIR /app
RUN pip install -r requirements.txt
EXPOSE 8501
RUN mkdir ~/.streamlit
RUN cp config.toml ~/.streamlit/config.toml
RUN cp credentials.toml ~/.streamlit/credentials.toml
RUN apt-get update ##[edited]
RUN apt-get install ffmpeg libsm6 libxext6  -y
WORKDIR /app
ENTRYPOINT ["streamlit", "run", "app.py"]
```

I know this is not the best way to fix it, that's why I created the issue.

title: Large text inside `beta_container` does not display
body:
### Summary

When using the new layout function `beta_container` and a long title the text correctly overflows to the next line however it cuts out from showing.

### Steps to reproduce

Code snippet:

```
import streamlit as st
import plotly.express as px

def make_volume_display(df, colname):
    _container = st.beta_container()
    _container.title(f"{colname.replace('_', ' ').title()} Volume")
    _agg_df = df.groupby('date').sum()[colname].reset_index()

    _container.plotly_chart(
        px.bar(_agg_df, x='date', y=colname)
    )

    return _container

funnel_df = pd.DataFrame(load_data())
stage_option = st.selectbox(
    label='Stage',
    options=_measures
)
make_volume_display(funnel_df, stage_option)
```

**Expected behavior:**

A title that auto adjusts within the `beta_container`
[image]

**Actual behavior:**

A title that gets trumped if the line overflows
[image]

### Is this a regression?

That is, did this use to work the way you expected in the past?
It's odd as we have a local development environment and it doesn't happen there, but on our production environment it doesn't work. The only difference between the two is that one is launched directly from the user computer and on production is launched from a Docker container.

- Python version: 3.7.10

Hi @user, could you provide a bit more context on your use case?

Neither the `_is_running_with_streamlit` attribute nor the `streamlit.cli` module are part of the API that we intend to expose to users (I don't believe there's a true way of making these attributes/modules private in a Python module), so strangeness seen when using them outside of the streamlit package itself is probably not something that we would consider a bug.

title: [FEATURE REQUEST] Research, Google Forms, CSV, Streamlit Application!
body:
_(Note, you don't have to fill out every section here. They're just here for guidance. That said, nicely detailed feature requests are more likely to get eng attention sooner)_

### Problem/Context

Hello!

For context and my dev experience, I'm new to using Streamlit, and recently, I made [this](https://robotiic.herokuapp.com/) as the solution to an assignment for my current course, "Artificial Intelligence". If you're interested in checking out the code, you can [see that here](https://github.com/Rubix982/Robotiic). Other than that, I have used Voila, Matplotlib, Seaborn, and Pyplot for visualizations.

Recently, I've been working on a research paper, and for that, I had to develop a questionnaire using Google Forms. The research basically aims at gathering data about their opinions, beliefs, academic/situational/learning factors that have affected their semester progression throughout the University. I have gotten plenty of data from the University's students, which I believe is immensely interesting.

Now I wish that I can easily share their results with other students in my University to show the impact that online education has influenced learning capabilities. Google Forms does give you access to see all the responses and the fancy graphs they make, but you can't make that public. You can also download all of that data as a .csv file, and I immediately thought of Streamlit, "Man, I wish I can just give this CSV file to a Streamlit application, tell it the format is from Google Forms, and then ask Streamlit to generate graphs similar to the graphs that Google Forms generates, and then share a link with everyone - maybe even more kinds of graphs!"

Unfortunately, I do not have enough time to write code from scratch for a Streamlit application and put it into production right now, and I also do not know of other technologies which can potentially do this. Maybe a potential solution is either PowerBI or Tableau, but I have no experience with them, and neither do I know of any easy way of putting an online web application that shows all these statistics.

In my opinion, Google Forms itself has an option, but being frankly honest, I find Google Forms to be visually very unappealing. Its UI looks outdated and makes filling forms a very boring experience. There is always `SurveyMonkey`, and `TypeForm`, but they aren't as free out of the box as Google Forms is. I don't think anyone sharing Google Form response results will appeal to anyone but a few executives or managers wanting to understand the data in whatever way.

### Solution

**MVP:** What's the smallest possible solution that would get 80% of the problem out of the way?

A feature in a Streamlit application that can read a CSV file, and which we can inform is from a Google Forms survey, which can generate some basic charts automatically with the `data` given, the `options` in them, some simple bar charts or pie charts

**Possible additions:** What are other things that could be added to the MVP overtime to make it better?

1. Giving the option to choose what `columns` to show from the CSV given, and what to hide.
2. Some advanced charts
3. Statistical analysis
4. Another file that can be fed to the Streamlit application. This is a bare minimum file that can be used to express the format of the UI that the Streamlit application can generate. Maybe you want that the 5th or 6th bar chart should come first. Maybe you want to have some text before a certain bar chart. Maybe you want data to be aligned differently - rather than the center, maybe text wrapping with the chart on the left or the right
5. Some different UI styles, maybe like the [Stack Overflow 2020 survey](https://insights.stackoverflow.com/survey/2020#salary)!
6. Some way to make this very appealing to business/data analysts. It will make sharing results across large communities/organizations very effective, easy, and visually appealing at the same time

**Preferred solution:** If you don't like the MVP above, tell us why, and what you'd like done instead.

You need somewhere to deploy to show the results, which is not always possible. Speaking for myself, I'm out of free Heroku Dynos. :/

### Additional context

_Add any other context or screenshots about the feature request here. For example, did this FR come from https://discuss.streamlit.io or another site? Link the source here!_

Not really, just had this idea.

Thank you!

title: Add native auth support using Kerberos keytab
body:
### Problem

I created a multi user app that deals with some sensitive data so naturally I needed a way to prevent it from getting into the wrong hands.

### Solution

As a solution I am running streamlit on top of a Nginx layer.
Nginx deals with the Kerberos authentication and redirects to streamlit with the REMOTE_USER proxy header.

I read the header within streamlit and verify auth for the user.

**Problems with this solution**

This approach has many flaws, for Instance someone can create another Nginx instance and redirect to the streamlit app with a hard coded REMOTE_USER header.

**Preferred solution**

The ideal solution to this would be the addition of native Kerberos authentication support with a keytab file.

title: Streamlit websocket timeout is set too low
body:
### Summary

`/stream` websocket timeout is set too low (1s)

It is set to 1 second [here](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/blob/96f17464a13969ecdfe31043ab8e875718eb0d10/frontend/src/lib/WebsocketConnection.tsx#L54), recommend it to be updated to 10 seconds.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Use linux traffic control to simulate high latency

```
# tc qdisc add dev lo root netem delay 1000ms
```

2. Run a basic streamlit application:

```
# test.py
import streamlit as st
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

st.write("Test")
st.write(pd.DataFrame({
    'first': [1, 2, 3, 4],
    'second': [10, 20, 30, 40]
}))
```

```
$ streamlit run test.py
```

3. Go to 127.0.0.1:8501

**Expected behavior:**

Connects

**Actual behavior:**

Websocket attempts to connect, but if it does not connect within 1 second, it is automatically cancelled and reconnects.

[image]
[image]

Recommend it to be set to 10 seconds.

Likely the root cause of #2389 #2312

### Is this a regression?

No

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: Streamlit, version 0.82.0
- Python version: Python 3.9.5
- Using Conda? PipEnv? PyEnv? Pex? No
- OS version: Arch Linux

title: Certificate generating error
body:
### Summary

When we try to generate a certificate via any method like email, qwiklabs etc. error is coming.

### Steps to reproduce
```

Check Your Progress by Email Id
Check Your Progress by Qwiklabs Public URL
Generate Your Profile Badge
Milestone Achievers

```
select any of them and enter a email or qwiklabs profile URL and hit enter then its getting error.

error like this :- 

```
AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'lower'
Traceback:

File "/app/.heroku/python/lib/python3.9/site-packages/streamlit/script_runner.py", line 333, in _run_script
    exec(code, module.__dict__)
File "/app/app.py", line 50, in <module>
    if sheet.cell(row=i, column=2).value.lower() == str.lower():
```

How To Fix?

```
I think the error is because the variable query is sometimes None. And you are applying .lower() function on it which only works on str type objects.

You can control this by putting your code inside a if loop which runs only when there's a string in query variable.
```

Thank you.

title: st.experimental_set_query_params() behaves differently locally vs. on sharing.streamlit.io
body:
First of all, thanks for all the work you all do! Just tried streamlit sharing and it is really nice. Keep up the awesome work!

### Summary

Locally, `st.experimental_set_query_params()` changes the query parameters in the URL bar, but doesn't trigger a refresh or rerun of the script. On sharing.streamlit.io it seems like it does.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Create `app.py` with the content below. This app prints the current query parameters, then allows you to create your own query parameter string to pass into the URL via `st.experimental_set_query_params()`. This code also lives at https://github.com/benlindsay/streamlit-sharing-query-params

    ```python
    # app.py
    from urllib.parse import urlencode, parse_qs
    import streamlit as st
    
    initial_query_params = st.session_state.get("initial_query_params")
    query_params = {k: v[0] for k, v in st.experimental_get_query_params().items()}
    if not initial_query_params:
        initial_query_params = query_params.copy()
        st.session_state["initial_query_params"] = initial_query_params.copy()
    
    st.write("Initial query params of the session:", initial_query_params)
    st.write("Query params before setting new ones:", query_params)
    
    new_query_string = st.text_area("New query params string (like 'a=b&c=d')", value=urlencode(initial_query_params))
    if st.button("Set new query params without starting new session"):
        st.experimental_set_query_params(**parse_qs(new_query_string))
    ```
2. Run `streamlit run app.py`. Type `localhost:8501?a=b` into a browser URL bar. It should look like this:

    [image]

3. Type `a=b&c=d` into the text area and press the button. The URL updates, but the query parameters printed above don't change, as expected. Looks like this:

    [image]

4. Press the button again and note that now the printed query parameters do match the query parameters in the URL bar, as expected.

5. Now deploy this app to `sharing.streamlit.io` and repeat the steps on the deployed app. I have it deployed to https://share.streamlit.io/benlindsay/streamlit-sharing-query-params/main/app.py. So start with https://share.streamlit.io/benlindsay/streamlit-sharing-query-params/main/app.py?a=b, then write `a=b&c=d` in the text area and click the button. This time, the query params higher up in the page change as well, as though the script was rerun after setting the query parameters at the end.

    [image]

I noticed this when trying to get a bootstrap tabs hack working in streamlit sharing. The code for the tabs test is here: https://github.com/benlindsay/streamlit-sharing-tabs and it's deployed to here: https://share.streamlit.io/benlindsay/streamlit-sharing-tabs/main/app.py. In the code, I always set the query parameters at the end. When running locally, this works fine, but because of the rerun on sharing, clicking on any of the tabs leads to a not-quite-infinite loop.

### Is this a regression?

This is my first try at streamlit sharing, so I don't know.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 0.85.1
- Python version: 3.9.1
- Using pip
- OS version: OSX Mojave 10.14.6
- Browser version: Chrome Version 90.0.4430.212 (Official Build) (x86_64)

comments.text:
Hey @user Thanks for the report. I have confirmed the issue, and the solution will require some thinking. The local development version is the most "accurate" expectation on how it should work. That is, the query params are set (at the end), but the script isn't re-executed. If you reran the script with no change, it would pick up the query params correctly.

There is a more _right_ way, which is to use callbacks.

```python
def set_new_params():
    st.experimental_set_query_params(**parse_qs(new_query_string))

st.button("Set new query params without starting new session", on_click=set_new_params)
```

Callbacks are executed _before_ the script runs, so this code should work both locally and in cloud.

Given the experimental nature of query params, we haven't quite determined whether the behavior should mimic the local behavior, the sharing behavior, or if experimental query params should be changed. I can say that in either case, callbacks is a safer bet to use.

@user you're probably running into #1532 with the selectbox. It's something to do with the cache and grokking what actually is happening is a little mind-bending. Nonetheless, I work around it by:

* check if `session_state.square_default_index` exists yet
* if not, compute the first index and store it in `session_state.square_default_index`. Never update this!
* _always_ use `session_state.square_default_index` as your index in your selectbox (it's supposed to be the initial index, not representative of the current index)

I'm going to stop hijacking this thread ---->  #1532 ;)

I am having the same issues with checkboxes as well. The first time the selectbox is changed og a checkbox is clicked, nothing happens. But after doing such a "refresh", the next change works properly.
Do I have to invoke session states? I do not use them currently.

Hi @user You've uncovered a common situation that occurs. One of the biggest challenges internally in Streamlit is identifying one line of code to which UI component on the screen. We've attempted to solve it in different ways, but we ended on a more simplistic approach. We [defined the behavior in our docs](https://docs.streamlit.io/library/advanced-features/widget-semantics).

The script you provided produces this behavior because of number 4. "A widget's identity depends on the arguments passed to the widget function." You've changed the index argument in the select box.

Good news is that session state solves this pretty easily.

```python
import streamlit as st

# Get param information
params = st.experimental_get_query_params()
metric = params.get("metric", ["0"])[0] # Note I modified the default value to work
metrics = [str(i) for i in range(5)]

# initialize selectbox value if the metric is in the list (ie it's valid)
if metric in metrics and 'num' not in st.session_state:
    st.session_state.num = metric

metric = st.sidebar.selectbox('What to square?', metrics, index=0, key="num")

st.markdown(f'# The square of {metric} is {int(metric)**2}.')
st.experimental_set_query_params(metric=metric)
```

Note that in the selectbox, the arguments never change. We simply set the initial value above and let the select box do the work of retaining its state (followed by updating the query param value)

title: Health endpoint for checking that a script compiles and runs correctly
body:
### Problem

Currently there is no way to detect that the streamlit app is actually not running - if there is an error inside the client script (e.g. missing dependency, script error) the application still starts and the /healthz endpoint returns success. 

S4T requires better app monitoring and it would be helpful to detect the applications that cannot start because the above type of error.

### Solution

A new endpoint  will be provided which will return 200 HTTP status code if the script compiles and runs correctly. Alternatively a 503 HTTP status code is returned and the body will contain the error message.

The endpoint by default will be `/check-script`. However, it can be changed by specifying the config option `server.checkScriptEndpoint`

title: file_uploader is slow when deployed
body:
### Summary

When I run my app locally, file uploads are fine. 13.6 MB video works fine, 1.21 GB video works fine, and file upload is fast.
When I deploy my app to Streamlit Sharing, Docker (on its own), and Heroku via Docker,  both uploads are much slower than locally, the 13.6MB video eventually makes it, but the 1.21 GB video crashes the app. 

I have `maxUploadSize=4096` in my .streamlit/config.toml and it is reflected in the file uploader widget:
[image]

Source code is here: https://github.com/kevinlinxc/UnpauseFFRK
### Steps to reproduce

Add a file uploader:
`uploaded_file = st.file_uploader("Choose a file", type=['mp4', 'avi'])`
Deploy to any of the above environments. I followed this guide https://github.com/ash2shukla/streamlit-heroku for docker+heroku, and just the standard stuff for streamlit sharing.
Upload a >1 gb Video file.

**Expected behavior:**

File upload is as fast or nearly as fast as it is when run locally. App does not crash for large files.

**Actual behavior:**

The app crashed.
Issue from when I thought this was just a streamlit sharing issue: https://discuss.streamlit.io/t/website-crashes-during-file-upload/16130
Some logs:
From streamlit sharing console:
`[manager] Streamlit server consistently failed status checks`
I've seen `H20 App Boot Timeout` numerous times

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 0.84.0
- Python version: 3.9.2
- Venv locally with requirements.txt, Docker otherwise
- OS version: Windows 10
- Browser version: Firefox 91

### Additional information

 I don't see other people having this issue with file_uploader so I decided to make this post.

title: Wrong display of app URL
body:
### Summary

When one starts a `streamlit` app, it shows a message saying that the app can then be viewed in browser. The port at which the app is exposed can be modified using `server.port` flag. If `.streamlit` directory with a `config.toml` file is present in the working directory, the URL displayed and the link that is opened automatically is incorrect. Both correspond to the values provided in the `config` file, while the app is actually exposed at the manually specified port correctly.

### Steps to reproduce

Code snippet:

```python3
import streamlit

streamlit.title("sample title")

```

Steps to reproduce the bug:

1. create an empty directory anywhere, say it's at `~/Desktop/bug_reprex_directory`
2. navigate to this directory and create `bug_reprex.py` using the code snippet above.
3. Start the app
    1. use: `python -m streamlit run --server.port 8502 bug_reprex.py`
    2. message displayed: `You can now view your Streamlit app in your browser. URL: http://localhost:8502` -> this is expected
    3. url opened: `http://localhost:8502` -> this is expected and the app gets shown correctly
4. close the app from browser and terminal
5. create configuration directory: `mkdir .streamlit`
5. create default configuration file: `python -m streamlit config show > .streamlit/config.toml`
6. Start the app again
    1. use: `python -m streamlit run --server.port 8502 bug_reprex.py`
    2. message displayed: `You can now view your Streamlit app in your browser. URL: http://localhost:8501` -> this is unexpected, expected `8502` instead of `8501`
    3. url opened: `http://localhost:8501` -> this is unexpected and the page does not load, as the app is actually exposed on  `http://localhost:8502`

**Expected behavior:**

1. Expected same behaviour in both cases, with and without configuration folder.
2. If not possible, expected same URL for both the displayed message and the actual URL where app is exposed for consistency

**Actual behavior:**

The message shows port `8501`, while the app is exposed at `8502` based on passed flag. Same goes for the opened URL.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: **0.87.0**
- Python version: **3.8.11**
- Using Conda? PipEnv? PyEnv? Pex?: **conda 4.10.3**
- OS version: **macOS 11.5.2**
- Browser version: **Safari 14.1.2**

comments.text:
Hi @user, this isn't quite a bug, but one could argue that we shouldn't encourage people to populate a default `.streamlit/config.toml` file by using the `streamlit config show` command.

What's happening here is that there are two config options that are port-related:

1. `browser.serverPort` sets the port that the app tries to connect to.
1. `server.port` sets the port the server is serving the app from.

By default, `browser.serverPort` gets set to `server.port`, but what's happening here is that setting your `config.toml` file via `python -m streamlit config show > .streamlit/config.toml` explicitly sets both to 8501, and then only changing the `server.port` config option leaves `browser.serverPort` serving from a port that doesn't match. This can be fixed by removing the `browser.serverPort` config option from your `config.toml` file so that it goes back to the default of matching what's set in `server.port`.

Hi @user, I completely missed `browser.serverPort` and your explanation makes sense. Thanks a lot 😊 

However, if you don't mind explaining a bit more, what is the point of making two configurations public? Is there any scenario where user will need to use different ports for these two? If not, can you not expose just one of them and set other to be same internally?

Hey @user,

There actually are scenarios where the two won't match -- they don't show up often, but it is possible for some to come up in more advanced deployment scenarios. The one that comes to mind would be if streamlit is deployed behind a reverse proxy like nginx, so the browser should connect to the port that nginx is serving from, and the streamlit server itself will be serving from a different port.

title: Event listener error on Safari when run with Docker
body:
### Summary

Streamlit versions newer than approx v0.78 can cause an event listener error in macOS Safari when Dockerised. This example below works fine in Chrome and Firefox, just not Safari.

### Steps to reproduce

Create a minimal Dockerfile:

```dockerfile
FROM python:3.9-slim-buster

WORKDIR /service

COPY requirements.txt .
RUN pip install -r requirements.txt

COPY app.py .

EXPOSE 8501
CMD ["streamlit", "run", "app.py"]
```

A requirements.txt:

```
streamlit==0.88.0  # broken on safari
# streamlit==0.79.0  # broken on safari
# streamlit==0.78.0  # works on safari
```

An example app.py:

```python
import streamlit as st
import time
import numpy as np

progress_bar = st.sidebar.progress(0)
status_text = st.sidebar.empty()
last_rows = np.random.randn(1, 1)
chart = st.line_chart(last_rows)

for i in range(1, 101):
    new_rows = last_rows[-1, :] + np.random.randn(5, 1).cumsum(axis=0)
    status_text.text("%i%% Complete" % i)
    chart.add_rows(new_rows)
    progress_bar.progress(i)
    last_rows = new_rows
    time.sleep(0.05)

comments.text:
Hi @user, I believe this is expected behavior.

The value of a `file_uploader` is not cleared until you reset the widget via the UI, so on subsequent script runs triggered by interacting with the app, the `if file_object is not  None:` statement will always run.

One way of achieving the behavior you desire would be to give your `file_uploader` widget a key and process newly uploaded files using an [on_change callback](docs.streamlit.io/library/api-reference/session-state#use-callbacks-to-update-session-state). The reason your file_uploader also needs a key is that the way that you can access the newly uploaded file from within the callback is to access it via `st.session_state.<your_file_uploader_key>`

title: Make hamburger menu mode configurable via config option
body:
### Problem

See #3856 . Developer would like the ability to configure whether the developer menu or viewer menu is displayed while they are developing on cloud IDEs like Gitpod or Github Codespaces

### Solution

Create a config option

```
showDeveloperMenu: true | false | auto
```

where
* **true**: always shows the developer menu locally and while deployed
* **false**: always shows the viewer menu locally and while deployed
* **auto**: shows developer menu when on localhost and viewer menu when on non-localhost deployment (This is the current behavior on Streamlit Cloud)

default is set to **auto**

---

Community voting on feature requests enables the Streamlit team to understand which features are most important to our users.

title: User's session_info.ws object is None on first page load
body:
### Summary

I'm using Streamlit v1.2.0, and I noticed that, on first page load, the `session_info.ws` attribute of the following snippet is `None` until the second time the user visits the page (i.e. via a refresh or re-run). Is this the expected behavior, or am I missing something?

My actual goal is to get the request headers, and the below snippet has been adapted from https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/1083

### Steps to reproduce

Put the below code snippet into a `main.py` file and then `streamlit run main.py`. You should see the warning markdown once your browser redirects to the app. Any future page refreshes, re-runs, etc. do not seem to have this issue. It's only on first run (when the server state is `WAITING_FOR_FIRST_BROWSER`) that the websocket is `None`.

Code snippet:

```
import streamlit as st
from streamlit.server.server import Server
from streamlit.report_thread import get_report_ctx

session_id = get_report_ctx().session_id
session_info = Server.get_current()._get_session_info(session_id)
if session_info.ws is None:  # at first page load, this is None
    st.markdown("Unable to get session websocket. Try refreshing the page.")
    st.stop()
headers = session_info.ws.request.headers
st.write(headers)
```

**Expected behavior:**

The `session_info.ws` object should be populated immediately on user connect, prior to the main app code being executed.

**Actual behavior:**

The `session_info.ws` object only seems to be populated on subsequent page refreshes or app re-runs.

### Is this a regression?

I don't think so.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.2.0
- Python version: 3.8.10
- Using Conda? PipEnv? PyEnv? Pex? Conda
- OS version: macOS 12.0.1
- Browser version: Chrome Version 96.0.4664.55 (Official Build) (arm64)

### Additional information

I've been running Streamlit behind NGINX for awhile now and only noticed this problem when trying to read from the request headers. It's possible that this issue is connected to some sort of misconfiguration in my NGINX setup, but that doesn't seem likely given that the actual issue is the `session_info.ws` object not being populated initially. To be clear, I'm able to reproduce this bug solely through `streamlit run main.py` and without NGINX even in the picture.

comments.text:
Hi @user,

This is happening due to some optimizations that we have in place to make the first page load of an app faster. When a streamlit server starts, we run the script immediately to warm a cache to allow the first load of a page to be almost-instantaneous (the output of the first script run is saved and sent to the browser on connect), and this is why `session_info.ws` is `None` until the page is refreshed.

I'm not entirely sure if there's a good way of fixing this as the `server` and `report_thread` modules are technically internal (I don't believe there's a good way of preventing users from importing the internal modules of a package in Python), so it's difficult for us to give any guarantees on functionality built using them. I'll leave this issue open and will spend some time thinking about it, but I'm not entirely sure if we'll be able to address it easily given the root cause.

@user btw. there is `st.experimental_rerun` to trigger a rerun which might help as a workaround here. 

@user I also had a few issues with preheating and came to the conclusion that it is a bit more problematic than useful. In case you take this issue on, I can give you a bit more context.

Thanks @user, I'll get your input on what's problematic about preheated script runs sometime soon.

I'm not sure if we'll have time to directly address this issue given the work we have currently planned / the fact that it's only possible to run into it when using internal modules, but I just realized that the multipage apps project (depending on the exact design) may also push us to consider removing preheated script runs entirely, especially given that the value diminishes greatly if the first page that opens is an index page linking to various apps rather than an individual page.

I'll keep this issue updated as we know more, but it looks like there's a relatively high chance of us deciding that this optimization isn't worth it and remove it entirely 🙂

The main issue is that anything that involves specific information about the current session or user is incompatible with preheating. I worked on a way to access the browser timezone of the current session in the python backend. However, the main blocking factor is that this is not compatible with preheating (since preheating does not have any knowledge about potential sessions). Preheating is also already deactivated if `experimental_get_query_params` is used ([see here](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/blob/4fc958b71b0ca19e572bec025eb042f718f4ed8f/lib/streamlit/report_session.py#L489)). Apps using anything related to `st.user` will also most likely not be able to use preheating.

Following as have Streamlit app deployed as Azure app service in which I'm logging telemetry including authenticated user derived from http headers retrieved from session_info.

As @user indicates, ws is None until page refresh.

Also, as suggested, checking and rerunning seems reasonable workaround:

```
if session_info.ws is None:
    st.experimental_rerun()
```

EDIT: above workaround OK when running in localhost. However, when streamlit deployed to Azure, the containerised web app fails to start, doesn't like the rerun. Doubt those container specific logs are useful

I can second what @user experienced. When using `st.experimental_rerun()`, the app fails to start when I deploy it to Kubernetes on GCP (I believe it has to do with some sort of health checks). I was able to get it to work locally, but obviously that is not an acceptable solution.

Following up on this:

We did some investigation, and it seems like the problematic optimization causing this weirdness is actually a vestigial feature from when Streamlit's main use case was very different than what it is now (I believe it was built before we quite knew what direction the library was going to go in -- apparently we didn't even have widgets then!)

Since it's starting to look like some projects/features we have planned for Q1 of next year are going to run into trouble with this exact optimization, we'll most likely aim to remove it relatively soon. I can't give an exact timeline on when this will happen, but I do think it's likely to begin soon after the start of the new year.
I can echo the experience here. We rely on the session_info to get the headers to verify the logged in user. Would be highly appreciated if this gets more stable soon.
@user Happy New Year, hope you had a great one. Soon for update?

Hi @user, happy new year to you, too!

I've started an internal discussion on this to make sure we're not missing anything in thinking that the problematic optimization can be safely removed. So far, it looks like there won't be any problems, but I want to give people a few more days to bring up any concerns they may have (much of the company is just starting to come back to work).

Assuming there aren't any complications, I would expect work on this to begin late this week or early next. I'm also fairly confident that the changes are straightforward, so they should be quickly finished and will ideally land in the next release or two.

Quick update since I know there are a few people watching this issue:

Removing preheated script runs was relatively easy, but doing so also uncovered a few places where our tests are flaky, and I'm currently working to fix those issues.

I don't expect it to take me too much longer from here to get #4259 merged, but since v1.4 is being released tomorrow, I would guess that #4259 will be released in v1.5 around the end of this month.

Merged! The fix should land in the v1.5 release (scheduled for the 27th)

Also, note that a refactor removed `streamlit.report_thread`, so you'll want to use `get_script_run_ctx` from `streamlit.script_run_ctx` to get the code snippet in the issue body to work again
@user Will there be another nightly release soon? I'd love to get ahead of this if possible, and I had some issues installing from source.
@user hopefully there will be one tonight or tomorrow -- it turns out that I was actually the one that broke the nightly job so am working on a fix now 😬

> Merged! The fix should land in the v1.5 release (scheduled for the 27th)
> 
> Also, note that a refactor removed `streamlit.report_thread`, so you'll want to use `get_script_run_ctx` from `streamlit.script_run_ctx` to get the code snippet in the issue body to work again

This has broken the import `from streamlit.report_thread import get_report_ctx` in version 1.4.0
I would also favor not to break the existing API contract with `from streamlit.report_thread import get_report_ctx`, if that's possible.

Hi @user, @user --

This is most likely not going to be something that gets changed back. The `streamlit.report_thread` module is an internal module that isn't considered part of streamlit's public API. While it's still possible to import it as I don't believe Python prevents you from importing a package's submodules, the `report_thread` module is undocumented, and thus we don't give any guarantees as to the stability of its API.

We're aware that importing internal submodules and using them has been suggested in the forums to achieve certain things that we don't officially support, but unfortunately we're unable to guarantee that we'll follow SemVer for modules that we consider internal.

title: Unable to use sidebar with columns in same web page
body:
### Summary

You will get an error "Missing Submit Button" when putting a sidebar and columns in a same page

### Steps to reproduce

Code snippet:

```python
import streamlit as st
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
import plotly.express as px
import plotly.graph_objects as go
#streamlit run app.py --server.port 8502
st.set_page_config(
        page_title="Summary",
        layout="wide"
)

st.title("Test")
#st.markdown("Example of markdown")
#st.header("Example of header")
col1, col2 = st.columns((3,2))
col3, col4 = st.columns((1,1))
with st.sidebar:
    myform = st.form(key='my_form')
    myform.title("Parameters")
    user_word = myform.text_input("Enter a keyword", "habs")
    select_language = myform.radio('Tweet language', ('All', 'English', 'French'))
    include_retweets = myform.checkbox('Include retweets in data')
    num_of_tweets = myform.number_input('Maximum number of tweets', 100)
    submit_button = myform.form_submit_button(label='Submit')

pd.set_option('display.max_rows',None)

if 'count' not in st.session_state:
    st.session_state.count = 0

with col1:
    st.markdown('In column 1')

with col2:
    st.markdown('In Column 2')
    st.markdown('')
    st.markdown('')
    st.markdown('')

    st.header("Sunburst Diagran")

with col3:
    option = st.selectbox(
     'How would you like to be contacted?',
     ('Email', 'Home phone', 'Mobile phone'))

with col4:
    st.markdown('')
    st.markdown('')
    increment = st.button('Increment')
    if increment:
        st.session_state.count += 1

st.write(f'Count = {st.session_state.count}')
st.write("Bye")
```

title: Allow console_scripts as streamlit run scripts
body:
### Problem

Right now streamlit requires a raw Python script (e.g. `your_script.py`) that is invoked, e.g.
```
streamlit run your_script.py [-- script args]
```

This is really frustrating if you want to package your streamlit application in a wheel file and distribute it to your friends & colleagues.  Streamlit's requirement of a raw Python script makes this impossible.

Assume I have created a proper Python package/distribution `my-streamlit-dashboard` and uploaded it to PyPI or some company-internal artefact store. If my colleagues now runs `pip install my-streamlit-dashboard`, my package will be installed but how would my colleague now run my dashboard? There is no `script.py` entry point for him or her to run. 

### Solution

For use-cases like this, Python packaging allows the definition of `console_scripts` which allow you to define command-line scripts that are installed e.g. within your virtual environment, and behave like normal shell scripts (but are actual Python scripts). All details can be found [here](https://python-packaging.readthedocs.io/en/latest/command-line-scripts.html#the-console-scripts-entry-point). Quite many Python tools & frameworks use this capability like for instance [PyScaffold's `putup` command](https://github.com/pyscaffold/pyscaffold), [Django's `django-admin` command](https://docs.djangoproject.com/en/3.2/ref/django-admin/), [poetry's `poetry` command](https://python-poetry.org/docs/) and streamlit's own `streamlit` command.

Continuing the example from above, I could define a console-script `my-cool-dashboard` within the package `my-streamlit-dashboard` that would act as the initial script to run for streamlit, i.e.
```
streamlit run my-streamlit-dashboard
```
For this to work, streamlit would need to allow console scripts defined by `console_scripts` as start points for dashboard. Technically this should be possible as they are just Python scripts. Doing this right now leads to the error:
```
Error: Streamlit requires raw Python (.py) files, but the provided file has no extension.
For more information, please see https://docs.streamlit.io
```
if the console script doesn't end with `.py`, which is common. Adding `.py` leads to:
```
Error: Invalid value: File does not exist: my-cool-dashboard.py
```
A crude and unsatisfying workaround is:
```
streamlit run `which my-cool-dashboard.py`
```
This seems to mostly work but also emits nasty errors during execution:
```
File "/Users/<user>/.mambaforge/envs/streamlit-demo/lib/python3.9/site-packages/streamlit/script_runner.py", line 354, in _run_script
    exec(code, module.__dict__)
File "/Users/<user>/.mambaforge/envs/streamlit-demo/bin/my-streamlit-dashboard.py", line 33, in <module>
    sys.exit(load_entry_point('my-streamlit-dashboard', 'console_scripts', 'my-cool-dashboard.py')())
```

### Additional context

What are the benefits of making packaging for streamlit apps possible? I'm glad you asked! 
* Another way of distribution. For production, a streamlit app would right now be deployed as docker container most likely. Allowing proper packaging would also make it possible for users to just install and run it locally via pip. Thus more **flexibility**.
* Proper **versioning**. Since Python packages/distributions are versioned, one could apply proper versioning to these packages and enforce certain processes within an organisation, like semantic versioning etc. which is hard if everyone is just cloning a git repo. 
* Enabling [**ML-Ops** principles](https://ml-ops.org/content/mlops-principles). Most organisation provide templates for Python projects that support developers in applying techniques like testing (CI/CD), reproducibility, documentation, deployment, etc. With the suggested solution it would be much easier to incorporate streamlit in such templates as e.g. provided by [PyScaffold](https://pyscaffold.org/).

---

Community voting on feature requests enables the Streamlit team to understand which features are most important to our users.

## Update 

The packaging use case is now supported via `st.App.run()` (added in #15563 and available since Streamlit 1.59.0), although `streamlit run <console-script>` itself still requires a Python-file target.

A package can expose a console script whose entry point does:

```python
from pathlib import Path
import streamlit as st

def main() -> None:
    st.App(Path(__file__).with_name("dashboard.py")).run()
```

Using an absolute package path is important because the generated console-script executable lives in the virtual environment's `bin` directory.

title: st.file_uploader returns HTTP code 400 with invalid session_id when deployed on Kubernetes
body:
### Summary

In my Streamlit app deployed in a standalone Docker container, local files can be uploaded via **st.file_uploader** without any problems. However, for the same app deployed on Kubernetes cluster in multiple replicas setting, st.file_uploader randomly returns HTTP status code 400 with an error message like: 

_**400: Invalid session_id: '1d319bd4-b1dc-4149-bfb2-24cdd48f3982'**_

[image]

The behaviour is non-deterministic - reloading (sometimes more than once) the browser tab helps.

### Steps to reproduce

- Deploy a Streamlit app on Kubernetes with multiple replicas
- Run the app in a browser
- Select any file in st.file_uploader's window.
- If the error doesn't occur, reload the browser tab and try again.

Code snippet:

```
st.file_uploader("Choose a file")
```

**Expected behavior:**

st.file_uploader works exactly the same way in a single Docker container and when deployed on Kubernetes cluster with multiple replicas.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.0.0
- Python version: 3.7.8
- continuumio/miniconda3:4.9.2 Docker image

### Additional information

The problem was reported previously in a comment https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/2803#issuecomment-948079579 , but without specific details.

Hi @user, this one might be a bit tricky to solve given that the `file_uploader` is by its nature a stateful widget. I haven't spent any time trying to reproduce the issue myself, but I'm fairly certain what's going on here is that the `/upload` endpoint that the streamlit frontend attempts to use is having its request routed to a different node than the one that the frontend is connected to via websocket.

One possible solution to this would be to turn on some form of sticky sessions / sticky request routing in your deployment to ensure that the server that receives the `/upload` request is the same one that the frontend initially connected to.

In the long run, we'll be thinking about these types of problems given that they'll start to come up more naturally as people build streamlit apps that need to scale to more and more users. In the short term, however, it's unlikely that we'll be able to address this soon as doing so would require a substantial overhaul to how the file uploader widget works, so your best bet to fix this soon would likely be to see if sticky sessions are possible for your use-case

Hey @user,

Coincidentally, we're currently working on a project that will eventually enable users to configure pieces of the file uploader widget so that it can operate more smoothly in multi-instance deployments.  We've recently worked on several projects with a similar theme of making the Streamlit internals more configurable, but the piece we're missing before we'll be able to expose all of these things publicly is a more advanced config system. See this comment on a similar issue for more context: https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/5849#issuecomment-1510010145.

That being said, even once everything is available for public use, I'd probably still recommend relying on session affinity to get `st.file_uploader` to work as expected in most multi-instance deployments.

The difficulty with getting a widget like the file uploader to work correctly when there are several streamlit server instances (assuming no session affinity) is that the file upload, which happens via HTTP as sending large files via websocket comes with its own set of difficulties, may land on a different server than the one the browser has a websocket connection to. As a result of this, a solution would require either
1. Streamlit servers to be able to talk to each other to pass files around
    * This would require some nontrivial configuration outside of streamlit itself to enable service discovery. It also feels somewhat hacky
2. A way to upload files to a shared location (like AWS S3 or some other intermediary service) rather than directly to an individual streamlit server
    * This is what the in-progress changes to the file uploader widget will enable. It feels like the more "correct" solution to me 

The difficulty with both solutions is that they're far from "automatic" -- developers will have to do a nontrivial amount of work outside of Streamlit to get everything set up. While some users will certainly have use cases where it's worth the effort to do this (including us at Snowflake, which is why we're building this configurability into the file uploader to begin with), I'd imagine that it wouldn't be worth the effort compared to just turning on sticky sessions in most situations.

I have gone through all the comments here but found no mention of a fix for Docker. I’m just echoing to see if anyone else has found a fix.

**Update (for whoever needs it):**

I was able to fix the issue by updating the NGINX server to properly load balance the replicas based on the user's IP. The fix was switching the load balancing algorithm from `least_connections` to `ip_hash`.

**One important note:**

Each replica of the Streamlit application must run on a separate port. So if you have 4 Streamlit containers, each should expose a unique port on the host machine:

```bash
Container A → 8601
Container B → 8602
Container C → 8603
Container D → 8604
```

Hope this helps anyone running into the same issue.

I was facing the same issue in some of my Streamlit applications deployed on Azure Web Apps.

The exact error I was encountering was _axios 400 invalid_id._

This was happening when uploading files using `st.file_uploader`, regardless of the file size or type (.xlsx, .pdf, .pptx, .zip, etc.). The behavior was inconsistent: roughly 1 out of 4 uploads would succeed, and the rest would fail with the axios 400 error. The only workaround was to retry multiple times until it eventually worked.

I also had a similar problem with `st.download_button`. In that case, the download would sometimes return a corrupted binary file, and again, multiple retries were required to get a valid file.

These issues never occurred in local environments — only on the deployed Azure Web App.

Initially, I checked the Azure Web App configuration, and the sticky sessions option (ARR affinity) was already enabled. Then, I noticed that the instance count for each environment (dev, uat, prod) was set to 5 instances. This means requests could be routed to different instances, which likely caused inconsistencies in session/file handling.

Solution: Reducing the instance count to 1 resolved the issue completely.

title: User's session_state is reset on websocket close
body:
### Summary

When using session_state on the backend and browsing the app, if the websocket close between the front and the back, on websocket re establishment session_state is lost.
 
### Steps to reproduce
Having a proxy between the front and the back, setting a connection timeout with the value of your choice, websocket will close after this value and session_state for this particular user will be lost.

It happened to me because I have my streamlit app running on GCP Cloud Run behind a Load Balancer. 
I can set the timeout to maximum 60 minutes but best behaviour would be that streamlit backend is able to recover session_state of a particular user on websocket re establishment.

**Expected behavior:**

User will see no change on websocket close -> backend is able to retrieve session_state for the user on websocket close/reopen.

**Actual behavior:**

User losts his work saved in session_state on websocket close.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.3.1
- Python version: 3.7.10
- Using Conda [X]

### Additional information
Would love to have a workaround I could apply now :)
And subsidiary question would be: is this planed to store session_state on an external datastore (redis?).
It seems that it would allow running multiple backends behind a LB to handle more users simultaneously.

title: Provide way to run with the WSGI/ASGI protocols
body:
### Problem

We have a Django backend and a Vue.js frontend. We also deploy Streamlit to render some charts with Django functions. Both Django and Streamlit are in the same repository and Docker image. In order to bring up both Django and Streamlit in the Kubernetes cluster we need two almost identical deployments of the same image: One for Django and one for Streamlit.

### Additional context

I'm putting into practice this advice of @user on the [forum](https://discuss.streamlit.io/t/running-streamlit-on-serverless/1356/5?u=stefanbrand): 

> If you’re finding ASGI support to be an important aspect of whether you want to use Streamlit or not, I would recommend filing an enhancement request 7 on our github repo.

It seems a prerequisite is ASGI support in Tornado: https://github.com/tornadoweb/tornado/issues/2666

---

Community voting on feature requests enables the Streamlit team to understand which features are most important to our users.

## Update

We are planning to migrate Streamlit to Starlette in https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/12772. This will make it compatible with other ASGI servers (e.g. FastAPI). However, its unlikely that we will add direct support for integrating Streamlit with Django.

Super excited for this. I just trialled this locally where I tried to mount a FastAPI app, as well as the Streamlit app into a parent app and it works. The trick was in the Streamlit setup and configuration (to run with Starlette), as well as making sure the Streamlit runtime is correctly started and (optionally) managed by the parent FastAPI app lifespan. 

The setup  looks something like:
```python
from contextlib import asynccontextmanager

from fastapi import FastAPI
from streamlit.runtime import Runtime, RuntimeConfig
from streamlit.web.server.starlette.starlette_app import create_starlette_app

from fastapi_app.main import app as base_app

runtime_config = RuntimeConfig(
    script_path=streamlit_script,  # path to where streamlit app is 
    command_line=None,
    media_file_storage=media_file_storage,  # mfs and ufm objects 
    uploaded_file_manager=uploaded_file_manager,
)

streamlit_runtime = Runtime(runtime_config)

streamlit_starlette_app = create_starlette_app(streamlit_runtime)

@user
async def lifespan(app: FastAPI):
    nonlocal streamlit_runtime
    if streamlit_runtime:
        await streamlit_runtime.start()

    yield

    if streamlit_runtime:
        await streamlit_runtime.stop()

app = FastAPI(lifespan=lifespan)

for route in base_app.routes:
    app.routes.append(route)

if streamlit_starlette_app:
    app.mount("/streamlit", streamlit_starlette_app)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    import uvicorn
    uvicorn.run(app, host="0.0.0.0", port=8000)
```

It would be cool to include a how-to / usage guide on this in the PR / follow-on PR. Happy to help contribute.
@user We are planning to make this even simpler, see: https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/13449

> [@user](https://github.com/jiriklein) We are planning to make this even simpler, see: [#13449](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/13449)

huh, that's pretty cool - so you'd effectively squash all of the `RuntimeConfig` and `Runtime` management into standalone `st.App` object, then mount that to a parent app if you so wish?
yep and it allows to apply some advanced configurations (e.g. routes / middelware ..)

## Update

Exciting news 🎉 Starting with **Streamlit 1.53**, we've added experimental ASGI support via the new Starlette integration.

You can now run Streamlit as a standard ASGI application:

```python
from streamlit.starlette import App

app = App("dashboard.py")

# Run with any ASGI server:
# uvicorn myapp:app
# gunicorn -k uvicorn.workers.UvicornWorker myapp:app
# hypercorn myapp:app
# or streamlit run myapp.py
```

This also enables deploying Streamlit alongside Django, FastAPI, Flask or other frameworks:

```python
from starlette.routing import Mount
from django.core.asgi import get_asgi_application
from streamlit.starlette import App

django_app = get_asgi_application()

# Mount Django into Streamlit
# Streamlit at /, Django at /django/*
app = App(
    "dashboard.py",
    routes=[Mount("/django", app=django_app)],
)
```

We'd love your feedback on this feature! Please try it out and report any issues in our [feedback thread](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/13600).

> **Note:** Requires `pip install streamlit[starlette]`

## Update

Starlette will become the default server in 1.57 which will make Streamlit ASGI compatible described above without having to install the `starlette` dependencies. The `App` object will also be available in the `st` namespace:

```python
import streamlit as st

...

st.App(...)
```
