title: Streamlit cloud requests read/write permissions to private repositories when deploying public application
body:
### Summary

When I want to deploy public application on streamlit cloud, I press the "New app" button and Streamlit starts to require additional permissions (full access to private repositories) - just before I can even choose the repository.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Go to share.streamlit.io
2. Login with GitHub, allow the first set of permissions (reading user data, "admin! access to repository hooks and services")
3. Click "New app" button (same if clicking on "New app->From existing repo")
4. Additional permissions described above are required (full public + private repositories access!)
5. When pressing cancel, redirecting to share.streamlit.io/error

**Expected behavior:**

It's expected to go to share.streamlit.io/deploy after pressing the "New app" button. Streamlit should require additional permissions only if I want to deploy private repository.

**Actual behavior:**

Requesting permissions which are not necessary, without explanation.

### Additional information

Related to my (unanswered) question here: https://discuss.streamlit.io/t/please-explain-better-required-github-permissions/21401.

title: Query parameters are not read on first run in streamlit cloud
body:
### Summary

When deploying an app to streamlit cloud, I discovered that query parameters behaved differently than in my local development version. In my app, I set a default value for a field in `session_state` if it is not provided through query parameters, but I could never get the query parameters to work on the cloud deployment. After some debugging, I found that query parameters always seem to be empty on the first run of the app in streamlit cloud.
 
### Steps to reproduce

Code snippet:

```python
import logging

import streamlit as st

params = st.experimental_get_query_params()
logging.info(f"{params=}")
if "my-field" not in params:
    st.session_state["MY_FIELD"] = "some default value"

params_second = st.experimental_get_query_params()
if "MY_FIELD" in st.session_state:
    logging.info(f"{params_second=} {st.session_state['MY_FIELD']=}")
else:
    logging.info(f"{params_second=}")

st.write(params)
```
Open app in browser with query parameter like this `?my-field=0`

**Localhost behavior:**

```
2022-02-01 12:47:46.902 params={'my-field': ['0']}
2022-02-01 12:47:46.903 params_second={'my-field': ['0']}
```

**Streamlit cloud behavior:**

```
2022-02-01 12:02:06.085 params={'timestamp': ['1643716924162']}
2022-02-01 12:02:06.085 params_second={'timestamp': ['1643716924162']} st.session_state['MY_FIELD']='some default value'
2022-02-01 12:02:06.319 params={'my-field': ['0']}
2022-02-01 12:02:06.319 params_second={'my-field': ['0']} st.session_state['MY_FIELD']='some default value'
```

You can see that the app seems to run twice on streamlit cloud. In the first run the query parameters are empty (except a `timestamp`). The default value will get set in the session_state. In the second run the query parameters are present but the default value has already been set.

### Is this a regression?

I don't know.

### Debug info

- Streamlit, version 1.4.0
- Python 3.9.10
- Browser version: Chrome Version 97.0.4692.99

comments.text: Hi @user, this does not seem to be a streamlit library issue but possibly a streamlit cloud issue? Is it possible you can send me the link to your deployed app on streamlit cloud?

Hey @user, thanks for your reply:
The link to the streamlit cloud app: https://share.streamlit.io/bomme/st-query-params-test/main
But I guess you will not be able to see the logs. Maybe you can fork this repository to deploy the same app yourself? https://github.com/Bomme/st-query-params-test
Hey @user any update on this? 😃

Hey @user, I did some additional investigation. Indeed, Streamlit Cloud seems to always run the app two times when there is an URL parameter. Here is another snippet to test this:

```python
import streamlit as st

if "run_counter" not in st.session_state:
    st.session_state["run_counter"] = 1
else:
    st.session_state["run_counter"] += 1

st.write("Run counter: ", st.session_state["run_counter"])
```

If this app is [run with a query parameter](https://share.streamlit.io/lukasmasuch/st-query-parameter-bug/main/app.py?test=1), the run counter is `2`. And in case there is [no query parameter](https://share.streamlit.io/lukasmasuch/st-query-parameter-bug/main/app.py), the run counter is `1`. Locally, the run counter is always at 1 regardless of the query paramter.

Unfortunately, I don't have conclusive explanation yet on why this happens. I will forward this issue to the engineers from our cloud platform for further investigation.

Hey @user, the reason for this is because Streamlit Apps are currently loaded as iframes in Streamlit Cloud and query parameters are not directly added to the iframe's URL, but passed as a message to the iframe. Now, when the app is loaded and the iframe is reachable, the app is executed for the first time. When the query parameters are passed from Cloud to the App, a re-run is triggered. This explains why an app is executed twice.
I agree that the fact that an app behaves differently when deployed to Cloud can be confusing; though, right now, I cannot say whether and when this behavior will change, but I hope this anyways sheds some light on it 🙂
This has been implemented for cloud and should work as expected. Let us know if there is a problem. @user

title: Enable `request_rerun`-ing session through external sources and using a session_id
body:
_(Note, you don't have to fill out every section here. They're just here for guidance. That said, nicely detailed feature requests are more likely to get eng attention sooner)_

### Problem

Dear StreamLit Team, first of all, thank you deeply for this awesome framework. I have learned quite a lot diving through the codebase and resolved some long lasting issues of mine thanks to your ScriptRunner magic :)

I have been playing with StreamLit recently and I have the need to refresh a user tab from an external source, ideally from external requests.

I couldn't find the recommended way to do it, so I hacked StreamLit internals. 

I found an almost unused Handler (DebugHandler) on the tornado routes and patched it to enable receiving a refresh from outside using its get method.

```py
...
if _STREAMLIT_AVAILABLE:
    import urllib.parse as _parse

    import streamlit as st
    import streamlit.bootstrap as bootstrap
    import tornado
    from streamlit import config
    from streamlit.bootstrap import (
        _fix_matplotlib_crash,
        _fix_pydeck_mapbox_api_warning,
        _fix_sys_argv,
        _fix_sys_path,
        _fix_tornado_crash,
        _install_config_watchers,
        _on_server_start,
        _set_up_signal_handler,
    )
    from streamlit.cli import _get_command_line_as_string, check_credentials
    from streamlit.report_thread import get_report_ctx
    from streamlit.server.server import Server
    from tornado.web import RequestHandler

    class RefreshSessionHandler(RequestHandler):
        def initialize(self, server):
... [9 lines trimmed] ...
            session = session_info.session

            session.request_rerun(session._client_state)

    st.server.server.DebugHandler = RefreshSessionHandler

def _render_ui(script_path, args=None, **flag_options):
    # This code has been taken from StreamLit, so we can patch the DebugHandler
    # with our RefreshSessionHandler
    bootstrap.load_config_options(flag_options=flag_options)

    if args is None:
        args = []

    if flag_options is None:
        flag_options = {}

    command_line = _get_command_line_as_string()

    st._is_running_with_streamlit = True
    check_credentials()
    _fix_sys_path(script_path)
    _fix_matplotlib_crash()
    _fix_tornado_crash()
    _fix_sys_argv(script_path, args)
    _fix_pydeck_mapbox_api_warning()
    _install_config_watchers(flag_options)
    _set_up_signal_handler()
    ioloop = tornado.ioloop.IOLoop.current()
    with mock.patch("streamlit.server.server.DebugHandler", RefreshSessionHandler):
        server = Server(ioloop, script_path, command_line)
    server.start(_on_server_start)
    server.add_preheated_report_session()
    ioloop.start()
```

This worked perfectly for StreamLit 1.3.9, but the API has changed quite a lot since then and this hack doesn't work.

However, I believe there would be a growing community need to have a more reliable way for external sources to refresh a StreamLit UI. I believe this would be worth prioritizing.

As a side note, I have been investigating how to unittest StreamLit UI behaviour and looked into this test [test_calls_widget_callbacks](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/blob/develop/lib/tests/streamlit/scriptrunner/script_runner_test.py#L142) in particular.

I have used the `TestScriptRunner` to test my StreamLit apps, but its API changed between versions. I would like to ask the StreamLit Team to invest in making the testing tool stable and part of the main package. This would become critical for users to reliability productionize StreamLit apps.
And I am afraid this would create friction to buy into the StreamLit ecosystem if this isn't made available by the Core Team.

Thanks for you deeply for your time and effort !

---

Community voting on feature requests enables the Streamlit team to understand which features are most important to our users.

title: `st.altair_chart` ignoring `sort=` passed to altair chart
body:
### Summary

streamlit's `altair_chart` does not seem to respect `sort=` passed to altair. I am getting different output to what I see in the notebook. 

I am confused, as there have been discussions and issues on this before (albeit a while ago), and this approach is supposed to work. Sorry if I have missed something.

### Steps to reproduce

[[image]](https://issues.streamlitapp.com/?issue=gh-4398)

Code snippet:

```python
# %%
import altair as alt
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import streamlit as st

# %%
df = pd.DataFrame(
    {
        "index_x": [1, 2, 3, 1, 2, 3, 1, 2, 3],
        "index_y": [1, 1, 1, 2, 2, 2, 3, 3, 3],
        "value": np.random.rand(9),
    }
)

# %%
# df

# %%
ordering = [2, 3, 1]

# %%
ch = (
    alt.Chart(df)
    .mark_rect()
    .encode(
        x=alt.X("index_x:O", sort=ordering),
        y=alt.Y("index_y:O", sort=ordering),
        color="value:Q",
        tooltip=[
            "index_x",
            "index_y",
            "value",
        ],
    )
)

# %%
# ch

# %%
st.altair_chart(ch)  # , use_container_width=True)
```

Then `streamlit run` app.

[image]

[image]

Yes. _According to discussions, not personal experience._

title: Streamlit share cannot detect the image files in the github repo..!
body:
### Summary

Here if we want to display any image to the screen, we need to 1st load it to the app right. Suppose there is a text file and there is an image file, both are having the same folder location. The problem is that for images it is giving an error: File not found, but for other file types, they can be accessed without any problem in the github repo.

### Steps to reproduce

#first put any image in the github repo in the same folder as the app, then run the following code
Code snippet-1:
image=st.image('example.png')

Code-snippet-2:
with open('example.png','r') as f:
     image=f

Code-snippet-3:
with open('document.txt','r') as d:
     doc = d

#Here in the above example, both document.txt and the example.png are in the same folder.

**Expected behavior:**

Here both the image and the document should be accessed without any error.

**Actual behavior:**

Here the error is only for .png/.jpg files , and not for other file types. This should have the same behavior as in the local system.

### Is this a regression?

From the past discussions , there seems no problem, but it was persistent and was solved with some hacks. But all the tricks are not working now. Streamlit share is bahaving as if there is no file present in the github repo.

Note that this is only happening in the github repo and with streamlit share and not in the local file system.

comments.text:
Hi @user,

I believe this behavior was intentional (with the rationale that the vast majority of the time, sensitive data doesn't appear in the traceback aside from its main error message), but I can see why this behavior can be a bit weird (and also I don't think the traceback is guaranteed not to have sensitive information, it's just uncommon).

I'll loop our product team into this so that we can reevaluate (CC @user)

Hello @user @user  

Thanks for handling this. 
I don't think displaying the trace it is expected behaviour. When the feature was added (see https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/2770), it clearly says "uncaught exceptions in a Streamlit app will result in a generic "Something went wrong!" warning in the browser, rather than the exception and its traceback".
So the traceback should be hidden in theory.

@user I wonder if you guys plan to address this. For public-facing apps, showing the trace is not desirable, and can be unsafe. I wish that there was an option to let the uncaught exceptions bubble up so that I could catch them and deal with them the way I want. For example, I could catch it and display a sad puppy's picture instead of `st.exception`.
I guess a third option [here](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/blob/97a72649f225d80e645708d24b42f1e555618d6c/lib/streamlit/error_util.py#L25), under which the exception doesn't get handled, would be great.

I agree that there is a mismatch between what `showErrorDetails` is supposed to do (per the docs / my initial understanding of it based on its name) and what it does.

Per the [docs](https://docs.streamlit.io/library/advanced-features/configuration):

`# If set to False, an exception will result in a generic message being shown in the browser, and exceptions and tracebacks will be printed to the console only.`

As noted in this issue, the traceback does appear regardless of `showErrorDetails`'s value.

Thanks!
+1 to regard this as a bug and would be very desirable if fixed. For production apps this is a security risk.

As Vincent stated above, this behavior was intentional. We wanted to give users a way to report where an error is coming from. But I can see that it could be problematic. We're looking into it and will see if we want to change it!

Will chime in here that it would be useful with this functionality to limit even what gets printed to the console in the stdout. (per my [thread here on the streamlit forum](https://discuss.streamlit.io/t/potential-security-concern-with-streamlit-caching-error-messages/30331/10)). I noticed that database creds were getting printed in the exception. While **showErrorDetails** should theoretically hide the exception in the browser, the documentation seems to imply that the exception would still be printed in its entirety to the console. (Please correct me if I'm mistaken here.) 

Also do support the original post on hiding the traceback as well as the exception.  Especially with systems where our deployed applications are logged, sensitive data getting written out to stored logs (either in the exception or the traceback) in any way can become a huge no no. Would be great to be able to fully control the verbosity of the error messages on deployed applications.
facing the same issue, hiding error on client side while keeping them on server side is paramount to keep using streamlit as frontend

Hey, I found a small workaround for this, until Streamlit finally changes these things:
You can use HTML style tag, to hide the elements that use the classes of the traceback. 
This could look like this:
```python
st.markdown(
"""
<style>
.css-nps9tx, .e1m3hlzs0, .css-1p0bytv, .e1m3hlzs1 {
   visibility: collapse;
   height: 0px;
}
</style>
""",
unsafe_allow_html=True
)
``` 

It doesn't look perfect and it's still possible to view the traceback via the chrome dev tools, but it's at least not that obvious.

Here's another option that will disable Streamlit's "scriptrunner" `handle_uncaught_app_exception()` method. I use Sentry to capture and log the exception when in production (with an environment variable `DEBUG` to toggle between displaying the error or logging to Sentry).

```python
import sys
import os
from sentry_sdk import capture_exception

script_runner = sys.modules["streamlit.runtime.scriptrunner.script_runner"]
handle_uncaught_app_exception = script_runner.handle_uncaught_app_exception

def exception_handler(e):
    # Custom error handling
    if os.getenv("DEBUG", "true").lower() == "true":
        handle_uncaught_app_exception(e)
    else:
        capture_exception(e)

script_runner.handle_uncaught_app_exception = exception_handler
```

+1, I agree with @user and I think this is one of the issues that could block any serious team from using streamlit in a production environment. 

Considering that this has been open for more than a year, can the team (maybe @user ?) please provide an update on whether and when they plan to address such a big security risk (such as exposing service account credentials to the data warehouse)?

Hey! We're looking into this right now. Already wanted to do it a few months ago but it got moved due to some other projects and then I lost track of it, unfortunately. 

My current plan is to fix this by
1. hiding the traceback when `showErrorDetails = false` and
2. introducing a new option `showErrorDetails = "traceback"`, which has the current behavior (i.e. hide the exception message but show the traceback). 

That way, we can keep showing the traceback on Community Cloud (which we find pretty useful for debugging but happy to hear other opinions!) and developers can turn it off completely when needed / if their app contains sensitive information directly in the code. 

I still need to verify some things with the eng time but I'm hopeful we can get this done within the next few releases.
Hey! That sounds like a very sensible solution that would cover all the bases. Thanks for replying and looking forward to using your solution. ;)

@user about hiding the exception message in the terminal output/logs: are you planning to capture the error in some other way in this case or not at all? I could see some cases where turning off logging of exceptions might be useful. But it also seems weird since that's the standard Python behavior and there's no way to capture the exception if you turn it off. 

Also, I guess you could just achieve that behavior with a global try/except blog around your code and handling all exceptions yourself, correct?

hello @user! thank you for picking this back up - my ideal state for this is to be able to control the traceback verbosity such that if we fail for DB exception, then the actual print out of the traceback/exception is limited. Similar to how the displayed exception is controlled on the frontend side of the app when `showErrorDetails = False`, it would be great to have the option to control the output on the backend as well that is conditional on the type of error or the actual component from which the error arises. I suppose I'm describing something akin to having an option to declare a traceback verbosity alongside each streamlit component declaration (maybe as a decorator), but your proposed solution of being able to turn off the exception logging via the `showErrorDetails` parameter on the backend as well seems like a reasonable starting point. I would still plan to capture the individual exception types directly in the script using try/except handling, but admittedly it has been a little while since I thought about this problem in earnest.

[There is a workaround and it works quite well](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/3426)

```
import streamlit as st

def set_global_exception_handler(f):
    import sys
    script_runner = sys.modules["streamlit.runtime.scriptrunner.script_runner"]
    script_runner.handle_uncaught_app_exception.__code__ = f.__code__

def exception_handler(e):
    # Custom error handling
    st.image("https://media1.tenor.com/m/t7_iTN0iYekAAAAd/sad-sad-cat.gif")
    st.error(f"Oops, something funny happened with a {type(e).__name__}", icon="😿")

set_global_exception_handler(exception_handler)
```

I'm shocked this isn't the default behavior for `showErrorDetails=false` 

+1 Please add this functionality!!!

When trying to implement the above workaround, I am getting:
```
AttributeError: module 'streamlit.runtime.scriptrunner.script_runner' has no attribute 'handle_uncaught_app_exception'
```
Anybody else encounter this? Am I looking in the wrong location within `sys.modules["streamlit.runtime.scriptrunner.script_runner"]`?

I am using `streamlit` version 1.37.1

**UPDATE 1**: Apparently in version 1.37.x the location of `handle_uncaught_app_exception` has moved (back?) to the `streamlit.error_util` module. So this monkey-patching method works if you use `script_runner = sys.modules['streamlit.error_util']`.

**UPDATE 2**: In case anybody else is reading this with similar issues, I will paste my final code that is working on `streamlit` version 1.37.1 with Sentry. The important parts are that the `handle_uncaught_app_exception` is located in the `streamlit.error_util` module, only the `__code__` attribute should be monkey patched, and the `sentry_sdk` library needs to be imported WITHIN the patched code so that `streamlit` has access to it. I have a condition where I check if sentry is initialized, and if it is not, then I print the full error (with stacktrace) to the application. This is because I am only initializing sentry in our dev/prod environments; but for local testing/development I want the full error visible.

```python
import sentry_sdk
import streamlit as st
import sys

# (Conditionally) initialize sentry. If running locally, I do not initialize sentry.
sentry_sdk.init(...)

def exception_handler(e):
    # Custom error handling
    import sentry_sdk  # Needed because this is executed outside the current scope
    st.image(
        'https://i.giphy.com/media/v1.Y2lkPTc5MGI3NjExYWh4OHM0cmg0bTJlMnBzNmV6cjdmYjlyejhjMm'
        'YyOTJja3I0amN3aSZlcD12MV9pbnRlcm5hbF9naWZfYnlfaWQmY3Q9Zw/l3xxTjIXYy3gchiH3L/giphy.gif'
    )
    if sentry_sdk.is_initialized():
        st.error(
            f'Oops, something funny happened with a {type(e).__name__}. We are looking into it.',
            icon='🙈',
        )
    else:
        # Sentry is not enabled - write full error to the application for visibility
        st.write(e)
    # Raise the error so that it shows up in the console and sentry can capture it
    raise e

error_util = sys.modules['streamlit.error_util']
error_util.handle_uncaught_app_exception.__code__ = exception_handler.__code__

# ... continue with streamlit application code ...
```

Hey all! Sorry for dropping this for quite a while. We looked into it two times in the past but always ran into some complications because Streamlit Community Cloud depends on this config option, so it's not trivial to change. However, we found a good solution now. 

We plan to switch over to the following literal values for `showErrorDetails`:

- `“full”` - show everything
- `“stacktrace”` - show type and stacktrace, hide message (= replace it with the generic error message we have today)
- `“type”` - show type, hide message and stacktrace
- `“none”` - hide type, stacktrace, and message

We will also slowly deprecate the `true` and `false` values since they are confusing. But this will be a very soft deprecation – we'll probably just mark them as deprecated in the docs for now so devs stop using them. And it will be a very long time before we remove them, so we don't break any existing production apps. 

Let me know if you have any feedback on this! We're currently busy with other projects but plan to work on this in November/December.

title: Slider tooltips with two values overlap
body:
### Summary

When a range slider is used with two large values and the ticks are dragged closer, the values in the tooltips overlap.

@user reported this issue in #3555, which was already closed after fixing a similar issue for only one slider value.

[image]

### Steps to reproduce

Code snippet:

```py
st.slider('Select a range of values', 100_000, 300_000, (200_000, 205_000))
```

**Expected behavior:**

* When the two tooltips come close to each other, they should stop following the tick movement, unless it is to move them apart
* Left slider tick should also respect the boundaries like the right tick (or the single tick)

**Actual behavior:**

* When the slider is used with two values, tooltips with large values overlap and make them illegible
* Left slider tick does not respect boundaries of the slider

## Update

We started implementing optional support for running Streamlit with [Starlette](https://starlette.dev/). This would also make Streamlit compatible with FastAPI (e.g. allows mounting a Streamlit app on a FastAPI endpoint). You can follow the progress here: https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/12772

## Update

Exciting news 🎉 Starting with **Streamlit 1.53**, we've added experimental ASGI support enabling seamless FastAPI integration.

**Mount FastAPI inside Streamlit:**

```python
from fastapi import FastAPI
from starlette.routing import Mount
from streamlit.starlette import App

api = FastAPI()

@api.get("/health")
async def health():
    return {"status": "healthy"}

app = App("dashboard.py", routes=[Mount("/api", app=api)])
# Streamlit at /, FastAPI at /api/*, Swagger at /api/docs
```

**Mount Streamlit inside FastAPI:**

```python
from fastapi import FastAPI
from streamlit.starlette import App

streamlit_app = App("dashboard.py")
api = FastAPI(lifespan=streamlit_app.lifespan())

@api.get("/data")
async def get_data():
    return {"data": [1, 2, 3]}

api.mount("/dashboard", streamlit_app)
# Run with: uvicorn myapp:api
```

**Mount Flask inside Streamlit:**

```python
from flask import Flask
from starlette.routing import Mount
from a2wsgi import WSGIMiddleware  # pip install a2wsgi
from streamlit.starlette import App

flask_app = Flask(__name__)

@flask_app.route("/health")
def health():
    return {"status": "healthy"}

# Wrap Flask (WSGI) for ASGI compatibility
app = App("dashboard.py", routes=[Mount("/flask", app=WSGIMiddleware(flask_app))])
```

We'd love your feedback on this feature! Please try it out and report any issues in our [feedback thread](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/13600).

> **Note:** Requires `pip install streamlit[starlette]`

## Update

Starlette will become the default server in 1.57 which will make it possible to integrate with FastAPI and Flask as described above without having to install the `starlette` dependencies. The `App` object will also be available in the `st` namespace:

```python
import streamlit as st

...

st.App(...)
```

title: streamlit's webserver not working when using BAZEL for installation bug
body:
### Summary

Related to https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/3132 .

An internal check to see if streamlit is running in development mode or not. This checks if some strings are present in the script's file path. This check is not valid for other installation types, e.g. bazel.

The script path in a bazel build is for example:
`/home/<user>/.cache/bazel/_bazel_{user}/b775940771a888524b9eed82a7f43708/execroot/{organization}/bazel-out/k8-fastbuild/bin/apps/daq/streamlit_main.runfiles/pip_deps_pypi__streamlit/streamlit/hello/hello.py`

This could be solved by also checking for "pip_deps_pypi__streamlit" in the development_mode check, or by just having a better check in general.

### Steps to reproduce

Code snippet:

streamlit_main.py
```
import sys
from streamlit import cli as stcli

if __name__ == '__main__':
    sys.argv = ["streamlit", "hello"]
    sys.exit(stcli.main())

```

BUILD.bazel
```python
load("@rules_python//python:defs.bzl", "py_binary")

py_binary(
    name = "streamlit_main",
    srcs = [
        "streamlit_main.py",
    ],
    main = "streamlit_main.py",
    visibility = ["//visibility:public"],
    deps = [
        requirement('streamlit')
    ],
)
```
If applicable, please provide the steps we should take to reproduce the bug:

run "bazel build streamlit_main"

**Expected behavior:**

To not run in development mode;

**Actual behavior:**

Runs in development mode. 

### Is this a regression?

no

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.8.1
- Python version: 3.7
- Using Conda? PipEnv? PyEnv? Pex? BAZEL
- OS version: Ubuntu 20.04
- Browser version:

### Additional information

Workaround: explicitly set developmentMode to false:

```
import sys
from streamlit import cli as stcli

if __name__ == '__main__':
    sys.argv = ["streamlit", "hello", "--global.developmentMode", "0"]
    sys.exit(stcli.main())

```

This code was released August 19, 2021. At that point, the codebase for that version was fixed, as PyPI doesn't let you delete and re-upload (as far as I know).

When you download the source from PyPI, it will have the `sudo` portion; that's why the original issue was opened, because that's not a good practice. It's also why it was removed.

So you have two choices/potential sources of the issue:

1. The Docker image used to have `sudo` and now doesn't. Add sudo to the Docker container
2. A different version than 0.87 of Streamlit was being used in the past; upgrade to the version that used to be used.

In either case, there's nothing we can do on the Streamlit end to fix this, since we can't change the past, and the current version is 1.8.1.

Docker installs things from scratch everytime a build is made and I have seen the download and install, it was clean. This ensures no mixed versions in my pip install. So no, the error is not due to mixed streamlit versions as well.

In semantic versioning, 1.0.0 also means something. People are seeing the same issue there as well. [Please refer to the other comments on the thread]. 0.87 might be called too early a version and luckily I won't lose my job due to hours of downtime today, but someone using 1.0.0 might do.

And its ok to say that you cannot fix older versions directly, no issues. 

People stuck with older versions need to know how to resolve, let's not place it on pip and move ahead when it can be changed by a small change in streamlit's code. {Please refer to my earlier comment about resolution, not sure how to solve it end to end yet.}  A version change in a 50 library requirements.txt might not be as quick and easy as replace 0.87 with 1.8.1. Hope no one sees a pip cyclic dependency resolution crash in production during an emergency downtime :)

Edit : 

So you have two choices/potential sources of the issue:

    The Docker image used to have sudo and now doesn't. Add sudo to the Docker container [NO]
    A different version than 0.87 of Streamlit was being used in the past; upgrade to the version that used to be used. [NO] I hope nobody has to do that kind of SRE :D

Again, if I were to guess, I would guess it's the Dockerfile. 3.8-slim-buster changed 16 days ago with the commit message:

`Update 3.8 to 3.8.13, pip 22.0.4`

https://github.com/docker-library/python/blob/6b9719086775ddce2dde10871da97cbeb87b81ad/3.8/buster/Dockerfile

So if the meaning of "3.8" is now different, then that's the first place I would look.

5 days ago, debian-buster-slim (the base image for 3.8-slim-buster) changed:

https://github.com/debuerreotype/docker-debian-artifacts/blob/a8f25eed890bf577a323b246cbd380093d116c3f/buster/slim/Dockerfile

title: Couldn't spawn debugee: [WinError 87] The parameter is incorrect
body:
### Summary

When running the streamlit example code on windows 10 through the VS Code debugger, using an Anaconda environment with a fresh streamlit installation, the debug process cancels with the message "Couldn't spawn debugee: [WinError 87] The parameter is incorrect [...]". I set up a fresh environment with only streamlit requirements installed and came to the same error.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Set up Anaconda environment
2. Install Streamlit to the new environment
3. Create a streamlittest.py file (code shown in code snippet section)
4. Create a launch.json (content also under code snippet)
5. Launch with VSCode standard debugger, using the newly created launch.json

Code snippet(streamlittes.py):

```
import streamlit as st
import altair as alt
import pandas as pd

from urllib.error import URLError

@st.cache
def get_UN_data():
    AWS_BUCKET_URL = "http://streamlit-demo-data.s3-us-west-2.amazonaws.com"
    df = pd.read_csv(AWS_BUCKET_URL + "/agri.csv.gz")
    return df.set_index("Region")

try:
    df = get_UN_data()
    countries = st.multiselect(
        "Choose countries", list(df.index), ["China", "United States of America"]
    )
    if not countries:
        st.error("Please select at least one country.")
    else:
        data = df.loc[countries]
        data /= 1000000.0
        st.write("### Gross Agricultural Production ($B)", data.sort_index())

        data = data.T.reset_index()
        data = pd.melt(data, id_vars=["index"]).rename(
            columns={"index": "year", "value": "Gross Agricultural Product ($B)"}
        )
        chart = (
            alt.Chart(data)
            .mark_area(opacity=0.3)
            .encode(
                x="year:T",
                y=alt.Y("Gross Agricultural Product ($B):Q", stack=None),
                color="Region:N",
            )
        )
        st.altair_chart(chart, use_container_width=True)
except URLError as e:
    st.error(
        """
        **This demo requires internet access.**

        Connection error: %s
    """
        % e.reason
    )

```
Code snippet(launch.json):
```
{
    "version": "0.2.0",
    "configurations": [
        {
            "name": "streamlit standard run config",
            "type": "python",
            "request": "launch",
            "module": "streamlit",
            "args": [
                "run",
                "${file}"
            ],
            "python": "${env:streamlit_python}",
        }
    ]
}
```

**Expected behavior:**

Execution of the streamlittest.py script in the same way, as if it was started from the VSCode command line through "streamlit run streamlittest.py".

**Actual behavior:**

An error message box appears, showing 
"Couldn't spawn debugee: [WinError 87] The parameter is incorrect
Command line:['', 'c:\\Users\\User1\\.vscode\\extensions\\ms-python.python-2022.4.0\\pythonFiles\\lib\\python\\debugpy', '--connect', '127.0.0.1:63234', '--configure-qt', 'none', '--adapter-access-token', '22f126c35272714a187c252561454deac32f341221c2e5e1bfa8f6b975d237eb', '-m', 'streamlit', 'run', 'c:\\<MYPROJECTFOLDER>\\.vscode\\launch.json']

That is, did this use to work the way you expected in the past?
no, I have never worked with streamlit before

title: Streamlit health check (/healthz) ignoring 302
body:
### Summary

[WebsocketConnection](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/blob/4d78c03a1d1fd8f9e9f96f4029a51214b9da0ef5/frontend/src/lib/WebsocketConnection.tsx#L612) causes a flood of /healthz requests in case an user session is expired. N users open an app at 9am access expires lets say at 10am, so servers get N requests a second. We see the /healthz storms pretty often at back-end logs.

### Steps to reproduce

1. A backend with an Auth (make JWT token to expire quickly)
2. Open the app page
3. leave the page opened till JWT expired
4. observe /heathz being called every second

**Expected behavior:**

title: [AuthError] Dropbox invalid_access_token on streamlit cloud
body:
### Summary

I want to download a pre-trained BERT model zip file (approx. 120 MB) from [my Dropbox](https://www.dropbox.com/sh/39ngkkt3gqeytgi/AAAh4WW7GIf6dytGTrTM2omva?dl=0) in the first part of my streamlit app. However, the downloading process fails when it is deploying on share.streamlit.io. Any help will be appreciated!

### Steps to reproduce

Code snippet:

```
import os
import dropbox
import zipfile

# check if you have model using dropbox API
if not os.path.isfile("./imdb_bert"):
    
    # my dropbox token is in token_dropbox.txt
    with open("token_dropbox.txt") as f:
        dropbox_token = f.read()

    dbx = dropbox.Dropbox(dropbox_token)
    dbx.files_download_zip_to_file(download_path="./imdb_bert.zip", path="/imdb_bert")

    with zipfile.ZipFile('imdb_bert.zip') as zip_ref:
        zip_ref.extractall("./")    

```

step to reproduce

1. git clone [repo](https://github.com/ferygood/nlp_streamlit)
2. create a python3 virtual environment
3. install packages `pip install -r requirements.txt`
4. Execute script `stream run bert_streamlit.py`
5. The app should be launched after downloading/extracting model (If the token expired, new token can be asked via response) 
6. After confirming the app works locally, you can deploy it to share.streamlit.io, then you will face the AuthError. 

**Expected behavior:**
Expected to see AuthError on Dropbox token as you deploying app on share.streamlit.io

**Actual behavior:**

You can see the error and manage app section on share.streamlit.io page [link](https://share.streamlit.io/ferygood/nlp_streamlit/main/bert_streamlit.py)

### Is this a regression?

That is, did this use to work the way you expected in the past?
no

- Streamlit version: 1.8.1
- Python version: 3.9.2
- Using PyEnv (virtualenvwrapper)
- OS version:  Debian GNU/Linux 11 (bullseye) and MacOS (v12. Monterey)
- Browser version: Firefox 91

### Additional information

Since the pre-trained model is a large file containing many variables, I need to find a way to deploy the app.
I have tried different methods, such as deploying it on GCP, AWS(ec2) or downloading from Dropbox. However none of these methods work.

deploy to [Google App Eingine](https://dev.to/whitphx/how-to-deploy-streamlit-apps-to-google-app-engine-407o)

title: 404 error on loading images from files
body:
### Summary

Our dashboard uses `st.image` with a local file to place images on the dashboard in columns. This usually works okay when running locally but not always, and when deployed on our AWS platform the images often fail to load with a 404 error.

I'm creating this issue to better understand how Streamlit handles images and under what conditions a browser might get 404. It feels like a race-condition.

### Steps to reproduce

This problem is intermittent, so hard to give code to reliably reproduce it here, although it does occur when running local (with a single process, on first load) as well as when hosted on AWS.

Code snippet representative of what we're doing:

```
import streamlit as st
from pathlib import Path

IMG = Path.cwd() / "img"

col1, col2 = st.columns([1, 4])
with col1:
    st.image(str(IMG / "example.png"), use_column_width=True)
```

Put an image in `img/example.png` in your project root.

**Expected behavior:**

The image should load every time.

**Actual behavior:**

The image sometimes fails to load with a 404 error, something like this:

```
Failed to load resource: the server responded with a status of 404 ()
https://<host>/media/39508d363b26adb7e031dd613bc507e63a6fbd13e02725ce8b982d74.png
```

The logging says:
```
2022-06-13 16:53:19.294Z ERROR (streamlit.server.routes)
  InMemoryFileManager: Missing file 39508d363b26adb7e031dd613bc507e63a6fbd13e02725ce8b982d74.png
  [4743693824:routes.validate_absolute_path#119]
```

### Is this a regression?

No

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.9.0
- Python version: 3.9.12
- Using Conda? PipEnv? PyEnv? Pex? just virtualenv
- OS version: macOS 12.4
- Browser version: Safari 15.5

### Additional information

Timeline recording from Safari attached showing one image fails to load (all three images placed in a loop so code in each case is identical). Each time the dashboard runs, different images may fail.

Safari timeline recording: [dashboard.json.zip](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/files/8841900/dashboard.json.zip)

Our dashboard uses `st.image` with a local file to place images on the dashboard in columns. This usually works okay when running locally but not always, and when deployed on our AWS platform the images often fail to load with a 404 error.

I'm creating this issue to better understand how Streamlit handles images and under what conditions a browser might get 404. It feels like a race-condition.

This problem is intermittent, so hard to give code to reliably reproduce it here, although it does occur when running local (with a single process, on first load) as well as when hosted on AWS.

Code snippet representative of what we're doing:

```
import streamlit as st
from pathlib import Path

IMG = Path.cwd() / "img"

col1, col2 = st.columns([1, 4])
with col1:
    st.image(str(IMG / "example.png"), use_column_width=True)
```

comments.text:
Hey @user,

Does your AWS setup happen to involve having multiple replicas of the Streamlit server?

What's likely going on here is that `st.image` (unlike many other widgets/elements) is naturally stateful -- the file gets served from the server at some URL, and the UUID created for the file is specific to the server that it came from. If requests for that image file then get load balanced to a different server, you end up with a 404.

The standard fix for this would be at the deployment level: enabling some sort of sticky routing so that after the browser hits a server for the first time, all subsequent requests land on the same replica.

Thanks, that's certainly a possibility as our AWS platform is built for stateless microservices; I will investigate. It seems likely that will be a common scenario for AWS-hosted dashboards, it would surely be better for the image widget to be stateless? I mean, couldn't the server generate the image when it's requested, rather than when the widget is created?

However, I've recently noticed the same thing when running one instance locally, where none of the images load when the dashboard is first rendered. Reloading the page fixes the images. It doesn't happen every time, so I still suspect there's a race going on.

Our dashboard service does have multiple instances, but usually only two (it auto-scales up and down with load). Even so, every time I load the page with images, I usually get one or two images as 404 errors. I would have thought that eventually all the instances would have a cached image so the 404s would stop. Or are the images not cached on the server?

Hey @user !
Thank you for reporting!

Another solution could be instead of keeping images inside app, just keep them in S3, and then you can use S3 static URL for `st.image` first argument instead of a file. 

In that case, images will be served directly from S3, and should work fine!

I will try getting our images hosted in S3 or some kind of internal CDN.

However, please note that I get 404 even when running locally.

```

2022-06-13 16:53:19.294Z ERROR (streamlit.server.routes) InMemoryFileManager: Missing file 39508d363b26adb7e031dd613bc507e63a6fbd13e02725ce8b982d74.png [4743693824:routes.validate_absolute_path#119]
2022-06-13 16:53:19.296Z ERROR (streamlit.server.routes) InMemoryFileManager: Missing file 2dc6ae0bb88cc6e434d5bc9a786608a9e3fd525246d3901d3d343f0c.png [4743693824:routes.validate_absolute_path#119]
```

Updated initial comment to include this local scenario.

Thank you very much  @user for finding and reporting this problem.

I am unable to reproduce it in my local environment right now, but based on the output of your log this problem is definitely exists. 
We will try to reproduce and solve it in future releases.

A simple solution here might be to add a configuration option to specify a local folder for static files, which Streamlit adds to its web server configuration. Then any client can fetch a static file from the server, and we can use http URLs with the `streamlit.image()` function to avoid those pesky 404s.

What do you think @user ?

Hi @user I know it's a little late to this party, but I wanted to let you know that @user just merged in support for the static serving idea that you proposed here last summer. So it should be available in the next release and support the same scenario you proposed.

https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/5691

Guessing you may have solved the issue another way by now, but if you give it a try and have feedback let us know! Thank you!

title: Allow sharing of Streamlit apps through JupyterHub
body:
**Problem.**
Working in a Jupyter Hub environment the best way to share applications/dashboards across an organization is to render them with voila and share the link to whoever needs it. Moreover, in such structure its always possible to run your streamlit solution in a port of your k8s instance, but that port if of course not accessible to other users.

**Solution.**
Using https://cdsdashboards.readthedocs.io/en/stable/ ContainDS to do that is in theory possible. 
It looks to me that containDS is a separate project to streamlit.

**Additional context.**
This thread shows how some organizations already use such approach for panel, one of the big four:
https://twitter.com/JamesABednar/status/1535371689323896842?s=20&t=sbk7MWdigcZbzl1ywmU78w

**Request/Question.**
Is there any specific documentation regarding rendering streamlit with voila in a Jupyter Hub environement?

**Comment:**
Being streamlit one of the most powerful dashboards frameworks it is so far out of scope for us since the first requirement is "sharability" via urls, within the jupyterhub  since it has to be transparent to several thousands of people who do not even know what python is (I.e. forgot about asking them to open the terminal to do this or that to fire a streamlit app)

### Voting for feature requests
Community voting on feature requests enables the Streamlit team to understand which features are most important to our users.

title: using a datetime slider, the session_state.value is not being held after submitting the form
body:
### Summary

When using a datetime slider to select a time-window inside a form, the widget value resets before being passed to the sessionstate after pressing submit. This is somehow linked to the fact that I am using datetime.now() to reset the initial input value of the slider upon form reset. 

### Steps to reproduce

Code snippet:

I've provided 5 forms where I try to pass on date, time or datetime selection.
You can see that by pressing "submit" the value is sometimes incorrectly being passed to the session state. 
Only when I use a datetime slider that is completely independent from datetime.now() calls, it works (the 3th form)

```python
import streamlit as st
from datetime import datetime, timedelta, time, date

with st.form("timeselect", clear_on_submit=True):
    start_time = st.slider(
        "timeselect",
        min_value= datetime.now() - timedelta(days=2),
        max_value= datetime.now() + timedelta(days=2),
        value=(datetime.now() - timedelta(days=1), datetime.now()),
        step= timedelta(hours=1),
        format="MM/DD/YY - hh:mm",
        key='selectedtime')
    submitted = st.form_submit_button("Submit")

    data = {
    'datetime' : str(st.session_state.selectedtime),
    }

    st.write(data)

with st.form("timeselect_fixed limits", clear_on_submit=True):
    start_time = st.slider(
        "timeselect_fixed limits",
        min_value= datetime(2022,1,20),
        max_value=  datetime(2024,1,20),
... [43 lines trimmed] ...
        key='timeselect'
        )
    submitted = st.form_submit_button("Submit")

    data = {
        'date' : str(st.session_state.dateselect),
        'time' : str(st.session_state.timeselect),
        }

    st.write(data)

with st.form("my_form2", clear_on_submit=True):
    coltop1, coltop2 = st.columns([1, 3])

    dateselect = coltop1.date_input(
        "Select date",
        value=datetime.now(),
        key='dateselect'
        )

    timeselect = coltop2.slider(
        "Select time (±5min):",
        value=datetime.now(),
        step=timedelta(days=1),
        format="MM/DD/YY",
        key='dateslider'
        )
    submitted = st.form_submit_button("Submit")

    data = {
        'date' : str(st.session_state.dateselect),

        }
```

Once the submit button is pressed, the datetime value is being passed to the sessionstate.

comments.text: Hey @user , thanks for submitting this issue. It looks like the 3rd and 4th forms are working properly but it seems like the 1st, 2nd, and 5th ones are properly working. Can you confirm if this is true?

Hey, 
That is correct: The 3rd & 4th forms are working as intended. 
The 1st, 2nd & 5th are not.

Hi @user , it was hard to debug this but I was able to do it with the help of my coworker. Sorry for the late reply. 

It looks like the bug is being caused by `datetime.now()` because datetime.now() is constantly changing. Just some context: Streamlit works by completely rerunning the script and keeping track of widget ids and those widget ids are a hash of the specific parameters. With that context given, because datetime.now() is always changing, that causes those widgets ids to change and as a result, the session state is not being kept. 

What would probably work is changing the time to the day, hour, or minute of `datetime.now()`  depending on your usecase. Based on the architecture of this system, I'm not sure we can exactly solve the datetime.now() issue anytime soon given the architecture of streamlit but I plan to make a PR that suggests to users to not use `datetime.now()` and maybe use the day or hour because of this issue. 

Sorry if this inconveniences you but thanks for submitting this issue. Happy streamlitting!

Hello @user ,
so I would have to convert the `datetime.now()` into sessionstate parameters that will be cached in order to bypass this issue. 
Thank you for figuring out this bug!
I think what you would have to do is not have the datetime.now() to be always changing. I'm not sure if caching that would solve your issue. If you try it out and it works, let me know!

title: UI does not display when serving at port 3000.
body:
### Summary

Streamlit UI does not display when serving at port 3000

- When running with `--server.port 3000`
- When running inside docker with `-p 3000:8501`
- When running with reverse-proxy to port 3000 (ex: in k8s)

### Steps to reproduce

```python
# app.py
import streamlit as st
st.text("Hello world")
```

Docker file
```
FROM python:3.9
WORKDIR /task
RUN pip install --no-cache-dir streamlit
COPY ./app.py /task/
ENTRYPOINT ["streamlit", "run", "app.py"]
```

Run locally
```bash
streamlit run app.py --server.port 3000
```

Run with Docker
```
docker build -t hello .
docker run --rm -p 3000:8501 hello
```

In K8S
```bash
kubectl port-forward my-hello-pod 3000:8501
```

Everything works fine when changing 3000 to any other port

Hi @user! 😃 

Thanks for sharing your question! Unfortunately we can't always dig deep and troubleshoot challenges like this on GitHub. We typically use GitHub for feature requests and bug reports.

For troubleshooting help, you can visit our awesome [community forums](https://discuss.streamlit.io/), where thousands of other Streamlit hackers help each other and talk about the amazing things they are creating!

Hi @user,
I created the ticket as un **Bug Report**, not an ask for help.
When searching the keyword `3000` in the Issues, I found multiple tickets that may be related to this bug.
But I understand the decision. Thank you for your answer and for the great product.

I also ran into this problem today, and I tracked down its cause and I think it's indeed a bug. When you set the server port to 3000, if you check the browser console you will find that it's still trying to access port 8501 for websocket connection which causes errors. The reason it's doing that is that port 8501 is hard-coded as the "development port" [(link)](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/blob/fb60c2756593f830cd3bb1aeab61b7c40a9354c1/frontend/src/lib/baseconsts.ts#L28), and the condition for streamlit to tell that it's in development mode is, interestingly, to check whether the server port is 3000 [(link)](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/blob/fb60c2756593f830cd3bb1aeab61b7c40a9354c1/frontend/src/lib/baseconsts.ts#L33) which I find unreasonable. I think development mode shouldn't be set based on which port the server runs on but through some configuration / environment variable. Can we re-open this issue and fix this?

title: Server headless detection doesn't play nicely with ssh port forwarding
body:
### Summary

The documentation says that `server.headless` mode is detected on linux when DISPLAY is but when I ssh in from windows either via git-bash ssh or via VS Code, the $DISPLAY variable echos empty but server.headless appears to be on (Localhost url is not displayed, and no attempt to open a browser.)

Related: headless behavior doesn't work well when developing with VS Code SSH remote. VS code will ssh Port forward and open a browser correctly if run with `--server.headless false`

### Steps to reproduce

Run any streamlit app via ssh. 

```
echo $DISPLAY
streamlit hello
```

Displayed url shows internal/external IP addresses. This implies `server.headless` has been set as true

```
streamlit hello --server.headless false
```

**Expected behavior:**

With DISPLAY not set, I expect server.headless to be false.

**Actual behavior:**

streamlit runs as if server.headless is true.

### Is this a regression?
no
### Debug info

- Streamlit version: version 1.11.0
- Python version: 3.9.12
- conda
- OS version: RHEL 7

### Additional information

headless detection ostensibly exists to help with remote development but the most common way to remote develop (ssh and VS Code remote) doesn't get any benefits from it.

title: Support configuring custom light & dark themes
body:
### Problem

I would like a way to declare custom light AND custom dark theme in the same app. I have been unable to find a solution for this. So here is a solution I came up with.

### Solution

Along with the already existing `[theme]` option, please create a `[theme.light]` and `[theme.dark]` option for the `config.toml` file. 

These be used the reduced form of:

```toml
[theme]
base="light"
```

and 

```toml
[theme]
base="dark"
```

respectively and will allows the user to create **BOTH CUSTOM DARK AND LIGHT MODE**.

---

Community voting on feature requests enables the Streamlit team to understand which features are most important to our users.

comments.text:
I want to be able to declare both custom dark and light mode and I think a simple way of allowing users to do that is:

```toml
[theme.light]
primaryColor="#B5838D"
backgroundColor="#B4E3E7"
secondaryBackgroundColor="#BFD7FF"
textColor="#0C2427"

[theme.dark]
primaryColor="#B5838D"
backgroundColor="#22272E"
secondaryBackgroundColor="#ADBAC7"
textColor="#768390"
```
Hi, is possible to change the theme from light to dark using a button?
To make myself clear, I am asking for a method to override the default "light" and "dark" modes.
Cool idea! We are not prioritizing any changes to theming at the moment but let's see if more people upvote this!

It would be very useful to be able to have a separate setting for defining the background color of the sidebar, and have this be separate from the background color used for most widgets.

While it's possible to do CSS styling via the `st.markdown` command, the problem is that the app will first show the default sidebar color, as defined in your config.toml file, and it will then load the extra CSS styling that you’ve defined in your code after the fact.
There’s a delay between those two things, and this (at best) creates a “flashing effect” or (at worst) displays the default colors for a second or two before it switches over to the new CSS styling.

What would be very helpful, and could be implemented very quickly, is to give us the capability of defining the background color for the sidebar as a separate config.toml variable.
At the moment we have to use secondaryBackgroundColor, and this applies a color onto BOTH the sidebar as well as for most interactive widgets.

I like using a dark background color for my sidebar, but you can’t have this same color for most interactive widgets.
Therefore being able to separate these two would be very useful.

I'm not sure quite when it was added but I see this is now [on the Roadmap for Aug-Oct 2025](https://roadmap.streamlit.app/#77595b58) 👀

Exciting!

# Update

Hey all, we just started working on this, will probably go into the next release (1.51) on October 21.

**UPDATE**
Feature has been merged and included in `1.51` release, which should be out later today 🎉

title: Add more options to `[ui]` in `.streamlit/config.toml`
body:
### Problem

Many, many users are already using CSS markdown trick to hide Hamburger Menu and Footer. The problems with this are (1) that it is an unofficial "trick", **and (2) that the Hamburger Menu and Footer can still be seen for a brief moment during initial app loading.**

### Solution

**Preferred solution:** Add a `hideMainMenu` and `hideFooter` parameter to the `[ui]` section of `.streamlit/config.toml`.

### Additional context

The `[ui]` section of `.streamlit/config.toml` already has the following options:

- `hideTopBar`
- `hideSidebarNav`

---

Community voting on feature requests enables the Streamlit team to understand which features are most important to our users.

comments.text: Maybe a parameter to freeze the sidebar size would be useful too (either `disableResizableSidebar` or `freezeSidebarSize`)
Thanks! Hiding the hamburger menu is already covered in #395. What's you use case for disabling the sidebar resizability?

Hey there @user, thanks for asking!

The sidebar "resizability" feature gives end-users a degree of control over the look of the app that it is not giving to the app's developer. Developers should at minimum get the same degree of control as end-users.

- **Before (without sidebar resizability):** Developer can decide when to add a sidebar, and when to switch between "expanded" or "collapsed" state. End-users get the "expand / collapse sidebar" button at the top-left of the app if there is a sidebar. I.e. developer always has more control than end user.

- **After (with sidebar resizability):** The sidebar size can now be controlled by end-users, but there is no accompanying increase in the "degree of control" given to developer.
 
Ideally developers would be able to fully control sidebar size; a bare minimum would be a boolean parameter to enable/disable resizability - hence my previous comment. Maybe adding parameters to `st.set_page_config()` would be the way to go, as it already has the `initial_sidebar_state` parameter.

Hope this makes sense, but let me know :)

As I said in my comment on https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/395 (_as far as I know there isn't anything covered yet for the hamburger menu for the past 3 years_):

I'd like to add to this ticket that people might assume since this workaround is suggested in the Streamlit knowledgebase(https://docs.streamlit.io/knowledge-base/using-streamlit/how-hide-hamburger-menu-app), that the hamburger menu is actually properly removed while it's not.

People might assume that it's safe to deploy Streamlit apps with this workaround but the hamburger menu can easily be turned visible again in the browser which visitors can use to mess with the app.

I really hope we can get a proper hide/show configuration item for it in either the .toml or set_page_config() function that removes the HTML as well 😄

Closing since removing the hamburger/app menu is now possible via the `toolbarMode` config option (see [here](https://docs.streamlit.io/library/advanced-features/app-menu#customize-the-menu)) and the "Made with Streamlit" footer just got removed completely. Feel free to open a separate issue for the sidebar resizability if that's still needed.

title: Accessing websocket headers in Streamlit 1.12.0
body:
### Problem

In previous versions, we used the following code to retrieve the access token header from the websocket headers:

```python
from streamlit.server.server import Server
from streamlit.scriptrunner.script_run_context import get_script_run_ctx

def get_access_token() -> Optional[str]:
    """Gets the access token from the websocket headers, if possible."""
    # Get headers
    session_id = get_script_run_ctx().session_id  # type: ignore
    server = Server.get_current()
    session_info = server._get_session_info(session_id)
    if session_info.ws is None:  # type: ignore
        # At first page load, this is None (at least until #4099 is fixed)
        st.markdown("Unable to get session websocket. Please refresh the page.")
        st.stop()
    headers = session_info.ws.request.headers  # type: ignore

    # Get access token
    access_token_key = "X-Access-Token"
    if access_token_key in headers.keys():
        access_token = headers[access_token_key]
    else:  # development environment
        access_token = None

    return access_token
```

We noticed the import paths changed for scriptrunner and server, however `Server.get_current()` apparently no longer exists. Is there still a way for us to get the websocket headers? 

This is very important for us, as we use the access token for group-based access control and there isn't another way for us to easily get the same information that we've been able to find. 

Currently we've just pinned the version to 1.11.1 but that's not great long-term as we do like to take advantage of new features as they come out.

### Solution

**MVP:** Whatever is easiest for us to be able to get the access token from the websocket headers.

**Possible additions:** Potentially some documentation support for the server side of the app would be great.

But! I totally get this ask; "access websocket headers" is something that was implicitly possible in Streamlit < 1.12, and no longer is. The best long-term solution to something like this is "provide a public - and therefore supported - streamlit API to do the thing". Ultimately that's a product decision, but I don't want to pass the buck entirely - I'll bring this up with the product team, pitch the use case to them, and see what our options are. You don't have to be stuck on version 1.11.1, as it's indeed possible to access websocket headers in **current** version 1.12.2.
Since Streamlit is opensouce, we can always find a way... It's just not officially supported in the API, so it may change in future releases, and you'll have to be creative and change the method every time it does.

How it can be done in current version 1.12.2:

    import gc
    from streamlit.runtime.scriptrunner.script_run_context import get_script_run_ctx
    from streamlit.runtime.runtime import Runtime

    # ...

    def st_runtime():

        global _st_runtime

        if _st_runtime:
            return _st_runtime

        for obj in gc.get_objects():
            if type(obj) is Runtime:
                _st_runtime = obj
                return _st_runtime

    _st_runtime = None

    # ...

    def session_id():

        script_run_ctx = get_script_run_ctx()
        return script_run_ctx.session_id if script_run_ctx else ''

    # ...

    runtime = st_runtime()

    if runtime:
        session_info = runtime._get_session_info(session_id())

        if session_info:
            request = getattr(session_info.client, 'request')
            host_name = request.host_name
            remote_ip = request.remote_ip

>

> 
> def session_id():
> 
>     script_run_ctx = get_script_run_ctx()
>     return script_run_ctx.session_id if script_run_ctx else ''
> 
> # ...
> 
> runtime = st_runtime()
> 
> if runtime:
>     session_info = runtime._get_session_info(session_id())
> 
>     if session_info:
>         request = getattr(session_info.client, 'request')
>         host_name = request.host_name
>         remote_ip = request.remote_ip
>         headers = request.headers
>         # ...
> ```

session_info = runtime._get_session_info(session_id()) is not working in the last version 1.26.0
You should replace it with the following 
session_info = runtime.get_client(session_id=session_id())

title: Emoji filenames breaks packaging with bazel
body:
### Summary

When we upgrade from 1.9.2 to 1.10.0, our build system, which is based on bazel, can no longer package streamlit into containers. Bazel, or rather the rules_docker/rules_python plugins, do not handle the emoji filenames gracefully and get confused.

### Steps to reproduce

Follow the instructions in rules_python and rules_docker to create a container build with a python binary. Add streamlit as a requirement. Build the image.

Yes, I could spend time to create a detailed bug report, but the cause and solution are pretty clear. Perhaps you could just avoid emojis in filenames in the distribution? It seems like asking for trouble for your users.

**Expected behavior:**

Successful build with bazel.

**Actual behavior:**

Build fails.

### Is this a regression?

yes

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.10.0
- Python version: 3.8.13

**Expected behavior:**

This crash should not happen since there is not documented constraints of where the python file can be placed.

**Actual behavior:**

### Is this a regression?

I am not sure. Have not bisected across versions.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.12.2
- Python version: 3.10.5
- OS: gLinux

### Technical details of crash

The reason this crash happens is because streamlit tries to **recursively** add inotify watchers on everything inside the parent directory of the python file. In this case, the parent directory is root itself. As a result, streamlit attempts to add inotify watchers in `/proc` filesystem. This fails because `watchdog/observers` package uses a directory file descriptor to read the contents of each directory. At some point, it comes across `/proc/<selfpid>/task/<selftid>/fd` directory. `getdents64(2)` results on this directory naturally includes the directory file descriptor which was used for `getdents64(2)`. Then the directory FD is closed. But `watchdog` package remembers the entry and tries to add inotify watcher on that entry. But that entry no longer exists because the directory FD has been closed. sections.technical details of crash:
The reason this crash happens is because streamlit tries to **recursively** add inotify watchers on everything inside the parent directory of the python file. In this case, the parent directory is root itself. As a result, streamlit attempts to add inotify watchers in `/proc` filesystem. This fails because `watchdog/observers` package uses a directory file descriptor to read the contents of each directory. At some point, it comes across `/proc/<selfpid>/task/<selftid>/fd` directory. `getdents64(2)` results on this directory naturally includes the directory file descriptor which was used for `getdents64(2)`. Then the directory FD is closed. But `watchdog` package remembers the entry and tries to add inotify watcher on that entry. But that entry no longer exists because the directory FD has been closed. comments.text: Hi @user , thanks for reporting this. I tried reproducing it on my mac system but I couldn't quite reproduce it. Is there a reason why you're putting in the root folder? That seems a little odd.

@user, this reproduces on Linux. If you don't have access to a Linux machine, you should be able to repro using Docker.

```
$ docker run --rm -it ubuntu bash
root@e5155b1e3e15:/# apt update
root@e5155b1e3e15:/# apt install -y python3-pip
root@e5155b1e3e15:/# pip install streamlit
root@e5155b1e3e15:/# touch /foo.py
root@e5155b1e3e15:/# streamlit run /foo.py
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/usr/local/bin/streamlit", line 8, in <module>
    sys.exit(main())
...
line 406, in _raise_error
    raise OSError(err, os.strerror(err))
FileNotFoundError: [Errno 2] No such file or directory
```

> Is there a reason why you're putting in the root folder? That seems a little odd.

I work on [gVisor](https://github.com/google/gvisor). We have multiple customers who are running streamlit under this setting. We were investigating this failure and noted that this is not a gVisor bug, because it happens on Linux too. And that [`proc(5)`](https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man5/procfs.5.html) filesystem is not compatible to be recursively watched using notify the way `watchdog` package does it.

So on streamlit side, we should probably avoid recursively watching into `/proc` directory (or any other procfs mounts).

Hello, @user, and thanks for the detailed response!

I think this is the same bug, we discussed here https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/4842

Yes, we not support running streamlit from the OS root directory since 1.10 .

We recommend specifying WORKDIR in Dockerfile https://docs.streamlit.io/knowledge-base/tutorials/deploy/docker

CC: @user it would be great to add a paragraph in documentation, that says that we don't support running streamlit from the root of OS

Hm, so I think that even with a workaround, we'll want to fix this rather than add an item to our docs about it (although the docs item is necessary until a fix is merged).

I do think doing so is relative low priority given that we do have an easy workaround for it, though.

Can the doc update be made in the interim, so people don't try to run streamlit in this way?

As for the fix, I guess it has to do with avoiding `procfs` mounts while adding watchers recursively.

> CC: @user it would be great to add a paragraph in documentation, that says that we don't support running streamlit from the root of OS
> Yes, we do not support running streamlit from the OS root directory since 1.10 .

Does this issue affect Linux, macOS, _and_ Windows, or just Linux distros?

In docs [PR #482](https://github.com/streamlit/docs/pull/482), I propose to add the following paragraph to [Main concepts](https://deploy-preview-482--streamlit-docs.netlify.app/library/get-started/main-concepts):

> As of Streamlit version 1.10.0 and higher, Streamlit apps cannot be run from the root directory of Unix-like operating systems, including Linux and macOS. If you try to run a Streamlit app from the root directory, Streamlit will throw a `FileNotFoundError: [Errno 2] No such file or directory error.` For more information, see GitHub issue [#5239](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/5239).

> If you are using Streamlit version 1.10.0 or higher, your main script should live in a directory other than the root directory. When using Docker, you can use the `WORKDIR` command to specify the directory where your main script lives. For an example of how to do this, read [Create a Dockerfile](https://deploy-preview-482--streamlit-docs.netlify.app/knowledge-base/tutorials/deploy/docker#create-a-dockerfile).

> [image]

I've also added a callout to our Docker and Kubernetes guides:
[image]

Please let me know if these changes are accurate and sufficient or if it needs improving. cc @user @user

> As of Streamlit version 1.10.0 and higher, Streamlit apps cannot be run from the root directory of Unix-like operating systems, including Linux and macOS.

@user I think @user confirmed above (in the second comment) that he can't reproduce this on his MacOS system. I am only aware of this issue occurring on Linux.
Hey @user , I only had read access on Mac and that's why it's only reproducible on Linux.

@user @user Thanks for confirming. I was able to get a macOS VM running on my personal Linux box. Found out that since the release of Catalina, the root volume on macOS hasn't been writeable. As such, it doesn't make sense to include it in this note, as users will not be able to write `.py` files to root to begin with.

On [#487](https://github.com/streamlit/docs/pull/487), I've removed mentions of macOS from the note and say that running Streamlit apps from root isn't possible in Linux distributions.

This sounds like a watchdog problem, not a streamlit problem.

I wouldn't expect anyone deploying via Docker (e.g. a read-only production-like situation) to be using watchdog.
Closing this as it should have been fixed in #9453

title: When binding to unix socket, startup script still shows TCP port
body:
### Summary

As of #1802, one can bind to a unix socket (useful for reverse proxy situations) by running something like

` streamlit run --server.address "unix://mysocket.sock" my_app.py`

However, the script still reports/prints a local url/network url for port 8501 that doesn't exist.

### Steps to reproduce

Run any streamlit app with a unix socket:

```
streamlit hello --server.address "unix://mysocket.sock"     
```

**Expected behavior:**

The URLs or some text confirms the app has launched binding to a unix socket.

**Actual behavior:**

Local/Network urls for port 8501 are displayed (that don't work.)

### Is this a regression?

Not sure.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: streamlit-1.12.2
- Python version: 3.9.13

### Additional information

It's working such that the socket is created and the app appears to bind to it, but the bootstrap script should reflect this state. The check on `server.address` has no affirmative branch for what to show if `server_address_is_unix_socket()` is `True`.

title: Multipage routing with URL param or URL hash
body:
### Problem

When I host Streamlit multipage apps (MPA) through a reverse proxy, the MPA requires the reverse proxy to map the requests to `/*` to `/` so that direct access to the sub-page URLs (`<host>/<pagename>`) can reach the Streamlit server and work as expected.

However, sometimes we don't have enough permission/access to the reverse proxy configuration to make it done.

### Solution

It would be better if, on the Streamlit side, a new option is available to use URL hash or URL params for the MPA routing instead of URL pathname, like [React Router's Routers`](https://reactrouter.com/en/main/routers/hash-router) which can be switched for each situation where either URL path or URL hash should be used.

---

Community voting on feature requests enables the Streamlit team to understand which features are most important to our users.

comments.text: Thanks for suggesting this @user! I think we won't support this in the near future (since it would introduce quite a lot of complexity on our side). But I'll leave this here and let's see if other people have the same problem!

I too strongly prefer this proposal.
If this proposal is not addressed in the foreseeable future, I would like to see an option that would disable the multipage mechanism.
Because although there is a great library called streamlit-router, it no longer works properly after streamlit has multi-page support.
If the multipage mechanism does not allow flexible routing definitions, we would appreciate it if you could make it easier to introduce other routing mechanisms.

I'm the author of [streamlit-router](https://github.com/mapix/streamlit-router).  I have experimented with many large streamlit based applications  beyond prototyping and streamlit-router works well as a query-style router, but it's not suitable for public use because it's too messy and informal.  (@user  Are you willing to describe the streamlit-router issue you encountered on the streamlit-router github issue? )

 I'm currently trying to find an extra hack to make streamlit perform like a traditional Path Style Web App, I have some ideas but they haven't been successful yet.

Hi again @user ,

I wanted to understand this a bit more, because Google Cloud Run offers max. 1000 concurrent requests per instance so the issue will show up if/when we reach that limit. Some questions that come to mind:

- **Without the use of custom components, what exactly counts as 1 request in a Streamlit app deployed to Google Cloud Run?** Does 1 refresh of the app = 1 request or is it more complex than that?

- **Do the generated requests just accumulate, or are they cleared when finished?** I did some testing with and, even with a high concurrency limit, it seems the custom components break after a while, maybe indicating requests are accumulating.

- **Are there expressions, anti-patterns, or app designs that might cause these requests to "accumulate" (and not be cleared when finished), and that we should therefore avoid?** For example, for loops, `st.experimental_rerun`, calling functions, spawning threads, updating a widget on each iteration of a for loop, etc.

- **When using custom components, is there a way to calculate how many additional requests will be generated?** Does it depend on the component, on how the existing v1 template works, or on both? 

And any additional performance tips to help alleviate this issue (or performance traps we should avoid) are kindly welcome 😊. Thanks a lot in advance!

Unfortunately, I haven't really investigated Google Cloud Run yet, so I cannot really provide good answers for your questions. But maybe a few relevant information:

- Streamlit serves only a couple of static frontend resources (html, css, js) via HTTP requests. The main communication during app run is via websocket stream. But I don't know how this is counted in Google Cloud Run.
- Custom components have their own static resources which needs to be served through HTTP request. This probably adds up very fast. But this also partly depends on how many static files a custom components uses. 

In case you look more into this, it would be super useful if you share your insights here :)

On another hand, I stumbled upon a few online discussions about solving this issue (custom components not rendering) by adjusting HTTP request  parameter `X-Frame-Options` to `SAMEORIGIN`.

Thank You!

@user @user looking forward to hearing your thoughts on the points below :) Thanks a lot in advance.

Finally found some time to test some more, and the issue still happens sometimes (even with session affinity on/off and increasing the concurrent requests limit in Cloud Run), **and always after using the app for a bit, never upon first load. Do you know why it could be working properly first and only later failing?**

On another hand, I reviewed the logs and noticed something that I want to mention, in case it is a symptom or even the cause of this whole issue:

- The requestUrl for my st_aggrid component's index.html file has the following format:

  `https://example.com/component/st_aggrid.agGrid/index.html?streamlitUrl=https%3A%2F%2Fexample.com%2F`

- The requestUrl for everything else has the following format:

  `https://example.com/static/js/main.951e143b.chunk.js`
  `https://example.com/component/st_aggrid.agGrid/static/css/main.8d4f52e2.css`

Now, because this whole issue seems to be related to requests to render custom components, I am starting to review the **ComponentRequestHandler** class in the Streamlit library ([/streamlit/web/server/component_request_handler.py](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/blob/develop/lib/streamlit/web/server/component_request_handler.py))... but this could definitely use more experienced eyes than mine. After first inspection, some hypotheses that came to mind were:

- In the `get()` method, maybe there is some problem to get the right path, that's why we are ending up at one of the two `self.set_status(404)`.
- In the `set_extra_headers()` method, cache is disabled for .html files but not for .js and .css. Note that there is also a condition that depends on the path length, which comes back to the question of "are we getting the right path".
- In a previous post I mentioned that some users are allegedly solving the issue by adjusting HTTP request parameter `X-Frame-Options` to `SAMEORIGIN`. Maybe this can be done inside this class.
