title: Unable to set enableCORS to false
body:
### Summary

enableCORS won't actually be set to false when adding enableCORS = false to the .toml settings. This happens on all my Streamlit Cloud deployments, but it might also be happening elsewhere.
See below for the output of a debug page I created to diagnose the issue.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Add the relevant config options to App settings -> Secrets in Streamlit Cloud 
```
[server]
enableCORS = false
enableXsrfProtection = false
```

2. Check the output of 
```
st.config.get_option("server.enableCORS")
st.config.get_option("server.enableXsrfProtection")
```

**Expected behavior:**

server.enableCORS should return False when enableCORS = false is added to the .toml settings.

**Actual behavior:**

server.enableCORS always returns True, completely ignoring the config settings.

[image]

### Is this a regression?

That is, did this use to work the way you expected in the past?

Not sure.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.13.0
- Python version: 3.10
- Using Conda? PipEnv? PyEnv? Pex? not relevant
- OS version: not relevant
- Browser version: not relevant

### Additional information

This is probably the same bug that keeps being reported in [this closed issue](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/837). I've also opened a thread on the forum since I'm not sure whether this happening only on Streamlit Cloud or elsewhere too.

title: Set config of pages in streamlit/config.yaml
body:
### Problem

I absolutely adore the new pages' functionality, but having all the config information in the filename is a bit messy. It's also now quite hard to start a Streamlit server with an emoji, since most non-mobile keyboards don't have emoji's on them. Finally, and this is just personal, I really don't like filenames that look like this `1_🔗_Preprocessing.py`. 🙃 

### Solution

I think it would be awesome if we could manually set the config of all pages in `streamlit/config.toml` or in `streamlit.pages.toml`. This would also allow for some more configs, like page names that are different from the file name, etc.

The great thing about this feature would be that its completely for Streamlit users. You don't have to add it to the TOML file because if you don't add it, the current rules apply.

Finally, it would allow for extra functionality in the future, like adding a disabled option, so you can remove a page without removing it from the /pages directory.

### Additional context

I think `streamlit/config.toml` could look something like this:

```
[server]
runOnSave = true

[theme]
base = "light"

[pages]
    ["main.py"]
        name = "My main page"
        emoji = 🌤️
        order = 1
    ["subpage1.py"]
        name = "A page"
        emoji = 🌤️
        order = 2
    ["subpage2.py"]
        name = "This is a currently disabled page"
        emoji = 🌤️
        order = 3
        disabled = true
```

---

title: Allow specifying custom website metadata
body:
### Problem

Streamlit apps are becoming more and more fully fledged web applications. However, the basic website metadata functionalities are still suboptimal, this causes the app to look kind of weird when shared online.

### Solution

I would appreciate it if we could specify more [web app manifest](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Manifest) parameters via `streamlit.config.yaml`, so the webpage looks better in search engine results and when shared:

- name
- short_name
- description
- author
- language
- display (default should be standalone)
- icons (ideally just a path to an image and Streamlit will convert it to the different required icon formats/sizes)
- theme_color (default should be theme.primaryColor)
- background_color (default should be theme.backgroundColor)

Personally, I really like how the Nuxt.js PWA module does this, for inspiration see https://pwa.nuxtjs.org/meta. 

This could possibly be added to `streamlit/config.yaml` like this:

```
[server]
runOnSave = true

[theme]
base = "light"
primaryColor = "#dc2626"

[metadata]
name = "My super long app name"
short_name = "Short app name"
display = "standalone"
icon = "./icon.png" 
```

---

Community voting on feature requests enables the Streamlit team to understand which features are most important to our users.

comments.text: Ah oops, sorry for closing this. #6567 is related but seems like this issue is also advocating for other parameters for PWA. Going to leave them both open.
this can also be a useful way to add analytics data, such as **Google Analytics** or **Search Console** codes as metadata to make it easier to index Streamlit apps
FYI work-around https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/6567#issuecomment-2143512104

## Update

Exciting news 🎉 Starting with **Streamlit 1.53**, we've added experimental support for custom routes via the new ASGI/Starlette integration.

You can now serve custom metadata files like `manifest.json`:

```python
from streamlit.starlette import App
from starlette.routing import Route
from starlette.responses import JSONResponse

async def manifest(request):
    return JSONResponse({
        "name": "My Analytics App",
        "short_name": "Analytics",
        "description": "Interactive data dashboard",
        "icons": [{"src": "/app/static/icon-192.png", "sizes": "192x192"}],
        "theme_color": "#ff4b4b",
        "background_color": "#ffffff",
    })

app = App("main.py", routes=[Route("/manifest.json", manifest)])
```

You can serve any custom metadata endpoint this way (`/sitemap.xml`, `/favicon.ico`, etc.).

We'd love your feedback on this feature! Please try it out and report any issues in our [feedback thread](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/13600).

> **Note:** Requires `pip install streamlit[starlette]`

title: Streamlit hosting for code hosted in Azure Repos
body:
### Problem

I'm using [Azure Repos](https://azure.microsoft.com/en-gb/products/devops/repos/) to host my Streamlit app code and would like to use Streamlit hosting! This is not possible right now as Streamlit hosting only allows Github repositories.

### Solution

**Preferred solution:** Support Azure Repos in the same way as Github repos are supported today.

### Additional context

Azure Repos may be more well known as "Azure DevOps repositories".

---

Community voting on feature requests enables the Streamlit team to understand which features are most important to our users.

comments.text:
Hey @user, thanks for sharing this request!

Since Streamlit Community Cloud serves as a free community resource for users getting started with Streamlit to deploy one private app + unlimited public apps, it's unlikely that it will be expanded to support platforms other than GitHub.

Fortunately, since Azure repos is just a set of version control tools, you can still deploy Streamlit apps that are stored in Azure repos. Our community deployment wiki lives [here](https://discuss.streamlit.io/t/streamlit-deployment-guide-wiki/5099) and features tutorials on deploying Streamlit apps with a number of platforms. You might also find [this guide helpful](https://towardsdatascience.com/deploying-a-streamlit-web-app-with-azure-app-service-1f09a2159743), which covers the process of deploying a Streamlit with Azure App Service.

title: Misconfigured _xsrf cookies
body:
### Checklist

### Summary

Hi,

I am running a Streamlit app on Azure, requiring authentication with AD, and `st.file_uploader` returns a 403 Forbidden error if `enableXsrfProtection` is on. It works locally, and I suspect that this is caused by the _xsrf cookie not getting though, because I can see the cookie in dev tools locally, but not when deployed.

In particular, the cookie is missing the SameSite and Secure attributes.

### Reproducible Code Example

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Open any Streamlit app
2. Open browser developer tools

### Expected Behavior

Cookies have `SameSite=None; Secure` attribute.

### Current Behavior

_xsrf cookie is not transmitted when deployed on the cloud with SSO and HTTPS-only.

Locally this is what I am getting:
[image]

Plus the deprecation warning:

>Some cookies are misusing the recommended “SameSite“ attribute
>Cookie “_xsrf” does not have a proper “SameSite” attribute value. Soon, cookies without the “SameSite” attribute or with an invalid value will be treated as “Lax”. This means that the cookie will no longer be sent in third-party contexts. If your application depends on this cookie being available in such contexts, please add the “SameSite=None“ attribute to it. To know more about the “SameSite“ attribute, read https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/HTTP/Headers/Set-Cookie/SameSite

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.15.0
- Python version: 3.10, 3.11

title: Bring your own Redis cache
body:
### Problem

Our micro-service hosting platform will auto-scale a service so that multiple instances are created or destroyed to adapt to varying traffic load. A user request might be routed to any one of these instances, as they are assumed to be stateless. However, our Streamlit dashboard service is not stateless due to the way session state and caches are implemented.

At the moment each instance of the service has its own Streamlit cache, which means users will often get a cache hit that’s followed immediately by a miss when their next request gets routed to another instance. We also get problems with session state not being mirrored across instances.

### Solution

Our platform provides Redis resources that are shared between instances so that to users there appears to be a single cache (rather than one per instance). What I want to do is to tell Streamlit to use this shared Redis resource as the cache, also using it to store session state.

### Additional context

We are not using Streamlit Cloud because we have our own PaaS that runs on AWS, so we want our Streamlit services to run there in order to comply with security policies for internal tools like dashboards. 

---

comments.text:
Thanks for filing this, @user! I'll relay this issue to our product team.

We've been thinking about doing something like this for some time now (from a different angle of being able to aggressively spin down Streamlit servers, but whatever solution we decide on will probably also help with running Streamlit more statelessly in general).

I can't give any sort of timeline right now (or even any definite guarantees that we'll be releasing this as a feature), but I can share that we're very likely to start a project to explore making the backing cache for `st.experimental_memo` configurable in the next month or so. Additionally, #5856 starts to lay the foundation for doing something similar with session state (I'm coincidentally implementing an extremely rough/hacky prototype of this for a company hackathon project 🙂).

My gut feeling says it'll take some time before we're confident in being able to give people this level of configurability over Streamlit internals (+ provide support for various community-supported adapters, documentation for advanced users that want to make use of this, etc.), but allowing for this is something that's actively being explored.

Additionally, #5856 starts to lay the foundation for doing something similar with session state (I'm coincidentally implementing an extremely rough/hacky prototype of this for a company hackathon project 🙂).
> 
> My gut feeling says it'll take some time before we're confident in being able to give people this level of configurability over Streamlit internals (+ provide support for various community-supported adapters, documentation for advanced users that want to make use of this, etc.), but allowing for this is something that's actively being explored.

Thank you for the insights 🙂 Are there any updates on this?

Thanks for the nudge on this @user

We've gotten closer to a world where this is possible with https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/6052, which abstracts our cache storage backend so that different implementations of it can be swapped out to replace the current one that persists data in local memory/disk.

This currently puts us in a place where it would be relatively easy to maintain a fork of Streamlit that swaps out session/cache backends without touching any internal code (aside from plugging in custom backend implementations into a [RuntimeConfig](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/blob/4289ea809619804043705318c1aef9795b57f2f1/lib/streamlit/runtime/runtime.py#L80)). This is, of course, an unreasonable amount of effort for most users as well as potentially unstable until we've finalized all of these APIs, but it does show where we are in the process of building support for this.

Before we're able to roll this out in an official way, the last missing piece is a more advanced configuration feature that allows developers to set config options more programmatically than what our static `config.toml` files currently support. We've been discussing this internally and think this will probably take the form of a python file similar to how [Django handles configuration](https://django-configurations.readthedocs.io/en/stable/).

It'll unfortunately likely be awhile before we're able to able to invest a ton of time working on this. @user might have some insight as to what our timelines look like, but as far as I know we won't be working on this for at least a few months 😕

As @user said - we have heard this request from a growing number of organizations and have some similar platform needs internally, so I think we'll definitely support it and planning to make headway on some of the designs in the next couple of months.

BUT I think we're still quite a ways away from launching them in a way that doesn't require forking Streamlit to use e.g. a custom Redis backend, as Vincent mentioned.

If you look at our [public roadmap](https://roadmap.streamlit.app/), I would guess this will launch on a similar timeframe to features around app state since they are very related.

In the meantime, our guidance for today is to use session affinity / sticky sessions in scaling / multi-pod scenarios. We know of a number of enterprise production-grade deployments that use this solution successfully today (while acknowledging that it may not be feasible for every use case).

Thinking more about this, it would be useful to be able to provide a way to persist sessions state across sessions, so that the same user gets the same session state as last time, even if it was last week.

Perhaps this could be done by allowing us to provide a session state key (e.g. a unique user identifier in a header added by an authenticating proxy) so that if the user had a previous session state, that's what gets recovered.
would be really nice to have guidelines on how to scale a streamlit apps on system like kubernetes, like an helm chart template and guidelines about ingress-nginx or common ingress providers.
+1 on this issue, with this we can make the streamlit stateless and can be deployed to any K8s/ECS or even serverless environment, I see this will be a huge step forward for streamlit.
+1 on this issue as my team looks to scale our streamlit app to multiple K8s pods.
+1 becoming a critical issue for maintaining state on Streamlit page during app server swaps when deploying updates.

title: Streamlit Cloud App Redirects and Renaming
body:
### Problem
When someone renames an app on Streamlit Community Cloud, old links break. (Mentioned on the forums but I couldn't find the official feature request here. Sorry if I missed it.)

### Solution

**MVP:** Redirect old links to the current one (or more specifically the last n links for some reasonable count n).

**Possible additions:** Allow users to manage a list of redirects for each app so they can make tweaks to their app url without worry. Especially if the number of redirects is small, this would allow users to prioritize which previous app url(s) are important to keep in the event of typos while editing.

**Preferred solution:** Even better, allow users to control app name redirects at the account level, and even be able to transfer them to other users, so that in the event of something significant like a re-deployment or transfer of ownership, there wouldn't be the risk of losing your app link.

title: Rename config option `server.enableCORS` to `server.enableCORSProtection`

### Problem

The name of the config option `server.enableCORS` is confusing. As mentioned by @user in this forum [post](https://discuss.streamlit.io/t/when-to-use-enablecors-and-enablexsrfprotection-parameters/32075/5), the real behavior of this option makes it so that a better name would be `server.enableCORSProtection`.

Rename config option `server.enableCORS` to `server.enableCORSProtection` (and remember to update API Reference docs).

The [linked site](https://www.chromium.org/for-testers/bug-reporting-guidelines/uncaught-securityerror-failed-to-read-the-localstorage-property-from-window-access-is-denied-for-this-document/) mentions the following: 

> If this setting is checked, third-party scripts cookies are disallowed and **access to localStorage may result in thrown SecurityError exceptions.**

And we believe that the main problem might be that we are accessing the `localStorage` for `sidebarWidth` and `activeTheme` without properly checking the permission / or catching the exception. This might be easy to fix, if this is indeed the only issue with the security update in Chrome. 

Browser error logs: 
[image]

@user 

Thank you, but It seems the problem still exists while the fix (#6100 ) has been [released with 1.18.1](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/compare/1.18.0...1.18.1):
[image]

Without the cookie blocking setting, I can see the embedded app whose Streamlit version is 1.18.1.
[image]

Thanks @user for pointing it out. Based on my observation, this seems like the same issue for the embedding issue in Streamlit Cloud, which they are looking into.

To be clear, it looks like the docs page works under standard chrome by default, but fails with stricter third-party cookie restriction, which is common for incognito and even Safari other stricter browsers.

@user Thank you! I have an investigation report from my side too:
While this bug seems to remain on the sample apps embedded on the doc, v1.18.1 actually resolves this problem at least in my local env where I tested with Streamlit app hosted from `http://localhost:8501/` and another page that embeds the app via iframe hosted from `http://127.0.0.1:8000/` (both pages are served from localhost, but we can reproduce this bug by accessing them via different domains, `localhost` and `127.0.0.1`).

comments.text: `/stream` and `/_stcore/stream` is not documented in any public documentation, so we made no promise that these endpoints would not change. Can you tell me a little more about your load balancer? Why is Tornado web server not performing protocol upgrades in your environment?

I know it’s not documented but streamlit used it since the beginning - it becomes your API over time.

We are using nginx load balancers in front of streamlit apps, these load balancers handle a custom authentication flow.

We can workaround by introducing another configuration item in the nginx configuration for /_stcore/stream but I am not sure this is a long term solution in case it will be changed again.

I mostly opened this ticket for awareness and to make it searchable for others. 

You might ask why nginx is not able to automatically upgrade any websocket request… unfortunately, I haven’t found a solution for it:

https://serverfault.com/questions/1116900/have-nginx-automatically-upgrade-websocket-connections-in-reverse-proxy

> We can workaround by introducing another configuration item in the nginx configuration for /_stcore/stream but I am not sure this is a long term solution in case it will be changed again.

We will prepare documentation that describes how to run Streamlit with Nginx to document this behavior and we are planning to keep these endpoint names stable for the foreseeable future,

I have a setup where changing the endpoint name requires business _days_.

So I made a temporary patch for myself and in case anyone needs it then they can use it: [here](https://github.com/joy13975/streamlit-endpoint-patch).

Closing since this is expected behavior. Sorry for the inconvenience due to changing the endpoint names but as mentioned above, this was never officially documented behavior. We had to change these names to avoid clashes on GCP in some setups. We do not plan to do any more changes to endpoint names for the foreseeable future.

title: Streamlit Cloud should support the --no-root option for poetry install
body:
### Problem

When using Poetry with a project that does not contain a main package, Streamlit Cloud fails to install the dependencies.

An example project structure that fails is below.
```
some-project
├── LICENSE
├── README.md
├── app.py
├── poetry.lock
└── pyproject.toml
```

It is because `poetry install` emits the following error.
```shell
$ poetry install
(...)
Installing dependencies from lock file
(...)
/path/to/some-project/some_project does not contain any element
```

The command `poetry install` expects this project contains a package root like `some-project/some_project/__init__.py` and tries to install the package itself in addition to its dependencies, while it actually doesn't exist.

### Solution

`poetry install` provide an option to deal with this case, `--no-root`.
(See https://python-poetry.org/docs/cli/#install)

I think Streamlit Cloud should run `poetry install` with the `--no-root` option because usually we don't need to deal with the Streamlit app projects as packages to install, but we just want to install the dependencies managed with Poetry.

### Additional context

[This repo](https://github.com/whitphx/streamlit-webrtc-hugging-face-transformer-example) is an actual project with which I encountered this problem.

[This revision](https://github.com/whitphx/streamlit-webrtc-hugging-face-transformer-example/tree/a6b77c2aacd182c7bb8409b725021aca1c6f7b6e) of the repo caused this error, and I fixed it by adding `streamlit_webrtc_hugging_face_transformer_example/__init__.py` as a workaround in [this commit](https://github.com/whitphx/streamlit-webrtc-hugging-face-transformer-example/commit/237026ca4b19dcb6e9b94240cfe1adb0657946fe) so that it works on Streamlit Cloud now.

---
The same error was reported at [this thread in the forum](https://discuss.streamlit.io/t/streamlit-cloud-deploy-is-failing-with-error-does-not-contain-any-element/31541)

---

Community voting on feature requests enables the Streamlit team to understand which features are most important to our users.

title: Favicon Error
body:
### Checklist

### Summary

When using the set_page_config and trying to set the page_icon to an emoji (⚡ ) it doesn't work. I've tried using the :zap: notation as well as simply just using the emoji itself. Both don't work. 

st.set_page_config(
    page_title="Test Dashboard",
    page_icon=":zap:",
    layout="centered"
)

I've also tried using different browsers to make sure that was not the issue also. Furthermore in my inspection, while i was trying to debug this issue, I saw that when you use the colon notation is references a twemoji link. 

`<link rel="shortcut icon" href="https://twemoji.maxcdn.com/2/72x72/26a1.png">
`
When you navigate to this link, you get the following response: `Couldn't find the requested file /2/72x72/26a1.png in twemoji.`

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
st.set_page_config(
    page_title="Test Dashboard",
    page_icon=":zap:",
    layout="centered"
)
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Set the page config and use an emoji for the page_icon field
2. verify the missing icon by launching streamlit run myapp.py
3. you can see the above html error if you use the colon notation

### Expected Behavior

The icon to show up in the tab when you have the streamlit app open on any browser

### Current Behavior

Currently shows the default streamlit favicon with a crown

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.16.0
- Python version: 3.10
- Operating System: Mac OS / AWS Linux
- Browser: Brave, Safari, Chrome
- Virtual environment: Conda

title: File uploader stops serving file after 30 seconds
body:
### Checklist

### Summary

I have a streamlit application deployed in gke, containerized, in one instance, no reloads.  I use it to upload and then process media files. When I upload video/audio, after some time it disappears with 404 error

I believe it may be my deployment problem, as stated here https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/4825. At least I have problems with reproducing it locally.

However, I did some tests and it seems like rather rare behavior of streamlit than my mistake.

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
# I believe this is enough however I haven't reproduced it with this code because deploy environment is harder to reproduce

import streamlit as st

class ChooseVideoWidget:
    def widget(self):
        st.markdown("### Upload video here")
        video_file = st.file_uploader("Upload video here", ".mp4")
        print(video_file)

    with st.spinner('⏳ Please wait...'):

Hi @user ,

This is a real bug actually. What's happening here is streamlit cloud is trying to load some context with cookies but safari blocks third party cookies automatically, which is resulting in that jittery effect. 

Here's the catch though: If the app is public, I would not expect any problems for the embedded app to load. However, if the app is private, i would expect some problems and the jittery effect would appear still when cookies are blocked. 

So I have pushed the bug to the streamlit cloud team to let them know public apps shouldn't have this problem. However, it looks like your app is private so not sure if that would ever be resolved. 

Cloud app:  https://willhuang1997-st-cloud-testing-debug-njmh2w.streamlit.app/ 
Reproducible on google sites: https://sites.google.com/view/kmcgrady-example/home
Actually when talking to the team, it seems like this is a duplicate issue of https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/6087#issuecomment-1428336938
Closing as #6087 was fixed by #6100

Glad to see this closed @user. Is this deployed for users embedding via *.streamlit.app or is there another location I could track to see when that happens? I'm not in a rush but would appreciate a place to keep an eye on. Also: I'm now seeing a new behavior on [my page](https://ibis-project.org/backends/support_matrix/) which involves an infinite loop of calls and errors. Not sure how that relates but the behavior is new as of the last couple of weeks.

Hi @user, whoops -- I may have closed this a bit too early as I wasn't aware of the Community Cloud issues with embedded pages when third party cookies are blocked. I just noticed the last comment mentioning that this is a duplicate of an issue that was closed some time ago and assumed that we just forgot to close this one out as a dupe 🙈 

We generally don't track Community Cloud issues in this repo, but I'll reopen this since I don't think there's a better place to track this at the moment, and I'll re-surface this to the Community Cloud team on Monday.
Thanks so much @user, we really appreciate it.

title: Transfer websocket messages as a sequence of custom defined small chunks
body: We have an issue where the streamlit server is behind a proxy that limits frame lengths to 65k (a limit set here: https://github.com/quarkusio/quarkus-http/blob/0558dd49954a3b305340a68f73d99aa3815a660e/websocket/core/src/main/java/io/undertow/websockets/ServerWebSocketContainer.java#L90). This means that for large datasets the data is unsuccessfully transmitted from the streamlit server to the browser. I've seen #414, but we'd need a way to specify how small chunks the server could split packets down to, not increase to. Do you have any advice for how to tackle this kind of scenario? Thanks!

selected_files = st.file_uploader("Select Fastq file pairs for upload:", help="Each pair must contain R1 + R2 files", type="gz", accept_multiple_files=True)

title: Firefox can’t establish a connection to websocket (started from within a devontainer)
body:
### Checklist

### Summary

I'm using a [devcontainer](https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/devcontainers/containers) on a remote docker-server started with VSCode.

When I start the streamlit script below, VSCode forwards the port 5000 automatically from the devcontainer to my host and I can see the streamlit page with `http://localhost:5000/` on my host-machine.

Unfortunatly on loading the page stays at the **Please wait...** message for about a minute and eventually shows a "connection time out" message. Sometimes it also manages to renders the final page. In the developer-tools from Firefox I get a loop of the two messages:

* Firefox can’t establish a connection to the server at ws://localhost:5000/stream
* The connection to ws://localhost:5000/stream was interrupted while the page was loading.

I also tried setting `--server.enableWebsocketCompression=false` with no success.

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
import streamlit as st

st.title('Hello World')
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1) Start Devcontainer from VSCode
2) Run `streamlit run streamlit_file.py --server.port=5000` inside the container
3) Open http://localhost:5000/ on host-machine.

### Expected Behavior

### Current Behavior

The connection to ws://localhost:5000/stream was interrupted while the page was loading.

Hi @user,

thanks for looking into this. My `devcontainer.json`is as simple as:

```json
{
    "name": "MyProject - DevContainer",
    "dockerFile": "../Dockerfile",

```

Hey @user,

I'm not certain that this is the case, but it's possible that you're running into our (previously) very strict websocket connection timeouts due to the latency added by the Streamlit server running on a remote docker container (my hunch is from the ~1s time each request to `/stream` takes before a retry occurs along with the fact that things occasionally do work). 

We recently relaxed these timeouts by a ton in Streamlit 1.20, so I would try seeing if upgrading to the latest version resolves this.

Hi @user,

upgrading to 1.20 indeed fixed the problem for me. 
Thank you so much for your help.

Hi, I have been struggling with the streamlit-webrtc component for the past 2-3 weeks. Before you write me off and ask me to go check with the component’s author here - [whitphx](https://github.com/whitphx), please hear me out.

I deployed a streamlit+webrtc app 2 weeks ago referencing component from [whitphx](https://github.com/whitphx) - using google’s stun server “stun:stun.l.google.com:19302” and it works fine.
Few days later, my streamlit app went down and webrtc component failed - I can’t view live video.
The original author’s app https://webrtc.streamlit.app/ also failed.

Then 2 days ago, I finally manage to get the webrtc component to work (with some latency issue) after I switched to a TURN server . But today, it stop working again.

On both occasion when i change STUN/ TURN servers, I tested it on [Trickle ICE](https://webrtc.github.io/samples/src/content/peerconnection/trickle-ice/) site and it works fine.

the original author’s app https://webrtc.streamlit.app/ has been working fine until 2 weeks ago, I have not much knowledge on network or webrtc, but I am trying like hell to figure out what is going on.

These are my tests on TrickleICE and Streamlit on 3 different browsers using my ISP 4G network (no WIFI to rule out any blocking).

title: Support case-insensitive lookup in _get_websocket_headers
body:
### Problem

The experimental `_get_websocket_headers` returns a `dict(the_underlying_header_object)`. I'm guessing that's to prevent user mutation (seems good to do 😁), but most header "dicts" returned by web packages are actually case-*in*sensitive wrappers, following [the HTTP spec](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7230#section-3.2).

### Solution

Rather than converting to a dict, which does case-sensitive lookup, could this function return a `copy.copy` (or `copy.deepcopy`) of the underlying header object? If it's also beneficial to standardize the return type (to handle the different `SessionClient` types), maybe a separate case-insensitive mapping could be added?

---

Community voting on feature requests enables the Streamlit team to understand which features are most important to our users.

title: Make "allowed message origins" a config option instead of hard-coded list
body:
### Problem

The list of **allowed-message-origins** is currently hard-coded, which means that in order to change it we have to manually alter the Streamlit library file `streamlit/web/server/routes.py`.

### Solution

**Preferred solution:** Enable **allowedMessageOrigins** as an option in the `.streamlit/config.toml` file.

### Additional information

Next to the hard-coded list in the `streamlit/web/server/routes.py` file, there is already a comment mentioning that in the long run the above solution is probably the way to go :)

---

title: Session gets stuck if disconnected while waiting for HTTP response
body:
### Checklist

### Summary

A Streamlit session will get stuck if a it disconnects while waiting for HTTP response, and then tries to reconnect.

### Reproducible Code Example

[[image]](https://issues.streamlitapp.com/?issue=gh-6442)

```Python
import requests
import streamlit as st

st.title('Streamlit gets stuck if session disconnects while waiting for HTTP response, and then tries to reconnect')

# Button that does something else
if st.button('Another button'):
    st.balloons()

# Button that sends request
if st.button('Send HTTP request'):
    with st.spinner():
        r = requests.post(url= "https://httpstat.us/200?sleep=6000")
        st.success('Request completed')
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Run the reproducible code example
2. Click on the "Send HTTP request" button to send an example request
3. While waiting for the response, disconnect from the Internet so the session gets disconnected
4. Reconnect to the internet after some time
5. Try to touch the other button but the session is stuck

### Expected Behavior

Session should either reconnect and receive HTTP response correctly, or simply reset the session entirely (which was the behavior in the past until the recent "Reconnect session" PRs).

A solution could be to have a `resetSessionsOnReconnect` option in the config.toml file that toggles this behavior.

### Current Behavior

Session tries to reconnect but actually gets stuck

### Is this a regression?

- [X] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.21.0
- Python version: 3.11
- Operating System: macOS
- Browser: Brave
- Virtual environment: conda

### Additional Information

FYI not fixed by the latest PR https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/6204

Thanks for reporting this @user!

I'll take a look to see if I can figure out what's going on here.
Thanks to you for checking @user , super appreciated!!!

Hey @user, sorry for the delay in being able to look into this.

Could you check if this still happens to you in version 1.22.0? I wasn't able to reproduce the issue on the newest Streamlit version. 

What I did notice in my testing on Community Cloud is that it seems like whether the page resets entirely or manages to print `'Request completed'` seems to be probabilistic, but this doesn't seem too unreasonable to me (as long as the page doesn't get stuck entirely) given the reconnect behavior is done on a best-effort basis + depending on how long the tab has been disconnected, it's possible that the session was cleaned up and the only option is to reset the page.

No worries @user!

I realized there is a big difference if (1) the browser client loses the connection, or if (2) the server that actually runs the request loses the connection.

**The problem still happens in 1.22.0 if the server loses the connection**. I just added a `st.spinner` to the reproducible example to make the issue more obvious: the spinner will continue forever and you cannot do anything else (so the session is actually stuck).

If only the client disconnects, then the behavior follows exactly what you describe (best-effort reconnect behavior). **I did notice however that when a session reconnects, custom components fail to load. After a second reload they render correctly.**

Curious to know your thoughts

Thanks for the additional information @user. Another thing that I have a hunch may be related here: do you happen to have the `runner.fastReruns` config option off?

I'm not able to reproduce this in the exact way you're describing on my local setup with the config option set to its default (I could get some weirdness to occur but couldn't force the session to hang indefinitely), but I was able to do so after turning it off and because of this have a theory as to what's going on here.

What I think is happening is as follows:
* The `requests` library, by default, doesn't set a timeout for requests to complete (see the [requests documentation](https://requests.readthedocs.io/en/latest/user/advanced/#timeouts))
* When the server loses its internet connection, the request in flight at the time will hang indefinitely after the connection is restored. This probably happens because of the lack of a timeout and due to requests itself being unable to recover after the internet disconnects/reconnects
* Before we implemented session reconnects, what would happen was that the reconnecting browser tab would always connect to a new session, and the old one would never recover but would most likely(?) end up being garbage collected eventually
* With session reconnects + fastReruns on, the next script interaction still works because we immediately start a new script runner when the user next interacts with the app (there's some weirdness you see with the spinner still sticking around, but at least the session doesn't get stuck forever)
* With session reconnects + fastReruns off, the session does reconnect successfully, but the original scriptrunner is still waiting for `requests.post` to return, which will never happen. This causes the browser tab to be stuck indefinitely

---

I'm not yet entirely convinced of this theory (verifying it should be possible by adding some logging code -- will spend some time doing that next week), but if it does turn out be what's happening here, I think a fix is unlikely to be prioritized on our end since it's not streamlit itself that's causing things to hang indefinitely. In this case, it'd probably be the responsibility of the app code to set a timeout to account for the internet resetting (or even just the request taking an abnormally long amount of time), but I'm happy to discuss further.

Actually, right after posting the mini-essay above (which I guess was still a useful thing to write as it helped me think aloud
😆), I realized that we might be able to improve this situation by always discarding the current scriptrunner when a session disconnects -- the script runner itself isn't part of the state that we want to preserve when reconnecting to a session. Will need to think more about this approach since there may be unintended side effects of doing this.

This won't be a complete fix as things will still hang indefinitely if the client and server are running on the same machine. If that machine disconnects from the internet, the call to `requests.post` will still hang forever, but the browser tab won't disconnect, so nothing will force us to discard the current script runner. I don't think the local-development case is where this bug is particularly painful, though.

Your hunch is correct, I had `runner.fastReruns` turned off 😅 (for some other weirdness but that is a different topic). Hadn't thought about it, but can confirm the difference in behavior you describe when turning it on. Thank you :)

On the other hand, not sure about "discarding the current scriptrunner when a session disconnects", if that means a script run could be discarded when it is only halfway done vs. expectation that all Streamlit script runs will be "top to bottom". For example, if a script run that should normally update several session state variables is discarded after some have been updated but not all.

Thanks for confirming! I'm fairly convinced of the theory outlined above in that case. Will have to think more about how to handle this scenario since I think you're right about potentially confusing behavior occurring if `fastReruns` is off and we still discard a scriptrunner early when a session disconnects.

I'll probably revisit this in a week or two when I have some more free time, but with the current information, it seems like this may not be something that we put a lot of effort into fixing soon as:
* it may just be one of those naturally hairy scenarios where there are notable edge cases to any solution
* there are reasonable arguments for both the case that user scripts should handle this (since it's the requests library that's likely locking up here, and setting timeouts is a good idea in general) and that streamlit should do something clever so that they don't have to (this particular bug would be difficult to diagnose without knowing what streamlit is doing under the hood)
I'm not able to reproduce this issue anymore here: https://issues.streamlit.app/?issue=gh-6442. @user one of the recent changes might have fixed it. Can we close it?
I was unable to reproduce this as well, so I am going to close this. Let us know if there is something to reproduce this.

title: Input lag with forms when using graphviz
body:
### Checklist

### Summary

This issue has been existing for a while and was supposedly fixed (https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/5336) but I find that it has not been fixed. I still experience this issue and it is causing issues - especially for mobile users, for whom the platform becomes unusable.

In the other topic it was suggested that every keypress is seen as an event that triggers a full rerender, but that means that the graphviz graph has to be rerendered as well which hits performance a lot.

It is possible that this was fixed momentarilty (after the PR in the linked issue) but clearly the issue is still present now, so I am marking it as a regression.

### Reproducible Code Example

- An example is here: https://huggingface.co/spaces/BramVanroy/text-to-amr
- Code: https://huggingface.co/spaces/BramVanroy/text-to-amr/blob/main/app.py

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Type in a sentence
2. Press the submit button
3. A plot will be drawn
4. Now try to type a new sentence. You'll notice input lag - especially on slower devices and detrimental on mobile devices

### Expected Behavior

No input lag.

### Current Behavior

Input lag. So much so that the app is unusable on (slower) mobile devices.

### Is this a regression?

- [X] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.19.0
- Python version: 3.10.7
- Operating System: Linux
- Browser: Edge
- Virtual environment: Docker

import streamlit as st

title: Hide the initial `Please wait...` callout when `?embed=true`
body:
### Problem

Streamlit apps show an initial "Please wait..." callout when the app is loading. This makes sense so you don't get a blank screen e.g. if on a slow connection. But it can be distracting when the app is embedded on another webpage. Especially if that page is doing heavy customization to the Streamlit app to adapt it to the look and feel of the outer page. The callout will still have the normal Streamlit because it's loaded before anything else.

### Solution

**MVP:** Get rid of the callout when `?embed=true`. Or only show it after a while, e.g. 3 seconds. 

**Possible additions:** Make it configurable, e.g. via another `?embed_options` parameter. 

---

Community voting on feature requests enables the Streamlit team to understand which features are most important to our users.

title: server side rendering
body:
### Problem

I'm always frustrated when streamlit takes 2 minutes to just load static content on a page.

### Solution

**MVP:** What's the smallest possible solution that would get 80% of the problem out of the way?

Do an initial static render of the HTML on the server side, and send that to browser. Then Load javascript & connect via websocket lazily.

### Additional context

I built https://gooey.ai/explore completely using streamlit. I love that streamlit allows us to iterate fast, but also at the same time seeing a lot of frustrated users when the initial page load times are slow. Plus, the google SEO stuff also gets hurt because everything has to be loaded via a websocket.

I also don't mind taking a shot at the MVP if someone can throw ideas at me around how this can be done

---

title: Graceful Shutdown of Server
body:
### Problem

I want to restart the server in a controlled manner via automation on some time scale like day/week or if I detect memory usage issues.  Pressing Ctrl-C at a prompt or a CLI-based kill command seems like a very blunt instrument for a task that should be well-defined.  __I don't expect streamlit to handle any scheduling.__  

### Solution

There are many ways to handle this issue without needing root access on the server.
    1. API call accessible from a streamlit page that would allow for either a shutdown or restart.   `st.shutdown()`,`st.restart()`
   2. Run a CLI command that would allow a graceful shutdown/restart. `streamlit --shutdown` `streamlit --restart`

### Slightly better solution
A mechanism for passwords to initiate this process might be useful.  My use-case, not so much.

---

Community voting on feature requests enables the Streamlit team to understand which features are most important to our users.

title: Schedule clear cache
body:
### Problem

I learned that the cache from "st.cache_data()" will only be cleared when the option "Clear cache" from developer options is manually activated by the owner of the app or if the cache expires. 

The problem with that is when you have multiple sets of data in your app that are scheduled to be updated in specific dates of the month, at specific times, you either go and manually clear cache yourself in each of this updates or you'll have outdated data in your app until the cache expires.
[image]

Of course you can leave a small time for the argument "ttl" in "st.cache_data()" to try to get around this issue but you will be querying your database multiple times, and also increasing user loading time, when you know the data hasn't changed (in my case, the data is only updated once a month). This also creates the issue that the user of the app won't have the most recent data as soon as it is released.

### Solution

It would be great to be able to leave a really long time as an argument to "st.cache_data()" and be able to schedule a "Clear cache" on the app settings (https://share.streamlit.io/) for when you know the data is gonna be released along the following months. 

The format for this scheduling would be great if it was something close to what the Windows Task Scheduler offers as triggers, with multiple dates that don't exactly follow a standard such as crontab from linux, Databricks and other tools. Why? Because the data I work with has some randomness on the date it is released. Sometimes the 5th, sometimes the 8th, some time 1st day of the month, and so on.

---

Community voting on feature requests enables the Streamlit team to understand which features are most important to our users.

title: Button / `st.session_state` bug introduced with 1.20?
body:
### Checklist

### Summary

It looks like `st.session_state` misbehaves since 1.20, at least when used together with an infinite loop.
Buttons on_click functions are no more executed a second time.

1) With version **1.19 it is OK**: clicking buttons it reacts correctly resetting and descreasing the respective counter.
2) With version 1.20+ a second click on a button is not recognized anymore, and the `st.session_state` dictionary complains that the `counter` key does not exist.

Was there a features change in 1.20 to justify this behavior?

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
import streamlit as st
import time

if "button" not in st.session_state:
	st.session_state["button"] = "----"
if "counter" not in st.session_state:
	st.session_state["counter"] = 0

def btn1_click():
	st.session_state["counter"] = 10
	st.session_state["button"] = "Btn1"

def btn2_click():
	st.session_state["counter"] = 20
	st.session_state["button"] = "Btn2"

cols = st.columns(3)
with cols[0]:
	st.button("Btn1", on_click=btn1_click)
with cols[1]:
	st.button("Btn2", on_click=btn2_click)
with cols[2]:
	ph = st.empty()

i = 0
while True:
	time.sleep(.1)
	
	if st.session_state["counter"] > 0:
		st.session_state["counter"] -= 1
		if st.session_state["counter"] == 0:
			st.session_state["button"] = "----"
	
	with ph.container():
		st.write(st.session_state)
	
	i+=1
	print(f"{i: 4d} button {st.session_state['button']} => counter {st.session_state['counter']}")
```

### Steps To Reproduce

Install streamlit 1.19, then 1.20.
Clicking each button you see that the behavior is completely different, because they stop working after the first click for the newest libraries. 

### Expected Behavior

### Current Behavior

### Is this a regression?

- [X] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.19 - 1.20+
- Python version: 3.8
- Operating System: Ubuntu
- Browser: Firefox, Brave, Edge
- Virtual environment: venv

title: st.experimental_data_editor does not keep changes when running on Google App Engine
body:
### Checklist

### Summary

Hi,

I am using the recent beta features for editable dataframes in Streamlit `streamlit = "^1.8.1"`. 
The app displays a dataframe and if any changes are entered (and a button is pressed) the changes are written to a BigQuery Database (this is also where the data is coming in the first place).

When running the app local, everything is working as expected (incl. write back to the same BQ).
When running in GCP App engine (flex environment), entered new values are vanishing after a second.

Local: enter value -> "running" appears -> values are stillt there -> can save them to BQ
App Engine: enter value -> "running" appears -> values are gone

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
import streamlit as st
import save_data_to_bq, load_data_from_bq

my_data = load_data_from_bq()

my_data_update = st.experimental_data_editor(
    (
        my_data.style.format(
            formatter={...}
        )
    ),
    use_container_width=True,
    num_rows="fixed",
)

# Get changes in the data
diffs_in_data = ~(my_data == my_data_update)
updated_rows = my_data_update[diffs_in_data.any(axis=1)]

if not updated_rows.empty:
    data_update_status = st.empty()
    save_button = st.button("Save")

    if save_button:
        job_successful = save_data_to_bq(updated_rows)
        if job_successful:
            data_update_status.success("Data updated successfully!")
        else:
            data_update_status.error("Data update failed!")

title: st.cache_resource alternative for non-threadsafe object (that can't be serialized / used with st.cache_data)
body:
### Checklist

### Summary

I'm trying to use the Google Drive API, which has a [quite ugly](https://developers.google.com/drive/api/quickstart/python) runtime generated client. When using `st.cache_resource` with the client, I get a variety of SSL errors (eg: `DECRYPTION_FAILED_OR_BAD_RECORD_MAC`, `BLOCK_CIPHER_PAD_IS_WRONG`, `BAD_RECORD_TYPE`, etc) when changing input triggers a page rerender or with multiple tabs open. I think the client keeps a connection or something open that is not thread/multiprocess safe, similar to described [here](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/64995178/decryption-failed-or-bad-record-mac-in-multiprocessing) or [here](https://medium.com/@philamersune/fixing-ssl-error-decryption-failed-or-bad-record-mac-d668e71a5409). Given this non-thread safety, `st.cache_resource` is not the right fit.

I think this same connection (or whatever) also prevents the client from being pickled (`TypeError: cannot pickle '_cffi_backend.FFI' object`), which means I also can't use it with `st.cache_data`.

---

What I'd like is something between the two: for an object to be cached once per thread/process (or "sessions"?). The [streamlit caching docs](https://docs.streamlit.io/library/advanced-features/caching#mutation-and-concurrency-issues) highlight mutation and concurrency issues, but don't really give any guidance for thread unsafe things.

I would have expected this to be a bit more common of an issue (perhaps things like SQLAlchemy's engine's built in thread pooling cover a lot of ground), but couldn't really find any similar issues.

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
import streamlit as st
from google.oauth2 import service_account
from googleapiclient.discovery import Resource, build

def get_google_drive_service() -> Resource:
    scopes = [
        "https://www.googleapis.com/auth/drive",
        "https://www.googleapis.com/auth/spreadsheets",
        "https://www.googleapis.com/auth/forms",
    ]
    parent_creds = service_account.Credentials.from_service_account_info(
        {"service account info": "private"}, scopes=scopes
    )
    return build("drive", "v3", credentials=parent_creds.with_subject("<email>"), cache_discovery=False)

gdrive = st.cache_resource(get_google_drive_service())
```

### Steps To Reproduce

Get some credentials to create a client as [described here](https://developers.google.com/drive/api/quickstart/python) and fill them in the snippet above. Then, open a couple different tabs (perhaps add some inputs to trigger rerendering - I can update if there's no obvious solution / this repro is actually worth looking into).

### Expected Behavior

There to be an argument to `st.cache_resource` OR alternative function that supports thread unsafe objects.

### Current Behavior

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.20.0
- Python version: 3.10.9
- Operating System: macOS 13.3.1 (arm64)
- Browser: Chrome
- Virtual environment:

### Additional Information

### Are you willing to submit a PR?

- [X] Yes, I am willing to submit a PR!

title: Execute streamlit scripts/apps by Python without any warning as a pure script
body:
### Problem

The streamlit run a Python script as following:

```
$ streamlit run app.py
```

This will create a server and we can browse the results in a web page.

However, I want to use `streamlit` as a **logging** tool to print out the results of each step when debugging, and deploy the scripts without any streamlit server.

For example, I write a web crawler, which should be run in **headless mode** (no server/browser required), and when I develop/debug that script, I want to print out the results for each step in the script. The `streamlit` is a **good visualization logging tool for complex results** (e.g. JSON, dataframe...), and we can view the well organized results in the browser instead of the console. For some scenarios, this will be a better dev tool than Jupyter Notebook or `print()`.

Currently, I can run the script by Python directly, but it shows warnings which I don't want:

```
# instead of `streamlit run`
$ python app.py
2023-06-02 17:37:09.208 
  Warning: to view this Streamlit app on a browser, run it with the following
  command:

    streamlit run uber_pickups.py [ARGUMENTS]
2023-06-02 17:37:09.208 No runtime found, using MemoryCacheStorageManager
2023-06-02 17:37:09.210 No runtime found, using MemoryCacheStorageManager
```

## Question and Feature Request

How can I silence the warning and make sure that the `streamlit` code in that script does not do anything while being executed by `python` (no performance impact/overhead)?

I don't want to remove the streamlit "logging" code when deploying, and when I need to debug that script, I just need to run it with `streamlit run app.py` again.

title: Access to the st.spinner object as a stand-alone UI element
body:
### Problem

I would like to show the default streamlit spinner while waiting for some data to compute. See here for more context: https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/6687

I know I can us st.spinner within a `with` block, but this is not what I'm looking for. 
I just want to be able to display a spinner 
### Solution

I would like to be able to use `st.spinner` outside a `with` block.

For example:

```python
import streamlit as st 
import time
 
st.title('Example')
placeholder = st.empty()

# This is what I want: 
# placeholder.spinner('This will show here until something else is written to the placeholder') # <- this does not exist

# This is to showcase the idea
placeholder.image('https://i.gifer.com/origin/34/34338d26023e5515f6cc8969aa027bca_w200.gif', width=35) # <- This is a hack pending an implementation

my_bar = st.progress(0, text='Please wait 3 seconds')

for percent_complete in range(300):
    time.sleep(0.01)
    my_bar.progress(min((percent_complete+1)/300, 1.0), text='Please wait 3 seconds')

placeholder.success('Thank you for waiting')
```

### Additional context

This is a blocker to my solution to this https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/6687

---

Community voting on feature requests enables the Streamlit team to understand which features are most important to our users.

title: UX Consistency: Add an option in set_page_config to replace OS/browser default emoji font with Twemoji
body:
### Problem

Emojis are rendered differently on different OS and browsers.

This results in different user experience.

Twemoji is already used by Streamlit for the favicon but the other emojis are rendered using the OS/Browser default emoji font.

### Solution

Add an argument in `set_page_config` to automatically replace emojis with the Twemoji counterpart.

The latest version of Twemoji is here: https://github.com/jdecked/twemoji
An example of JS+CSS to properly render Twemoji's SVG emojis : https://gist.github.com/Armster15/db063ab0dc5be699ae07a067a7333752

A poor attempt at doing this with streamlit components today:
https://discuss.streamlit.io/t/user-experience-ux-consistency-replace-emojis-with-twemojis/45036

---

Community voting on feature requests enables the Streamlit team to understand which features are most important to our users.

title: Cannot Ctrl+C to end streamlit process from CLI without an open tab (in Windows)
body:
### Checklist

### Summary

This has had [a few comments in the forum](https://discuss.streamlit.io/t/cant-stop-streamlit-app-using-ctrl-c-if-the-app-has-been-closed-in-the-browser/38738) and I couldn't find mention in a current or closed issue, so documenting here. This is merely a minor inconvenience with an easy workaround for most, but noting for completeness/future searches.

In Windows, the `streamlit run` process cannot be terminated from command line with `Ctrl+C` if there are no connected tabs. The terminal itself must either be closed or a new tab open and connected to the session to register if `Ctrl+C` has been typed. The forum thread mentions a connection to tornado.

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
# Any valid streamlit app
import streamlit as st
st.write('hi')
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. From a terminal in Windows, `streamlit run app.py`.
2. Close any/all tabs connected to the session.
3. Ctrl+C in the terminal
(nothing happens)
4. Open a tab and connect to the session
(terminal immediately registers the previous command and correctly proceeds `Stopping...`)

### Expected Behavior

Ctrl+C should stop the process even if there are no active users

### Current Behavior

A connected tab is required to stop the process without closing the terminal

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.23.0
- Python version: 3.10.11
- Operating System: Windows 10
- Browser: Edge...or rather "none"
- Virtual environment: Conda

### Additional Information

Thematically related to #6611

### Are you willing to submit a PR?

- [ ] Yes, I am willing to submit a PR!

title: Streamlit reinstalling packages by itself causing incompatibilities
body:
### Checklist

### Summary

When deploying the app via streamlit, it runs an automatic check to see if Streamlit is already installed. It is specified in my requirements, so it should stop at that. However, since I use Streamlit == 1.14.0 for compatibility reasons with streamlit-extras, it detects that I should be using altair <5 to be compatible with streamlit as well. And so, even though altair == 4.2.2 is already installed, it reinstalls it, and with it it's dependencies, namely numpy == 1.25.0 which cause problems as it is incompatible with the latest version of the shap library.

Now I'm not sure if this is considered a bug, as everything seems to be working as intended, but I don't understand why it would reinstall altair even though it already is. And I have no idea what I can do to avoid this issue on my side.

### Reproducible Code Example

### Steps To Reproduce

Deploy the app via streamlit using the repositery linked.

### Expected Behavior

When i use the dashboard created locally via a brand new venv, everything installs and works as expected with no issues, and I can display the dashboard perfectly.

### Current Behavior

Now what happens is, all the packages install properly from the requirements.txt. But after the packages installation, Streamlit runs an automatic check to verify that the Streamlit package is installed. And this follows in the logs of the app : 

> Checking if Streamlit is installed
> 
> 2023-06-30 15:38:50.451 INFO    matplotlib.font_manager: generated new fontManager
> 
> Found Streamlit version 1.14.0 in the environment
> 
> Streamlit 1.14.0 is present which is incompatible with altair>=5.0.0. Installing altair 4.*
> 
> Collecting altair<5
> 

And so by doing that, it goes and reinstall altair < 5 even though it already is, and by doing that, reinstalls numpy == 1.25.0, which isn't compatible with shap, causing the app to fail to deploy.

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

These are the relevant packages causing the issue.

streamlit == 1.14.0
altair < 5
streamlit-extras==0.2.7
shap==0.41.0
numpy==1.23.5

### Additional Information

Here's the log file with the issue

[logs-haelios-projet_7_oc-main-Dashboard-streamlit_dashboard.py-2023-06-30T16_02_38.954Z.txt](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/files/11918374/logs-haelios-projet_7_oc-main-Dashboard-streamlit_dashboard.py-2023-06-30T16_02_38.954Z.txt)

title: "Deploy this app" option in the app's hamburger menu incorrectly fills Community Cloud deployment information
body:
### Checklist

### Summary

From the app menu in the upper-right corner, there is an option to "Deploy this app" when viewing a local app. This _almost_ works but the Community Cloud deployment page has an extra `.git` in the repo name where it's not needed. This results in an error and the repo is not recognized. Deleting `.git` corrects the format and it becomes deployable.

[image]

### Reproducible Code Example

### Steps To Reproduce

0. Be signed in to GitHub and Community Cloud in your default web browser.
1. View a locally running app (from a git repo, up-to-date with remote).
2. Open the app menu in the upper-right corner.
3. Click "**Deploy this app**"

### Expected Behavior

The deployment page for Community Cloud should open with correctly pre-filled informaiton.

### Current Behavior

The deployment page for Community Cloud does open with mostly correct information, but the repo has a `.git` suffix which is not correct for the field. (Manually deleting the `.git` ending rectifies the error.)

- Python version: 3.11

title: `st.cache_data` does not work and runs function on every app rerun
body:
### Checklist

### Summary

I have a fairly complex app where I use `st.cache_data` for a function which sends SQL query using database connection to get pandas DataFrame. The app uses streamlit-authenticator and has multiple tabs. The connections config is passed to the function using `_connection_config` argument. I use `st.cache_data(ttl=300, max_entries=128)` decorator but I noticed that the query is run every time. It is used in a separate file which I import in another sub-app file. My assumption was that there is some kind of limitation on the streamlit side which prevent caching but I've created a minimal example and the cache still doesn't work.

I searched for different issues related to `st.cache_data` and found something related to `hash_funcs` but I don't think it's relevant here. I've tried using `hash_funcs` and it didn't change anything. Besides, my cached function arguments are simple python primitives.

requirements.txt:

```
streamlit==1.24.0
watchdog==2.1.9
```

How I run the app:

```
streamlit run --server.port 8505 app.py
```

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
import time

import pandas as pd
import streamlit as st

st.cache_data()
def test_cache(n: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
    time.sleep(5)
    return pd.DataFrame({"test": [1] * n})

df = test_cache(5)

st.dataframe(df)

st.button("rerun")
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Create virtual env for python 3.11.4
2. Install dependencies: `python -m pip install streamlit==1.24.0 watchdog==2.1.9`
3. Run streamlit app: `streamlit run --server.port 8505 app.py`
4. Open the app and click "rerun" button a few times

### Expected Behavior

Only the first time loading the data frame takes 5 seconds and all consecutive runs return cached data frame.

### Current Behavior

The function decorated with `st.cache_data()` runs every time and loading the data frame takes 5 seconds on every app rerun.

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.24.0
- Python version: 3.11.4
- Operating System: masOS 12.3
- Browser: Chrome, Safari
- Virtual environment: pyenv

### Additional Information

### Are you willing to submit a PR?

- [ ] Yes, I am willing to submit a PR!

comments.text:
Hey, @user!

`st.cache_data` is decorator, so to use it properly you need to decorate your function with `@st.cache_data`. 

For code in your example: 

```python
import pandas as pd
import streamlit as st

@st.cache_data()
def test_cache(n: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
    time.sleep(5)
    return pd.DataFrame({"test": [1] * n})

df = test_cache(5)

st.dataframe(df)

st.button("rerun")
```
It should work correctly. 

Also please note, if you need to cache not just data, but e.g. connection instance (when you need the same instance) you can use `st.cache_resource`, or specifically for a connection you can also use `st.experimental_connection`.

title: Custom config options in `config.toml`
body:
### Problem

I would like to add my own configuration keys to the `.streamlit/config.toml` file so I can configure settings which affect the whole project in one location.

### Solution

**MVP:** Allow user-specified configuration options in the configuration file and have them accessible via `streamlit.config.get_option('foo.bar)` from within the code. To avoid clashes with any section names the streamlit team wants to add, you could limit user specified configuration to one section, e.g. `[user]`

**Possible additions:** As listed in the linked forum post (below), this could be extended to support different deployment environments so different settings are applied depending on the current environment.

**Preferred solution:** ---

### Additional context

Example config file structure
```toml
[theme]
primaryColor="#c0ffee"

[user]
my_custom_setting_1="foo"
```

Access within code

```python
import streamlit
import streamlit.config

streamlit.write(streamlit.config.get_option("user.my_custom_setting_1"))
# will print "foo" in browser
```

I've seen a similar request in the forums [here](https://discuss.streamlit.io/t/can-we-create-a-custom-section-in-config-toml/42827). But that one is a bit more complex than this one since it involves deployment environments (which are out-of-scope of my request)

---

Community voting on feature requests enables the Streamlit team to understand which features are most important to our users.

**MVP:** Allow user-specified configuration options in the configuration file and have them accessible via `streamlit.config.get_option('foo.bar)` from within the code. To avoid clashes with any section names the streamlit team wants to add, you could limit user specified configuration to one section, e.g. `[user]`

**Possible additions:** As listed in the linked forum post (below), this could be extended to support different deployment environments so different settings are applied depending on the current environment.

**Preferred solution:** ---
sections.additional context:
Example config file structure
```toml
[theme]
primaryColor="#c0ffee"

[user]
my_custom_setting_1="foo"
```

Access within code

```python
import streamlit
import streamlit.config

streamlit.write(streamlit.config.get_option("user.my_custom_setting_1"))
sections.will print \"foo\" in browser:
```

I've seen a similar request in the forums [here](https://discuss.streamlit.io/t/can-we-create-a-custom-section-in-config-toml/42827). But that one is a bit more complex than this one since it involves deployment environments (which are out-of-scope of my request)

@user I hacked "multiple environments" by having one common config file and one for each environment. Via CI, where we build our container images, I merge the common config with the specific environment I need. I'm using https://github.com/miracl/conflate for that.
+1: custom keys in config.toml

I can think of 3 workarounds:
- [PyYAML](https://pypi.org/project/PyYAML/) if you need to read/write human readable config files

- [Hydra](https://hydra.cc/) - built with OmegaConf, for merging multiple config files more easily

title: streamlit chat_input callback (on_submit) not returning the message you input
body:
### Checklist

### Summary

The image below shows a test I'm running to show the issue. The error happens after running streamlit run app.py on the terminal and writing a message on the chat_input box that appears on screen. Once you press enter, this error happens.

[image]

I think the error happens because the streamlit callback is not returning anything. If you use the second function (print_args) you will see that it's not printing anything in any of the variables that could be outputting something.

[image]

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
# Code to reproduce the first error:
# You need to start the app with streamlit run app.py first
import streamlit
def print_text(chat_input):
    print(chat_input)

streamlit.chat_input("Start a conversation!", on_submit=print_text)

# Code to reproduce the second error:
import streamlit
def print_args(*args, **kwargs):
    print("Args:", args)
    print("Kwargs:", kwargs)

streamlit.chat_input("Start a conversation!", on_submit=print_args)
```

### Steps To Reproduce

To reproduce both error you need to open a terminal, navigate to where the app.py file that contains the code above is located and execute: streamlit run app.py

Then you have to open a browser window (if it doesn't open for you directly), write localhost:8501 and enter a message in the chat box that will appear on your browser

### Expected Behavior

If this was working as I'm expecting it to work, the callback would return the message that the user passed as a variable like the on_change argument works in a streamlit.text_input block.

### Current Behavior

TypeError: print_text() missing 1 required positional argument: 'chat_input'
Traceback:
File "/usr/local/lib/python3.11/site-packages/streamlit/runtime/scriptrunner/script_runner.py", line 548, in _run_script
    self._session_state.on_script_will_rerun(rerun_data.widget_states)
File "/usr/local/lib/python3.11/site-packages/streamlit/runtime/state/safe_session_state.py", line 68, in on_script_will_rerun
    self._state.on_script_will_rerun(latest_widget_states)
File "/usr/local/lib/python3.11/site-packages/streamlit/runtime/state/session_state.py", line 484, in on_script_will_rerun
    self._call_callbacks()
File "/usr/local/lib/python3.11/site-packages/streamlit/runtime/state/session_state.py", line 497, in _call_callbacks
    self._new_widget_state.call_callback(wid)
File "/usr/local/lib/python3.11/site-packages/streamlit/runtime/state/session_state.py", line 249, in call_callback
    callback(*args, **kwargs)

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.24.0
- Python version: 3.11.3
- Operating System: MacOS
- Browser: Google Chrome
- Virtual environment: Docker container on a python slim buster base image

### Additional Information

@user This is the expected behavior. The `chat_input` value is not passed to the callback as a parameter, but instead, you can access it from the session state:

```python
import streamlit

```

title: Restrict filetypes that can be uploaded via API request in accordance with st.file_uploader type parameter
body:
### Problem

A community member noted that despite restricting the filetypes that can be uploaded via a `st.file_uploader` using the `type` parameter, someone could still make a POST request to `/_stcore/upload_file HTTP/1.1` and successfully upload a file of any type.

### Additional context

[Forum post](https://discuss.streamlit.io/t/insecure-file-upload-functionality/47182)

> My streamlit application has a csv upload functionality that reads the file and saves its contents to a database table. I use streamlit’s st.file_uploader, which sends a POST request to /_stcore/upload_file in the background. Our upload feature is used to read csv file, the files are just loading into memory and not being saved.
> 
> In the front-end I can restrict other file types from upload by specifying the type on st.file_uploader and which works fine.
> 
> However, this filetype verification measure was found to be implemented only on the client side. It will therefore possible to bypass this control and upload files that could contain malware or be used to mount further attacks. That means, someone can send POST request used to upload files directly to the application without use of a web browser. This bypass method can be used to upload Windows executable files using the below POST request
> 
> POST /_stcore/upload_file HTTP/1.1
> 
> This request will return HTTP 200, indicating that the file upload was successful. This response had the same format as when a valid CSV file was uploaded.
> 
> So my question is, does it cause any security vulnerabilities, and if so, how can we prevent them? Could anyone suggest solutions/hacks for this security vulnerability?
> 

---

title: Proposed fix to: (The app is attempting to load the component from ****, and hasn't received its "streamlit" message.)
body:
### Problem

Custom components often fail to load when apps are deployed to Azure Container Apps or GCP App Run.

[image]

This has been reported many times and there is no known solution:

- https://discuss.streamlit.io/t/the-app-is-attempting-to-load-the-component-from-and-hasnt-received-its-streamlit-message/36968
- https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/3315
- https://github.com/okld/streamlit-ace/issues/13
- https://github.com/PablocFonseca/streamlit-aggrid/issues/7

### Solution

I think implementing some optional caching of custom component resources (e.g. style sheets) at installation time / the first time the app is run would greatly mitigate this issue.

Hey @user,
Thanks for flagging this! Just wanted to confirm that 1. This is happening when your app is deployed on Azure Container Apps and GCP App Run (not Community Cloud), and 2. You're using the most recent version of Streamlit?

Yes, this has been an issue with basically all versions of Streamlit since custom components came out - but to be clear, I'm on 1.25.0 at the moment.

I’m deploying to cloud run and could at least mitigate the issue by using session affinity: https://cloud.google.com/run/docs/configuring/session-affinity

However it still pops up once in a while.
That's super helpful, @user – I saw a few users mention that in the forum as well

My thought is that this is an issue with the plugin ecosystem in general - there may be solutions for CloudRun or for AzureContainerApps and elsewhere - but the common issue seems to cut across many type of deployments.

I think the root cause is that some of the files needed to run the Streamlit Custom Components are fetched over the network when an app starts. The issue is made worse by these ephemeral container runtime given each instance starts with a "blank slate" and has to fetch the resources on start up.

@user I think using session affinity fixes the problem. When using session affinity, all requests of the same client are sent to the same server replica. @user described how to activate session affinity for Google Cloud [here](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/7046#issuecomment-1652185237).

If you are deploying using Kubernetes, you can enable session affinity like this for your service:

```
[...]
spec:
  [...]
  sessionAffinity: ClientIP
```

Read more about Kubernetes Session Affinity [here](https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/networking/virtual-ips/#session-affinity).

streamlit - custom components (streamlit addgrid, streamlit elements, streamlit andt design, and a few others)

Hey @user, thanks for reporting this!

This is behavior that's known but unfortunately a bit tricky to fix. The main difficulty is that making these endpoint calls tied to the root can be hard as it's not always entirely clear what the root of an app is in every deployment scenario.

For example, a Streamlit app being served behind a reverse proxy (that may be transparent to the streamlit server/client) with root at `https://example.com/foo/bar` and page `bar` of an app being served at `https://example.com/foo` initially look identical to the web client. We could probably solve this by including the paths to all pages of an app in the `index.html` so that we can determine when an initial request is being made to a subpage and change where we send the initial healthchecks accordingly , but it'd be a decent amount of work to do for what I think is a relatively small improvement and thus lands pretty far down the backlog. (There are some edge cases around this too like if an app served at `https://example.com/foo/bar` has subpage `bar`. I feel like these are contrived enough that we'd be okay with just accepting the weird behavior for these, though)

Of course, if we have enough people complaining that this additional 404 when navigating directly to a subpage is a huge issue for their apps, we can bump up the priority on this.

What are the consequences of the 404s? Is there a loss of functionality? If not, why are these endpoints called to begin with?
