title: Health check endpoint seems to break when deployed in certain cloud environments
body:
### Checklist

### Summary

Hi,
I really enjoy using streamlit to deploy all sorts of applications, but I consistently run into an issue that I have started to be able to reproduce, but is very difficult to understand. I have seen people discuss this issue before, but I haven't been able to find a version of streamlit that fixes the issue. Essentially, the application seems to refresh on me after a certain period of time. Here is one example.

https://discuss.streamlit.io/t/i-get-kicked-out-of-my-app-at-random-times/28316

### Reproducible Code Example

N/A

### Steps To Reproduce

Deploy a long running application to a non streamlit cloud environment using docker.

### Expected Behavior

I expect the _stcore/health to not throw an exception, seemingly causing my application to refresh.

### Current Behavior

Essentially, the gist of the issue is that when I deploy this using Docker to a cloud environment (AWS/Azure), I find the call made to the /_stcore/health endpoint **fails to parse on the frontend**. The endpoint produces a response with the text "ok", but further into the code, it seems the axios library tries to parse this response as json using JSON.parse(). However, this results in an error, which seems to refresh the page. I don't know how often the health endpoint is called, but it seems like it happens approximately every 5 minutes, so for long running processes, these don't end up finishing.

I tried to trace the bug through the streamlit codebase and found that perhaps you are returning the text "ok" on line 519 in the function labeled "is_ready_for_browser_connection". This seems to get returned to the UI, likely through in the "HealthHandler" class on line 148 in the get function. I suspect self.write() will converts dictionaries to json and text is just returned as text through the API. However, perhaps returning the dictionary {"status": "ok"} might fix the issue. 

From the code and stacktrace, it seems there is a websocket that attempts to close, and before closing, it pings the server (the health check), however, the health check indicates it is "ok" and should keep the websocket open. However, an exception occurs during the parsing of the health check, so the connection is closed and perhaps that is when the page refreshes.

Importantly, this does not seem to happen for me in the Streamlit Cloud nor locally, likely because neither seem to call the health check endpoint. The streamlit cloud seems to call the app/status endpoint and locally, no health checks are performed.

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.24.0
- Python version: 3.8.16
- Operating System: Windows
- Browser: Chrome/Edge

@user Is there any way we could prioritize this? I have several applications that seem to suffer from the same issue.

Hey @user, thanks for reporting this!

Do you happen to have an example of a stacktrace from when this issue occurs? We do rely on this healthcheck endpoint both in Streamlit Cloud as well as in apps running locally (in fact, calling this endpoint is part of the normal app initialization process in any environment), so I'm confused as to how this problem only seems to manifest in Docker deployments of Streamlit apps in other cloud envs.

To make things more strange, I'm fairly certain that we never access the response body of this endpoint (we only verify that the endpoint is returning a non-error status code in the [one place in the web client that we call it](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/blob/873a52ebf8a418555216c88278389a128dd989ed/frontend/app/src/connection/WebsocketConnection.tsx#L703)), but some quick checks that I did still seem to show that accessing the `.data` property of the axios response that we're currently just ignoring does work as expected (it just contains the string "ok").

I think something about certain deployment environments is causing some underlying axios code to try to parse the endpoint response body when we never explicitly do so, but I'll need a bit more info to investigate further.

@user Thanks for the reply. Let me see if I can ask around and double check what kind of deployment we are actually doing and get back to you. I am surprised this issue hasn't come up before. It feels like something within the dockerfile is messing up some of the calls.

One thing I did notice is that within the application, the healthcheck endpoint is called far more often than in other environments. When I look at the network tab, I see it being called perhaps every 5 minutes, versus when the application is deployed in the streamlit cloud, I never see it called in the network tab (I am on Chrome)

Interestingly, there is also a very good chance I am getting a timeout. Just got this error while running a long running process, which caused the application to refresh. It tried to call the stcore/health endpoint. Potentially, if I have a long running process, perhaps this causes a timeout, which refreshes the application?

[image]
So perhaps a timeout causes the exception, which leads to the refresh (versus the json response of ok)?

> It feels like something within the dockerfile is messing up some of the calls.

This is my current guess since in theory there shouldn't be any possible differences between deployment environments when it comes to the web client -- the static assets sent to the browser should be identical for a given streamlit version regardless of how streamlit is deployed. I'm still at a loss as to what could be going on here, though.

> When I look at the network tab, I see it being called perhaps every 5 minutes, versus when the application is deployed in the streamlit cloud, I never see it called in the network tab

Hmm, I'm pretty surprised by this. At the very least you should see a call to the endpoint in the network tab during app initialization (I double checked and am seeing this happen for an app I have deployed to Community Cloud). Also, IIRC the load balancer that we're using in Community Cloud can't keep a websocket connection alive for more than ~half an hour due to how some timeout configurations are set, so you'd also expect to see calls to this endpoint periodically on there as well, although every 5 minutes would probably be more frequent than average on a stable internet connection.

```

We are severely affected by this issue as well when the streamlit app is deployed to a cloud environment and executes a long-running operation – those health checks executing approx. every minute cause the app to rerun resulting in the long-running operation to continue on a different thread.

Re-prioritizing this and addressing rather soon is highly appreciated!

Mine is a multipage app with long running processes that reruns pages midway, coinciding with the healthcheck.
Everything worked fine when I developed on the laptop, but the app is unusable when deployed on cloud.
I'll have to look for another framework now :(

I managed to understand the issue and solve the issue ✅ at my **streamlit application**.

I recently faced this frustrating refresh issue. After quite a lot of investigation, I was convinced it is a specific issue with **cloud containerized environments** as I discovered the issue when deploying a production-grade **streamlit app** in a GCP GKE cluster. So, for a workaround, I moved it to a VM to meet the deadline, unaware of the root cause, and it was working.

The next is that I was trying a different thing, which accidentally helped me to **understand this refresh issue and solve it**. This helped me to reproduce the same issue in my **local system** when I fronted it with a **Squid proxy**.

### My findings
👉 The Culprit `Websocket` HTTP headers.
👉 The issue appears when `streamlit app` is fronted with any proxy (which is very likely the case of any cloud environment).

Sharing the details here https://github.com/Utshab500/my-tech-assets/tree/main/streamlit-issue-poc

@user @user Though I haven't moved my actual production-grade app to GKE again but I am betting pretty much on this finding because most of the cloud container applications are fronted with Loadbalancers (Ingress in Kubernetes) type of services, which act as a proxy. Hence, they must be configured to handle `Websocket` HTTP headers. 

Let me know if this helps or gives you any direction for your issue.

title: Built-In run_query with session_state
body:
### Checklist

### Summary

In conjunction with the st.experimental_connection feature, it would be nice to have sql queries that take one line of code. In addition, these queries could have an option to use existing results in a session_state if the query errors out

### Why?

These three components - the connection, the query and the error handling - all seem built out already and it would be nice to have them efficiently together as a built-in method

### How?

I'm not sure if the st.experimental_connection is included in the new method - it seems like that might be a separate first step and then step two would be something like st.run_query_with_handling(query: str, client: client, use_state: bool = True, state_name: str = None) to pull the data (client is a made-up type here, it would probably be a generic connection type defined in the class)

For st.run_query_with_handling, there could be two steps:

1. From https://docs.streamlit.io/knowledge-base/tutorials/databases/bigquery - as an example. Create a connection based on the conn_type and pull data with the query:

```
# Perform query.
# Uses st.cache_data to only rerun when the query changes or after 10 min.
@st.cache_data(ttl=600)
def run_query(query, client):
    query_job = client.query(query)
    rows_raw = query_job.result()
    # Convert to list of dicts. Required for st.cache_data to hash the return value.
    rows = [dict(row) for row in rows_raw]
    return rows
```

2. Create a wrapper that attempts the run #1 but uses existing results in st.session_state if use_state=True, else throws an error

```
def run_query_with_handling(query, client, use_state, state_name):
    try:
        output_data = query_func(query, client)
        st.session_state[state_name] = output_data
    except Exception as e:
        if state_name in st.session_state and use_state:
            log_str = (f"Unable to pull the most recent {state_name}, "
                       f"using data from the previous pull instead. "
                       f"Please check your internet connection and try "
                       f"again if necessary.\n"
                       f"Error: {e}")
            st.sidebar.warning(log_str)
            output_data = st.session_state[state_name]
        else:
            log_str = (f"*******************Error*******************\n"
                       f"Could not get {state_name}. If another error is "
                       f"not present, either {state_name} doesn't exist in "
                       f"the database or the connection is broken.\n"
                       f"Error: {e}")
            st.error(log_str)
    return output_data
```

Note that the output (st.sidebar.warning and st.error) seem like nice communication with the user, but could be optional or done in another way.

### Additional Context

title: CLI should not make blocking interactive requests unexpectedly
body:
### Checklist

### Summary

A colleague of mine used `streamlit` to create a debug tool for one of our projects. It looks like it could be great, however on first use I was greeted with an interactive prompt for my email. This prompt doesn't seem to have any detection of whether `streamlit` is running in an interactive environment, meaning that there's a blocking interactive prompt at startup for all users including in service environments.

I tested this by disabling `stdin` and piping the output through `cat`, like `streamlit run ... < /dev/null | cat`, which caused the process to exit on showing the email prompt.

As far as I can tell the prompt is just to sign up to a mailing list, yet there's nothing telling me who the data controller is for my information (email address) nor how to unsubscribe.

I'm assuming that this is a first-run operation, which further implies that streamlit is somewhere tracking whether or not I've used it before.

It looks like this behaviour originated from https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/63. I can see there that the issue of this causing apparent crashes in production-like environments raised, though the suggested solution (of setting configuration options/environment variables) doesn't work as well for others working in the same codebase who are using but not developing the streamlit code.

### Reproducible Code Example

### Steps To Reproduce

### Expected Behavior

There should not be an interactive prompt on startup, nor early exit if `stdin` is not available.

Showing a banner with a link to the project homepage and a suggestion that users sign up to receive notifications about updates would probably be ok, but this should not be a blocking operation. There should probably also be a way to turn this off, ideally mentioned as part of the banner.

### Current Behavior

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.25.0
- Python version: 3.11
- Operating System: Ubuntu 22.04 LTS
- Browser: n/a

### Additional Information

I can see there that the issue of this causing apparent crashes in production-like environments raised, though the suggested solution (of setting configuration options/environment variables) doesn't work as well for others working in the same codebase who are using but not developing the streamlit code.

There should not be an interactive prompt on startup, nor early exit if `stdin` is not available.

Showing a banner with a link to the project homepage and a suggestion that users sign up to receive notifications about updates would probably be ok, but this should not be a blocking operation. There should probably also be a way to turn this off, ideally mentioned as part of the banner.

comments.text: Hi @user, thanks for your submission! 🎈 I was able to reproduce and confirm this is a bug - looks like our app sizing on mobile isn't taking into account the parts of the app covered at bottom and/or top by the browser navigation elements.

A similar issue reported by other users on the [forum](https://discuss.streamlit.io/t/st-chat-input-is-either-hidden-or-covered-by-the-hosted-by-streamit-icon-on-iphone/53640/3?u=tonykip) where the `st.chat_input` box is completely hidden under the bottom of the screen and a user would have no idea it is there.

Taking a look at this, this looks like an issue of hosted apps on Community Cloud, but not on Streamlit itself. Likely the iframe is having issues in resizing.

https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/assets/69432/7e540829-3e3c-4a50-82b5-1a4066139e13

It seems to be associated with CSS in Streamlit Community Cloud. Right now, we use `100vh` for the iframe, and that can look weird on Mobile Safari/Chrome due to the dynamic address bar appearing. This is particularly annoying for chat applications where the chat input is at the bottom of the screen. There's a couple solutions for this:

1. Ignore it and just say it is what it is. Likely not the best answer, but there are workarounds, and this is a weird subject.
2. We can leverage `svh`, which is the smallest available viewport. The disadvantage is when the address bar goes away, it does not expand. There are dynamic values but there are issues with performance associated with them.
   a. We can apply it only in mobile settings as well.
   b. We may need to apply `vh` should `svh` not be available (it's semi-new to browsers)
5. We use `100%` and map that to the top-level HTML and propagate it down to the iframe.
   a. There's some peculiarity and sensitivity here, but it could provide the best scenario.
Going to close this as we have filed the issue on our Community Cloud team and this is not an issue with the Open Source Library. Thank you for reporting this!

comments.text:
Hi @user, this is a known issue with using the file uploader widget in deployments with multiple replicas. What's happening is that all of the files live on the instance that the browser has its websocket connection to / is running your user script, but HTTP requests to fetch the video content may be load balanced to other instances, resulting in the 404.

The fix for now is to enable some sort of sticky sessions / session affinity in your kubernetes cluster. We have some projects being worked on that will eventually allow developers to configure the storage backend for these types of files, but even then we'd probably recommend enabling sticky sessions as the fix for most users (see some of the comments in the linked issue for more information)

Closing as a duplicate of #4173
@user Thank you for your response. I've create a custom video player component that has resolved my issues. [st-video-player](https://pypi.org/project/st-video-player/)

### Summary

Making a Bazel build that anyone on my team can use to run streamlit locally and am having issues with components. I have the same problem. Looking at the webpage, I found this 403 forbidden ERROR from the server. (see the screenshot)

This ERROR only appears when I do `bazel run` or directly run `bazel-bin/....` executables, but doesn't appear when I use python from conda to directly run the python file inside the bazel runfiles. The same observations as @user  

[image]

I wonder if this is somehow triggering some security alert so the browser is preventing the page to proceed
@user have you found a workaround for this?
Because I don't have the issue when using `streamlit_folium.folium_static` but do with `streamlit_folium.st_folium` and `st_aggrid.AgGrid`, I believe this is specific to bi-directional components.

I didn't find a work around, unfortunately. I gave up on streamlit and switched to gradio, although I really wanted to have the AgGrid functionality. It's a tradeoff, gradio doesn't have AgGrid, but it is much easier to run via Bazel.
@user, I saw in your PR (https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/8372) that you are also building streamlit with Bazel. Have you possibly run into any issues similar to this one?

Hi @user , I'm not familiar with `streamlit_folium`, but just would like to mention another issue I've encountered is that the using streamlit in bazel is that the built files may be from a hidden folder e.g. `.foo`, which is blacked listed by streamlit in https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/blob/60ed8c151789598131a92ab5365cb7a9e21750f1/lib/streamlit/folder_black_list.py#L23, and I don't think it can be removed at this point.

Hi, I faced the same issue where I wanted to use [`streamlit-local-storage`](https://pypi.org/project/streamlit-local-storage/) with bazel and I think I figured out the issue.

Bazel imitates the folder structure by making the exact same folder tree on build, but symlinking every file in all folders to the actual file to save disk space.

This causes a problem in the following code:

https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/blob/066dad796e3a21c37180eab6f46ff617f9e466be/lib/streamlit/web/server/component_request_handler.py#L45-L54

In the above code, `component_root` is somewhere in bazel's auto generated folder structure, whereas `abspath` is the path to the actual file in the system because `os.path.realpath` resolves symlinks and points to the destination of the symlink(s).
Therefore these variables do not share a common path and a 403 is returned. 

FYI, these are the values of the variables in my case (I masked some parts).

```python
component_root='/private/var/tmp/_bazel_$USER/XXXXXXX/execroot/.../bazel-out/darwin_arm64-fastbuild/bin/.../streamlit_main.runfiles/.../pip_deps_streamlit_local_storage/site-packages/streamlit_local_storage/frontend/build'
abspath='/private/var/tmp/_bazel_$USER/XXXXXXX/external/.../pip_deps_streamlit_local_storage/site-packages/streamlit_local_storage/frontend/build/index.html'
```

If I `ls -la` in the folder, you can see that the files are actually symlinks to a different path.

```bash
$ ls -la "$component_root"

drwxr-xr-x 7 $USER wheel 224 Aug 15 11:54 .
drwxr-xr-x 3 $USER wheel  96 Aug 15 11:54 ..
lrwxr-xr-x 1 $USER wheel 192 Aug 15 11:54 asset-manifest.json -> /private/var/t...
lrwxr-xr-x 1 $USER wheel 190 Aug 15 11:54 bootstrap.min.css -> /private/var/tmp...
lrwxr-xr-x 1 $USER wheel 194 Aug 15 11:54 bootstrap.min.css.map -> /private/var...
lrwxr-xr-x 1 $USER wheel 183 Aug 15 11:54 index.html -> /private/var/tmp/_bazel...
drwxr-xr-x 3 $USER wheel  96 Aug 15 11:54 static
```

I think this behavior was overlooked when https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/5046 was merged so I hope this can be fixed. ( cc @user. I'm sorry to ping you if you were unrelated. )

title: Streamlit Crashing with Error: `free(): double free detected in tcache 2`
body:
### Checklist

### Summary

**UPDATE**: I believe the culprit is a bug in the `@st.cache_resource` logic and/or the way streamlit handles db connections that try to persist (had same issues using `session_state`). See my follow-up message below. 

My initial issue:

Unfortunately I have a fairly complicated app. My streamlit application is crashing and I'm not sure why. The error seems somewhat ominous, but there's really not much information that helps me figure out what's going on, which is why I've made this issue. 

I've seen this error on rare occasion when building my complex application. Normally, this happens after I update the file and hit 'rerun', so I just chalk it up to: something happens when I hot-reload a new version of the file that breaks things. Nothing I'm concerned about since I don't expect to do this in production.

However, after adding a normal [selectbox](https://docs.streamlit.io/library/api-reference/widgets/st.selectbox), streamlit intermittently crashes when I use [this](https://github.com/hoggatt/st-combobox) simple custom component that gives me the ability to define my own auto complete function. I don't actually think it's related to the combobox itself, it's just that when the combobox is auto-completing, it's rerunning a lot. This was working before I added a normal `st.textbox`, but now it's completely broken. However, the fact that I saw it very infrequently before indicates to me it's probably not directly related to the selectbox. 

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
# THIS IS PSEUDO-CODE #

search_input = st.text_input()

...
many conditional statements doing something with the search input including setting st.experimental_set_query_params at one point
also queries the database using a cached_resource mysql connector (see below)
...

value = st.selectbox(items based on search_input)

# allow selecting something using a combobox (st-combobox) with autocomplete
def search_files(searchterm):
  refine search based (in part) on value
selected_value = st_combobox(search_files, ...)

# this method is cached
file = get_file(selected_value)

...
setting up controls for the plot based on the file loaded
uses st.experimental_set_query_params at some point
no database or complex cached stuff
...

# make plotly plot(s) here
```

### Steps To Reproduce

Unfortunately I'm not able to figure out exactly why this happens. It doesn't seem to happen consistently. 

However, often I see this error nearby: `2013 (HY000): Lost connection to MySQL server during query`. 

I have a method that looks like this:
```
@st.cache_resource
def loaddb():
    creds = ...
    dbconn = SQL("EXAMPLE", "example.com", creds["username"], creds["password"], True)
    return dbconn
```

### Expected Behavior

I expect this crash not to happen. 

### Current Behavior

This is all that happens. Streamlit prints out two lines in the console, then hard-crashes:
```
free(): double free detected in tcache 2
Aborted
```

Sometimes I see this error too (maybe it's related to the cache_resource having issues?):
```
2013 (HY000): Lost connection to MySQL server during query
```
This error doesn't seem to crash outright, but something tells me it's related. 

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.26.0
- Python version: 3.11
- Operating System: Ubuntu 20.04
- Browser: Brave Version 1.57.62, Chromium: 116.0.5845.180 (Official Build) (64-bit)

### Additional Information

I'm going to be trying to nail down exactly why this issue is happening over the next few days (try to figure out how to reproduce it) but I wanted to make the issue now since it seems like a very strange error someone on the team might have insight into.

comments.text:
With some further digging, I've found out two very useful pieces of information:

1. If I type slowly into the combobox (so the app reloads less frequently), it does not crash nearly as often. 
2. If I remove the `@st.cache_resource` decorator from the `loaddb()` method described above, the app seems to work without any issues no matter how quickly/often it reloads (although the db connection is no longer cached). For those of you looking for a more satisfactory solution than "don't use cache", unfortunately the [st.session_state](https://docs.streamlit.io/library/api-reference/session-state) api causes the same issues.

### My non-expert opinion

This `free(): double free detected in tcache 2` error is being generated in c++ or c code (possibly cpython stuff). My guess is that something in the `cache_resource` logic doesn't like very rapidly reloading the app (especially when the app has more complexity). My initial research indicates some variable is being freed in memory, then some other variable is being assigned to it. However, this only seems to happen in situations with more complex applications and frequent reloads. Since the `cache_resource` function is newer, my guess is there is some bug that shows up under these conditions with multiple threads/restarts. I hope this helps someone figure out what is going on.

I ran into the same error/behavior when trying to use `session_state` to store the database connection. This is strange and points to something a big deeper than just the cache_resource logic. Looks like restarting quickly in general + database connections that try to persist in any way cause issues.

I agree with your guess that it is coming from some C/C++ code, probably triggered by many reruns starting in separate threads at the same time and accessing the same database connection instance. Unfortunately this will be difficult to debug, and it isn't clear what we could do about it.
Closing this issue due to inactivity and it appears that it might not be directly related to Streamlit.

title: _MultiPathWatcher unnecessarily watches parent folder of given path
body:
### Checklist

### Summary

When starting streamlit in a standard way, it unexpectedly printed `OSError: [Errno 24] inotify instance limit reached` message, even though high number of files were not around.

`_MultiPathWatcher` in `streamlit/watcher/event_based_path_watcher.py` watches parent directories of a given path, thereby possibly including unrelated directories with files of no interest.

I believe watching for the requested directory is enough, without watching for it's parent.

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
At Streamlit startup streamlit starts watching for the important files and folders.

1. _register_necessary_watchers() in streamlit/watcher/local_sources_watcher.py calls into
2. EventBasedPathWatcher() in streamlit/watcher/event_based_path_watcher.py, which calls into
3. _MultiPathWatcher::watch_path()
4. Here, the following line steps up in the hierarchy, possibly including lot of unrelated files and folders:
folder_path = os.path.abspath(os.path.dirname(path))
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Have a directory structure like this:
- main
- --code
- --data
2. Place your minimal streamlit project into `code`, or include something from `code`, so `LocalSourcesWatcher` will watch it
3. Place a dataset with 10000s of files into `data`
4. Start streamlit
5. Observe that you are out of inotify watches

### Expected Behavior

Only `code` folder is watched for changes, which has only 10-100 code files.

### Current Behavior

The parent of `code`: the `main` folder is watched for changes. With this, `data` folder is also watched, and as it contains 10000s of files, inotify is over the limits, and even `code` will not watched in reality.

Increasing the inotify limit or choosing poll policy are workarounds, but that is not the proper solution.

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.27
- Python version: 3.9
- Operating System: Ubuntu
- Browser: Firefox (not related)

### Additional Information

title: Add --config-file arg to `streamlit run` for manual specification of config.toml location
body:
### Checklist

### Summary

The `.streamlit/config.toml` file currently only works if the file exists at specified locations ([docs](https://docs.streamlit.io/library/advanced-features/configuration)). `streamlit run` should have an arg where I can pass the full path of any config file, and it will run the streamlit app with those configuration options.

### Why?

Sometimes I have multiple streamlit projects defined in a single repo, but I want to be able to run them from the root of my repo, such as `streamlit run project/sub-project/app.py`, and have a config file defined at `project/sub-project/.streamlit/config.toml`. 

### How?

Add an arg to streamlit run:
`streamlit run /project/app.py --config-file /path/to/config.toml`

### Additional Context

title: SnowflakeConnection.query() retries on errors that will never succeed
body:
### Checklist

### Summary

`SnowflakeConnection.query()` method is intended to refresh the connection and retry for errors that might be transient, such as due to a stale connection.

However the current behavior is to retry on any kind of `snowflake.connector.Error` including things like SQL syntax errors that will clearly never succeed

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
# conn_bug.py
import streamlit as st

conn = st.connection("snowflake")
# SQL syntax error that will never succeed
df = conn.query("SELECT sdgdsgdfds as HIGH_FIVES", ttl=0)
st.dataframe(df)
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. `streamlit run conn_bug.py`
2. Observe the app retrying the exception (multiple spinners and multiple stack traces printed

### Expected Behavior

The app will attempt the above query once and then return an error

```
snowflake.connector.errors.ProgrammingError: 000904 (42000): SQL compilation error: error line 1 at position 7
invalid identifier 'SDGDSGDFDS'
```

### Current Behavior

The app attempts the above query 3 times, showing the spinner 3 times and printing the exception stack trace 3 times

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.28
- Python version: 3.11
- Operating System: MacOS
- Browser: Chrome

title: Allow user using setup script to interact with streamlit app out of Script runner

### Checklist

### Summary

We need an entry to do something outside script runner.

### Why?

Users sometimes want to do some operations at the app level. For example, add a custom handler, run some background tasks (without being triggered by the visited page), and initialize some very slow data.

Some of these tasks are not supported at all, and some have a bad user experience. 

### How?

If streamlit can provide a fixed script  entry `setup.py` similar to the pages folder, or pass it in through command line parameters, streamlit can execute it during the startup process, which can provide users with a more flexible experience.

### Additional Context

I create a lib [streamlitgo](https://github.com/PaleNeutron/streamlitgo) to do this. It access a setup script before run streamlit server thus user can do anything more than hooks.
This is really interesting @user !! Thank you!

## Update

Exciting news 🎉 Starting with **Streamlit 1.53**, we've added experimental lifespan hooks via the new ASGI/Starlette integration.

You can now run initialization code outside the script runner, before any Streamlit script executes:

```python
from contextlib import asynccontextmanager
from streamlit.starlette import App

@user
async def lifespan(app):
    # Setup: runs ONCE at server start, outside script runner
    print("🚀 Running setup...")

    import os
    os.environ["MY_CONFIG"] = "production"

    # Initialize shared resources
    from myapp import setup_logging, init_services
    setup_logging()
    init_services()

    yield

    # Teardown
    print("👋 Cleanup...")

app = App("main.py", lifespan=lifespan)
```

This runs at server startup, completely independent of the Streamlit script runner.

We'd love your feedback on this feature! Please try it out and report any issues in our [feedback thread](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/13600).

> **Note:** Requires `pip install streamlit[starlette]`

title: On session start/shutdown hooks
body:
### Checklist

### Summary

For global resources, it would be nice if there were hooks that were:
- Called once on start up
- Called once at shut down

### Why?

Configuring global resources can be triggered in this manner.

For example, you can have a back end connection that outlasts any Streamlit front end session.

### How?

Two ideas are adding this capability to either `session_state` or `st.set_page_config`

### Additional Context

Coming from https://discuss.streamlit.io/t/on-session-shutdown-hook/54953

Thanks @user! This has been on my mind too. Do you have a specific example for global resources in an app you would use this for?

In terms of how - I think you'd ideally want to configure it outside of any particular page. Maybe with something like https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/7667

Nice! My use case right now is Socket.IO clients.

To share my workarounds:

- Start up: code at the module-level of a module being imported into the main script
    - Code imported from other modules only gets run once
- Shut down: registering a shutdown handler with [`atexit.register`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/atexit.html#atexit.register)

Can I also request onPageStart, onPageComplete and onPageRerun hooks for advanced users? @user as for implementation, I was thinking about this the other day. A few ideas:

1. Something like pytest's `conftest.py` where you define specifically-named hook functions that are called (if they exist) by streamlit.
2. A [hooks] section in `config.toml`, where each hook is given as the string value of the import path to a function (e.g. `mypackage.mymodule.onSessionStart` and the function is loaded dynamically.

```python
with setup_sockets():
   streamlit.web.cli.main_run(target="Main.py", prog_name="streamlit")
```

Also, you gotta be careful while developing with that module-level code when developing -- Streamlit's "reload changed modules" mechanic can play all kinds of havoc with that. (Source: I have been burned more times than I care to admit)

Nice - we're working on a mechanism right now that allows you to run common code before (and probably after) every page run in a multi-page app. I looked at some "hook" designs but I think it will be a bit simpler and easier to use for the first pass. More on this soon.

The start and end of session thing will take a bit longer - I'd still like to support it but figuring out the best way. I guess "end of session" is really more important since you can do a lot with initializing session_state keys for "start of session" type stuff? Thanks for these great ideas!

Just chiming in to add I'm looking for a shutdown hook right now and it would help a lot. I have a simple chat-bot application that I'd like to persist the chat logs when the session ends cleanly and a shutdown hook would be ideal for that.
I create a lib [streamlitgo](https://github.com/PaleNeutron/streamlitgo) to do this. It access a setup script before run streamlit server thus user can do anything more than hooks.

I would also like this feature. I'm looking to persist some state (from edits in the `data_editor`). Persisting these changes eagerly seems very tricky given the limitations of how changes are tracked in the `session_state`. So my current desired approach is to persist once before the session terminates.
While it doesn't allow session-based start/shutdown hooks, you can now run code on server startup/shutdown. You can find more information [here](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/13600).

title: Enable https to access external IP
body:
### Checklist

### Summary

We try to deploy a streamlit app on a windows server that only allows external connections via https. 

When accessing the deployed app, it does not completely load and in the console we repeatedly see the following warning
```
2023-11-10 18:15:16.923 Did not auto detect external IP.
Please go to https://docs.streamlit.io/ for debugging hints.
```

We identified the root of this warning within this library module: [https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/blob/018f49f5ddb0fa0119c17aaf2bff1bc7f25f70e1/lib/streamlit/net_util.py#L32](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/blob/018f49f5ddb0fa0119c17aaf2bff1bc7f25f70e1/lib/streamlit/net_util.py#L32)

Apparently the hardcoded url
```python
_AWS_CHECK_IP = "http://checkip.amazonaws.com"
```
is called to retrieve the external IP of the server.
Since we can only access urls via https, the streamlit app does not continue loading.

Since "https://checkip.amazonaws.com" (using https) works as well, it would be great if a fallback would be implemented to try getting the ip via https when the http response is None.

Thanks and best regards
Lars

title: net_util.get_external_ip from AWS causes disabling CORS
body:
### Checklist

### Summary

We are running streamlit in openshift (not AWS). The app started perfekt and everything worked fine, till we wanted to enable a "beautiful URL" on a nginx in front. 
As we did this the first call on the streamlit app caused the following messages to appear:

_**Starting new HTTP connection (1): checkip.amazonaws.com:80
Did not auto detect external IP.**_

After this the app crashed and the container restarted as the health check detected the app is offline.

First I searched the internet and found some articles relating the problem, but the solutions are not realy understandable (why they work).

I then diged into the source code and found that the method net_util.get_external_ip is causing the problem.

This method appears in two places:

1) bootstrap.py (at server startup)
2) server_util.py (at cors check)

As the server starts correctly and the problem only appears when we call the app from another origin, the problem must be in server_util.py

The implementation here shows that the method is called at the last line of the allowed_domains list

allowed_domains = [  # List[Union[str, Callable[[], Optional[str]]]]
        # Check localhost first.
        "localhost",
        "0.0.0.0",
        "127.0.0.1",
        # Try to avoid making unnecessary HTTP requests by checking if the user
        # manually specified a server address.
        _get_server_address_if_manually_set,
        # Then try the options that depend on HTTP requests or opening sockets.
        net_util.get_internal_ip,
        **net_util.get_external_ip**, 
    ]

The only chance of running streamlit in openshift now is to turn off the CORS check otherwise the app allways crashes. As we turned CORS off, everything works fine. I don't think you intent everyone running not on AWS to turn off CORS.

Next I looked at the implementation of get_external_ip. And there is one thing I really don't understand. Why is there a hardcoded AWS IP in the framework. This is really very bad coding (sorry), as this means streamlit is designed only to run in AWS, what I don't beleave.

Here my suggestion for improvement:

There should be two variables for the config file to make everything clear and clean:

EXTERNAL_IP_PROVIDER -> (ENVIRONMENT_VARIABLE, AWS, GOOGLE, OPENSHIFT, AZURE ...)
EXTERNAL_IP_PROVIDER_VALUE -> 

- ENVIRONMENT_VARIABLE -> name of the environment Varialbe containing the IP
- AWS -> URL of the Endpoint, if not set current default value
- GOOGLE, OPENSHIFT,.... if needed you could here implement platform based endpoint calls, as different platforms can have different formats.

In my case I would just set a ENVIRONMENT_VARIABLE with IP, as this is possible on openshift. I have seen openshift also has a service for providing this stuff, but I don't know this, so a ENVIRONMENT_VARIABLE would be best for me and I also think this would be a very open solution for everyone.

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
This is the codeblock with the root cause of the problem:

def get_external_ip() -> Optional[str]:
    """Get the *external* IP address of the current machine.

    Returns
    -------
    string
        The external IPv4 address of the current machine.

    """
    global _external_ip

    if _external_ip is not None:
        return _external_ip

    response = _make_blocking_http_get(_AWS_CHECK_IP, timeout=5)

    if _looks_like_an_ip_adress(response):
        _external_ip = response
    else:
        LOGGER.warning(
            # fmt: off
            "Did not auto detect external IP.\n"
            "Please go to %s for debugging hints.",
            # fmt: on
            util.HELP_DOC
        )
        _external_ip = None

    return _external_ip

I will not provide any sample code here, as you can use any streamlit app, just run it in a non AWS environment and call it over a proxy router.
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Take any streamlit app with CORS enabled
2. run it on any container platform not AWS (openshift, Azure, google,....)
3. call it over a proxy in front to get into the CORS check

### Expected Behavior

1. The app should not crash!!
2. There should be two error messages which :

a) unable to connect to external IP Provider xy
b) "CORS Error, Unable to reach External IP Provider {xy}, URL {url}, Please set the external IP Correctly to make CORS check work, or disable CORS Check"

### Current Behavior

The app crashed with a not usefull message:

_**Starting new HTTP connection (1): checkip.amazonaws.com:80
Did not auto detect external IP.**_

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.12.0
- Python version: 3.9.12
- Operating System: RHEL Linux
- Browser: Chrome

### Additional Information

comments.text:
Hey @user!
Thank you for opening this issue. 

Most probably the app crushes not because of `get_external_ip` returning None, but because of misconfigured CORS origins (`get_external_ip` is just a part of it).

If you server your streamlit app behind the reverse proxy, you need to explicitly specify 
```toml
[browser]
serverAddress = "app.domain.name"
```
config option either via config file, environment variable, or CLI argument: https://docs.streamlit.io/library/advanced-features/configuration

You can also take a look at the tutorial here, which helps configure NGINX as a reverse proxy for streamlit app: https://medium.com/featurepreneur/streamlit-with-nginx-bde7a9a41e6c

Related to a hardcoded AWS IP in the framework, it is not intended to restrict deploying Streamlit apps on other 
Cloud providers ( `checkip.amazonaws.com` is a public service, and could be reached from anywhere if it is not restricted by network rules on your or your cloud provider side).

This is also not intended to work as the source of obtaining a real origin, if your app is not accessible with an external IP address.
 
I am going to close this issue, please reopen it and add a comment if you will have further questions. 

Thank you!

title: Config option for hiding traceback in uncaught st.exception
body:
### Checklist

### Summary

As a developer, I am concerned about the Streamlit framework displaying Python interpreter stack trace to the end user in case of the uncaught exception, as it can lead to potential security issues in closed-source self-hosted applications. I want to introduce a config option that prevents displaying a traceback on the client.

### Why?

Displaying an exception stack trace to the end user in a Streamlit application can introduce some severe security issues:
 1. **Information Disclosure:** The stack trace can reveal sensitive information about the application's internal structure, such as file paths, library versions, and database schemas;
 2. **Error Handling Exposure:** This can lead to various exploitations, like causing the application to crash or behave unpredictably;
 3. **Attack Vector Identification:** Detailed error messages can help attackers in identifying the parts of the code that are vulnerable to specific types of attacks, such as SQL injection, cross-site scripting (XSS), or remote code execution.

These security issues pose a potential threat to the production Streamlit applications.

### How?

I want to introduce a new boolean option `client.showErrorTraceback` to the Streamilt config, which if set to `false`, the application will not send traceback information to the client. Here is an example:

```toml
[client]

# Default: true
showErrorTraceback = false
```

Code:

```python
raise ValueError("This is an error")
```

title: Allow different paths for storing configuration files
body:
### Checklist

### Summary

I am currently deploying my Streamlit app on Google Cloud using Cloud Run but running into issues with `secrets.toml` and `config.toml` files under the `.streamlit` directory.

Since the `secrets.toml` file should be kept a secret, I have deployed my secret to Google Cloud Secret Manager and when I deploy the service, I mount it as a volume: `--set-secrets=/app/.streamlit/secrets.toml=streamlit-secret:latest`.

When I view the deployment in a web browser, the theme from the `config.toml` is not rendering.

When I view the logs of my Cloud Run instance, I see the following warning:
```
textPayload: "Could not open file at path /secret_volume_0/config.toml. The path is in a mounted secrets volume, but the exact path does not correspond to any secret specified in the mount configuration."
```

So it seems like I cannot use a `secrets.toml` and `config.toml` file together in the same directory if I am mounting `secrets.toml` as a volume mount path.

I tried to create a new secret and mount `config.toml` but [Cloud Run does not allow you to mount multiple secrets at the same path because two volume mounts cannot be mounted at the same location](https://cloud.google.com/run/docs/configuring/services/secrets#disallowed_paths_and_limitations).

I have tried to change the path from `/app/.streamlit/config.toml` to `/app/secret_volume_0/config.toml` but that didn't seem to do anything.

### Why?

I feel stuck that there is a limitation between both Cloud Run and Streamlit due the architecture of both projects.

### How?

Maybe allow Streamlit to read configuration files from either `pyproject.toml` or allow a specific configuration directory?

title: Using st.connection with creator function in create_engine_kwargs results in UnhashableParamError
body:
### Checklist

### Summary

When using `st.connection` with `creator` function in `create_engine_kwargs` ,  the error occurs in `cache_resources`.

```
    raise UnhashableTypeError() from ex
streamlit.runtime.caching.cache_errors.UnhashableParamError: Cannot hash argument 'creator' (of type `builtins.function`) in '__create_connection'.

To address this, you can tell Streamlit not to hash this argument by adding a
leading underscore to the argument's name in the function signature:

@st.cache_resource
def __create_connection(_creator, ...):
    ...

```

However, `creator` is an argument used in [sqlalchemy](https://github.com/sqlalchemy/sqlalchemy/blob/e7c0ed0d702948ba9cf9d45f00ef0700e71e16e7/lib/sqlalchemy/engine/create.py#L639C9-L639C16), so we cannot change it.

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
import os
import streamlit as st
from google.cloud.sql.connector import Connector, IPTypes
import pymysql

DB_INSTANCE_CONNECTION_NAME = os.getenv("DB_INSTANCE_CONNECTION_NAME") # Cloud SQL instance name e.g. 'project:region:instance'
ip_type = IPTypes.PRIVATE if os.environ.get("PRIVATE_IP") else IPTypes.PUBLIC
connector = Connector(ip_type)

def getconn() -> pymysql.connections.Connection:
    conn: pymysql.connections.Connection = connector.connect(
        instance_connection_string=DB_INSTANCE_CONNECTION_NAME,
        driver="pymysql",
        user=os.getenv("DB_USER"),  # e.g. 'my-db-user'
        db=os.getenv("DB_NAME"),  # e.g. 'my-database'
    )
    return conn
st.connection(
    os.getenv("DB_NAME"),
    type="sql",
    url = "mysql+pymysql://",
    creator=getconn,
)
```

### Steps To Reproduce

run the above script `app.py`

```
python app.py
```

### Expected Behavior

able to cache or disable cache as an option

### Current Behavior

```
    raise UnhashableTypeError() from ex
streamlit.runtime.caching.cache_errors.UnhashableParamError: Cannot hash argument 'creator' (of type `builtins.function`) in '__create_connection'.

To address this, you can tell Streamlit not to hash this argument by adding a
leading underscore to the argument's name in the function signature:

@st.cache_resource
def __create_connection(_creator, ...):
    ...

```

Hi @user can you say a little more about why you need to set the `creator` arg when using st.connection? From your repro it's not really clear why it's needed vs just using the default creation method provided by SQLAlchemy.

I'm wondering if it's something we need to support via st.connection (which is not necessarily intended for super complex scenarios). If it's required, you might just want to create your own connection object management.

Hi, @user

As I attached the example above, I'd like to specify creator like https://pypi.org/project/cloud-sql-python-connector/.

@st.cache_resource

    ...
```

One possible solution is to skip the cache for variable with `_` prefix and then remove the prefix `_` from the argument in `create_engine_kwargs`.

The problem was solved when I downgraded the streamlit package to the previous version as follows. For now, I'll use the old version until I find the clear answer.

I added the requirements.txt file as follows.

streamlit==1.25.0

Hey. We are closing the issue as expected. The deprecations are valid and @user is right, we do not implicitly create a `config.toml` file. 

It looks like the config file is located here: C:\Users\<user>\config.toml. Not sure what's in this file, but Streamlit will pull from a .streamlit/config.toml in the user directory.

title: `st.multiselect` returns empty on dynamically changing options.
body:
### Checklist

### Summary

Streamlit multi_select element `st.multi_select` not working as expected inside streamlit form `st.form`. After selecting multiple options through the multi select element, on form submission, the multiselect widget giving empty value `[]`. 

### Reproducible Code Example

[[image]](https://issues.streamlitapp.com/?issue=gh-7855)

```Python
import streamlit as st

with st.form(key="async_testing_config"):
        # Components : Select async api endpoints for testing.
        components = st.multiselect(
            "Select async api endpoints",
           external_call_to_aws_api_to_get_list_of_endpoints(),
            key="components"
        )

        # Submitted - BOOLEAN
        Submitted = st.form_submit_button("Submit")
        if Submitted:
            print("project id: ", project_id)
            print("endpoints: ",components)
```

### Steps To Reproduce

### Expected Behavior

After submitting the form, user should be able to get all options selected through multi select widget. 

### Current Behavior

User getting empty value after submitting. Note: the options passed to the multiselect widget is an external api call to aws api to list of endpoints (options). I tried with streamlit version 1.28.2 and also latest version 1.29.0 as well, facing the same issue.

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.28.2
- Python version: 3.9
- Operating System: Mac
- Browser: Chrome

### Additional Information

comments.text: @user Thanks for reporting this issue. Unfortunately, I couldn't reproduce this issue [here](https://issues.streamlit.app/?issue=gh-7855) by using static options. Is the `external_call_to_aws_api_to_get_list_of_endpoints` always returning the same set of options?

@user Thanks for the response. the `external_call_to_aws_api_to_get_list_of_endpoints` won't return same set of options all the time. the list of options it returns changes dynamically. 

on contrary, `st.selectbox` is working fine even though it receive options same as in above manner, dynamically from aws api.

Ok, interesting. Updated the example [here](https://issues.streamlit.app/?issue=gh-7855) to reflect dynamically updating options. And indeed, `multi_select` doesn't seem to work when the options update dynamically.
Hey @user, any idea when this enhancement will be fixed?
@user nope, sorry :( I don't have any ETA on this.
Any updates on this? This is causing problems with our apps inside Snowflake - Streamlit as well.
@user  You have mentioned this used to work in previous version, can you specify which version it was working fine? Thanks
I'm facing this problem too. Thanks for the report.

> @user You have mentioned this used to work in previous version, can you specify which version it was working fine? Thanks

@user I am using versions 1.28.2 and 1.29.0 only, I don't think it is working on any of the streamlit versions. 
A workaround solution i tried to tackle this bug is , by using `st.session_state` for storing options: 

code:
```
def func():
    if "options" not in st.session_state:
                st.session_state["options"] = aws_api_call_to_fetch_options()
    
     with st.form(key="test"):
        components = st.multiselect(
            "Select options",
            st.session_state.options,
            key="components",
        )

        Submitted = st.form_submit_button("Submit")

        if Submitted:
            ....
            ....
            # To fetch latest options, removing "options" from st.session_state
            if "options" in st.session_state: 
                del st.session_state.options
```
Thanks @user I ended up implementing `session_state` based solution and ditched `st.form` altogether.

This doesn't seem like a bug to me. A widget will lose its state if its definition is changed (whether it's in a form or not). I think it's expected that you'd need to do something with Session State if you have dynamically changing options. Should this issue be closed?

@user I think it's fine to keep it open since it is not anymore marked as a `bug`. We have some plans to eventually allow dynamically changing parameters if a `key` is provided. So, it's a valid feature request that might get implemented at some point.
This is another instance of #11277. Please upvote that issue if you want to see this fixed!

title: Apply logger config to all logger instances
body:
### Checklist

### Summary

Starting from version 1.22.0 of Streamlit and above, the options in the config.toml file under the [logger] section no longer function. I am currently in the process of upgrading from Streamlit version 1.10.0 to the latest 1.29.0 and have observed that logs cease to display while the application is running. 
The logging level is set to 'Info' in the file, but logs are only appearing from the 'Warning' level and above. Additionally, the formatting doesn't match the configuration file.

config.toml
[logger]
level = "info"
messageFormat = "%(asctime)s - %(levelname)s %(filename)s:%(lineno)-4d - %(message)s"

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
import streamlit as st
import logging

log = logging.getLogger("my_tool_logger")

st.write("Some text of page")

log.info("Page loaded")
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Install streamlit version 1.29.0
2. Insert the following line into the [logger] section of the config.toml file: level = "info"
3. Execute the code example I have provided."

### Expected Behavior

Logs are displayed in the standard output.
https://img.serpstat.com/kaisa/2023-12-19_ZFDITjqD.png

### Current Behavior

When the logging level is set to 'info,' logs do not appear in the standard output. The message format does not conform to the configuration specified in the 'config.toml' file.

### Is this a regression?

- [X] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.29.0
- Python version: 3.8
- Operating System: Ubuntu 22.04
- Browser: Chrome

### Additional Information

I tested this on every version from 1.29.0 to 1.21.0, and it appears that it broke starting from version 1.22.0. It worked fine in version 1.21.0.

comments.text:
@user Thanks for reporting this issue! I was able to reproduce this, but I think the logger settings are mostly for the Streamlit internal logging. And this is working as expected. If you like to apply the same settings to your logger instance, you can initialize it like this:

```python
import logging

import streamlit as st
from streamlit.logger import get_logger

log = get_logger("my_tool_logger")

st.write("Some text of page")
```

But this is more like an internal API, so it might be changed in future versions. I'm also adding @user to this thread since he made some changes to the logger recently.

@user Thank you for the suggestion, but I find it a bit unclear. The documentation for config.toml and the logger section doesn't provide any clues about this issue. It seems like a bug. I came across this discussion: [link to the GitHub issue](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/6377#issuecomment-1550158588).
Yep, I agree that we should clarify this a bit more in our docs. Maybe it's also an unexpected behavior, @user might be able to say more on this.

Hey @user, thank you for opening this issue!

You are right, the one implication that we have changed our root logger to a "streamlit" logger, is that just getting the logger via `logging.getLogger` does not apply configs `from config.toml` per se. 

So my [comment here](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/6377#issuecomment-1550158588) is partially wrong. 

The idea of that PR was to give streamlit app developers more freedom to configure their app logs, and not bound them with streamlit internal logger. 

In order to keep the old behavior, you can either import `get_logger` from stremalit logger (as @user mentioned)
```python
import logging

import streamlit as st
from streamlit.logger import get_logger

log = get_logger("my_tool_logger")

st.write("Some text of page")
```

or use "streamlit" logger explicitly
```python
import streamlit as st
import logging

log = logging.getLogger("streamlit")

st.write("Some text of page")

log.info("Page loaded")
```
this should also work. 

I agree that it is not clear from the documentation, so we should change docs to highlight the fact that logger configuration applies to streamlit logger.
@user or @user, can one of you update the docstring to make this more clear and close this issue?
Any updates on this ?

@user I have a PR to update the description, but this issue is currently labeled as an enhancement request to change the behavior. Do you want this closed with the clarification "this setting is for Streamlit's internal logger" and "won't do" for the enhancement request? Or, do you want to keep this open as an enhancement request?
Yeah I think we can close this issue once the docs changes are merged. I don't think we'll revert that back to the old setting again.

title: Allow custom location for secrets.toml
body:
### Checklist

### Summary

Currently, `secrets.toml` file will be read from `~/.streamlit/secrets.toml` or `$CWD/.streamlit/secrets.toml` [according to the docs](https://docs.streamlit.io/library/advanced-features/secrets-management). It would be useful to be able to specify a custom location to search for `secrets.toml` files

### Why?

I have a hashicorp vault sidecar in my kubernetes pod containing my streamlit application. This sidecar gets the DB creds from vault and then writes them out to a file in a specific directory shared between the sidecar and the streamlit container. In order to get this file to streamlit's attention, I have to copy / symlink it over to streamlit's expected locations, and also do so each time the file is updated due to cred rotation. 

### How?

Add a new command to streamlit like `--secrets-path=/path/to/secrets.toml` which would allow a custom file location, or an environment variable like `SECRETS_PATH=/path/to/secrets.toml` which would do the same.

The currently allowed locations are stored 
These locations are hardcoded [here](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/blob/7ef2aa66dabc740fef8f5c7a072ea8dcece8f73c/lib/streamlit/runtime/secrets.py#L41).

title: session_state stats are not tracked correctly on metrics endpoint
body:
### Checklist

### Summary

Streamlit provides a metrics endpoint that exposes information about memory usage by cache and session_state at `/_stcore/metrics`. Based on the inspection of the contents and the response type header, this is intended to follow the [OpenMetrics standard](https://github.com/OpenObservability/OpenMetrics/blob/main/specification/OpenMetrics.md).

However for the session_state metric, I obseved that when multiple sessions are active the endpoint prints multiple lines, one for each session, with the same labels. E.g.

```sh
% curl localhost:8501/_stcore/metrics
# TYPE cache_memory_bytes gauge
# UNIT cache_memory_bytes bytes
# HELP Total memory consumed by a cache.
cache_memory_bytes{cache_type="st_session_state",cache=""} 4848
cache_memory_bytes{cache_type="st_session_state",cache=""} 4248
cache_memory_bytes{cache_type="st_session_state",cache=""} 4248
```

This breaks the OpenMetric standard which states that a metric name + set of label values must be unique and appear only once in a response.

### Reproducible Code Example

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Run any streamlit app
2. Open multiple sessions, such as by navigating to the app on two tabs
3. Call `curl localhost:8501/_stcore/metrics` (or whatever the host/port is)
4. Observe multiple session state lines with identical labels

### Expected Behavior

Each line in the result will be unique.

### Current Behavior

Multiple lines with the same name and labels.

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.29
- Python version: 3.11
- Operating System: MacOS
- Browser: Chrome

### Additional Information

I believe the [function that needs to be fixed is here](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/blob/1.29.0/lib/streamlit/runtime/state/session_state.py#L671-L676)

Suggested fix would be to either:
* Sum the memory usage of all sessions and record it in one line, OR
* Add a session_id label to each line so they labels are distinct

For a quick fix, I would suggest the first option.

title: Using `switch_page` forces the page to finish running before rendering
body:
### Checklist

### Summary

When switching pages via a button and `switch_page`, instead of the following page being loaded as expected, the screen freezes until the code of the page finishes executing. This does not occur if I use the sidebar to load the other page.

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
# in main.py
import streamlit as st

if st.button("Go to page1"):
    st.switch_page("pages/page1.py")

# in pages/page1.py
import time

import streamlit as st

progress_text = "Operation in progress. Please wait."
my_bar = st.progress(0, text=progress_text)

for percent_complete in range(100):
    time.sleep(0.1)
    my_bar.progress(percent_complete + 1, text=progress_text)
time.sleep(1)
st.text("Operation done")
```

selection = alt.selection_multi(fields=['name'])
color = alt.condition(selection, alt.Color('name:N'), alt.value('lightgray'))

title: --global.disableWatchdogWarning deprecated with no other way to suppress watchdog warning
body:
### Checklist

### Summary

Run any streamlit application without a file watcher. 

```bash
python -m streamlit run app.py --server.fileWatcherType none
```

This command emits a message about watchdog:

```
  For better performance, install the Watchdog module:

  $ xcode-select --install
  $ pip install watchdog
```

Prior to Streamlit v1.29.0, the `--global.disableWatchdogWarning` command-line option could suppress this message. Now, using that option prevents the application from running.

```bash
python -m streamlit run app.py --server.fileWatcherType none --global.disableWatchdogWarning True
```

The error output (without the stack trace):

```
streamlit.errors.DeprecationError:
════════════════════════════════════════════════
global.disableWatchdogWarning IS NO LONGER SUPPORTED.

global.disableWatchdogWarning has been deprecated and will be removed in a future version.

Please update command-line argument or environment variable.
════════════════════════════════════════════════
```

Two observations:

First, watchdog should no be probed unless it is needed. In this example, we are trying to suppress file watching entirely, which should avoid all use of watchdog.

Second, the warning notes that support will be removed, but the fact that this use is an error is effectively the same as removing support.

It does not appear as if there is any way to suppress the watchdog message.

### Reproducible Code Example

### Steps To Reproduce

See commands given in the summary. Run a Streamlit app with `--server.fileWatcherType none` and note the message about watchdog.

### Expected Behavior

No message about watchdog when file watching is not active.

### Current Behavior

A message about watchdog even when the file watcher is disabled. The previous configuration option was "deprecated" but its use produces an error.

### Is this a regression?

- [X] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.29.0

### Additional Information

This is similar to https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/7818 and caused by the changes in https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/7584

The deprecated configuration is still present in code:

https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/blob/829933e3c9ec9065ad7533d69948cf18f4bfcf4a/lib/streamlit/watcher/path_watcher.py#L69-L84

comments.text: @user Thanks for reporting this issue! I believe we should just disable the warning if `--server.fileWatcherType none`

@user - We do not have a case for `global.disableWatchdogWarning`. We disable the warning because we are running applications in situations where their backing files will not change -- removing the need for file-watching. The warning is unnecessary in that context.

We are updating our integration to remove the `--global.disableWatchdogWarning True` argument, as that fixes folks using Streamlit 1.29.0 and 1.30.0.

I don't have the full history of Streamlit + watchdog, but it looks like watchdog is a strong dependency, meaning it will always be installed/available on Linux. It's possible that we saw the warning on macOS and incorrectly assumed that we should suppress it on Linux, or maybe the warning was emitted at some point in the past on Linux.

Are there versions of Streamlit where watchdog was not a strong dependency?

At any rate - I think that we're set on our end.
Is there any ETA on the PR here ?

> And we're also working on a fix to just show a warning in the logs if a deprecated config option is set, and not throw an exception.

It definitely feels like this change is needed (warn rather than error). We have a number of folks using Streamlit who have encountered this problem. Even after we release an update which removes `global.disableWatchdogWarning` as a command-line option, it will take some time for users to upgrade to that fixed version.

Is this change to the treatment of deprecated options still in-flight?

This watchdog message will be disabled when `none` or `poll` watcher type are selected in Streamlit >= `1.31` (will be released next week).

> Is this change to the treatment of deprecated options still in-flight?

Yep, `1.31` will change the expiration behavior to a warning instead of an exception: https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/7985

Please be sure to update the following to omit disableWatchdogWarning 
`streamlit config show `
fyi - this hard broke production for us.

> @user `1.31` or `1.30`? 

1.30. Updated on Sat but was a dependabot PR iirc.
`1.30` fixes the issue. It will not throw an exception if the deprecated config exist.
tried 1.30, but looks issue still exists.
@user Do you get a warning if you run it with: `--server.fileWatcherType none`?

This exception is still affecting me with version 1.37 of streamlit being deployed on posit connect. None of the recommendations above or in other forums helped. Can you please tell me how to fix this? I dont have a terminal in posit and cannot change the command that is used to run the streamlit app. I can define environment variables or create a config.toml file though.
The Posit Connect 2024.01.0 release adjusted how Connect runs Streamlit content. Starting with that release, Connect no longer provides the `--global.disableWatchdogWarning` command-line option.

title: Incorrect streaming chat responses when using Azure OpenAI client's chat completions
body:
### Checklist

### Summary

When using `write_stream()` with chat completions from the Azure OpenAI client (not the regular one!), the first `ChatChunkCompletion` returns an empty `choices` list because it returns extra Responsible AI information first prior to sending the actual chat completions. When attempting to `write_stream()` this, it ends up pre-filling the chat response with the str of the ChatChunkCompletion

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
import streamlit as st
from openai import AzureOpenAI

client = AzureOpenAI(...) # need an active OpenAI model and Azure subscription to fill out this

# set up using LLM chatgpt Streamlit tutorial, just including the assistant portion below for brevity
 
with st.chat_message("assistant"):
    stream = client.chat.completions.create(model="gpt-4", message=messages, stream=True)
    response = st.write_stream(stream)
    st.session_state.messages.append({"role": "assistant", "content": response})
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Create an Azure OpenAI model deployment for any model that supports chat completions
2. Create a streamed response from Chat Completions method 
3. Try to use `write_stream()` to write the stream 

### Expected Behavior

The response should be written if there is actual content to display in the `ChatCompletionChunk` 

### Current Behavior

[image]

In the above image you can see that the `choices` list is empty which it's usually not for regular OpenAI client calls. 

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.31.0
- Python version: 3.11.4
- Operating System: macOS Sonoma 14.3
- Browser: Safari/Chrome

### Additional Information

While this issue is specific to Azure OpenAI client and should ideally be fixed upstream, I don't think it would hurt if Streamlit  could do a check in its write API (e.g. `if len(chunk.choices > 0)`) to make sure there is actually content to write 

I think it's possible to workaround this as user by just swallowing the first chunk of the stream (e.g. `next(stream)`) before sending to `write_stream()` but I haven't tried yet.

Same as this issue: https://github.com/microsoft/semantic-kernel/issues/3650

See other examples of guarding against this: https://github.com/AbanteAI/mentat/pull/430

STREAMLIT_SERVER_HEADLESS=true streamlit hello

title: SQLAchemy dynamic authentication tokens not working with cached connection/data
body:
### Checklist

### Summary

Hello everybody,

I have been dealing with a annoying bug this week, which I will attempt to describe in detail below.

My data is sourced from Azure Synapse Analytics; therefore, authentication with the database occurs via an authentication token. As [SQLAlchemy suggests](https://docs.sqlalchemy.org/en/20/dialects/mssql.html#connecting-to-databases-with-access-tokens), one method to generate dynamic authentication tokens involves setting up an event listener on the engine that adds the credential token to the dialect’s connect call. Specifically for Synapse/SQL Server, this token is passed as an ODBC connection attribute within a data structure [described by Microsoft](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/sql/connect/odbc/using-azure-active-directory#authenticating-with-an-access-token).

The first time the app runs, it operates without any problems. However, the issue arises when the query changes. I believe this problem is related to the caching mechanism, which invalidates the event listener, at this point the event listener might be set to a different object; – which is not the one coming from cache?

Because when the query changes I start getting the error "sqlalchemy.exc.DBAPIError: (pyodbc.Error) ('HY000', '[HY000] [Microsoft][ODBC Driver 18 for SQL Server]SSPI Provider: No Kerberos credentials available (default cache: FILE:/tmp/krb5cc_1000) (851968) (SQLDriverConnect)') (Background on this error at: https://sqlalche.me/e/20/dbapi)" which seems to be caused by the fact that SQLAlchemy adds the ";Trusted_Connection=Yes" parameters which should have been removed by the event listener, and probably the lack of authentication token at all.

Below is a minimal Streamlit app that demonstrates the issue:

```python
import struct
from datetime import timedelta
import streamlit as st
from azure.identity import DefaultAzureCredential
from dotenv import load_dotenv
from sqlalchemy import create_engine, event
from sqlalchemy.engine import URL

load_dotenv() # Load secrets

# The callback function for the event listener
def provide_token(dialect, conn_rec, cargs, cparams):
    SQL_COPT_SS_ACCESS_TOKEN = 1256  # Connection option for access tokens, as defined in msodbcsql.h
    TOKEN_URL = "https://database.windows.net/.default"  # The token URL for any Azure SQL database
    cargs[0] = cargs[0].replace(
        ";Trusted_Connection=Yes", ""
    )  # remove the "Trusted_Connection" parameter that SQLAlchemy adds
    credentials = DefaultAzureCredential() # It reads app secrets from env
    # Lets build the token and send to the ODBC driver
    raw_token = credentials.get_token(TOKEN_URL).token.encode("utf-16-le")
    token_struct = struct.pack(f"<I{len(raw_token)}s", len(raw_token), raw_token)
    cparams["attrs_before"] = {SQL_COPT_SS_ACCESS_TOKEN: token_struct}

connection_url = URL.create(
        "mssql+pyodbc",
        host="tcp:<resource_name>.sql.azuresynapse.net,1433",
        database="<database>",
        query={
            "driver": "ODBC Driver 18 for SQL Server",
            "LongAsMax": "Yes",
            # "autocommit": "True",
            "MARS_Connection": "Yes", # For chunk reads
        },
    )

conn = st.connection(
    "synapse",
    "sql",
    url=connection_url,
    # autocommit=True,
    connect_args=dict(ignore_no_transaction_on_rollback=True),
)

event.listen(target=conn.engine, identifier="do_connect", fn=provide_token)

df = conn.query("SELECT * FROM schema.database;", ttl=timedelta(days=1))
```

As a workaround, how should I set the event listener so it does not break when the object is depickled from cache? Any other suggestion on how to deal with this?

### Reproducible Code Example

### Steps To Reproduce

### Expected Behavior

### Current Behavior

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.31.0
- Python version: 3.11.7
- Operating System: Linux 6.1.75-0-virt 1-Alpine aarch64 GNU/Linux
- Browser: Chrome

### Additional Information

title: File Caching Results in Authorisation Bypass
body:
### Checklist

### Summary

Hello, 

I have built an application which is deployed on Azure and is accessed by authenticated users (via Azure AD) to download files by doing an API call to my backend with is built using fast api. The api checks if the user is part of the project and authorises the file download only if the user is part of that project.

Once a user has downloaded the file, it caches the file and creates a download link which the user can easily get from the Downloads section in the browser. 

This link "https://www.example.com/media/file-hash.extension" can be shared with users who are authenticated but not part of the project and they can also download the file. 

The file can be downloaded by unauthorised users because it stays in the media. Is there a way to clear out the in memory cache where the file is stored once the file has been downloaded or is there a way we can directly stream the download to the browser without caching?

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
def download_file(url, auth_header):
    local_filename = url.split("/")[-1]
    # NOTE the stream=True parameter below
    with requests.get(url, headers=auth_header, timeout=60, stream=True) as r:
        r.raise_for_status()
        with open(local_filename, "wb") as f:
            for chunk in r.iter_content(chunk_size=8192):
                f.write(chunk)
    return local_filename

file = download_file(f"{BASE_API_URL}/v1/projects/{export_project}/files/{option}", auth_header)
                    with open(file) as f:
                        btn = st.download_button(
                            label=f"Download {option}",
                            data=f,
                            file_name=f"{option}",
                            mime=mimetypes.guess_type(option)[0],
                        )
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1- Create a download button for a file 
2- Download the file using a browser
3- Goto downloads section in the browser 
4- Right click on the downloaded file and copy download link
5- Paste the link in some other browser and download the file

### Expected Behavior

The download link should become invalid after the file has been downloaded or the in memory cache should be cleared

### Current Behavior

The cache is not cleared and the download link can be used to download files.

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.25.0
- Python version: 3.11
- Operating System: linux
- Browser: Edge

### Additional Information
