Hey @user, thank you for opening this issue!
We store content for the `download_button` under `/media` endpoint, the file removal from there happens based on the visibility of the download button (so in case if download button is visible, we keep storing it in memory). 

To solve your problem I see these options:
1. If you have control over that, also add authorization to `/media` endpoint URLs (via proxy for example)
2. Or an easier solution could be not to store files inside MediaFileManager, and for downloading it provide an original link to your object/API via `st.link_button`. Then solve authorization on that level (for example issuing one-time links).

We have used something like this to remove files from the cache directly after downloading.

```python
import streamlit as st

...

def remove_from_cache(**kwargs):
    time.sleep(10)  # Sleep so that the file is not removed before downloading
    mfm = st.runtime.get_instance().media_file_mgr
    file_name = kwargs["file_name"]

    # Find the file hash
    found_file_hash = ""
    for file_hash, memory_file in mfm._storage._files_by_id.items():
        if memory_file.filename == file_name:
            found_file_hash = file_hash
            break

    session_ids_with_refs = []  # Find the sessions that use the file hash
    for session_id, coor_hash in mfm._files_by_session_and_coord.items():
        refs = coor_hash.values()
        if found_file_hash in refs:
            session_ids_with_refs.append(session_id)

    # Delete the sessions that use the file
    for session_id in session_ids_with_refs:
        del mfm._files_by_session_and_coord[session_id]

    mfm.remove_orphaned_files()  # 1 - Mark files for removal from cache
    mfm.remove_orphaned_files()  # 2 - Actual removal of files
    # The cache is cleared for this file!

# ...
# some dropdown selects the file into variable: option.

# When clicking on the download button, trigger an on_click event and pass the file_name:
with open(path_to_file, "rb") as f:
    download.download_button(label="Download", data=f,  file_name=option, ..., on_click=remove_from_cache,  kwargs={"file_name": option})
```

Hi, 

We use streamlit as a collaborative platform to host some of our small data viz applications. 
It's behind a reverse proxy with authentication, but once authenticated, all the links are available to all users.

Our cyber security dpt. also flagged this /media exposure issue, as a link leakage allows un-authorized access to any media of any user. 

Also, the link seems to be still valid even after the user closes his browser, for more than 30 minutes. 

We are considering switching to a custom files exposure api with per user authentication and using st.link_button but this is making everything harder. 

Having a user session header check when accessing the link or just streaming bytes maybe great.

title: Scan for `config.toml` file relative to main app file before defaulting to working directory
body:
### Checklist

### Summary

Currently, Streamlit looks for `.streamlit/config.toml` in the directory where `streamlit run` is executed. If you execute `streamlit run app/main.py` then Streamlit will not see or use `app/.streamlit/config.toml`.

### Why?

This creates a problem on Community Cloud, for example. When you deploy more than one app from the same repository, you are restricted to one, global `config.toml` file which must be placed in `.streamlit/config.toml` in the root of the repository.

### How?

Although there could be a Community-Cloud-specific solution to this, Streamlit could also be modified to look for (and prioritize) any `.streamtlit/config.toml` files that exist relative to the entry-point file.

This is similar to how it works for `requirements.txt` files: first check relative to the app's main file, then check in the root of the repo (where the command is executed). This principle could be extended for all `.streamlit`, environment, or configuration-like files.

### Additional Context

Related to #7578

title: Respect console do not track
body:
### Checklist

### Summary

Streamlits collects telemetry data and is transparent about it, as it shows on the first run:

```
  - This open source library collects usage statistics.
  - We cannot see and do not store information contained inside Streamlit apps,
    such as text, charts, images, etc.
  - Telemetry data is stored in servers in the United States.
  - If you'd like to opt out, add the following to ~/.streamlit/config.toml,
    creating that file if necessary:

    [browser]
    gatherUsageStats = false
```

It still requires an explicit opt-out in an own config file and doesn't seem to respect [Console Do Not Track](https://consoledonottrack.com/) yet. It would be nice if it could (additionally) respect this flag, which is thought as a way for users to send a Do-Not-Track signal to console apps similar to a browser sending it to websites, if they do not want to be tracked by any app.

### Why?

Console Do Not Track is an approach to provide a simple way for users to opt-out telemetry of all apps. Streamlit obviously likes to respects the wish for an opt-out, so it probably would also not have a problem to support this flag.

### How?

Parse the environement variables and treat `DO_NOT_TRACK=1` in the same way as `gatherUsageStats = false`

### Additional Context

comments.text:
I would also like this bug fixed/feature added.

The [documentation](https://docs.streamlit.io/library/advanced-features/configuration) and [this post](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/63#issuecomment-1108835602) seem to suggest that setting:
Windows: `set STEAMLIT_BROWSER_GATHERUSAGESTATS=false`
Linux: `STEAMLIT_BROWSER_GATHERUSAGESTATS=false`
should work to toggle this setting but this does not currently work at all.

`set gatherUsageStats=false` mentioned above does not work either, meaning there is no way to get streamlit to honor the user's decision except for manually toggling the setting during runtime as a CLI option, or adding configuration files as indicated here.

Modifying the local system globally is not a valid option for running streamlit in isolated versions of python like in venv and adjusting the CLI every time during runtime is overly cumbersome, especially during development when streamlit is being invoked in the simplest way possible for debugging.

Reading the CLI environmental variables would:
1. Honor the user's decision for this without having to modify the local system with config files on the file system or having to modify the runtime command every time.
2. Conform to the existing documentation. It seems misleading currently because the telemetry section does not explicitly mention that environmental options to disable it do not work when the section right above it said environmental variables are supported.
So how to disable `browser.gatherUsageStats` in code??

title: Keep symbolic links / re-resolve symlinks if target changes
body:
### Checklist

### Summary

Streamlit seems to resolve the path to a directory if there is a symlink on the way. Expected behavior would be to remember the given original path and reuse that on updates. This is important when using Kubernetes ConfigMaps for the code.

### Reproducible Code Example

### Steps To Reproduce

```
ln -s my-dir this-stays
streamlit run this-stays/Dashboard.py
(other shell)
mv my-dir other-dir
ln -sf other-dir this-stays
```
Dashboard now throws errors because it expects the scripts/files at `my-dir/...`

Streamlit continues to work correctly

### Current Behavior

FileNotFoundError: [Errno 2] No such file or directory

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

- Streamlit version: Streamlit, version 1.31.1
- Python version: Python 3.10.13

### Additional Information

We're mounting ConfigMaps into a container. Kubernetes sets symlinks and automatically updates those if the ConfigMap changes. To avoid breaking our deployments, we'd need Streamlit to work with the symbolic links better. Right now we have to restart the container each time.

title: Sidebar button disappears for apps on mobile phones after keyboard use
body:
### Checklist

### Summary

On a mobile phone, after clicking on a text input of an app with a sidebar the keyboard appears which makes the sidebar arrow completely disappear after the keyboard usage. From my understanding, the sidebar arrow can only be visible again after a refresh. **Therefore, especially for multipage apps, this is a very important issue that hinders users navigation on the website**

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
To the best of my knowledge, this is reproducible for any apps with a sidebar and a text input or dropdown menu. For instance, this can be tested in one of the community shared apps

comments.text: @user Does that happen every time? We have the check if there are newer version which might cause this, but this check is only done in 10% of server starts as far as I know.
@user Yes. I initially suspected it was the version check, but the hang happened even after I disabled the check.

It appears that I have this issue if I use the code from a release a few months ago, which I'm pretty sure I worked on offline without encountering this issue. So I suspect this is caused by something like a recent dependency update

Further investigation turned up a few things:

The issue is only triggered in headless mode, because that is the only codepath that calls `net_util.get_external_ip()`. I recently enabled headless mode in my config, which is why I didn't experience it before.
The issue is in the http requests that function makes, which hang even though a connection timeout is set.
It gets stuck right after urllib3 starts a new connection, with no further information. Would have to dig into it deeper, possibly with some tracing tools, to work out what's happening.

I don't know if we actually need an external ip address lookup for running headless mode, but this is also quite an edge case, so it is probably not worth removing the lookup.
Is this possibly related to the bug on Windows where a headless server hangs on closure / startup? Possibly a different root cause but might be hanging in a similar place...
Closing this since I believe we have fixed this recently by adding a timeout.

title: Support setting path to `.streamlit/` through streamlit run CLI or similar?
body:
### Checklist

### Summary

Instead of doing `streamlit run app.py`, we commonly do `streamlit run /path/to/app.py` instead.

In this case, Streamlit fails to use the `config.toml` and `secrets.toml` files, as they are not placed in a certain way with respect to where I launch the app.

This sounds like a very hardcoded and silly solution which I was surprised to learn there did not seem to be an API to change the behaviour.

Would it be possible to add support for doing something like this:
```
streamlit run --streamlit-dir /path/to/.streamlit/ /path/to/app.py
```

This would remove the need for placing the `.streamlit/` directly next to the `app.py` for this to work.

In this case where a `.streamlit/` dir could not be found, it would also be great if there was a warning about this, if thats not already the case. Took a while before our team caught that this was actually an issue and that our configuration file was not being used in our deployment setup.

### Why?

This allows the streamlit app to live and to be launched completely independent of where the `.streamlit/` directory is placed.

### How?

Add an API like this, or similar, to override the default behaviour:
```
streamlit run --streamlit-dir /path/to/.streamlit/ /path/to/app.py
```

### Additional Context

title: Streamlit Deploy as a Jupyter Server extension.
body:
### Checklist

### Summary

A way to deploy the streamlit app as a Jupyter server extension, both with the [notebook](https://github.com/jupyter/notebook) server or with [jupyter_server](https://github.com/jupyter/jupyter_server).

When running the Jupyter server, the app can accessible from the base URL suffixed with Stremlit/Appname.

### Why?

Most companies have internal Development and Production Notebook servers(ex. JupyterLab) for Data scientist. 
If a user can deploy his/her Streamlit app on the existing Jupyterlab server with some suffix, it would **significantly reduce** the post-dev effort from the user side. It will allow the user to leverage the scalable infra (Kubernates/Cloud/Docker etc) for his/her deployment with zero effort as they will piggyback on the existing Jupyter server deployment.

This also allows easy sharing of the deployed app as user would not be creating/maintaining the static link for the app. 

### How?

A way to deploy the streamlit app as a Jupyter server extension, both with the [notebook](https://github.com/jupyter/notebook) server or with [jupyter_server](https://github.com/jupyter/jupyter_server).

### Additional Context

Voila allows deploying an app on the Jupyter server. 
A similar approach can be leveraged here.

title: Native asyncio support
body:
### Checklist

### Summary

Streamlit needs native asyncio support.

I would like to point the following:

- asyncio interface is also important for snowflake, so usability or applicability of that should be a no brainer
- all modern databases have async interfaces and they will only expand with time
- streamlit is based on asyncio itself, so at least properly exposing the original tornado's event loop would also not require to much work for you

Known problems for now:
- when using asyncio.run() -> RuntimeError: Event loop is closed if the requests follow concurrently in the tornado eventlets
- every eventlet with own event loop -> tasks are getting to the wrong event loop
- cached event loop for all eventlets through session state -> best for now, gets event loop is closed when multile sessions are acessing the app simultaneously

So with that said, very ugly workaround that I found working best for now:

```python
@st.cache_resource(show_spinner=False)
def get_event_loop():
    loop = asyncio.new_event_loop()
    asyncio.set_event_loop(loop)
    return loop

if not st.session_state.get("event_loop"):
    st.session_state["event_loop"] = get_event_loop()
```

then pass that event loop wherever your data is coming from, here is motor example:

```python
async def setup_db(force=False):
    if force or not st.session_state.get("db_client"):
        with st.spinner("Loading..."):
            client = AsyncIOMotorClient(
                os.environ["MONGODB_URI"],
                tls=MONGODB_TLS,
                io_loop=st.session_state["event_loop"],
            )
            st.session_state["db_client"] = await init_database(client=client)
            return client
```
init_database is a call to beanie's init database

I understand that making the entire framework async would require too much work and would prb confuse the ML/AI crowd too much, but streamlit is such a gorgeous framework, the only place it fails in misery is the async

### Why?

Asyncio data technologies should be natively or at least easily accessible from streamlit apps.

### How?

Runs with asyncio.run() should not result to errors.
Concurrent access also should not be broken.
Asyncio loop from tornado app should be available in the scripts.

Handling st.* calls async seems quite unimaginable, but at least the functioning asyncio in the eventlets would give us a lot.

Also async support for on_change and on_click callbacks and caching functions.

### Additional Context

Related issues:
- https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/744
- https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/8308
- https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/12076

comments.text: 2024 and no async support... yet, gonna thumbs this up 10 times

Hello -

Just a bit of experimentation around Streamlit, threads, and asyncio.

My understanding:
- Every time a re-render is required (state change, user interaction, etc), a new thread is created and the script is run fresh. The old thread, if it hasn't already completed the script, may keep going (due to fastRerun) but any interaction with st objects will throw a Shutdown Exception.
- Streamlit does not care about asyncio, rather only if the thread has terminated or not.

I'm not sure how scalable this is -- threads will be active for each user potentially -- but my approach has been:
- Use asyncio.run() at the end of the script. This will create a new event loop for the thread (and render).
- The asyncio loop has tasks, which may run forever, *must* frequently interact with st (e.g. st.session_state) to trigger potential Shutdown exceptions to clean up the threads.
- If the asyncio loop ends early, then the "Running" indicator stops. So you can see the thread is still busy.

I haven't done scaled testing, but this approach seems to be working sensibly in my tests.

Having done a bunch of experimentation myself I have a few things to add.  There is a lot of inaccurate information floating around on the web about this subject.  The really important thing to remember is what's mentioned in the comment by @user above:

> Every time a re-render is required (state change, user interaction, etc), a new thread is created and the script is run fresh. The old thread, if it hasn't already completed the script, may keep going (due to fastRerun) but any interaction with st objects will throw a Shutdown Exception.

This means that whlie you can use `asyncio.run()` in your script (the [Medium post](https://sehmi-conscious.medium.com/got-that-asyncio-feeling-f1a7c37cab8b) unfortunately linked from Streamlit's own documentation falsely claims otherwise), you can't allow any interaction with your app while the event loop is running, and any tasks you launch on it can't reliably access `st.` functions for the reasons mentioned above.  It will also lead to a possibly large number of threads being created since, as mentioned above, the resulting asyncio event loop may run forever.

While you can manually create an event loop, set it for the current thread, and recover it on future invocations of your script **in that same thread**, this isn't particularly useful because your script code may or may not (actually won't, probably) run on that thread.  You also can't, for example, call `run_until_complete` on the event loop for [well-known reasons](https://github.com/python/cpython/issues/66435).

Also, despite what said Medium post claims, calling `asyncio.get_running_loop` **definitely does not** return Streamlit's own event loop, as it will always be on a different thread than the one that runs your script.  This is, of course, what this bug is actually about :-)  If you don't care about security, reliability, stability, etc, and you don't want to call `st.` functions from your tasks, you can get it by calling `_get_async_objs()` on the session runtime.  For instance:

```python
import asyncio
import time
import streamlit as st

loop = st.runtime.get_instance()._get_async_objs().eventloop

async def do_nothing(seconds):
    await asyncio.sleep(3)
    print("HELLO WORLD", seconds)

if st.button(label="Do something"):
    loop.create_task(do_nothing(time.time()))

if st.button(label="Do something else"):
    st.toast("Hello!")
```

The best workaround for the moment, if you need to use asyncio for something, is probably to explicitly create a separate thread to run asyncio tasks, using `add_script_run_ctx` to give it access to the session state so that it can communicate with the rest of the UI.

I also don't really see how a solution to this problem could easily be implemented in Streamlit.  Conceptually, what is necessary, is what the original poster's "ugly workaround" is supposed to do, and what the Medium post claims Streamlit does, but which neither of them actually do, namely creating (possibly on demand) an event loop for each session context which script code can use to launch tasks.  Why this doesn't work:

- Simply creating an event loop doesn't actually start it!  So calling `create_task` on said loop will not do anything at all.
- Running an event loop is a blocking, non-reentrant operation.   Obviously a Streamlit `AppContext` (which runs in the main thread) can't do this.   But also a Streamlit `ScriptRunner` (which runs in its own thread) can't do this either, because there could be any number of threads for a given session context.

I don't claim to really understand Streamlit's architecture but it seems like a possible implementation woud be to create a separate thread for each script context, run an event loop there, and somehow give script code access to this event loop so that it can create and wait on tasks launched in it.  The evil solution would be to do magic on `await` in script code to make it do that ;-)

Here's a sketch of how you can do what's mentioned in the previous comment.  There are a couple of caveats:

- Accessing the ui from a coroutine doesn't work for some reason, most likely because at the moment when you might want to do so, the script is no longer actually running, or a new script runner has been started (this is not clear to me).
- There is no signal handling possible in the local event loop.  So you have to hit Control-C multiple times to stop the server, and you will get an "Event loop is closed" exception.
- Any running tasks will do ... something undefined, I think ... if you stop the event loop, and Python will complain about this.

Gist here: https://gist.github.com/dhdaines/574d58eed7da9c459e3ef2b50a3ac27b

While not officially supported, I think Streamlit mostly works with this simple pattern (my [user-space effort towards easier concurrency](https://concurrency.streamlit.app/) is based on this and other workarounds):

```py
# a_page.py
import asyncio
import streamlit as st

async def task1(): ...

async def task2(): ...

async def main():
  res1, res2 = await asyncio.gather(task1(), task2())
  # update widgets if required 

asyncio.run(main())
```

A Streamlit `scriptThread` is a 'clean' one without an event loop, just as `asyncio.run()` requires. A new event loop will get created, used, and shutdown properly. Code in coroutines have access to `ScriptRunContext` and should still work.

> reuse tornado's event loop

While not impossible this looks risky to me:

1. An eventloop for net IO should be kept away from possibly blocking code. Like a `async def fun(): a_slow_long_function()`
2. When `ScriptRunContext` and other thread-local object are involved, they may get leaked during interleaved coroutine execution.
    - This applies to other shared event loop solutions. IMO an event loop should not be shared at a scope larger than Streamlit session.

> possiblity of leaked or forever-spinning user-created event loop

Yes, a solution should take care of this. I'm still trying to.

My current thought is to expose script run / session shutdowns to user code, and allow some form of cancellation (forced or cooperative).

Until this is fixed, there is possibility to use nest_asyncio, However nested event loops might have performance impact, 
```
pip install nest_asyncio

import nest_asyncio
nest_asyncio.apply()
```

And then at least for me everything works as expected, I am using streamlit with combination with AutoGen AssistantAgent

Hey Everyone! I am working on a project Parallel Fragments that will help optimize the performance of certain apps, particularly ones that are doing a lot of data loading, for e.g. BI dashboards.

And also a demo app that I made for the feature: https://parallel-fragments.streamlit.app/

An update on this conversation. We have recently shipped two features in 1.64 that address two major themes for async support.

title: `st.selectbox` sometimes ignores user input when order of `options` changes
body:
### Checklist

### Summary

Hi Streamlit team! I have found a weird edge case where 50% of the time, my `st.selectbox` user input is ignored, and the other 50% it works as expected.

I have noticed that this happens specifically when I try to change the order of the `options` value. I have included a code example tested on Streamlit `v1.33.0` that shows the issue. 

[image]

### Reproducible Code Example

[[image]](https://issues.streamlitapp.com/?issue=gh-8496)
```Python
import streamlit as st

# set up some dummy session state variables
if 'options' not in st.session_state:
    st.session_state.options = ['D', 'C', 'B', 'A', 'F', 'E']

st.session_state.selected_option = st.selectbox(
    label='Select an option',
    options=st.session_state.options,
)

st.markdown(f'You selected: {st.session_state.selected_option}')

# move the selected option to the front of the list if it is not already
if st.session_state.selected_option != st.session_state.options[0]:
    st.session_state.options.remove(st.session_state.selected_option)
    st.session_state.options.insert(0, st.session_state.selected_option)
```

### Steps To Reproduce

You should be able to run the above code and see the issue as shown in the attached GIF!

### Expected Behavior

Ideally, when the user selects another option, we always respect that as the truth and show that option in the rendered select box.

@user thanks for reporting this 👍  I reproduced it [here](https://issues.streamlit.app/?issue=gh-8496). As @user explained correctly, its a behaviour that's currently expected (-> changing this to a feature request). But we are aware that it is causing trouble in some usecases. 

Related issues for other widgets are:
- https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/7749
- https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/7855
- https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/8410
- https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/4854 (I believe this is probably a bit overlapping with this issue)
is there any workaround to fix this issue

@user @user thanks for the reply and linking some similar issues, I appreciate the response! I tried moving the option sorting logic into a function called by the `selectbox`'s `on_change` but the issue still happens :(

As a workaround in the meantime, I've been caching the options sent into the `selectbox` so the widget doesn't reset each time until the set of options actually change. It's a *SUPER* hacky, but it works well-enough for my use case: 

```python
import streamlit as st

# set up some dummy session state variables
if 'options' not in st.session_state:
    st.session_state.options = ['D', 'C', 'B', 'A', 'F', 'E']

# cache the options to the ``st.selectbox`` doesn't reset and ignore a user's input if the order of
# the options changes
if set(st.session_state.get('_cached_options', [])) != set(st.session_state.options):
    st.session_state._cached_options = sorted(st.session_state.options)

    if 'selected_option' in st.session_state:
        st.session_state._selectbox_index = (
            st.session_state._cached_options.index(st.session_state.selected_option)
        )
    else:
        st.session_state._selectbox_index = 0

st.session_state.selected_option = st.selectbox(
    label='Select an option',
    options=st.session_state._cached_options,
    index=st.session_state._selectbox_index,
)

st.markdown(f'You selected: {st.session_state.selected_option}')

# move the selected option to the front of the list if it is not already
if st.session_state.selected_option != st.session_state.options[0]:
    st.session_state.options.remove(st.session_state.selected_option)
    st.session_state.options.insert(0, st.session_state.selected_option)

# dummy logic to add an option just to see how ``st.session_state.options`` changes
if st.button('Add an option'):
    option_to_add = 1

    while True:
        if str(option_to_add) not in st.session_state.options:
            st.session_state.options.append(str(option_to_add))
            st.rerun()

        option_to_add += 1
```

[image]

@user hmm, I think that might be a bit overkill. This should be what you want

```python
import streamlit as st

# set up some dummy session state variables
st.session_state.setdefault("options", ['D', 'C', 'B', 'A', 'F', 'E'])

def update_options():
    # move the selected option to the front of the list if it is not already
    if st.session_state.selected_option != st.session_state.options[0]:
        st.session_state.options.remove(st.session_state.selected_option)
        st.session_state.options.insert(0, st.session_state.selected_option)

st.selectbox(
    label='Select an option',
    options=st.session_state.options,
    key="selected_option",
    on_change=update_options,
)

st.markdown(f'You selected: {st.session_state.selected_option}')
```

Here's what's happening:

1. You create the options list in session_state
2. You create a selectbox that is tied to the selected_option key
3. When the selection changes, the update_options function is run before your script code and updates the list in session state, causing the order to change.

title: Native authentication support for Streamlit
body:
### Summary

We are investigating approaches to add native authentication support for Streamlit, as it is one of the top most requested community features. This is a rough proposal for how it might work, which is shared for your feedback.

### Goals

**Goal 1:** Provide the building blocks for integrating more robust auth solutions including:
- documented support for reading headers (replace the undocumented but heavily used `_get_websocket_headers()`
- native support for reading and writing cookies ( #861 )
- native redirect ( #7123 )
- hooks to add identity information in `st.user`
- _[longer term]_ Support custom http endpoints ( #439 ) - this will be a bigger effort but know we probably need to get there eventually to have a really robust support
- ??? What else ???

**Goal 2:** Provide an out-of-the-box native integration which covers the most common use cases, especially for developers getting started. To that end, we propose **standardizing on OAuth2 & OpenID Connect as the natively supported protocols in Streamlit**.
- This would be an opinionated and minimal implementation, geared towards integrating with standardized OIDC providers.
- Goal would be, with a few lines of config / secrets, you can be set up with `login()` / `logout()` methods and the users verified email, OAuth2 token, and potentially other claims from a JWT readily available through a standard API (likely attributes on `st.user`).
- Ideally, include an easy integration with cookies support so it's trivial to maintain the user auth session across tabs for some time. However, we still need to investigate whether this is feasible or has other major implications.

**Why OpenID Connect (OIDC)?**
- From our perspective, OIDC seems like the most modern, standardized authentication protocol we can use which enables a standard format of user identity claims (including roles / groups) and minimal custom code across providers.
- We also see a wide range of adoption across identity providers both in the consumer space (Google, Apple, etc) and enterprise space (Auth0, AWS Cognito, MSFT Entra ID, etc).
- For most app developers who aren't working in a more sophisticated existing platform, it seems to cover the typical use case for "single sign on" for relatively low fuss and configuration required in the provider side.

**Non-goal: Replace the use of reverse proxy in higher security environments**

We know this practice of running Streamlit behind an auth proxy and forwarding authenticated requests to the app is fairly common among Streamlit usage in bigger companies or those with higher security requirements. We want to build library features that make that easier to run (such as documented headers support) but not replace it or build extremely hardened security into Streamlit, since it isn't our expertise.

But, we think this proposal can still unblock many developers operating in somewhat lower stakes environments who experience a lot of friction today.

### VERY ROUGH API sketch

Here's a very rough first idea of how the API might work for the built-in OIDC.

```toml
# .streamlit/secrets.toml or similar

[auth] # reserved group for defining auth, could also support multiple like [auth.google]
type = "oidc"
provider = "google" # or api_base_url="accounts.google.com"
client_id = "SOME ID"
client_secret = "SOME SECRET"
default_ttl = "7d" # if we have some easy cookie support

```

Once this is configured, you can call some standard methods in the app which will redirect to the appropriate OIDC flow. Streamlit will automatically expose an OAuth2 callback endpoint which handles the response from the identity provider.

In the case below, calling `login()` will simply redirect to the OAuth2 flow. When the user returns from the flow, their identity values will be available in `st.user`. Calling `logout()` will clear the values from `st.user` in that session along with any browser cookies.

```python
# streamlit_app.py

if st.user.logged_in(): # verify log in, including cookie from an earlier session
    st.write(f"Welcome, {st.user.name}!")
    st.sidebar.button("Logout", on_click=st.user.logout)
else:
    st.sidebar.button("Login", on_click=st.user.login)
```

### Other authentication protocols

We know other protocols are used today, such as looking up a username / password in a database (e.g. [Streamlit-Authenticator](https://github.com/mkhorasani/Streamlit-Authenticator)), or more complex delegated authentication schemes like SAML / LDAP. In some cases, the existing plugins / components for these can work pretty well. We'd like to provide some hooks to make them more consistent with the native support (maybe similar to `st.connection`), but it may not be in the initial launch.

### What do you think?

If this proposal and approach sounds good and meets your use case, please give a 👍 . Also, we'd love to hear any comments about what you like, don't like, or would change, or any use case you have which would not be supported. Thanks!!

Hi! Are you considering to include Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) within the SSO authentication management? 

Currently, while SSO protects access to the app, it does not support role-based page access, limiting our ability to tailor user experiences based on roles. We are trying to build that, and it would be extremly useful to be native as adhoc does not work as we would like to...
 
**Current Challenges:**
 
1. **General Page Access:** The current configuration (config.toml) applies globally, allowing all authenticated users to access the same set of pages without differentiation by roles.
2. **Workaround Approaches:**
   - **Multiple TOML Files:** We attempted to create multiple config files (config_id.toml) for each role defined in Azure. While this worked to an extent, it required all files to reside on the server, which complicates management and increases the risk of unauthorized access.
When a user with a different assigned role logged in, as we load the pages for its TOML file, the available pages for previously logged users changed
   - **Conditional Page Access:** Our current approach involves displaying all pages in the sidebar but restricting access upon selection based on user roles. This results in a suboptimal user experience as users see pages they cannot access.
 
**Proposed Solution:**
 
Integrate role-based access control within the SSO authentication management, allowing the following:
1. **Role Assignment:** Define roles within the app configuration or through SSO integration (e.g., Azure AD).
2. **Role-Based Page Access:** Specify page access permissions within config.toml or another configuration file, restricting visibility and access based on user roles.
3. **Dynamic Sidebar:** Automatically adjust the sidebar to show only the pages the logged-in user has access to, improving user experience and security.
 
**Benefits:**
 
- **Enhanced Security:** Restrict access to sensitive pages based on user roles.
- **Improved User Experience:** Users see only relevant pages, reducing confusion and navigation complexity.
- **Simplified Management:** Centralized role definitions and access control, minimizing the need for multiple configuration files and reducing maintenance overhead.

To me the ability to manipulate arbitrary cookie is an XY problem. What developers really want is to have a way to keep track of user session so that they can restore user state after a user reopen a streamlit app he has accessed before.

So instead of implementing a feature to allow user to set or delete whatever cookies they want, which gonna to be a complicated and time consuming task, we can simply get started with allowing user to keep track of user session. That's what I try to show in this PR: https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/8847

When a user access streamlit app for the first time, a unique cookie will be set and then all requests of the same user will have this unique cookie in its header, so that developers can use it to track of user session. That's all, and it is a common way to solve problem of this kind back to the days that everything can only be done in the backend.

And with this feature all developers need is to start a stream app with `--enableSession True`, and then they can access the cookie from the websocket header.

```python
import streamlit as st

def get_cookie():
    from streamlit.web.server.websocket_headers import _get_websocket_headers
    from http.cookies import SimpleCookie
    headers = _get_websocket_headers()
    cookie_str = headers.get("Cookie")
    return SimpleCookie(cookie_str)

cookie = get_cookie()
st_session_id = cookie["ST_SESSION_ID"].value

# you will see the same value if open multiple tabs in the same browser
st.write(f'ST_SESSION_ID is: {st_session_id}')

```

title: Not handled DecodeError on the server side on file upload with double extension
body:
### Checklist

### Summary

Hello streamlit team,

first of all thank you for the great work!
We have developed an application using streamlit, deployed our application as a container using Azure App services and in order to tackle the security concerns we have been performing penetration tests.

A minor finding was related to improper error handling, as both on client side and the server side, a traceback should not be displayed because this can pose security risks.

We can't solve it on the application side as the error gets displayed from the streamlit scripts.

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
try:
    with st.form("file-upload-form", clear_on_submit=True):
        uploaded_file = st.file_uploader(label='Please select a file.', accept_multiple_files=False, type="xlsx")
        submitted = st.form_submit_button("Upload")
except Exception as e:
    msg = "The file could not be uploaded."
    logger.error(msg)
    st.write(msg)
    raise ValueError(msg)
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Download BurpSuite https://portswigger.net/burp/communitydownload 
2. Onboard yourself with:
          - https://portswigger.net/burp/documentation/desktop/getting-started/intercepting-http-traffic 
          - https://portswigger.net/burp/documentation/desktop/getting-started/modifying-http-requests
3. Access the application from the browser from BurpSuite
4. Upload a file with double extension: e.g. test_file.php.xlsx
5. After file upload, enable "Incercepting" and update the file extension in the raw message removing .xlsx:
[image]
[image]
6. Click forward 2-4 times
7. DecodeError is displayed on the server side: 
[image]

### Expected Behavior

I expect that the DecodeError is properly handled, no traceback is displayed on server but rather a custom message.

### Current Behavior

Error message on server:
```
DecodeErrorError parsing messageFile "/usr/local/lib/python3.9/site-packages/streamlit/web/server/browser_websocket_handler.py", line 164, in on_message
    msg.ParseFromString(payload)
```
Handled error on client:
[image]

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.29.0
- Python version: 3.9
- Operating System: OS FROM python:3.9-slim
- Browser: Chrome

### Additional Information

Hi @user,

I'm not sure if there's much we can do about this in the Streamlit OS lib side. The issue is most likely because, in a Community Cloud deployment, the connection is indeed an http connection since the TLS connection isn't terminated by the Streamlit server, it's terminated at the load balancer level (and security is maintained by having the network permissions set such that the Streamlit server only accepts traffic from the load balancer in front of it).

This would be true of any deployment made where the Streamlit server itself isn't configured to terminate the TLS connection, and while we do have some basic configurability for this included in our config options (see the `server.sslCertFile` and `server.sslKeyFile`), it's unlikely we'll add full support for this in Community Cloud given the community focus of the product.

Interesting!

Well, fixing this isn't crucial for me, so feel free to deprioritize it, etc.
Closing this since this is referring to an internal tornado API, and we have migrated to Starlette recently

title: Console script returning RuntimeError
body:
### Checklist

### Summary

When you create a Python package, you may want to provide a user-friendly CLI, via an [entry point console script](https://setuptools.pypa.io/en/latest/userguide/entry_point.html). Here is an excerpt from setuptools explaining it:

> Entry points are a type of metadata that can be exposed by packages on installation. They are a very useful feature of the Python ecosystem, and come specially handy in two scenarios:
> 
> 1. The package would like to provide commands to be run at the terminal. This functionality is known as console scripts. The command may also open up a GUI, in which case it is known as a GUI script. An example of a console script is the one provided by the [pip](https://pypi.org/project/pip) package, which allows you to run commands like pip install in the terminal.

A practical example is when you install streamlit, and want to check which version is installed. So you run in the terminal:

```
streamlit --version
```

This is a console script.

Acknowledged! This behavior change seems to have been introduced via [this PR](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/8457/files#diff-dd19937f664be9342c4eb5127a08d4eb9772df960892440eb8eaadbda4070cb9R87), since now the Component Registry is loaded from the runtime and is not a singleton anymore. Hello,
this is the same issue I raised here: https://github.com/NathanChen198/streamlit-rsa-auth-ui/issues/1
Worked in 1.33 but in 1.34 its broken. Raises a RunTimeError too.

I can confirm the same issue as well for the import of custom components. 

Reproducable code:
Expects custom component `streamlit_elements` is installed
### file: streamlit_bug_report.py
```python
import streamlit as st
# This line raises "RuntimeError: Runtime hasn't been created!" in streamlit>=1.34.0
from streamlit_elements import elements, dashboard, mui, nivo

def app():
    # assume somthing with the streamlit_elements component happens here
    st.write("Hello World")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    app()
```
runs fine if one starts the app with `streamlit run streamlit_bug_report.py`

But if the app is started via cli with help of streamlit.web.bootstrap its now raising an error since streamlit version `1.34.0`.
### file: streamlit_bug_report_cli.py
```python
import streamlit as st
import streamlit.web.bootstrap as st_bootstrap
from streamlit_bug_report import app

def main():
    if st.runtime.exists():
        # The app has been executed with `streamlit run app.py`
        app()
    else:
        # If the file has been executed with python (`python app.py`), the streamlit functionality
        # won't work. This line reruns the app within the streamlit context, as if it has been
        # executed with `streamlit run app.py`.
        # This is necessary when installing this project from a .whl package, since the executable
        # only gets execute by python and not by streamlit.
        st_bootstrap.run(
            __file__,
            is_hello=False,
            args=[],
            flag_options={},
        )

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```

Running ` python streamlit_bug_report_cli.py` will raise `RuntimeError: Runtime hasn't been created!`
The issue also affects automated tests in packages like `streamlit-folium`, where custom components are tested without actually running Streamlit.

title: Inconsistent case sensitivity (`streamlit run`, `st.switch_page`, and the file name)
body:
### Checklist

### Summary

When using `st.switch_page` to go to your app's homepage on a Mac, the function is case sensitive to how the app was initialized with `streamlit run` and not with the actual file name.

### Reproducible Code Example

```python
#App.py

import streamlit as st

if st. button("a"):
    st.switch_page("pages/a.py")
```

```python
#pages/a.py
import streamlit as st

if st.button("app"):
    st.switch_page("app.py")

if st.button("App"):
    st.switch_page("App.py")
```

### Steps To Reproduce

On a Mac (I used Chrome, but the Mac is the important part.)

1. `streamlit run App.py`
2. Clicking the first button (app) on `pages/a.py` results in an error (can't find page).
3. Clicking the second button (App) works as expected.

On the other hand
1. `streamilt run app.py` (The app still runs)
2. Clicking the first button (app.py) works
3. Clicking the second button (App) results in an error.

When I do the same on a Windows computer, there's no problem either way. It's case insensitive.

### Expected Behavior

I don't know if I'd expect a Mac to throw an error on `streamlit run` if the case doesn't match, but I definitely think `st.switch_page` (if it's going to be case sensitive) should match the case of the actual file.

### Current Behavior

`StreamlitAPIException: Could not find page: App.py. Must be the file path relative to the main script, from the directory: Sandbox. Only the main app file and files in the pages/ directory are supported.`

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

- Browser:

@user are you working on this or do you want me to take a stab at it? I can at least cover Linux and Windows (don't have a Mac to test on). I think the behavior on Linux might actually be a third option: it is more restrictive than Windows or Mac since you cannot start the app unless the file name case matches exactly, so you don't get into a situation where you have an indeterminate starting state.

Testing on Ubuntu on streamlit 1.34.0:
1. `streamlit run app.py` fails
2. "App.py" button works
3. "app.py" button fails

I've got my hands full on documentation, so the devs will need to comment on how they want to prioritize and approach this. (And yes, Linux should be tested, too. I just had a Mac laptop and Windows laptop on my desk, so I started there to get the report in.) 😁

@user dug into this a little more. Unfortunately I'm not even sure that `pathlib.Path` is necessary a fix-all solution here. until about Python 3.12, `pathlib.Path` has a fixed preference for POSIX-like systems (it treats them as case sensitive) even though OSX file-systems are typically case-insensitive like on Windows (although that can be modified by the user).

Python 3.12 seems to do better by using a system call to `os.fspath` to "normalize" a path, which allows the user's filesystem to determine whether two paths are equal.

If we're willing to accept that, however, then 
```python
# execution_control.py
matched_pages = [p for p in all_app_pages if Path(p["script_path"]) == Path(requested_page)]
```
would do the trick for this particular bug. Or, one could store the Path objects themselves in `source_util.get_pages`.

@user I imagine the `st.nagivation` changes might screw around with the existing script_path code a bunch, so to avoid conflicts with that I think it would at least make sense to wait to fix this until after that API is settled down.
defer to @user but yeah that may make sense - this will be a good one to fix though! Thx for flagging Debbie, Alex and Karen!

title: default of browser.serverAddress is not actually "localhost"
body:
### Checklist

### Summary

https://docs.streamlit.io/develop/api-reference/configuration/config.toml#browser says the default of serverAddress  is "localhost". However, this can't be true, because if I `streamlit run` a file *without*
```
[browser]
serverAddress = "localhost"
```
in the config.toml

I get something like the following:

```
  You can now view your Streamlit app in your browser.

  Network URL: http://[some private IPv4 address]:8501
  External URL: http://[some public IPv4 address]:8501
```

And when I *add* the lines to the config.toml I get

```
  You can now view your Streamlit app in your browser.

  URL: http://localhost:8501
```

instead. (Which is the desired behavior in my case.)

localhost:8501 works to access the application either way.

This is either a documentation issue or a true bug.

The bound address itself should depend on [tornado's listen method](https://www.tornadoweb.org/en/stable/tcpserver.html#tornado.tcpserver.TCPServer.listen) which we call [here](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/blob/develop/lib/streamlit/web/server/server.py#L196).

```

```
as well.

Assuming the behavior is desirable: add note (in both places?) that server.headless overrides the browser.serverAddress setting.

If the behavior isn't desirable: make it not do that, I suppose.

title: streamlit does not produce WebSocket ping frames
body:
### Checklist

### Summary

streamlit is supposed to generate WebSocket ping to ensure that the connection to the end-user is not terminated by any proxy sitting between the user and streamlit

### Reproducible Code Example

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Build Dockerfile with streamlit==1.34.0 requirements.txt
2. Use `ENTRYPOINT ["streamlit", "hello"]`
3. Run container, e.g.  podman run --rm -p 8501:8501 streamlit
4. Oper browser to localhost:8501, open Network inspector and select WebSocket connection messages
5. Note missing ping messages after initial data transfer over WebSocket

[image]

### Expected Behavior

In `server.py`, there is TORNADO_SETTINGS (https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/blob/406b1e617a4d7c147d199073063c20d6d45cfa3e/lib/streamlit/web/server/server.py#L61-L74) that states that WebSocket ping messages should be sent every second. This does not occur, and causes the WebSocket connection to be dropped when a component between the end-user and streamlit determines that the TCP connection is idle / not active.

Since this function does not currently work (tested in 1.34.0 of streamlit), deploying streamlit in any environment can cause connectivity issues, unless the developer writes their own ping logic into streamlit.

### Current Behavior

No WebSocket ping messages is sent, code suggests it should be sent.

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: streamlit, version 1.34.0
- Python version: Python 3.12.3
- Operating System: (python:3 container image, Linux cdf8d47bc708 6.8.4-200.fc39.aarch64 #1 SMP PREEMPT_DYNAMIC Thu Apr  4 21:00:27 UTC 2024 aarch64 GNU/Linux
- Browser: N/A, but Version 124.0.6367.201 (Official Build) (arm64)

### Additional Information

I'm assuming this is a regression or upstream bug as a result of library update.

I've found similar issues and code changes related to this:
https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/3464
https://discuss.streamlit.io/t/websocketconnection-websocket-onerror/46298/10

I noticed the same, that the streamlit code on this area has been stable for some time. For whats it worth, it seems that https://github.com/tornadoweb/tornado/pull/3376 is solving the issue of tornado closing the ws connection prematurely, but with the logic error.

I'm experiencing the same issue and it is an issue of streamlit configuration.

But I found out that `WebSocketProtocol13.ping_timeout` somehow set to 1, but streamlit explicitly set it to 30 with `websocket_ping_timeout` parameter. Debugger shows up where exactly problem appears.

Tornado expects that ping interval would be greater than timeout.
Source: https://www.tornadoweb.org/en/stable/_modules/tornado/websocket.html
Source code:

```python
    @user
    def ping_timeout(self) -> float:
        timeout = self.params.ping_timeout
        if timeout is not None:
            if self.ping_interval and timeout > self.ping_interval:
                de_dupe_gen_log(
                    # Note: using de_dupe_gen_log to prevent this message from
                    # being duplicated for each connection
                    logging.WARNING,
                    f"The websocket_ping_timeout ({timeout}) cannot be longer"
                    f" than the websocket_ping_interval ({self.ping_interval})."
                    f"\nSetting websocket_ping_timeout={self.ping_interval}",
                )
                return self.ping_interval
            return timeout
        return self.ping_interval
```

But streamlit set `ping_timeout` to 30 and `ping_interval` to 1, and tornado would use 1 for timeout as well.

On slow networks, where delay is probable, this causes to reconnect quite often. And most sadly, it breaks up streaming of content (with empty AI message at the end).

Please, provide a feature to configure this parameters for your users.
Thanks.

I'm closing this since Streamlit does produce websocket pings, but they are not shown in the Chrome dev console. You can see them within the Firefox dev console.

> Please, provide a feature to configure this parameters for your users.

We added a setting in 1.48 that lets you configure the interval (+ timeout): `server.websocketPingInterval` -> default is 30s for both with the latest Streamlit version.

body:
### Checklist

### Summary

As a developer, this API will allow me to access the `tornado.Application` instance, so that I can use the low level API to implement features that are unsupported by the `streamlit` for now.

### Why?

`streamlit` has some limitations which make it very hard to implement some common features. for example,  to keep user session after refresh web page.  Before `streamlit` has formal support for features like set cookies, to allow developer to access the low level `tornado.Application` instance would be a practical temporary solutions.

For example, in my case I would like to set a session cookie when a user login my app via OAuth. This could be done by implement a dedicated `raw-api/login.html` endpoint to return a html page with set cookie headers in it and then redirect to the real target page. It is a common pattern to handle 3rd party login but unfortunately there is no `streamlit` API to implement it.

If I can access the tornado instance, this can be easily done by add a custom route handle to return a dynamic login.html page with set cookies header in the response.  And I believe a lot of similar issue  can be solved this way. I don't think it would take too much effort to provide this API.

Reference:
* https://discuss.streamlit.io/t/is-it-possible-to-create-a-raw-html-endpoint-for-setting-session-cookie/69419

### How?

By just implement an experimental API named `get_tornado_instance` should be enough IMO.

Thanks @user 

It's unlikely that we'll directly support using the Tornado instance since we've intentionally avoided exposing Tornado internals since early Streamlit. We're also beginning to look at moving Streamlit to an ASGI framework in the not too distant future (you heard it here first! 😉) so that would break any Tornado compatibility.

We're _actively_ working right now on auth use cases similar to the one you described, see https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/8518

We're also doing some planning and design on custom HTTP endpoints similar to what you described in a more general way, along the lines of what I [described here](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/439#issuecomment-1963159872).

In general today, most developers use the undocumented-but-supported [headers API](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/5457) for similar use cases. We will likely add a fully-documented-and-supported version of that in the near future.

I'm sure it's not quite the answer you hoped for, but that's the current state and we are definitely putting more energy in this direction than we have historically.
@user That's great to hear! Is there any update on moving to ASGI?

## Update

Starlette will become the default server in 1.57 and Tornado will be removed as a dependency. The Starlette app can be configured as described in https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/13600

title: Streamlit unnecessarily runs the file watcher against every path in imported modules, even when watching is disabled
body:
### Checklist

### Summary

We are running an application that has a bunch of module dependencies.
Recording some profiles, we often see stack traces like this

[image]

https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/blob/ad3dc4e19d261fc66560a25bab92a7a560068338/lib/streamlit/runtime/app_session.py#L604

This happens despite the file watcher type being set to `none`, because the local watcher does not gate on that setting. It is only when the per-file watch request addition happens that the setting is checked and it determines that no watch is required. This is incredibly wasteful as it incurs a `isfile` check (along with an fnmatch) for ~40000 files in our case. If I understand the code correctly, this happens at the end of every successful page load.

This seems like it could easily be avoided if the app session also consulted the setting.

Don't iterate over a bunch of files when file watching is disabled.

title: WebSocket header HTTP_SEC_WEBSOCKET_PROTOCOL value changed to 'streamlit, PLACEHOLDER_AUTH_TOKEN' which gives connection error
body:
### Checklist

### Summary

After this change https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/commit/fd1037ba61 in the file https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/blame/1.29.0/frontend/app/src/connection/WebsocketConnection.tsx#L435 the request header `Sec-Websocket-Protocol` from the webpage client has no longer the value `'streamlit'` but from Streamlit version **1.29.0** the value is `'streamlit, PLACEHOLDER_AUTH_TOKEN'`.

I use a Streamlit app where the server side of the app is in a docker and the communication between the webpage client and the server goes through a proxy based on Flask and uwsgi.

That changed header prevented the webpage client from connecting to the server ( URL `/_stcore/stream failed`).

My fix was to replace the value `'streamlit, PLACEHOLDER_AUTH_TOKEN'` with `'streamlit'` in my proxy layer before establishing the websocket handshake, so I did a patch for that.

Maybe it's a good idea for you guys that you rethink the solution? Maybe it can be more robust?

Hey @user ! Thanks for filing the issue. I will have to follow up with @user who is more knowledgable of the code. According the comment, an empty string is an invalid value to provide. See https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/7608 for some context.

I do know we are doing some more work with regards to auth and headers, which might be of interest in providing a more robust solution. Tagging @user and @user who's been thinking in this space.

Following up. I've confirmed with @user that this is expected behavior, and so I am going to close the ticket. @user Hi I would love to hear any feedback from the streamlit team. I can raise a PR if there's interest in it. 

I read it somewhere that streamlit is departing from tornado and switching to an asgi. I wonder if that will make this feature request self-resolved(like new webserver has this bultin). If that's the case, could you please share your expected timeline for the effort? Thanks!

@user yep, we are evaluating options to switch out our server or allow Streamlit to be used with different servers. This is very early in the evaluation phase, but I assume a feature like an IP whitelist would make sense to connect to this project (cc @user).

## Update

Exciting news 🎉 Starting with **Streamlit 1.53**, we've added experimental support for custom middleware via the new ASGI/Starlette integration.

You can now implement IP whitelisting:

```python
from streamlit.starlette import App
from starlette.middleware import Middleware
from starlette.middleware.base import BaseHTTPMiddleware
from starlette.responses import Response

ALLOWED_IPS = {"127.0.0.1", "192.168.1.100", "10.0.0.0/8"}

class IPWhitelistMiddleware(BaseHTTPMiddleware):
    async def dispatch(self, request, call_next):
        client_ip = request.client.host
        if client_ip not in ALLOWED_IPS:
            return Response("Forbidden", status_code=403)
        return await call_next(request)

app = App("main.py", middleware=[Middleware(IPWhitelistMiddleware)])
```

For more advanced IP range checking, you can use the `ipaddress` module.

We'd love your feedback on this feature! Please try it out and report any issues in our [feedback thread](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/13600).

> **Note:** Requires `pip install streamlit[starlette]`

## Update

Starlette will become the default server in 1.57 which will allow configuring IP whitelisting described above without having to install the `starlette` dependencies. The `App` object will also be available in the `st` namespace:

```python
import streamlit as st

...

st.App(...)
```

title: Expose additional theming options
body:
### Checklist

### Summary

Expose additional theming options in `config.toml` to allow better customization of apps. 

### Why?

The current set of [theming options](https://docs.streamlit.io/develop/concepts/configuration/theming) is quite minimal and doesn't allow to create a cohesive theme. A couple of additional options would allow better app customization, especially for aligning Streamlit apps better with company themes. 

### How?

Provide additional theming options that can be defined in `config.toml` like:

- Allow custom fonts (via URL?)
    - Related feature requests: #7274 & #5803

- Allow changing predefined colors used for:
  - Alert elements like `st.info`, `st.warning`, `st.success`, …
  - Chart theme colors used in `altair_chart`, `plotly_chart`, and our internal charts. This is mainly referring to a categorical, diverging, and sequential color palette.
  - Markdown: link color & inline-code color
  - Metrics delta color
  - Markdown: text and background color like red, green , …
 - Default text size
   - maybe only with a couple of predefined options (small / medium / large)
 - Default spacing (to influence padding & gaps used around and within elements)
    - maybe only a couple of predefined options (compact / default)
 - Roundness (radius) of elements
   - maybe only a couple of predefined options (none / small / medium / large)
 - Default border width & color
 - Sidebar text color

For example: 

```js
font: "sans serif" | "serif" | "monospace" | str (custom font URL)

text_size: "small" | "medium" | "large"
radius_size: "none" | "small" | "medium" | "large"
spacing_size: "compact" | "default" | "large"

sidebar_text_color: str (hex color)

success_color: str (hex color) 
warning_color: str (hex color)
info_color: str (hex color)
error_color: str (hex color)

link_color: str (hex color)
inline_code_color: str (hex color)

chart_categorical_colors: list[str] (list of hex colors)
chart_diverging_colors: list[str] (list of hex colors)
chart_sequential_colors: list[str] (list of hex colors)

positive_delta_color: str (hex color)
negative_delta_color: str (hex color)
```

I hate to be the party pooper for such a powerful feature, even though most people believe that custom fonts and colors are just for fun. When you have features like st.write and are compiling automated scripts from random people, those fonts can run difficult to detect code tricks from parsers and linters in various environments. 

With agentic AI already out in the wild, these features go against transparency and ultimately trust in using the more powerful and privacy preserving features of AI in the long run. If you’d like, I can share some ideas and code about how these features can be developed in a safer and easier way.
As part of this effort - any chance the [Figma Components](https://blog.streamlit.io/prototype-your-app-in-figma/) for Streamlit will be updated?
May I suggest a config to hide the app skeleton loading animation?

> May I suggest a config to hide the app skeleton loading animation? 

@user Do you have more information about your use case for hiding the loading skeleton?

I am using Streamlit to create a cross-team dahboarding solution (a thin wrapper around Streamlit basically that adds a bunch of standard stuff in our org; logo, authentication, etc.), allowing the teams to customize the appearance is nice to have, the loading skeleton is just another example of visual elements that characterized Streamlit.
You are probably referring specifically to the app loading skeleton shown when the page is loaded and not the skeletons that are sometimes shown for specific elements that are too slow to load?
Yes precisely @user , since it is the app loading animation, we can't customize it with css injected via `st.markdown`.
It would be great if we could set different colors for the text and background on the sidebar.
https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/5065 is now closed. Did it include the option to set border radius? Or is that still pending?
Yes, we'll have an option to set radius, it's already implemented but currently hidden. We plan to make it official in the next release in early April.

# Update

Hey all! In the next release (1.44) that will go live tomorrow, we're adding the following new theming options:

- linkColor
- codeFont
- headingFont
- baseRadius
- borderColor
- showWidgetBorder
- baseFontSize
- showSidebarBorder
- codeBackgroundColor

Also, you'll be able to define custom fonts (for the existing `font` config option as well as for the new `codeFont` and `headingFont` options) and set the sidebar theming parameters independently from the rest of the app (via `[theme.sidebar]`). 

We'll continue to add a few more config options in the next releases, will update here once we're there!
Is there a plan to support specifying colors for dark and light themes?
Not yet, but we're thinking about doing that at some point soon!

Going to close this! With the next release (1.47) the following theming options will be available in Streamlit:

We will still add a few more options to customize colors in the next few months and might add a few additional theming improvements such as custom dark theme or a `theme.toml` file that you can reuse in apps. Will update in the relevant issues!

title: Newline in st.chat_input not rendering correctly in st.chat_message
body:
### Checklist

### Summary

When using `st.chat_input` to input text with newlines and displaying it with `st.chat_message`, single newlines are not rendered correctly. The newlines are ignored, causing the text to appear as a single line.

1. `st.chat_input`
[image]

2. `st.chat_message`
[image]

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
import streamlit as st

user_input = st.chat_input("Enter your message:")

if user_input:
    with st.chat_message("user"):
        st.markdown(user_input)
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Run the provided code.
2. Enter a message with single newlines in the `st.chat_input` textarea.
3. Submit the message.
4. Observe that the newlines are not rendered in the `st.chat_message` output.

### Expected Behavior

The newlines entered in the `st.chat_input` should be rendered correctly in the `st.chat_message`, preserving the text formatting.

### Current Behavior

The newlines entered in the `st.chat_input` are ignored in the `st.chat_message`, causing the text to appear as a single line.

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

comments.text:
Hi @user,

I believe this is expected behavior. What's happening here is that single newlines are treated as a space in standard markdown.

Note that writing the following renders the same way:
```python
st.markdown("""
aaa
aaa
aaa
"""
)
```

You'll need to either use `st.text` instead of `st.markdown`, process the return value from `st.chat_input` to replace single newlines with double newlines, or do something similar to get things to display as you expect.

@user 
Thank you for your clarification and suggestion! I understand now that this is the expected behavior. I'll try using st.text or processing the return value from st.chat_input as you suggested.

title: Reconnect to existing sessions instead of creating new upon unclean websocket close.
body:
### Checklist

### Summary

Similar to the issues linked, if the network connection is intermittent/flaky the existing session is lost and a new one created, causing unpleasant/unexpected user experience.

See:

https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/1386
https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/1628
https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/6442

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
import streamlit as st
import time

if "counter" not in st.session_state:
    st.session_state.counter = 0

st.write(f"Run count = {st.session_state.counter}")

st.session_state.counter += 1

time.sleep(3)

st.rerun()
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Run the reproducible code example provided in streamlit on one server host.
2. Observe the "Run count = X" increase steadily in a client host different from the server host.
3. Disable the client network connection and wait for some arbitrary time duration.
4. Re-enable the client network connection.
5. Observer the "Run count = X" start from zero again.

### Expected Behavior

The user session should be restored so they may continue where they left off in the face of their network/internet connection being flaky (packet drops, high latency etc) causing unclean websocket close behind the scenes.

### Current Behavior

Observe streamlit warning log "Session with id %s is already connected! Connecting to a new session." and user loses their streamlit session and starts afresh.

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.35
- Python version: 3.10
- Operating System: Windows 11
- Browser: Chrome/Firefox

### Additional Information

I have been able to make a potentially naive code change (will link a PR as a proposal to this issue) which I am unable to run against full test suite because I have been unable to build the streamlit project. I have been able to test partially by modifying the python code in my installed streamlit venv.

title: Use Rye as a package manager to deploy apps on the Streamlit Community Cloud.
body:
### Checklist

### Summary

* Currently, only pipenv, conda, pip, and poetry are supported as package managers for deploying to Streamlit Community Cloud ([reference](https://docs.streamlit.io/deploy/streamlit-community-cloud/deploy-your-app/app-dependencies)).
* My request is to add support for Rye.

### Why?

As [Rye](https://github.com/astral-sh/rye) is gaining popularity, it would be great if Streamlit Community Cloud supported Rye as a package manager.

### How?

When using Rye, package dependencies are described in `requirements.lock`. Therefore, searching for this filename could be part of the solution.

### Additional Context

The current workaround is to create a symbolic link to behave like `pip`:

`ln -s ./requirements.lock requirements.txt`

title: Add Support for Streamlit Configuration in pyproject.toml
body:
### Checklist

### Summary

Currently, Streamlit requires configurations to be set in a `.streamlit/config.toml` file. This proposal aims to enhance Streamlit by allowing users to specify their configurations directly in the `pyproject.toml` file. This change simplifies project setup by consolidating configurations in one place, reducing the need for multiple configuration files.

### Why?

Integrating Streamlit configuration into `pyproject.toml` makes project setup more straightforward, especially for users managing their projects with [Poetry](https://python-poetry.org). It eliminates the need for an additional `.streamlit/config.toml` file, reducing file clutter and centralizing configuration management.

### How?

The implementation requires modifying the `get_config_options` function. The modification will involve adding logic to read the `pyproject.toml` file, extracting Streamlit configuration from the _[tool.streamlit]_ section, and integrating these settings with the existing configuration sources. The function will check for the presence of `pyproject.toml`, parse it if available, and merge its contents with the current configuration options, ensuring that configurations specified in `pyproject.toml` take precedence where applicable.

### Additional Context

title: Add a user entrypoint executed on startup before page loding
body:
### Checklist

### Summary

When running a streamlit application, it is not possible to execute a startup script to modify some internal workings of streamlit application or to execute a user custom action. This issue is to allow it.

### Why?

There are two motivations for this feature. First one is to execute a user defined background job to do processes and or other work. Currently, when the intention is to execute another background task, either a healthcheck, API updater, or some watchdog, it is not really possible to do or user has to execute separate process by himself. For example, in our environment the `entrypoint.sh` contains `multirun 'streamlit' 'some other process'` which executes multiple applications and then these application use a shared file for communication. It would be much simple to use python threads (in our case). Related: https://discuss.streamlit.io/t/is-there-a-way-to-have-a-process-run-in-the-background-independently-of-the-page-im-using/69172 , https://discuss.streamlit.io/t/how-to-separate-fetching-data-from-user-interaction/46007 . 

The other motivation is to mask or improve features of streamlit on the fly by allowing users to execute a custom init script. For example the functionality of https://bartbroere.eu/2024/03/27/adding-custom-tornado-handlers-to-streamlit/ could be implemented by overwriting `streamlit.web.server.Server = CustomServer`. In particular, this way would easily allow, overall as a hack, to implement custom HTTP requests the way mentioned in https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/439 .

### How?

I propose to introduce a new option `init` to configuration file tht will point to a module path executed at startup.

    [server]
    init = startup:cli

Then before executing `bootstrap.run` I propose to import the module and execute the function specified by the user, at https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/blob/develop/lib/streamlit/web/bootstrap.py :
 
```
import importlib

def _run_init_script():
    init = config.get_option("server.init")
    if init:
        mod, func = init.split(":")
        getattr(importlib.import_module(mod), func)()

def run(
    main_script_path: str,
    is_hello: bool,
    args: list[str],
    flag_options: dict[str, Any],
) -> None:
    """Run a script in a separate thread and start a server for the app.

    This starts a blocking asyncio eventloop.
    """
    _fix_sys_path(main_script_path)
    _fix_tornado_crash()
    _fix_sys_argv(main_script_path, args)
    _fix_pydeck_mapbox_api_warning()
    _fix_pydantic_duplicate_validators_error()
    _install_config_watchers(flag_options)
    _run_init_script()

    # Create the server. It won't start running yet.
    server = Server(main_script_path, is_hello)

    .... # rest of run()
```

### Additional Context

Hi.

> the entrypoint page in https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/8388 can be used for such purpose?

From the link:

> ... the contents of streamlit_app.py will automatically run before every page ...

No. The streamlit_app.py there is loaded when __user__ loads the website. I do not want any user interaction. If application starts, it is started, the entrypoint should execute at the time I type `streamlit` in the terminal, not after user interaction.

I also miss such a feature.
I want to prefetch and cache resources right after the start of the app and not on the first page loading.

Can this be a workaround? Behind `venv/bin/streamlit` the real CLI entrypoint `main()` is just a `click` decorated function.

I tried this in a simple streamlit app, [demo of my lib](https://github.com/jokester/streamlit-concurrency/) and everything seemed to work.

```sh
❯ cat run.py
# like venv/bin/streamlit but prepending custom code
from streamlit.web.cli import main

print(f"before main()")  # get printed
main()
print(f"after main()")  # never printed in Ctrl-C

❯ venv/bin/python run.py run streamlit-concurrency.py
before main()

  You can now view your Streamlit app in your browser.

  Local URL: http://localhost:8501
  Network URL: http://MASKED:8501

2025-05-01 12:17:08,748 INFO ScriptRunner.scriptThread streamlit_concurrency.demo.bootstrap - <module>: streamlit_concurrency.demo loaded
^C  Stopping...
```

## Update

Exciting news 🎉 Starting with **Streamlit 1.53**, we've added experimental lifespan hooks via the new ASGI/Starlette integration.

You can now run startup code (like cache pre-warming) before accepting connections:

```python
from contextlib import asynccontextmanager
from streamlit.starlette import App

@user
async def lifespan(app):
    # Startup: runs BEFORE first user connects
    print("🚀 Pre-warming caches...")

    # Call your @st.cache_resource functions here
    from myapp.cache import load_ml_model, init_db_pool
    load_ml_model()   # Populates cache
    init_db_pool()    # Ready for connections

    print("✅ Ready!")
    yield

    print("👋 Shutting down...")

app = App("main.py", lifespan=lifespan)
```

First users get instant results instead of waiting for slow initialization!

We'd love your feedback on this feature! Please try it out and report any issues in our [feedback thread](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/13600).

> **Note:** Requires `pip install streamlit[starlette]`

## Update

Starlette will become the default server in 1.57 which will make it possible to run startup code (like cache pre-warming) before accepting connections as described above without having to install the `starlette` dependencies. The `App` object will also be available in the `st` namespace:

```python
import streamlit as st

...

st.App(...)
```

Hey @user Thank you for the issue! This error seems very strange to me. I would need to investigate with Snowflake on why it's unable to identify the default connection.

Hey @user , as you pointed out we assume today that an app using SnowflakeConnection will supply some arguments through either Streamlit secrets.toml or Snowflake connections.toml

[connections.snowflake]

```
