comments.text:
Thanks @user for taking your time to open the issue with a detailed description and screen recording! I was able to reproduce it.
Just to make this clear for fellow readers and future reference: the _state_ of the widgets is persisted in the backend as well as in the web app. The "only" thing that happens is that the page is scrolled to the top. This is correct, right @user?

:information_source: Fix:
It looks like that if you set `show_spinner=False` for the `@st.cache_data` decorator in `@st.cache_data(ttl=3, show_spinner=True)`, the issue goes away. Could you please try that out and confirm it?

---

It seems to come from the `st.empty` element we create in the spinner [here](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/blob/develop/lib/streamlit/elements/spinner.py#L54), as the issue goes away also when I comment it out and that `empty` message is never sent.
This `empty` element in `st.spinner` has caused some other issues in the past (see https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/9951), because the amount of empty messages slowed down the browser. @user @user We should start to think about whether we can refactor `st.spinner` and get rid of the implicit `empty` message that is causing some issues, especially with the built-in spinner of the `cache` functions.

> We should start to think about whether we can refactor st.spinner and get rid of the implicit empty message that is causing some issues, especially with the built-in spinner of the cache functions.

IMO we should try to refactor spinner to not be part of the full delta tree logic and introduce a more temporary mechanism for placing it at a specific delta position in our frontend -> this would also resolve some of the stale issues we have with spinner, especially in combination with `chat_message`, e.g.:

- https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/9239
- https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/2820
Yeah that would be fantastic! Will create a Notion project so we keep this in mind.
That sounds like a good idea! And thanks for creating the project 😊👍

> Thanks [@user](https://github.com/stefanadelbert) for taking your time to open the issue with a detailed description and screen recording! I was able to reproduce it. Just to make this clear for fellow readers and future reference: the _state_ of the widgets is persisted in the backend as well as in the web app. The "only" thing that happens is that the page is scrolled to the top. This is correct, right [@user](https://github.com/stefanadelbert)?

- The widget state is not lost, e.g. the value of a a text_input or the selected items of a multiselect remain intact
- The page is scrolled to the top
- But, the active element (the one that was being being edited at the time) is lost, e.g. if a text_input widget is being edited and "enter" is pressed then that widget should remain the active widget, but that "context" is lost

🙏 Thank you for the quick turn around on this. I will get back to you when I've tested with the spinner disabled.

 page itself.

title: The error message for adding over 100 viewers to a streamlit community cloud app does not persist long enough
body:
### Checklist

### Summary

If you add over 100 emails to the list of viewers in an app's App settings > Sharing > Invite viewers by email box

(nota bene: the description of this box says "Enter a comma-separated list of emails.", but it should actually say "Enter a comma- or whitespace-separated list of emails.", in my experience)

an error message will appear, telling you that this is not allowed, and the new email list will not save. However, the window will still close, as though your changes did save, and therefore you can't read the error message!

display error message and not close

title: Page Refresh detection and data persistance between refresh page
body:
### Checklist

### Summary

Currently, 
- There is no way to detect page refresh 
- There is no way to persists data between page refresh

### Why?

I want to open serial port manually and it should be keep opened serial port object, even user press page refresh button on browser. secondly it should close it on page exist.

### How?

Currently i am using @st.cache_resource to open it by opening fixed serial port and close it using atexit.register(app_closed)

title: Feedback Emojis Not Appearing in Safari After Deployment (Works Fine Locally and in Chrome)
body:
### Checklist

### Summary

I’ve built a chatbot application using Streamlit, and I’m gathering user feedback via the `streamlit_feedback` method. The feedback is collected through clickable happy and sad emoji buttons that work perfectly on both Chrome and Safari when running locally. However, after deploying the app in my company's environment, the feedback emojis fail to appear in Safari, even though they still function correctly in Chrome.

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
feedback = streamlit_feedback(
            feedback_type="faces",
            # on_submit=_submit_feedback,
            key=f"feedback_{st.session_state.feedback_key}",
            optional_text_label="Please provide some more information"
        )
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Deploy a Streamlit app using the streamlit_feedback method to gather feedback with emoji buttons.
2. Access the deployed app on Safari (version - 17.2).
3. The emoji buttons do not render or are invisible in the Safari browser.
4. Access the same deployed app in Chrome, where the emojis appear and work as expected.

### Expected Behavior

The feedback emojis (happy and sad) should appear in both Chrome and Safari when the app is deployed.

### Current Behavior

The feedback emojis are not visible in Safari, although they work perfectly in Chrome. The issue only occurs in the deployed environment (locally works fine in both browsers).

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.38.0
- streamlit-feedback: 0.1.3
- Python version: 3.12
- Operating System: MacOS 
- Deployment Environment: AWS cloud
- Browser: Safari

### Additional Information

- The issue is only present in Safari on the deployed environment.
- Local development works fine in both Chrome and Safari.
- Other interactive elements in Streamlit seem unaffected by this issue.
- Clearing cache and reloading does not resolve the issue in Safari.

comments.text:
Hey @user, thank you for opening this issue!
The "provider" is just a identifier in secrets.toml that then you use as a argument in `st.login` function

So you can configure multiple providers that in reality works with the same Identity Provider (e.g. Microsoft), but just different registered apps/flows. 

So modify your secrets a little bit:
```
[auth.microsoftapp1]
redirect_uri = "http://localhost:8502/oauth2callback"
client_id = ""
client_secret = ""
server_metadata_url = "https://<>.b2clogin.com/b2cdebugger.onmicrosoft.com/<sign-in-user-flow>/v2.0/.well-known/openid-configuration"

[auth.microsoftapp2]

redirect_uri = "http://localhost:8502/oauth2callback"
client_id = ""
client_secret = ""
server_metadata_url = "https://<>.b2clogin.com/b2cdebugger.onmicrosoft.com/<sign-up-user-flow>/v2.0/.well-known/openid-configuration"
```
Should work correctly, you just need to use either `st.login(provider="microsoftapp1")` or st.login(provider="microsoftapp2") in your Stremalit app code.

title: Support .env files for configuration
body:
### Checklist

### Summary

Configuration options provided through the environment are ignored by streamlit and default are used instead.

This directly contradicts intended behaviour:
- As per described the [configuration options](https://docs.streamlit.io/develop/concepts/configuration/options)
- As per described per option when running `streamlit run --help`

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
`.env`
.env
# ? Streamlit
STREAMLIT_GLOBAL_DEVELOPMENT_MODE=False

## ? Server variables
STREAMLIT_SERVER_HOST='localhost'
STREAMLIT_SERVER_PORT=80
STREAMLIT_SERVER_MAX_UPLOAD_SIZE=1000
STREAMLIT_SERVER_ENABLE_STATIC_SERVING=True

## ? Theme variables
STREAMLIT_BROWSER_SERVER_ADDRESS='localhost'
STREAMLIT_BROWSER_SERVER_PORT=80
STREAMLIT_BROWSER_GATHER_USAGE_STATS=False

## ? Theme variables
STREAMLIT_THEME_BASE="dark"
STREAMLIT_THEME_PRIMARY_COLOR="#5c49e1"
STREAMLIT_THEME_BACKGROUND_COLOR="#0E1117"
STREAMLIT_THEME_SECONDARY_BACKGROUND_COLOR="#373e75"
STREAMLIT_THEME_TEXT_COLOR="#FAFAFA"

`main.py`

import os
import streamlit as st
from dotenv import load_dotenv

load_dotenv()

options = [
    "global.developmentMode",
    "server.address",
    "server.port",
    "server.maxUploadSize",
    "server.enableStaticServing",
    "browser.serverAddress",
    "browser.serverPort",
    "browser.gatherUsageStats",
    "theme.base",
    "theme.primaryColor",
    "theme.backgroundColor",
    "theme.secondaryBackgroundColor",
    "theme.textColor"
]

st.header("Variables matching `STREAMLIT_*` in ENV")
env_matches = []
for entry in os.environ:
    if "STREAMLIT" in entry:
        env_matches.append(f"{entry}={os.getenv(entry)}")
st.write(env_matches)

st.header("Used variables, as read by `st.get_option()`")
option_matches = []
for option in options:
    option_matches.append(f"{option}={st.get_option(option)}")
st.write(option_matches)
```

### Steps To Reproduce

With the folder structure:
```
/error_to_reproduce
   /main.py
   /.env
```

3. Create a `virtualenv` and activate it: `python -m venv venv && source venv/bin/activate`
4. Install dependencies: `pip3 install streamlit python-dotenv`
5. Execute application `streamlit run main.py`

### Expected Behavior

The expected behaviour would be for streamlit to use the supplied environment variables:
- As per described in the [configuration options](https://docs.streamlit.io/develop/concepts/configuration/options)
- As per described per option when running `streamlit run --help`
  - See environment examples in image:
    [image]

### Current Behavior

The current behaviour is that the configuration options set in the environment are ignored for defaults. See example using the provided reproducible steps below.
[image]

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

- Operating System: Linux
  - Distribution `Pop!_OS 22.04 LTS x86_64`

After further debugging, it has become clear to me, that this happens because streamlit expects the `STREAMLIT_*` env variables to be pre-exported, otherwise it will use defaults. This means that `.env` files cannot be used for `STREAMLIT_*` variables which is not clear from the ambiguous nature they are described in the docs and help-string(s).

- Explicitly declaring `ENV STREAMLIT_*` for each variable in the Dockerfile → ✅ it will use the `STREAMLIT_*` variables

However, this is not inline with expected behaviour or most common use-cases where `.env` is used instead 😕

Hey @user Thanks for the issue! You are correct. We don't support .env. I'm going to modify this to an enhancement request.

Our recommended way is to use the [config.toml](https://docs.streamlit.io/develop/api-reference/configuration/config.toml) file You can also set the env variables before like you mentioned above. Hope that helps!

@user Let's have @user 's take on whether there is a feature to support this. I personally would prefer not to have multiple ways for configuration since the `config.toml` should work well. Is there a problem with that solution or is it a convenience ask?

Yeah I agree that we probably don't want to have a separate way to set config options but just keep it in `config.toml`. 

The behavior above also seems pretty intuitive and expected to me. Streamlit loads its config options when it starts, so it uses defaults, then the Python code loads the `.env` file, which sets the environment variables, but at this point it doesn't affect Streamlit anymore. We also note [here](https://docs.streamlit.io/develop/concepts/configuration/options) in the blue info box at the top that in order for changes in config options to take effect, you need to restart Streamlit (except for theming config options).
Got it, thanks for the answer! Then it turns out that Isuue is closed?

> [@user](https://github.com/ashm-dev) Let's have [@user](https://github.com/jrieke) 's take on whether there is a feature to support this. I personally would prefer not to have multiple ways for configuration since the `config.toml` should work well. Is there a problem with that solution or is it a convenience ask?

I can see two clear issues:
1. It conflicts with expected behaviour as per stated in docs and CLI tooltips. The way these are currently written is ambiguous and reads as if `.env` is supported.
2. It conflicts with expected behaviour by hosting/infra providers for containerized deployments such as Portainer, Dokku, Caprover (etc) which limit deployments to a `docker-compose` and a `.env` (or helm chart if in k8s), meaning you often cannot upload arbitrary files, especially not per library/sdk/framework used.

As a result of the abovementioned, you cannot add streamlits settings alongside the rest of the application & service variables in `.env`, meaning you **must** do one of the following work-a-rounds:
- Add `config.toml` to Dockerfile, locking it to the image and with the rest of the variables being in .env (antipattern)
- Explicitly declare and export all of streamlits settings in the Dockerfile, with the rest being in `.env` (messy code + antipattern)
- Explicitly add all of streamlits non-default settings _and only those_ directly on the `docker-compose` file (antipattern)
- Put all application variables on `docker-compose` file (highly inconvenient, would require rewrites for many projects).

While I understand Streamlit cannot account for everything, I do hope supporting docker/docker-compose without work-a-rounds and antipatterns can be expected.

As a minimum, I would strongly recommend explicitly stating on the configuration page and for the CLI tooltips that `.env` is not supported, and that environment variables must be declared either directly in the `Dockerfile` or 1-by-1 for the environment itself.

Or in short; The problem is that the docs & CLI tooltips imply support for `.env`, which is how most people set their environment variables, while not actually supporting `.env`. This causes unnecessary confusion, issues and effort when deploying an application using `streamlit`, as its primary way of configuration is incompatible with many forms of container deployments without messy work-a-rounds.

> It conflicts with expected behaviour as per stated in docs and CLI tooltips. The way these are currently written is ambiguous and reads as if .env is supported.

I'm still not really sure why it might be intuitive that Streamlit supports `.env` files, though? If you run a Python script with `python my_script.py`, it will also not consider `.env` files in your directory at startup. Streamlit just acts in the same way. 

And agree we can keep this issue open :)

- For the CLI, you can run `streamlit run --help` and the corresponding env var per option is listed, but it's never mentioned that `.env` isn't supported. (Which seems to be the case overall, hence the ambiguity)

> I'm still not really sure why it might be intuitive that Streamlit supports .env files, though? If you run a Python script with python my_script.py, it will also not consider .env files in your directory at startup. Streamlit just acts in the same way.

While comparing expected behaviour from a python script, to that of a library or full web application is a bit of comparing apples & oranges, this just isn't the case when using other common frameworks in Python:
- Flask supports `.env` (using `python-dotenv` I think?)
- Django supports `.env` with plugins
- FastAPI supports `.env` (using Pydantic BaseSettings)
- Dash (By Plotly) supports `.env`
(I _really_ can go on...)

And even if you run a standalone python script, you can load `.env` with [python-dotenv](https://pypi.org/project/python-dotenv/) which how a lot of frameworks and individual projects* do it. This, however, doesn't work with streamlit either.

Having support for `.env` is common enough that it's an expected default for many platforms and consumers alike, making streamlit the 'odd one out' in this case.

> When you have one env var (or a few), these can be exported. When you have multiple, it's default & assumed that these go in .env [See Step 3](https://docs.streamlit.io/develop/concepts/configuration/options)
For the CLI, you can run streamlit run --help and the corresponding env var per option is listed, but it's never mentioned that .env isn't supported. (Which seems to be the case overall, hence the ambiguity)

Thanks for finding these! I don't really see in these examples how we imply that `.env` would be supported – I mean we even explicitly show exported env variables in the docs page you linked. But FYI @user in case you think we should change anything on that page or mention that `.env` files aren't supported, up to you!

> Flask supports .env (using python-dotenv I think?)
Django supports .env with plugins
FastAPI supports .env (using Pydantic BaseSettings)
Dash (By Plotly) supports .env
(I really can go on...)

Thanks for these examples, that's great context. We usually try to stick as close as possible to raw Python behavior. I'll leave this issue open and if we see that there's more demand/upvotes, I'm happy to have a closer look at these examples and if we want to align with them. I think there might also be a great chance to just write a small plugin/wrapper for streamlit that loads from a `.env` file and passes config options from there to Streamlit, similar to how e.g. it also works for Django.

title: v1.42.0 - st.login() Error: Proof Key for Code Exchange is required for cross-origin authorization code redemption.
body:
### Checklist

### Summary

I have SSO setup in Azure (Microsoft EntraID) as a Single Page Application (SPA).  When I try to authenticate, it returns the following error:

`AADSTS9002325: Proof Key for Code Exchange is required for cross-origin authorization code redemption.`

The [research ](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/answers/questions/1626192/how-to-fix-aadsts9002325-proof-key-for-code-exchan) I've found suggests this is because the Openid auth is not using the PKCE flow.

Is this a bug in my code, in the implementation of the new streamlit feature, or not supported?  If not supported, adding SPA support would be very much appreciated.

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
secrets.toml

[auth]
redirect_uri = "https://server.mydomain.com:8501/oauth2/callback"
cookie_secret = "xxxxREDACTEDxxxx"
client_id = "xxxxREDACTEDxxxx"
client_secret = "xxxxREDACTEDxxxx"
server_metadata_url = "https://login.microsoftonline.com/{myTennantIDHere}/v2.0/.well-known/openid-configuration"

client_kwargs = { "prompt" = "login", "scope" = ""xxxxREDACTEDxxxx"/.default" }

app.py

import streamlit as st

if not st.experimental_user.is_logged_in:
    if st.button("Log in with 3M Azure SSO"):
        st.login()
    st.stop()

if st.button("Log out"):
    st.logout()
st.markdown(f"Welcome! {st.experimental_user.name}")
```

### Steps To Reproduce

[image]

Setup a "Single Page Application" in MS Azure
- Input redirect_uri
- copy client_id 
- copy client_secret
- enter corresponding values into `.streamlit/secrets.toml`

Run included streamlit app.py
- button is rendered to sign in
- click button, redirected to MS Azure SSO
- Enter valid user/pass
- MS spits out error:
```
Sorry, but we’re having trouble signing you in.

AADSTS9002325: Proof Key for Code Exchange is required for cross-origin authorization code redemption.
```

### Expected Behavior

I'd expect SPA registrations to work with this auth tool.  SPAs seem to be much easier to setup than Web platforms (at least in my experience).

If you won't be supporting SPA's, then it would be good to note in the documentation for clarification so users setup the right kind of SSO integration.

### Current Behavior

Error message from MS Azure at signin:
```
AADSTS9002325: Proof Key for Code Exchange is required for cross-origin authorization code redemption.
```

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version:  1.42.0
- Python version: 3.12.8
- Operating System:  Linux (RHEL9)
- Browser: Chrome/Edge (latest at time of submission)

No streamlit error, SSO provider is where the error manifests, and does not send back to streamlit app due to error during auth process.

body:
### Checklist

### Summary

Hi everyone, hope you all are doing well.
I have been using Streamlit in some little projects and upscaled it to bigger projects over the time, and I have to say it works very well with my type of use. 
Recently I had an idea to make a hub (one or two Streamlit pages, one welcome page and one with all apps to choose which to use) for my Streamlit apps. So I started looking into Streamlit docs to see if it already had this server/hub feature builded into it, I found it to not be the case.
In my reaserch I found an issue adressed to the same requirement (Issue #2709) and apparently te user Jayden-Elliott made a project in a repo named streamlit-server that brings this feature to life, but I still wanted it to be integrated with all the Streamlit vast enviroment.

### Why?

Make a hub that contains all your created apps with the possibility of making user authentication, put text and images to present the hub and host all of your apps inside of it. 

### How?

I think in this case it is more of structure case than a st command case, I think it like the "Pages" folder, a structure in a folder that categorizes it as the hub like Jayden made it. 

### Additional Context

https://github.com/Jayden-Elliott/streamlit-server

title: Ensure `user_key` is a string in `compute_and_register_element_id`
body:
### Checklist

### Summary

On Mac Os,
with Python 3.9.6
with streamlit version 1.42.0

I encountered the bug

```
venv/lib/python3.9/site-packages/streamlit/elements/lib/utils.py", line 161, in _compute_element_id
    h.update(user_key.encode("utf-8"))
AttributeError: 'int' object has no attribute 'encode'
```
I managed to make a quick fix on my machine by replacing this line, in the function _compute_element_id

https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/blob/c23392e8730e6fd810be8cf5f6d559459f913566/lib/streamlit/elements/lib/utils.py#L174

by

```python
h.update(str(user_key).encode("utf-8"))
```

However I guess that the real fix should be made in one of the caller functions, that provides an int instead of a string.

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
import streamlit as st
from streamlit.web.server import routes
import warnings
import sys
import os
import json
import logging
from msal_streamlit_authentication import msal_authentication

warnings.filterwarnings("ignore")
routes.ALLOWED_MESSAGE_ORIGINS = "[]"
st.set_page_config(layout="wide")

# these environment variables do not have to be defined to reproduce bug
client_id = os.getenv("API_CLIENT_ID") 
tenand_id = os.getenv("AAD_TENANT_ID") 
scopes = [f"api://{client_id}/access_as_user"]

def get_token(debug_token: bool = False):
    value = msal_authentication(
        auth={
            "clientId": client_id,
            "authority": f"https://login.microsoftonline.com/{tenand_id}",
            "redirectUri": "/",
            "postLogoutRedirectUri": "/",
        },
        cache={"cacheLocation": "sessionStorage", "storeAuthStateInCookie": False},
        login_request={"scopes": scopes},
        key=1,
    )

    if debug_token:
        with open("./token.json", "w") as tkf:
            json.dump(value, tkf)
    return value

def get_user(token: dict) -> str:
    username = "Anonymous"
    try:
        return token["account"]["username"]
    except Exception as msg:
        logging.warning(msg)
        return username

def main():
    st.sidebar.title("Hello")
    st.session_state.clicked = False

if __name__ == "__main__":
    st.title("My App")
    arguments_list = sys.argv
    token = get_token()
    if token:
        username = get_user(token)
        st.write("Welcome", username)
        if username:
            main()
```

### Steps To Reproduce

mkdir repro_bug
cd repro_bug

paste the Reproducible Code Example into a new file called app.py

python3.9 -m venv venv
source venv/bin/activate
pip install --upgrade pip
pip install streamlit==1.42.0 msal-streamlit-authentication==1.1.0 dotenv
streamlit run app.py

### Expected Behavior

I expect the SSO window to show.

### Current Behavior

I have error messages displayed in my browser and no SSO window appears.

```
venv/lib/python3.9/site-packages/streamlit/elements/lib/utils.py", line 161, in _compute_element_id
    h.update(user_key.encode("utf-8"))
AttributeError: 'int' object has no attribute 'encode'
```

- [x] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

- Python version: 3.9.6
- Operating System: Mac Os 15.3
- Browser: Brave

title: Default `set_page_config` through `.streamlit/config.toml`
body:
### Checklist

### Summary

Currently, when setting `st.set_page_config()` with `page_title` and `page_icon`, Streamlit still displays the default "Streamlit" title and icon during the initial loading phase. This behavior can be disruptive for larger web applications where branding consistency is important. 

It would be useful to define default values for `set_page_config` parameters inside `.streamlit/config.toml`, ensuring that even before `st.set_page_config()` is explicitly called in a script, the title and icon match the expected defaults.

### Why?

I'm always frustrated when the page first loads with the Streamlit default title and icon, even though I have set my own values using `st.set_page_config()`. This creates an unpolished user experience, especially for production-ready applications.

### How?

Introduce the ability to specify default values for `page_title`, `page_icon`, `layout`, and other `st.set_page_config` parameters inside `.streamlit/config.toml`. If a user does not call `st.set_page_config()` in their script, Streamlit should use these defaults from the config file instead of falling back to "Streamlit" and the default icon.

For example, the `.streamlit/config.toml` file could support:
```toml
[theme]
defaultPageTitle = "My App"
defaultPageIcon = "favicon.png"
```

### Additional Context

title: Cannot serve audio file when its served behind a reverse proxy
body:
### Checklist

### Summary

`st.audio` creates a HTML5 audio widget with the URL of the audio file, but since such URL is opened by streamlit in advance, both the browser and streamlit must access to the audio resource the same way. This is not possible when running both streamlit and the software serving the audio file behind a reverse proxy.

Workarounds:
- read the audiofile from within streamlit and pass it as bytes to `st.audio` (which means having to keep the whole file in memory)
- inject custom HTML `st.html(f'<audio src="{file_url}" controls />')`

Couldn't streamlit just create an audio widget without to opening the file in advance? If that is not possible, can the URL be rewritten before being sent to the browser?

comments.text:
Hello @user thank you for opening this issue!

If you don't want to load a file into the memory, `st.audio` widget could accept a URL and serve file from there. 

If you upload an audio file into S3, then you can use:

```st.audio(data=YOUR_S3_URL)```

and streamlit will serve it from there (or from any other source that could serve a file). 
See: https://docs.streamlit.io/develop/api-reference/media/st.audio

Passing the URL would not work, because both Streamlit and the server hosting the assets are behind a reverse proxy. The browser and Streamlit use two different URL to access to the same resource. Streamlit needs to get the audio (for some reason) and then create the HTML code for the `audio` tag which includes the very same URL, used behind the reverse proxy, which is not valid outside.

```mermaid
graph LR
  browser[Browser]
  subgraph OuterBox [Private network]
    streamlit[Streamlit]
    webserver[Audio files]
    reverseproxy[Reverse proxy]
  end
  streamlit --> webserver
  reverseproxy --> streamlit
  reverseproxy --> webserver
  browser --> reverseproxy
```

title: Custom Font Support doesn't work on 1.43
body:
### Checklist

### Summary

I have an app that uses custom fonts, its currently deployed to Azure using 1.41. I was about to push a new branch today and though it would be good time to update to 1.43 (I wanted that timezone support). I did a pip install --upgrade streamlit in my local venv. When i launched the app under 1.43 my custom font was gone. I used pip to go back to 1.41 and the font was correctly rendered again. When i launched in 1.43 i didn’t get the standard streamlit font, i instead got some ‘Time New Roman -like’ serif font, so i assume its trying to render my custom font but can’t and falling back to the browser default.

Another user at https://discuss.streamlit.io/t/custom-fonts-stopped-working-in-1-43/94177 has confirmed that rolling back to 1.42 also resolves the issue.

### Reproducible Code Example

[[image]](https://issues.streamlitapp.com/?issue=gh-10714)

```Python
css_path = 'assets/styles/style.css'
with open(css_path) as css:
        st.markdown(f'<style>{css.read()}</style>', unsafe_allow_html=True)
```
style.css:
```
@user {
    font-family: 'My Custom Font';
    src: url('../fonts/my_custom_font.otf') format('opentype');
}
h1 {
    font-family: 'My Custom Font', sans-serif !important;
}

}

install 1.43, use CSS to inject custom font

### Expected Behavior

Custom font to be rendered in browser

Default HTML serif font is rendered by the browser

comments.text:
Hey, @user. We're actually in the process of adjusting the sleep logic for Streamlit Community Cloud apps _at this very moment_ and you may be noticing one of the changes we're enacting.

The latest logic is: make the app go to sleep after 12h of inactivity.

So maybe your auto-committer is set to an interval longer than 12h? 

Also be aware that we may soon change the definition of "activity" to "user activity" rather than "user activity or commits". And although we don't currently have any plans to block users from programmaticaly keeping their apps up, I can't promise we won't start trying to block them at some point. After all, Streamlit Community Cloud is meant as a free space for the community to share what they're building, and without strong guard rails we'll quickly enter a [tragedy of the commons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tragedy_of_the_commons) scenario.

If you're using Community Cloud for professional purposes, consider a paid solution, like [Snowflake](https://signup.snowflake.com/?utm_source=streamlit&utm_medium=referral&utm_campaign=main&utm_content=-ss-github-issue). These can provide much stronger guarantees around uptime, stability, security, and performance.

title: HTTPS Production Environment Support
body:
### Checklist

### Summary

Streamlit [docs](https://docs.streamlit.io/develop/api-reference/configuration/config.toml) provide HTTPS support but don't recommend hosting in a prod environment due to lack of testing: "'DO NOT USE THIS OPTION IN A PRODUCTION ENVIRONMENT. It has not gone through security audits or performance tests." I would like to see these tests happen as the alternative would be to use a reverse proxy like nginx but with a SSL connection a lot of the diverse documentation online has recommended to disable CORS and the XSRF functionality in the config.toml file:     --server.enableCORS=false --server.enableXsrfProtection=false. This seems like a greater security risk than just using the inhouse HTTPS Support provided [here](https://docs.streamlit.io/develop/concepts/configuration/https-support) and I would like to see this feature fully ready for an enterprise production grade application.

### Why?

I've been greatly frustrated by the documentation to use a reverse proxy like nginx since it is all very diverse in how people configure there .conf files, a lot of the ubuntu documentation doesn't pair well with RHEL, and there's no clear explanation of the steps in why something should be set up the way it is in the examples I've seen. The need to disable CORS and Xsrf for SSL to work also worries me about whether it would be more secure to ignore the documentation warning and just use streamlits in house Server SSL features. Security should be of utmost importance and I wish Streamlit would put more eggs in the HTTPS basket.

### How?

In the config.toml file of the .streamlit directory I would like to see more support for sslCertFile & sslKeyFile to be production grade ready.

### Additional Context

Raising issue here as instructed from my discussion post https://discuss.streamlit.io/t/updates-on-streamlits-in-house-https-hosting/94710?u=oaklius

title: Make ODBC Driver 18 for SQL Server available in Community Cloud
body:
### Checklist

### Summary

Streamlit Community Cloud [comes with ODBC Driver for SQL Server pre-installed](https://docs.streamlit.io/develop/tutorials/databases/mssql#add-pyodbc-to-your-requirements-file) (super helpful, thanks!). The version that is available is version 17. [Version 18 of the driver is now available](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/sql/connect/odbc/download-odbc-driver-for-sql-server?view=sql-server-ver16).

### Why?

a. Always good to support the latest version of software
b. [The driver name needs specifying when connecting using `pyodbc`](https://docs.sqlalchemy.org/en/20/dialects/mssql.html#connecting-to-pyodbc). Many users will have version 18 installed locally - making version 18 available on Community Cloud will mean there's no need to tweak variables between local + deployed

### How?

Main proposal: Install ODBC Driver 18 for SQL Server by default to the Community Cloud environment

Alternative proposal: Allow users to install this themselves using `packages.txt`. This doesn't work currently as the driver has an EULA which (AFAIK) there's no way of accepting. But is there a way that the operation of `packages.txt` can be tweaked so that EULAs like this can be accepted? In GitHub Actions this is handled by running `sudo ACCEPT_EULA=Y apt-get install msodbcsql18 -y`.

title: Add QR code for Network URL access in Streamlit app launch message
body:
### Checklist

### Summary

When launching a Streamlit app, display a QR code in the terminal that encodes the Network URL, allowing users to quickly access the app on mobile devices by scanning the code.

### Why?

Currently, when launching a Streamlit app, users see text URLs (Local and Network) in the terminal. While copying the Network URL is straightforward on the same device, accessing the app from a mobile device requires manually typing the URL, which is error-prone and time-consuming. Many modern development tools (like npm, Vite, etc.) already provide QR codes in the terminal for quick access from secondary devices. Adding this feature would improve the developer experience and align Streamlit with current developer tool standards.

### How?

1. When a Streamlit app is launched, generate a QR code that encodes the Network URL
2. Display this QR code in the terminal alongside the existing text URLs
3. Use a terminal-friendly ASCII or Unicode QR code representation that works across different terminal environments
4. Ensure the QR code size is reasonable for standard terminal dimensions
5. Consider making this feature optional through a configuration setting (e.g., `--show-qr-code` flag or in `.streamlit/config.toml`)

### Additional Context

This feature would be particularly useful for:

- Mobile-first development workflows
- Testing responsive designs
- Demonstrations and presentations where quickly sharing access is important
- Collaborative development environments

Similar implementations can be found in:

- npm (with --qr flag)
- Vite development server
- Vue CLI development server

The implementation could leverage existing QR code generation libraries to minimize development effort.

comments.text:
Hi @user , thank you for filing an issue!

There were a few changes between 1.43.x and 1.44.0 around Multipage Apps and general React rendering. With that said, it would be very helpful if you could help us by providing some reproducible code here to help us narrow down the issue. Thank you in advance!
@user Also, if there are any errors (whether from Python or the browser console) you can provide us with, that would also be helpful. Thanks again!

Not seeing any errors, just stuff isn't rendering where it should

Here's a mockup I just created - it's using the newest method of st.navigation, pg.run. It actually shows a different issue in that the sidebar itself isn't rendering

I would expect to see a sidebar with Metrics as a group and Summary as a page, as well as both "Test Sidebar" and "Summary" in the main area of the page (instead of just "Test Sidebar")

[https://testsidebarpages-gm2uwcr4tjsrzvebwdkgnp.streamlit.app/](url)
[https://github.com/msquaredds/TestSidebarPages](url)

@user Thank you for the test repo! That was very helpful. There are 2 things here that contribute to the behavior observed

1. There was a change in 1.44.0 where `__page__` is now `__main__`. That explains why the `Summary` text isn't rendering in the given example. Changing [the conditional check](https://github.com/msquaredds/TestSidebarPages/blob/main/pages/0_Summary.py#L8) to use `__main__` will fix this.
2. In terms of the Sidebar not rendering with just a single page in the navigation, this is logic that has been around for a while and is not new in 1.44.0. Adding a second page will show the Sidebar.

I spoke with the team and the change from `__page__` to `__main__` is an intentional implementation change. We think this is overall the right move and wish to keep it, but if anyone has a valid use case for maintaining `__page__`, please let us know here!

Got it, that makes sense on both fronts. I've never used a single page in the navigation, I had just tried to make the app as simple as possible. I made the change from `__page__` to `__main__` and that fixed everything - I must've missed that in the latest release notes. Thanks for your help!

I was also affected by the `__name__` change. I personally like the python convention of having an entry-point function that is called within an if `__name__` condition, and I use it in all of my streamlit apps and other python projects. The actual name is not important for me (whether it is `"__page__"` or `"__main__"`), but the fact that it changed matters, because now I have to go through all of my pages in all of my apps and change the if check to `"__main__"`.

title: Watch changes in uv workspaces
body:
### Checklist

### Summary

Support watching/hot reloading of uv workspaces modules.

### Why?

`uv` have become extremely popular package manager (for good reason). I'm often leaning into using [`uv workspaces`](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/concepts/projects/workspaces/). However I can't get it working properly with streamlit's watch feature.

### How?

I'm not sure how to do it unfortunately.

### Additional Context

I've made this [repo](https://github.com/NixBiks/uv-workspaces-with-streamlit) is to investigate how to make [`uv workspaces`](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/concepts/projects/workspaces/) work properly with `streamlit`s hot reload feature.

### Project structure

```
├── apps
│   └── streamlit-app
│       ├── main.py
│       └── pyproject.toml
├── packages
│   └── hello-world
│       ├── pyproject.toml
│       └── src
│           └── hello_world
│               ├── __init__.py
│               └── py.typed
├── pyproject.toml
└── uv.lock
```

### The problem

If I run my streamlit app

```
uv run streamlit run apps/streamlit-app/main.py
```

then the hot reload works just fine if I make changes in `apps/streamlit-app`. However any changes to `packages/hello-world` is not picked up.

title: theme.fontFaces doesn't load font which requires multiple font files
body:
### Checklist

### Summary

If I need multiple font files to define a font (e.g. one for normal style and one for italic style), Streamlit will not contextually switch between the two files correctly.

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
import streamlit as st

st.header("**fgThis** _fgis_ ***fga*** `fgheader`")
st.subheader("**fgThis** _fgis_ ***fga*** `fgsubheader`")
st.write("**fgThis** _fgis_ ***fga*** `fgwrite`")
st.code("**fgThis** _fgis_ ***fga*** fgcode block #And a code comment")
st.sidebar.header("**fgThis** _fgis_ ***fga*** sidebar `fgheader`")
st.sidebar.subheader("**fgThis** _fgis_ ***fga*** sidebar `fgsubheader`")
st.sidebar.write("**fgThis** _fgis_ ***fga*** sidebar `fgwrite`")
st.sidebar.code("**fgThis** _fgis_ ***fga*** sidebar fgcode block #And a code comment")
```

### Steps To Reproduce

Get Noto font files form Google:
https://fonts.google.com/specimen/Noto+Sans
https://fonts.google.com/specimen/Noto+Sans+Mono

config.toml
```toml
[server]
enableStaticServing = true
[[theme.fontFaces]]
family="noto-sans"
url="app/static/NotoSans-Italic-VariableFont_wdth,wght.ttf"
style="italic"
[[theme.fontFaces]]
family="noto-sans"
url="app/static/NotoSans-VariableFont_wdth,wght.ttf"
style="normal"
[[theme.fontFaces]]
family="noto-mono"
url="app/static/NotoSansMono-VariableFont_wdth,wght.ttf"
style="normal"
[theme]
font="noto-sans"
codeFont="noto-mono"
```

1. Run the app.
2. The normal style font is used everywhere. Italic is simulated by skewing the normal style.

Look at the `f` ang `g` characters. `f` extends below the bottom of the font in the italic Noto Sans, but not for Noto Sans italic.

Also, the default Source Sans script has a different `g` for normal vs italic (normal has the fancy squiggly bottom) but Noto has the simple bottom on `g` for both styles.

### Expected Behavior

I should be able to create multiple theme.fontFaces entries to fully define a font.

### Current Behavior

Not all of the font files are available to the front end:

[image]

If you reverse the order of the italic and normal font in `config.toml` and restart the Streamlit server, then everything will be italic. In that case, the italic file will be available to the front end but not the normal file.

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version:
- Python version:
- Operating System:
- Browser:

### Additional Information

Furthermore, if I configure italic first and normal second, but add weight to the normal file's configuration, Streamlit only uses the italic file.

```toml
[server]
enableStaticServing = true
[[theme.fontFaces]]
family="noto-sans"
url="app/static/NotoSans-Italic-VariableFont_wdth,wght.ttf"
style="italic"
[[theme.fontFaces]]
family="noto-sans"
url="app/static/NotoSans-VariableFont_wdth,wght.ttf"
style="normal"
weight="100 800"
[[theme.fontFaces]]
family="noto-mono"
url="app/static/NotoSansMono-VariableFont_wdth,wght.ttf"
style="normal"
[theme]
font="noto-sans"
codeFont="noto-mono"
```

When italic is configured first and the following weight is added to the normal-style font, Streamlit will only use the italic font:
`100`
`"100"`
`"100 800"`

When italic is configured first and the following weight is added to the normal-style font, Streamlit will only use the normal font (but all in the same weight):
`400`
`"400"`

title: theme.fontFaces.weight doesn't accept a weight range
body:
### Checklist

### Summary

The `weight` property in `theme.fontFaces` passes to the [`font-weight`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/@font-face/font-weight) CSS `@user` descriptor. This is parsed correctly if the weight is an integer or an int-like string. However, if a range of weights is passed (like `"400 600"`) the font is not correctly interpreted and it doesn't load to the front end.

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
import streamlit as st

st.sidebar.header("fg **fg** _fg_ ***fg*** `fg`")
st.sidebar.subheader("fg **fg** _fg_ ***fg*** `fg`")
st.sidebar.write("fg **fg** _fg_ ***fg*** `fg`")
st.sidebar.code("fg **fg** _fg_ ***fg*** `fg` #And a code comment")
st.header("fg **fg** _fg_ ***fg*** `fg`")
st.subheader("fg **fg** _fg_ ***fg*** `fg`")
st.write("fg **fg** _fg_ ***fg*** `fg`")
st.code("fg **fg** _fg_ ***fg*** `fg` #And a code comment")
```

### Steps To Reproduce

Get Noto font files form Google:
https://fonts.google.com/specimen/Noto+Sans
https://fonts.google.com/specimen/Noto+Sans+Mono

Consider the following configuration (with the appropriate font files saved in the static hosting directory.

```
[server]
enableStaticServing = true
[[theme.fontFaces]]
family="noto-sans"
url="app/static/NotoSans-Italic-VariableFont_wdth,wght.ttf"
style="italic"
[[theme.fontFaces]]
family="noto-sans"
url="app/static/NotoSans-VariableFont_wdth,wght.ttf"
style="normal"
weight=800
[[theme.fontFaces]]
family="noto-mono"
url="app/static/NotoSansMono-VariableFont_wdth,wght.ttf"
style="normal"
[theme]
font="noto-sans"
codeFont="noto-mono"
```

The makes the non-italic font all have weight 800.

If the weight line is changed to:
```
weight="400"
```
...then all non-italic font has normal weight.

However, if the weight line is changed to:
```
weight="400 800"
```
...the non-italic font doesn't load and everything uses the italic font instead (as the closest available font).

### Expected Behavior

### Current Behavior

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

title: Rerun when `config.toml` is created
body:
### Checklist

### Summary

Today, Streamlit automatically reruns when you change certain config options in `.streamlit/config.toml` (e.g. for theming). But it doesn't rerun when a config file is first created. Instead, you need to reboot the server in order for the config file to be recognized. We should handle that automatically!

### Why?

The current behavior is annoying and can be confusing for new users. 

### How?

If no config file exists, look for it, and when a new one is created, automatically rerun the app and apply the options as much as possible. 

### Additional Context

sections.summary: Today, Streamlit automatically reruns when you change certain config options in `.streamlit/config.toml` (e.g. for theming). But it doesn't rerun when a config file is first created. Instead, you need to reboot the server in order for the config file to be recognized. We should handle that automatically!
sections.why?: The current behavior is annoying and can be confusing for new users.
sections.how?: If no config file exists, look for it, and when a new one is created, automatically rerun the app and apply the options as much as possible.

comments.text: This is becoming increasingly important with AI agents, since they can create a `config.toml` (e.g. to apply theming), and then it's confusing why the app doesn't pick that up.

Since streamlit generally handles incremental port assignment, could you provide a little more context as to what you are trying to do and why the passing of 0?

port=$(( ( RANDOM % 64511 )  + 1024 ))

title: st.context.timezone becomes empty str ("") after reloading new saved changes
body:
### Checklist

### Summary

When using `st.context.timezone` in a Streamlit app, the component initially returns the correct timezone string of the user's browser.
However, after making any change to the associated `.py` files and saving them, the page refreshes automatically, causing `st.context.timezone` to become `""`.
If you refresh the page by interacting with other Streamlit components, like a button, it recovers it's initial correct state.

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
import streamlit as st

st.set_page_config(
    page_title="Streamlit App",
)

st.write(f"Timezone: {type(st.context.timezone).__name__}, {st.context.timezone}")
st.write(st.context.timezone == "")
st.button("Click me!")
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Create a Streamlit app with the provided code snippet.
2. Run the app and observe that `st.context.timezone` returns the correct timezone string (e.g., Europe/Madrid).
3. Make any change to the `.py` file, such as adding a blank line, and save the file.
4. Observe the automatic page refresh and check the value returned by `st.context.timezone`.
5. Click the button or refresh the page to recover the initial correct timezone.

### Expected Behavior

After making changes to the `.py` files and saving them, the page should refresh automatically, and `st.context.timezone` should consistently return the correct timezone string of the user's browser.

### Current Behavior

After saving changes to the `.py` files, the page refreshes automatically, causing `st.context.timezone` to return `""`. 
The correct timezone is restored by the page.

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.45.0
- Python version: 3.10.11
- Operating System: Windows 11
- Browser: Chrome and Edge

### Additional Information

comments.text:
Hi @user, thanks for your submission! I wasn't able to repro your issue using the code above - its returning my correct timezone despite python file changes, reruns, etc.
So running just the code above with a python file change returns `st.context.timezone == ""`?
Could you provide any additional info?

Here you have a demo of the issue that I described before. Hope it helps!

[image]

Thanks for the clarification! This is a bug with the combination of `st.context` properties that come from the browser (`timezone`, `timezone_offset`, `url` & `locale`) and the `runOnSave=true` config option. 
The file change with `runOnSave=true` triggers a reload and the script is re-executed before the browser has a chance to send the context information, resulting in an empty string.

If you want to keep `runOnSave=true`, the workaround would be to save the context information in `session_state` to persist across reruns.

I'll work with that for now
Ty!

comments.text:
## Update

Exciting news 🎉 Starting with **Streamlit 1.53**, we've added experimental support for custom HTTP routes via the new ASGI/Starlette integration, which enables hosting an MCP server alongside your Streamlit app.

**Custom MCP endpoint:**

```python
from streamlit.starlette import App
from starlette.routing import Route
from starlette.responses import JSONResponse

async def mcp_handler(request):
    body = await request.json()
    # Handle MCP protocol messages here
    return JSONResponse({"result": "..."})

app = App("main.py", routes=[Route("/mcp", mcp_handler, methods=["POST"])])
```

**Using MCP libraries like [fastapi-mcp](https://github.com/tadata-org/fastapi_mcp) or [FastMCP](https://github.com/jlowin/fastmcp):**

```python
from fastapi import FastAPI
from fastapi_mcp import FastApiMCP
from starlette.routing import Mount
from streamlit.starlette import App

api = FastAPI()

@api.get("/data")
async def get_data():
    return {"items": [1, 2, 3]}

# Add MCP server to expose endpoints as MCP tools
mcp = FastApiMCP(api)
mcp.mount()

# Mount into Streamlit - MCP available at /api/mcp
app = App("dashboard.py", routes=[Mount("/api", app=api)])
```

This allows AI tools to interact with your Streamlit app via MCP.

We'd love your feedback on this feature! Please try it out and report any issues in our [feedback thread](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/13600).

> **Note:** Requires `pip install streamlit[starlette]`

## Update

Starlette will become the default server in 1.57 which will allow adding MCP compatible endpoints as described above without having to install the `starlette` dependencies. The `App` object will also be available in the `st` namespace:

```python
import streamlit as st

...

st.App(...)
```

title: Cannot use common tenant with microsoft login: authlib.jose.errors.InvalidClaimError: invalid_claim: Invalid claim 'iss'
body:
### Checklist

### Summary

When setting server_metadata_url (in secrets.toml [auth]) to https://login.microsoftonline.com/common/v2.0/.well-known/openid-configuration, i.e. tenant set to "common" the following error occurs:

```authlib.jose.errors.InvalidClaimError: invalid_claim: Invalid claim 'iss'```

This error does not occur when limiting logins to personal accounts with server_metadata_url set to https://login.microsoftonline.com/consumers/v2.0/.well-known/openid-configuration.

This means that non-personal accounts (i.e. work accounts) cannot login to streamlit significantly reducing the utility of streamlit microsoft login support.

It looks like this is a problem with authlib

https://github.com/authlib/authlib/issues/605

For others struggling with this, a workaround I've found is to manage the login yourself directly using the msal library. A good code example can be found here https://github.com/Prhmma/Streamlit_Azure_AD/tree/main

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.44.1
- Python version: 3.12.3
- Operating System: Ubuntu
- Browser: Chrome

comments.text:
Hi I am facing a comparable situation (when trying to support multiple tenants and work accounts, hence using `server_metadata_url = "https://login.microsoftonline.com/common/v2.0/.well-known/openid-configuration"`) and explored a few options on how to work around the issue without waiting for a fix in `streamlit` or `authlib`.

When digging I realized that by default, Streamlit's `OpenIDMixin` loads the server metadata using `authlib`. When using multi-tenant scenarios, the endpoint `https://login.microsoftonline.com/common/v2.0/.well-known/openid-configuration` returns an issue with the value `https://login.microsoftonline.com/{tenantid}/v2.0`. `authlib` doesn't replace the `{tenantid}` with the actual tenant id, which makes sense given different tenants might be valid.
A Entraid token usually has a `tid` property that specifies the tenant the token belongs to.

I explored how I could workaround the issue without changing authlib or streamlit, the following options came to my mind:

1. Monkeypatch the `validate_iss` in the `authlib` library to fix the issuer validation.
2. Patching a CustomJWTClass with the adjusted logic.

In the process I realized that we that Streamlit doesn't pass `claims_options` when calling `authorize_access_token` (`TornadoOAuth2App` in `streamlist.web.server.oidc_mixin.py`).
When this call happens and no claims_options are passed the OAuth metadata is used during the token validation process (see `parse_id_token` in `OpenIDMixin`).

While the support in `authlib` is probably benefical I realized that I can simply implement the following as a workaround.
**This workaround currently below allows any issuer** -> Pass your explicit issuer claim option (if single tenant, or a list of specific tenants).

```python
from streamlit.web.server.oidc_mixin import TornadoOAuth2App, TornadoOAuth
import tornado.web

class TornadoOAuth2AppWithEntraAuth(TornadoOAuth2App):
    
    
    def authorize_access_token(
        self, request_handler: tornado.web.RequestHandler, **kwargs
    ):
        return super().authorize_access_token(
            request_handler, claims_options={}
        )

class TornadoOAuthWithEntra(TornadoOAuth):
    oauth2_client_cls = TornadoOAuth2AppWithEntraAuth

```

I then only need to monkeypatch the streamlit app at the top of the app.py:

```python
from app.streamlit.adauth import TornadoOAuthWithEntra

import streamlit.web.server.oauth_authlib_routes

streamlit.web.server.oauth_authlib_routes.TornadoOAuth = TornadoOAuthWithEntra # type: ignore

```

Alternatively, as a workaround it might also be feasible to monkeypatch the validate_iss (for more complex scenarios).

```python
def validate_iss(self) -> None:
    """Validate the 'iss' claim for Azure AD."""
    claim_name = "iss"

    option = self.options.get(claim_name)
    if not option:
        return

    value = self.get(claim_name)

    option_value = option.get("value")
    if option_value and value != option_value:
        raise InvalidClaimError(claim_name)

    option_values = option.get("values")

    # replace '{tenantid}' with actual tenant ID (option_values is a list of options)
    option_values = [
        v.replace("{tenantid}", self.get("tid", ""))
        for v in option_values
    ] if option_values else None

    if option_values and value not in option_values:
        raise InvalidClaimError(claim_name)

    validate = option.get("validate")
    if validate and not validate(self, value):
        raise InvalidClaimError(claim_name)
```

```python
from app.streamlit.azuread_jwt_claims import validate_iss
import authlib.jose.rfc7519.claims

authlib.jose.rfc7519.claims.JWTClaims.validate_iss = validate_iss
```

Overall these seem to be only workarounds for now, but hope they help.
Hi @user thanks for finding and filing this issue. And thanks to both of you for providing workarounds in the meantime while we investigate.

@user Thanks for your investigation! Do you think this is something we can fix in Streamlit (e.g. by making claims_options configurable and passing it to `authorize_access_token`) or is it better to get this fixed in authlib?

Thanks for the detailed write-up—and great find on the workaround with MSAL.

You're absolutely right that setting `server_metadata_url` to use the `common` endpoint:

```
https://login.microsoftonline.com/common/v2.0/.well-known/openid-configuration
```

results in an `invalid_claim: Invalid claim 'iss'` error. This occurs because when using the `common` tenant, Microsoft returns a tenant-specific `iss` (issuer) in the ID token like:

```
https://login.microsoftonline.com/<tenant_id>/v2.0
```

which does **not match** the `common` issuer used in the discovery metadata. Authlib (which Streamlit uses internally) enforces strict OIDC compliance here and raises an error due to the mismatch—see [authlib/authlib#605](https://github.com/lepture/authlib/issues/605) for background.

This **is not a bug in Streamlit**, but rather a limitation stemming from Microsoft’s use of dynamic tenant-specific issuers combined with Authlib's validation rules.

That said, it **does limit utility for work/school accounts**, which is a totally valid concern. I’ll mark this as an enhancement to track possible improvements:

- Improving documentation around this `common` vs. `consumers` vs. `organizations` distinction
- Possibly supporting more flexible auth flows via MSAL or community examples

Thanks again for raising this—really helpful context, and the workaround you shared will be useful for others hitting this edge case.

title: file_uploader fails for files with Unicode characters in filename (Streamlit Community Cloud)
body:
### Checklist

### Summary

When uploading files with Unicode characters in their filenames (e.g., Hebrew, Arabic, Chinese, Emoji) using st.file_uploader on Streamlit Community Cloud, the upload fails with a 400 Bad Request error. The same code works without issue locally.

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
import streamlit as st

uploaded_file = st.file_uploader("Upload a file")
if uploaded_file is not None:
    st.write("File uploaded successfully.")
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Deploy the Streamlit app to Streamlit Community Cloud

2. Try uploading any file with a Unicode filename such as:

מסמך.pdf (Hebrew)

اختبار.pdf (Arabic)

测试.pdf (Chinese)

テスト.pdf (Japanese)

file_🙂.pdf (Emoji)

3. The file fails to upload, and the frontend shows this error:

"AxiosError: Request failed with status code 400"

### Expected Behavior

Files should upload successfully regardless of the filename's character encoding.

### Current Behavior

The upload fails when the filename contains Unicode characters, showing a 400 error.

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.45.1
- Python version: 3.11.12
- Platform: Streamlit Community Cloud
- Browser: Google Chrome (latest version)

### Additional Information

Works fine locally using streamlit run

ASCII-only filenames upload without issues.

Unicode filenames consistently trigger this error in the Community Cloud.

All dependencies were installed correctly, as shown in deployment logs.

The issue appears to be specific to the Community Cloud environment.

comments.text: Hi @user, thanks for filing this enhancement request. We'll take a look at it.
Related: https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/9450

## Update

Streamlit 1.59 introduces an officially supported alternative to calling the internal `streamlit.web.bootstrap.run` API directly.

The new public API is:

```python
import streamlit as st

app = st.App("your_app.py")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    app.run()
```

`App.run()` starts a local Streamlit server for the app and supports programmatic config overrides:

```python
app.run(config={"server.headless": True, "server.port": 8502})
```

So instead of documenting `bootstrap.run` as a stable public API, we now have a supported public entry point for launching an `st.App` from Python code. This is planned to ship in Streamlit 1.59.

title: Disable LaTeX page wide in configuration file to avoid breaking markdown text containing "$"
body:
### Checklist

### Summary

Add an option to disable LaTeX rendering page wide using `.streamlit/config.toml` file.

### Why?

LaTeX is great for describing mathematical formulas, but I guess a very large percentage of all Streamlit pages ever created doesn’t have that kind of content. A more common content would be a dollar sign - $ - and unfortunately this breaks markdown formatted text. A workaround is to escape the dollar sign with backslash – `text.replace("$", "\$")` – but this is cumbersome if you have a complex page.  
The issue has been discussed in #7638 where the developers have hinted about a way to disable LaTeX rendering using a parameter `extensions` but it's unclear how strings with $ would be rendered in other situations when markdown is rendered except `st.markdown`. Therefore, using the settings would be more convenient.

### How?

Add an option to disable LaTeX rendering page wide in the `.streamlit/config.toml` file.

### Additional Context

Hi @user , thank you for filing this issue!

I believe the root cause of the `400: Expecting value` error is a misconfiguration in your `.streamlit/secrets.toml` file. The `st.login` command is designed to use the OpenID Connect (OIDC) discovery mechanism, which requires the `server_metadata_url` to point to a JSON document containing the provider's configuration. This code looks to have this value set to Microsoft's authorization endpoint (`https://login.microsoftonline.com/tenant-id/oauth2/v2.0/authorize`).

To fix this, you should update the `server_metadata_url` to point to Microsoft's OIDC discovery document, as shown in the [`st.login` documentation](https://docs.streamlit.io/develop/api-reference/user/st.login).

I believe the separate `authlib` script works because it bypasses this discovery mechanism by providing the `authorize` and `token` URLs directly to the client. In contrast, `st.login` is a higher-level abstraction that uses the OIDC standard discovery flow, which is why it relies on the metadata URL for its configuration. Correcting this URL in your secrets file should resolve the issue.

title: Websocket Notify component to allow for Push-Notifications without polling
body:
### Checklist

### Summary

Provide a component that will trigger a server-side render when it receives a message from a specified websocket server.

### Why?

Currently, streamlit requires an execution-flow, that starts in the browser. Usually, the user is interacting with a component (e.g. changing the value of input components, or pressing buttons, etc...), which triggers a render operation on the server-side. As a result of this paradigm, it is difficult to implement flows, that start with the server sending a push event to the client.

Some examples would be:

- A chatroom where the server notifies each of the participants that a new message was sent
- A live presentation where the presenter wants to push updates to all viewers, e.g. for highlighting some of the presented data, or for "changing to the next slide" by triggering a rerun that renders a new layout
- A dashboard that displays the current state of a system, which only changes sporadically and with long time-periods in between

All of these examples can be solved by polling for updates in an infinite loop, e.g. by using third-party components like [streamlit-autorefresh](https://github.com/kmcgrady/streamlit-autorefresh). The issue with this approach is that it results in a lot of wasted computation and requests where a rerun is triggered without any changes occurring. This also doesn't scale well with more and more session-threads.

This polling approach can be avoided by adding a component that only triggers a server-side rerun when it receives a websocket message on the client-side. The currently implemented execution-flow stays the same, since everything starts with a change on the client-side. 
But instead of requiring a user-interaction like a button-click, a websocket server can trigger it remotely.

### How?

On the python side, the implementation could look very similar to any of the existing input-widgets:

```python
# allow for http-header customization to enable authentication and individualized socket connections
raw_message: bytes = st.websocket_receive(url="https://some-websocket-server-address", http_headers={"Authorization": "Basic ..."})
# directly receive strings
# message: str = st.websocket_receive(url=..., encoding="utf-8")

# everytime a socket-message was received, this should trigger a redraw that shows the received message
st.write(raw_message.decode("utf-8"))
```

On the client side, the component would open a websocket using the specified URL and header fields and will update the component value as soon as it receives a message. *(I am not really familiar with js/ts... so I can't provide example code for this part of the implementation)*

## Added Bonus:

With such a component, the [multithreading section](https://docs.streamlit.io/develop/concepts/design/multithreading) in the docs could also be updated with an additional example. Instead of having to join the worker-thread, it could be a deamon that starts a websocket-server and asynchronously communicates with the streamlit app via the proposed websocket component.

## Notes on Security

The proposed implementation requires the client to know both the URL and the custom header fields, and it should be highlighted in the documentation that those should only contain values that the client is allowed to know about.

### Additional Context

Issue #2927 proposes a very similar approach but also provides a [solution](https://github.com/FloWide/streamlit_callbacks/tree/main) that only uses websockets on the server-side, which doesn't really solve the polling issue. As far as I can tell, they added the socket-listener thread to the ScriptRunContext which can result in unexpected behavior and fatal errors and may not work for all streamlit commands *(according to the [multithreading documentation](https://docs.streamlit.io/develop/concepts/design/multithreading))*. What I want to propose instead, is an implementation that starts at the client-side and fits more to the currently supported execution flow of streamlit apps.

On the python side, the implementation could look very similar to any of the existing input-widgets:

```python
sections.everytime a socket-message was received,:
st.write(raw_message.decode("utf-8"))
```

On the client side, the component would open a websocket using the specified URL and header fields and will update the component value as soon as it receives a message. *(I am not really familiar with js/ts... so I can't provide example code for this part of the implementation)*
sections.added bonus:: With such a component, the [multithreading section](https://docs.streamlit.io/develop/concepts/design/multithreading) in the docs could also be updated with an additional example. Instead of having to join the worker-thread, it could be a deamon that starts a websocket-server and asynchronously communicates with the streamlit app via the proposed websocket component.
sections.notes on security: The proposed implementation requires the client to know both the URL and the custom header fields, and it should be highlighted in the documentation that those should only contain values that the client is allowed to know about.
sections.additional context: Issue #2927 proposes a very similar approach but also provides a [solution](https://github.com/FloWide/streamlit_callbacks/tree/main) that only uses websockets on the server-side, which doesn't really solve the polling issue. As far as I can tell, they added the socket-listener thread to the ScriptRunContext which can result in unexpected behavior and fatal errors and may not work for all streamlit commands *(according to the [multithreading documentation](https://docs.streamlit.io/develop/concepts/design/multithreading))*. What I want to propose instead, is an implementation that starts at the client-side and fits more to the currently supported execution flow of streamlit apps.

title: connection breaks up because WebSocketProtocol13.ping_timeout=1, but expected to be 30
body:
### Checklist

### Summary

In server.py there is configuration for tornado:

```
TORNADO_SETTINGS = {
    # Gzip HTTP responses.
    "compress_response": True,
    # Ping every 1s to keep WS alive.
    # 2021.06.22: this value was previously 20s, and was causing
    # connection instability for a small number of users. This smaller
    # ping_interval fixes that instability.
    # https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/3196
    "websocket_ping_interval": 1,
    # If we don't get a ping response within 30s, the connection
    # is timed out.
    "websocket_ping_timeout": 30,
    "xsrf_cookie_name": "_streamlit_xsrf",
}
```

But if we go to tornado sources https://www.tornadoweb.org/en/stable/_modules/tornado/websocket.html
then we will find out:

```python
    @user
    def ping_timeout(self) -> float:
        timeout = self.params.ping_timeout
        if timeout is not None:
            if self.ping_interval and timeout > self.ping_interval:
                de_dupe_gen_log(
                    # Note: using de_dupe_gen_log to prevent this message from
                    # being duplicated for each connection
                    logging.WARNING,
                    f"The websocket_ping_timeout ({timeout}) cannot be longer"
                    f" than the websocket_ping_interval ({self.ping_interval})."
                    f"\nSetting websocket_ping_timeout={self.ping_interval}",
                )
                return self.ping_interval
            return timeout
        return self.ping_interval
```

Obviously, that streamlit have pint_timeout set to 1, which is super inconvenient with unstable connection (like delay on 1s will breaks up streaming)

```Python

```

### Steps To Reproduce

Just go with debugger to tornado/websocket.py line where get_websocket_protocol is defined and check that `WebSocketProtocol13(self, False, params)` will return both ping_timeout and ping_interval equals 1.

I expect streamlit will provide an ability to set this parameters somewhere in config.

### Checklist ### Summary Silent login fails with error App deployed on AWS ECS error_description=AADSTS50058%3a+A+silent+sign-in+request+was+sent+but+no+user+is+signed+in. +The+cookies+used+to+represent+the+user%27s+session+were+not+sent+in+the+request+to+Azure+AD. +This+can+happen+if+the+user+is+using+Internet+Explorer+or+Edge%2c+and+the+web+app+sending+the+silent+sign-in+request+is+in+different+IE+security+zone+than+the+Azure+AD+endpoint+ (login.microsoftonline.com). ### Reproducible Code Example ```Python Adding only the auth configs here [auth] cookie_secret = "value" redirect_uri = "https://app-url/oauth2callback" tenant_id = "value" server_metadata_url = "https://login.microsoftonline.com/tenant-id/v2.0/.well-known/openid-configuration" client_id = "value" client_secret = "value" [auth.microsoft] cookie_secret = "value" redirect_uri = "https://app-url/oauth2callback" tenant_id = "value" server_metadata_url = "https://login.microsoftonline.com/tenant-id/v2.0/.well-known/openid-configuration" client_id = "value" client_secret = "value" client_kwargs = {"prompt" = "none"} ``` ### Steps To Reproduce 1.Create an azure app and link it to an AD group with certain members 2.Check SSO for users in AD groups with above secrets.toml file config 3.Check SSO for users not in AD group with the same secrets.toml config ### Expected Behavior To be shown this page as expected without {"prompt" = "none"} [image] ### Current Behavior No error message displayed , simply redirected to the main SSO page with an error found via the browser error_description=AADSTS50058%3a+A+silent+sign-in+request+was+sent+but+no+user+is+signed+in. +The+cookies+used+to+represent+the+user%27s+session+were+not+sent+in+the+request+to+Azure+AD. +This+can+happen+if+the+user+is+using+Internet+Explorer+or+Edge%2c+and+the+web+app+sending+the+silent+sign-in+request+is+in+different+IE+security+zone+than+the+Azure+AD+endpoint+ (login.microsoftonline.com). ### Is this a regression? - [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version. ### Debug info - Streamlit version: 1.42.0 - Python version:3.11.6 - Operating System: Windows/Linux - Browser: Chrome/Edge ### Additional Information It would be great if there is a plan to implement this [issue](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/10160) which would help a lot I dont think the user session has expired but also adding ChatGPT's response if it helps | Root cause | Typical scenario | | --------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | **No user is actually signed in** | You called `acquireTokenSilent` (or hit a page that does an iframe / hidden‑window auth flow) before the interactive sign‑in completed, **or** the user’s session has expired. | | **Cookies didn’t reach Azure AD** | • Third‑party cookies blocked (common in Safari, Brave, Chrome Incognito).
• Browser in “strict” tracking‑protection mode.
• Ad‑block / privacy extensions stripping cookies.
• `SameSite=Lax` / `None` mis‑config for custom domains.
• You’re testing on `http://localhost` in Edge/IE and the site is in **Intranet** or **Trusted Sites** while `login.microsoftonline.com` lives in **Internet** zone, so the cookie is suppressed across zones. | | **Wrong account context** | You call `acquireTokenSilent` with the wrong `account` object or empty `loginHint`, so MSAL picks “no account” and falls back to silent ‑‑> fails. |

title: Make `st.context.ip_address` work with a proxy or load balancer by setting Tornado's `xheaders` parameter
body:
### Checklist

### Summary

Currently, the `st.context.ip_address` feature will _always_ return `None` if you're using a proxy or load balancer because Streamlit doesn't set the Tornado server's `xheaders` setting to `True`. Therefore, even if you correctly configure the `X-Forwarded-For` and `X-Real-Ip` headers on your proxy, `st.context.ip_address` will never work because the Tornado server isn't configured to observe those headers. (And currently can't be configured, except via some elaborate monkey patching.)

In other words:
* `st.context.ip_address` relies on Tornado's [remote_ip](https://www.tornadoweb.org/en/stable/httputil.html#tornado.httputil.HTTPServerRequest.remote_ip) feature.
* → If a proxy or load balancer is involved, that relies on the Tornado `xheaders` setting being set to `True`.
* → When [Streamlit initialises the Tornado server](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/blob/1.46.0/lib/streamlit/web/server/server.py#L138-L142) it doesn't pass that setting.
* → That setting [defaults to False](https://github.com/tornadoweb/tornado/blob/d3bf1ee425a6d44f9e57c21a3763860f60babd8c/tornado/httpserver.py#L171).
* → 😭 

I think the solution is a simple one-line change to pass `xheaders=True` when creating the `tornado.httpserver.HTTPServer` instance.
