comments.text:
For the 502 Error regarding the login issue check nginx header size limits. That fixed the problem for me! 

```
Request headers (browser -> Nginx):
client_header_buffer_size
large_client_header_buffers

Response headers (upstream -> Nginx, e.g., large Set-Cookie):
proxy_buffer_size
proxy_buffers
```

Hi @user , thanks a lot for the suggestion!

I tried doing what you suggested, my Ingress yaml config looks something like following:
```
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: Ingress
metadata:
  annotations:
    <...>
    kubernetes.io/ingress.class: nginx
    nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/client-header-buffer-size: 16k
    nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/large-client-header-buffers: 4 32k
    nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/proxy-buffer-size: 16k
    nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/proxy-buffers: 8 16k
```

Unfortunately, with Streamlit 1.53, still no luck (although it doesn't display the `502 Bad Gateway – nginx` error page now, it hangs on the Streamlit loading page forever). With Streamlit 1.52, having or not having these additional configs for the Ingress both work correctly.
Does yours Ingress config look similar to this?

> 1. st.login() no longer works when deployed on Kubernetes (NGINX Ingress)

Here is a quick Claude investigation on this:

> The Kubernetes/NGINX failure is the part that looks partly fixable in Streamlit. Larger auth cookies in 1.53 can absolutely trip ingress header/buffer limits, which matches the reporter comment that larger buffers changed the symptom from 502 to a hanging app (issue comment). But I also found a Streamlit-side regression: the implementation was persisting token cookies on login even when expose_tokens was not enabled, despite the feature spec saying the feature is disabled by default. That unnecessarily bloats headers.

Here is what Claude proposes to fix this: https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/14331 Might be good to have someone with more knowledge abot this area look at this (cc @user @user)

btw. are you running it with multiple replicas? If so, it might be important to activate session affinity since you will otherwise run into [this issue](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/13773), which could explain the "loading forever". 

> 2. st.logout() now asks me to choose which account to log out of

I believe this is by-design. The `st.logout()` now redirects to the provider’s end_session_endpoint for proper OIDC logout. Many providers show account selection at this endpoint. But not sure if there is a way somewhere to configure that? Maybe we should add some option here?

@user thank you for your answer!

> Larger auth cookies in 1.53 can absolutely trip ingress header/buffer limits, which matches the reporter comment that larger buffers changed the symptom from 502 to a hanging app (issue comment)

Indeed, this matches my observation. Any ideas what might be causing my app to hang when I increase the buffers sizes, and how to possibly solve it?

> btw. are you running it with multiple replicas?

No, I'm running a single replica 🤔.

> Here is what Claude proposes to fix this: https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/14331 .

Thanks! As far as I understand, this Pull Request doesn't embed the access token into the header if not explicitly configured to do so. This would solve the backwards-compatibility problem (Streamlit suddenly stops working from 1.53 version because of larger headers). But if I want to have this token - I'd still have the `502 Bad Gateway – nginx` issue, or the hanging app issue if I try to configure the Ingress buffers. So this Pull Request doesn't fully close my issue, right?

> I believe this is by-design. The st.logout() now redirects to the provider’s end_session_endpoint for proper OIDC logout.

I see. I also think that an option or a way to configure this would be very welcome, as having to select which account I want to log out of breaks the smooth logout experience from earlier versions. Unfortunately I don't have a very deep understanding of OAuth2 and OIDC, therefore I don't have any ideas for this :(

Thanks again for your time!

One additional regression of behaviour I would like to point out is that is likely related to the change implemented in 1.53 is now the OAuth logout forces logout of all sessions related to that Identity Provider. 

Using MS Entra - A logout of the Streamlit OAuth session is also doing a logout of all MS Entra related sessions, like Outlook. 

Previously a logout of Streamlit did not trigger a logout of Outlook. Now the users have to login back to Outlook - it would be really annoying for users if we updated to this release and raises the long term problem of updating in the future.

Is there a way to specify which OAuth token you want to logout of?

Hi. I'm the contributor that wrote the logout code as it currently stands.

The one thing that became pretty clear is that there is a LOT of heterogeneity in how OAuth providers work, and that the standard is taken at best as a loose set of guidelines. For instance, many providers require extra parameters on the loguout query that are clearly labeled as optional in standards (description of https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/12693 covers these cases with links to bug reports from the first time I tried implementing it). 

So in response to the question
> Is there a way to specify which OAuth token you want to logout of?

Yes, there is, the token is being passed to the logout request and the provider is not doing anything with it. And that is to be expected considering the heterogeneity (and to a degree, vagueness of the standard on what the logout should actually do). 

Now for context: 
What logout did pre 1.53.0 is it just deleted the session auth cookie for streamlit. So next time you logged in, login flow would get called again. Which for many OIDC providers (such as Frontegg which is what we are using) just automatically succeeds if a cookie for the provider is still present. And it is, because that is only cleared when calling the logout endpoint.  Effectively for us, logout did functionally nothing pre 1.53.

So, unfortunately, fixing it for me broke it for you. So I apologise and sympathise. 

I believe the best way forward is more configuration. Most notably, the ability to turn off the logout redirect via .secrets [auth] configuration, which should be very straightforward to implement and should effectively restore the pre 1.53 state for those for whom that was better. 

As for the original issue and https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/14331 - I believe the fix, while technically solving the issue for now, is fundamentally misguided. Assuming you eventually want to implement token refresh https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/12696#issuecomment-3861008419, which I assume you will as short-lived access tokens is an increasingly common pattern for OIDC providers, you will need to be storing the refresh token, running head-first into the same header issues as here. So I'd say the correct response is documenting the behavior and saying you should configure your http server to accept large headers as in https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/14290#issuecomment-4030052450 (as it seems to be on average a rare'ish occurrence)

Or, for an even more concrete reason why removing tokens is not a good fix:  even the ID token itself is technically unbounded in size and can blow past the header size limits: https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/12518

Hi @user , thanks a lot for your insights!

---

First, regarding my issue with cookies that are too large for the K8s Ingress Controller, and the "hanging app":
this configuration
```
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: Ingress
metadata:
  annotations:
    <...>
    kubernetes.io/ingress.class: nginx
    nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/client-header-buffer-size: 16k
    nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/large-client-header-buffers: 4 32k
    nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/proxy-buffer-size: 16k
    nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/proxy-buffers: 8 16k
```
actually solved my issue with logging in! The reason it was hanging previously is probably because of saved old cookies not matching the new format anymore; after deleting all cookies from my browser, with the latest version of Streamlit, I can log into my app again! So this part is solved - thanks for the hint @user 🙏!

---

Regarding the log out part - I think I understand it better now. 

If I understand you right @user - previously we weren't really logging out - just deleting the auth cookie from Streamlit, but without actually deactivating it on the OIDC provider's side. Your contribution was to do a "real logout", i.e. actually send a logout request to the OIDC provider when `st.logout()` is executed. This explains why I wasn't asked to pick-up the account I want to log out of prior to Streamlit 1.53, and that now I am.

Furthermore, if I still follow you correctly, you say that it should be possible to configure the system for the provider to pick-up which account I want to log out of automatically, without the need for me to specify. You say that Streamlit actually sends this information in the request. So, in your opinion, this configuration needs to be done on the OIDC provider's side, because currently it doesn't take into account the information about which session I want to end, right? 

I use Microsoft as OIDC provider. And, interestingly, there are other apps I use where authentication is carried out by the same OIDC provider, typically **Databricks**. When logging in into Databricks - I go through the exact same authentication stages as the ones during `st.login()` in my Streamlit app. But during logout from Databricks - I'm not being asked which account I'm logging out of! So there must be a difference in the requests sent to Microsoft *from Databricks* and *from my Streamlit app*. What do you think about this?

_[Update:]_ I tried analyzing and comparing the HTTP requests sent by my Streamlit app during st.login() and st.logout(), and by Databricks during login and logout. In the request sent by Databricks to Microsoft during logout, I don't even see the `id_token_hint`, but somehow Microsoft understands which account I'm logging out of. The link is certainly done somewhere else. On the other side, in my Streamlit app, I do see the `id_token_hint` passed as URL parameter when redirected to Microsoft EntraID, so why isn't Microsoft picking it up? 🤔

---

Regarding the message of @user - I don't observe this on my set-up 🤔
After selecting my account in the OIDC provider during log out, I am effectively logged out in my application, but not in the other services where I use the same account.

> If I understand you right @user - previously we weren't really logging out - just deleting the auth cookie from Streamlit, but without actually deactivating it on the OIDC provider's side. 

Yep, exactly. It was a pseudo-logout - which as explained, ended up not doing anything for our OAuth provider. 

> Furthermore, if I still follow you correctly, you say that it should be possible to configure the system for the provider to pick-up which account I want to log out of automatically, without the need for me to specify. You say that Streamlit actually sends this information in the request. 

Yes. The parameter for this is `id_token_hint` and it literally sends your id token, that contains all your user info, back to the provider. So if the provider wants, they have the information to determine the user. But, this key is technically optional.

Looking at [Microsoft OIDC spec](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity-platform/v2-protocols-oidc#send-a-sign-out-request), they instead use a different parameter called `logout_hint`. It is actually in [the standard](https://openid.net/specs/openid-connect-rpinitiated-1_0.html#RPLogout), but makes it very hard for generic provider-independent solutions to use as per the spec: "The value and meaning of this parameter is left up to the OP's discretion. "

So the situation is effectively: this could be solved on a provider-by-provider basis, and might be worth it for some of the bigger ones (Microsoft undoubtedly being one of them), but it would require provider-dependent code, so I'm not sure how far Streamlit wants to go down that path. Maybe @user wants to weigh in?

For context, it is likely ~4 lines of code to make it work per provider: 2 to detect provider, 2 for a function that extracts hint value from user_data (supposedly, usually email or username, for microsoft a field called `logout_hint`). So it's not a lot of code per provider, if just done for a few big ones

Hey! regarding the logout account picker issue (point 2), this is related to #14601 where Cognito has a similar problem with non-standard logout params.

I opened a draft PR (#14868) that adds an `[auth.logout_params]` config in secrets.toml. For the Entra account picker specifically, you'd be able to pass `logout_hint` with the user's email:

```toml
[auth.logout_params.additional_params]
logout_hint = "{email}"
```

The `{email}` gets substituted from the logged-in user's info. This follows @user's suggestion of making logout more configurable rather than trying to detect providers.

Still needs approval (and a more thorough review) to land but curious if this would work for folks hitting the Entra picker issue.

Making this as a conf template is very elegant. Embaraced I did not think of that. Good work @user .

So for microsoft I guess it would be `logout_hint = "{login_hint}"` for instance (and you have to make sure login_hint is also in the claims list)

I spent some time measuring where the auth cookie bytes actually go, since the discussion above turns on that question. Sharing the numbers in case they are useful.

**Method.** `TestClient` driving the real Starlette auth routes and the real signer, with a `groups` claim of N sha256 hexdigests — incompressible enough that the zlib pass inside `itsdangerous` does not flatter the result. Sizes are the request `Cookie` header the browser sends back, which is what `large_client_header_buffers` and `proxy_buffer_size` actually limit. Note that no tokens are stored in these runs: everything below comes from the identity cookie alone.

## 1. The header is claim values and almost nothing else

| claim | cookies | request `Cookie` header | values | names + separators |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 400 groups | 12 | 21,474 B | 21,242 B | 232 B |
| 100 groups | 5 | 5,627 B | 5,529 B | 98 B |

98% of the header is claim values. Two consequences for the fixes discussed above:

- Changing how the cookie is split, named or packed can only ever recover the last column — 232 bytes out of 21,474. I built a version that packs the chunks to the byte and measured it; the header moved by 1.5%. There is no variant of that idea that matters.
- These figures were produced with **no tokens stored at all**. Making token exposure opt-in (#14331) therefore cannot bound the header either: at 100 groups, the identity cookie alone already exceeds the 4 KB `proxy_buffer_size` default before a single token is added. That is the same ceiling @user pointed at, measured.

If the goal is to get under NGINX's defaults, the only lever with enough range is carrying fewer claims — or not carrying them in a cookie at all.

## 2. A separate bug found along the way: orphaned chunks are never cleared

A chunked auth cookie is a main cookie holding the count plus `{name}_1`, `{name}_2`, … siblings. When a later login produces fewer chunks than an earlier one, the surplus siblings are never removed: they carry a valid signature, so `_clear_invalid_auth_cookies` — which only fires for cookies that fail signature validation — leaves them in place. They persist for the full 30-day cookie lifetime and are sent on every request, including the WebSocket upgrade.

Two consecutive logins in one browser session, a large claim followed by a small one:

| | after login 1 (400 groups) | after login 2 (1 group) |
|---|---|---|
| `develop` | 12 cookies, 21,474 B | 12 cookies, 21,671 B |
| with the fix below | 12 cookies, 21,474 B | 2 cookies, 329 B |

On `develop` the header does not shrink after the second login — it grows slightly, because the main cookie reverts to holding the payload while `_streamlit_user_1` … `_streamlit_user_10` remain behind.

This matters most for #12518, which was closed on the grounds that cookies are now chunked properly. The users there resolved their problem by reconfiguring Entra to emit fewer groups, which is precisely the case that strands the earlier chunks: the app stays broken after the cause has been removed, until the user manually clears their browser cookies.

**Fix:** [`15bdbac`](https://github.com/herley-shaori/streamlit/commit/15bdbac61ee2b54de95bb05b66d71d51991ba618) on [`fix/clear-orphaned-auth-cookie-chunks`](https://github.com/herley-shaori/streamlit/tree/fix/clear-orphaned-auth-cookie-chunks), rebased on `665efd4e6`. `_set_auth_cookie` deletes the chunk siblings present in the request before writing the fresh cookies; rewritten chunks are set again afterwards and win, since the browser applies the last value for a cookie name. The sibling scan is shared with the existing clearing path. Covered by a callback-level regression test that fails on `develop` with three orphaned chunks remaining; ruff, mypy and `lib/tests/streamlit/web/server/` (771 tests) pass.

To be explicit about scope: this does **not** fix the oversized-header reports in this issue. It fixes the recovery path, which is a different problem.

I could not open a pull request — the repository currently limits that to collaborators. Happy to submit one if that is lifted, or feel free to take the commit directly.
I tried blindly upgrading to 1.61.1, and I haven't had any problems with `st.login` anymore. I didn't delve too deep into it, but just noting that I'm not experiencing an issue now.

@user that is consistent with #15420 ("Clear stale and invalid auth cookies on login", June), which clears the pre-1.53 format cookies that were the likely cause of the hangs reported earlier in this thread. Worth keeping separate from the chunk-clearing bug in my comment above, though, because the two have different triggers.

I re-checked against the released wheel rather than `develop`, using `streamlit[auth]==1.61.1`:

```
streamlit version under test: 1.61.1
  after login 1 (400 groups): 12 cookies, 21474 B
  after login 2 (1 group):    12 cookies, 21671 B
  orphaned chunks remaining:  10
```

`lib/streamlit/web/server/starlette/starlette_auth_routes.py` and `lib/streamlit/auth_util.py` are byte-identical between the `1.61.1` tag and `develop`, so nothing has changed there in the meantime.

The orphan case requires the chunk count to shrink between two logins, which only happens after a first login large enough to be split across cookies. Most deployments never reach that state, so the absence of symptoms on 1.61.1 is expected — the behaviour is latent rather than fixed.

title: Validation function of `st.cache_resource()` to receive the same arguments that are passed to the cached function.
body:
### Checklist

### Summary

As seen [here](https://docs.streamlit.io/develop/api-reference/caching-and-state/st.cache_resource#:~:text=receives%20the%20cached%20value%20as%20its%20only%20parameter%20and%20it%20must%20return%20a%20boolean.) in the documentation of `st.cache_resource()`, `validate`
> receives the cached value as its only parameter and it must return a boolean.

I'd like the validation function to receive the same arguments that are passed to the cached function.

### Why?

As seen [here](https://docs.streamlit.io/develop/api-reference/caching-and-state/st.cache_resource#:~:text=is%20useful%20e.g.%20to%20check%20the%20health%20of%20database%20connections.) in the documentation, `validate`
> is useful e.g. to check the health of database connections.

The cached function could be responsible for caching multiple database connections, based on an argument it receives. The validation function would then need to receive the same argument(s) to check the health of the corresponding database connection.

As a simpler, more concrete example, I'd like to cache the content of big files and invalidate the cache if the files change. Note the addition of the `path` argument in `validate`:
```py
@st.cache_resource(validate=lambda cached, path: cached[0] == path.stat().st_mtime)
def get_big_file(path: Path):
    return path.stat().st_mtime, load_big_file_with_expensive_compute(path)
```

Side note: depending on the situation, `st.cache_data()` might be more appropriate than `@st.cache_resource()`, so the `validate` argument could also be added to `st.cache_data()`.

### How?

I can think of two ways to avoid a breaking change to the current `validate` function:
1. We could inspect if `validate` expects arguments, something like
   ```py
   validate(*args, *kwargs) if inspect.signature(validate).parameters else validate()
   ```
1. We could introduce a new function like `validate_with_args`. The two functions would be mutually exclusive.

### Additional Context

As a workaround, I can create one cached function for every file:
```py
# File 1
@st.cache_resource(validate=lambda cached: cached[0] == path1.stat().st_mtime)
def get_big_file1():
    return path1.stat().st_mtime, load_big_file_with_expensive_compute(path)

# File 2
@st.cache_resource(validate=lambda cached: cached[0] == path2.stat().st_mtime)
def get_big_file2():
    return path2.stat().st_mtime, load_big_file_with_expensive_compute(path)
```
But if I my paths are dynamic, that gets complicated. I implemented a decorator that dynamically creates a cached function (with a unique `__qualname__`) as well as the corresponding validation function for each path. See `cache_file` below.

Without the `__qualname__`, the first file would work, but not any subsequent file, as the first `validate` function would be used for all the files. That's feels hacky/fragile.

```py
from collections.abc import Callable
from pathlib import Path
from typing import TypeVar
from unittest.mock import MagicMock, patch

import streamlit as st
from streamlit.testing.v1 import AppTest

T = TypeVar("T")

def cache_file(f: Callable[[Path], T]) -> Callable[[Path], T]:
    def decorated(path: Path, **kwargs):
        def validate(cached):
            return cached[0] == path.stat().st_mtime

        def cached(path: Path, **kwargs):
            return path.stat().st_mtime, f(path, **kwargs)

        cached.__qualname__ = str(path)

        return st.cache_resource(cached, validate=validate)(path, **kwargs)[1]

    return decorated

def _test_app(path0, path1):
    from pathlib import Path

    import streamlit as st

    from apps.utils import cache_file

    @cache_file
    def get_text(path: Path):
        return path.read_text()

    st.text(get_text(path0))

    st.text(get_text(path1))

@patch.object(Path, "read_text", autospec=True, wraps=Path.read_text)
def test_cache_file(mock_read_text: MagicMock, tmp_path: Path):
    paths = (tmp_path / "0.txt", tmp_path / "1.txt")
    paths[0].write_text("0A")
    paths[1].write_text("1A")

    at = AppTest.from_function(_test_app, args=paths)

    for _ in range(2):
        at.run()
        assert not at.exception
        assert at.text[0].value == "0A"
        assert at.text[1].value == "1A"
        assert mock_read_text.call_count == 2

    paths[0].write_text("0B")

    for _ in range(2):
        at.run()
        assert not at.exception
        assert at.text[0].value == "0B"
        assert at.text[1].value == "1A"
        assert mock_read_text.call_count == 3

    paths[0].touch()

    for _ in range(2):
        at.run()
        assert not at.exception
        assert at.text[0].value == "0B"
        assert at.text[1].value == "1A"
        assert mock_read_text.call_count == 4

    paths[1].write_text("1B")

    for _ in range(2):
        at.run()
        assert not at.exception
        assert at.text[0].value == "0B"
        assert at.text[1].value == "1B"
        assert mock_read_text.call_count == 5
```

title: st.cache_data / st.cache_resource provide no way to inspect cache size or memory usage
body:
## Description

In production Streamlit apps that cache large datasets, developers have no programmatic way to answer:
- How much memory is my cache consuming?
- Which cached function is using the most memory?
- How many entries are currently cached?
- Which entries are closest to TTL expiration?

The only option is `st.cache_data.clear()` — a nuclear option that evicts everything.

## Use Case

Streamlit apps deployed on memory-constrained containers (512MB on Community Cloud, small Docker/K8s pods) can hit OOM kills with no advance warning. Developers set `max_entries` and `ttl` through trial and error because there is no way to observe the cache at runtime.

## Proposed API

```python
info = st.cache_data.info()
# Returns:
# {
#     "load_data": {"entries": 12, "approx_bytes": 52428800, "oldest_entry_age": timedelta(minutes=45)},
#     "fetch_users": {"entries": 3, "approx_bytes": 1048576, "oldest_entry_age": timedelta(minutes=12)},
# }
```

This would enable:
1. Monitoring dashboards for cache health
2. Informed decisions about TTL and max_entries tuning
3. Debugging memory issues without restarting the app
4. Conditional clearing of specific function caches when approaching limits

## Context

Related but distinct from #14357 (cache_resource validate args) and #3018 (configurable cache location). Neither addresses runtime introspection of cache state.

title: st.cache_data on class methods intermittently raises UnserializableReturnValueError
body:
### Checklist

### Summary

When `@st.cache_data` decorates a method that returns a custom class instance, `pickle.dumps()` intermittently fails with `PicklingError: Can't pickle <class 'X'>: it's not the same object as X`. This happens because Streamlit's `LocalSourcesWatcher` deletes watched modules from `sys.modules` on file changes, creating a class identity mismatch between the instance being pickled and the class found by pickle's resolution mechanism.

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
### `repro_model.py`

"""Local module — simulates any user-defined class in a local .py file."""

class MyResult:
    def __init__(self, output: str = "", value: int = 0):
        self.output = output
        self.value = value

### `repro_agent.py`

"""
Helper module imported once by repro.py.
Simulates agents/__init__.py — only loaded once, holds a stale class reference
after sys.modules is invalidated by the file watcher.
"""
import streamlit as st
from repro_model import MyResult  # bound once at import time

@st.cache_data(show_spinner=False)
def get_result(key: str) -> MyResult:
... [9 lines trimmed] ...
import sys
import importlib
import repro_agent  # imported once — simulates agents/__init__.py

st.title("cache_data pickle race condition repro")

if st.button("1) Normal call (works)"):
    try:
        result = repro_agent.get_result("test")
        st.success(f"Got: {result.output}")
    except Exception as e:
        st.error(f"{type(e).__name__}: {e}")

if st.button("2) Simulate file-watcher then call (fails, and keeps failing)"):
    # This is exactly what LocalSourcesWatcher.on_path_changed does:
    #   for wm in self._watched_modules.values():
    #       del sys.modules[wm.module_name]
    if "repro_model" in sys.modules:
        del sys.modules["repro_model"]

    # Re-import creates a NEW class object in sys.modules
    importlib.import_module("repro_model")

    # Clear cache so pickle.dumps is attempted again
    repro_agent.get_result.clear()

    try:
        # repro_agent still uses the OLD MyResult class.
        # pickle resolves sys.modules["repro_model"].MyResult → NEW class.
        # OLD is not NEW → PicklingError → UnserializableReturnValueError
        result = repro_agent.get_result("test")
        st.success(f"Got: {result.output}")
    except Exception as e:
        st.error(f"{type(e).__name__}: {e}")
```

### Steps To Reproduce

**Steps:**
1. `streamlit run repro.py`
2. Click **"1) Normal call"** — succeeds.
3. Click **"2) Simulate file-watcher"** — fails with `UnserializableReturnValueError`.
4. Click **"1) Normal call"** again — **also fails**, until Streamlit is restarted.

### Expected Behavior

Step 4 demonstrates persistence: `repro_agent` is never re-imported, so it keeps
using the old class, while `sys.modules` keeps the new one.

Neither step 3 not step 4 should throw the `UnserializableReturnValueError`.

Expected behavior : 

[image]

### Current Behavior

`UnserializableReturnValueError` is thrown

[image]

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- **Streamlit**: 1.55.0
- **Python**: 3.13.7
- **OS**: Windows 11 / Linux (Kubernetes)
- Occurs more frequently in local dev (active filesystem) than in deployed containers

### Additional Information

> **Disclosure**: This bug report was written by an LLM (Claude) after a deep investigation into a production issue. The root cause analysis, reproduction script, and identified problematic code path are all LLM-generated

## Suggested Fixes

### Option A: Chain the original exception (low-effort, improves DX)

In `_handle_cache_miss`, chain the original exception so users can see the real error:

```python
raise UnserializableReturnValueError(
    return_value=computed_value, func=self._info.func
) from ex  # <-- add "from ex"
```

### Option B: Guard `write_result` against stale class references

Before calling `pickle.dumps()` in `DataCache.write_result`, re-import the module and verify class identity:

```python
import importlib
cls = type(value)
mod = sys.modules.get(cls.__module__)
if mod is not None:
    current_cls = getattr(mod, cls.__qualname__, None)
    if current_cls is not None and current_cls is not cls:
        # Module was reloaded — update the instance's class to the current one
        value.__class__ = current_cls
```

### Option C: Don't delete modules from `sys.modules` preemptively

Instead of deleting all watched modules on every file change, only invalidate the module that actually changed. Or defer the deletion to the start of the next script run rather than doing it immediately from the watcher thread.

## Workaround

Return only pickle-safe primitives (dicts, strings, numbers) from `@st.cache_data` functions, and reconstruct custom objects outside the cache boundary:

```python
@st.cache_data(show_spinner=False)
def _cached_call(key: str) -> dict:
    result = do_expensive_work(key)
    return result.__dict__  # dict is always pickle-safe

def get_result(key: str) -> MyResult:
    return MyResult(**_cached_call(key))
```

comments.text:
## Reproduction Assessment: **CONFIRMED** (via code analysis)

This bug is confirmed real. I was unable to do a live reproduction (no Cognito user pool available), but the root cause is unambiguous from the source code.

### Root Cause

In [`lib/streamlit/auth_util.py:223-226`](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/blob/develop/lib/streamlit/auth_util.py#L223-L226), `build_logout_url()` hardcodes the OIDC standard parameter name `post_logout_redirect_uri`:

```python
logout_params: dict[str, str] = {
    "client_id": client_id,
    "post_logout_redirect_uri": post_logout_redirect_uri,
}
```

AWS Cognito's logout endpoint does **not** follow the OIDC RP-Initiated Logout spec. It requires `redirect_uri` (or `logout_uri`), not `post_logout_redirect_uri`. It also ignores `id_token_hint`.

So Streamlit sends: `?client_id=...&post_logout_redirect_uri=...&id_token_hint=...`
But Cognito expects: `?client_id=...&redirect_uri=...`

This matches the exact error reported: *"Required String parameter 'redirect_uri' is not present"*

### Why logout still works

The server-side logout (cookie clearing) happens **before** the redirect to the provider's logout endpoint. So the Streamlit session is invalidated regardless of whether the provider redirect succeeds — which is why pressing back shows the user as logged out.

### Scope

This likely affects any OIDC provider whose `end_session_endpoint` doesn't follow the RP-Initiated Logout spec parameter naming. Related: #12169 showed Auth0 had the same issue.

A potential fix would be to allow users to configure custom logout query parameters, or to detect non-standard providers and adjust the parameter name accordingly.

Hey! The diagnosis here seems right. Cognito's logout endpoint doesn't follow the OIDC RP-Initiated Logout spec and expects `redirect_uri` instead of `post_logout_redirect_uri`.

I put together a draft PR (#14868) that adds an optional `[auth.logout_params]` section to secrets.toml so you can override the default parameter names. For Cognito it'd look like:

```toml
[auth.logout_params]
redirect_uri_name = "redirect_uri"
include_id_token_hint = false
```

Still needs a more thorough review/approval but wanted to get it out there. Would love to know if the config shape makes sense for your use case.

title: st.cache_data shares cache across st.Page pages for same-named functions with different source code
body:
### Checklist

### Summary

st.cache_data functions with the same name but different source code in different page files (loaded via st.navigation + st.Page) share the same cache. This is because st.Page executes all pages via exec() with
  __module__ == "__main__", and inspect.getsource() fails in that context. The fallback to func.__code__.co_code (bytecode) does not include string constants, so functions with identical structure but different inline strings (e.g., different SQL queries) produce the same cache key.

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
# main.py
import streamlit as st

st.set_page_config(page_title="Cache Bug Demo", layout="wide")
pg = st.navigation(
    {
        "Page A": [st.Page("page_a.py", title="Page A")],
        "Page B": [st.Page("page_b.py", title="Page B")],
    }
)
pg.run()
# page_a.py
import streamlit as st

@st.cache_data(ttl=3600)
def load_data():
    return {"source": "page_a", "columns": ["col_a1", "col_a2"]}

data = load_data()
st.write("Page A data:", data)
st.write("Expected source: page_a, Got:", data["source"])
# page_b.py
import streamlit as st

@st.cache_data(ttl=3600)
def load_data():
    return {"source": "page_b", "columns": ["col_b1", "col_b2"]}

data = load_data()
st.write("Page B data:", data)
st.write("Expected source: page_b, Got:", data["source"])
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Create the three files above (main.py, page_a.py, page_b.py)
2. Run streamlit run main.py
3. Open Page A — displays source: page_a (correct)
4. Navigate to Page B — displays source: page_a (wrong, should be page_b)
5. Clear cache and open Page B first — displays source: page_b (correct)
6. Navigate to Page A — displays source: page_b (wrong, should be page_a)

### Expected Behavior

Each page's load_data() should have an independent cache, since they are defined in different files with different source code. Navigating between pages should return each page's own data.

### Current Behavior

Whichever page is loaded first caches its result under the function key. When the other page calls its own load_data(), the cached result from the first page is returned, because both functions produce the same cache key.

Root cause: In streamlit/navigation/page.py, st.Page.run() executes page scripts as:

module = types.ModuleType("__main__")
exec(code, module.__dict__)

This means func.__module__ is "__main__" for all pages. When inspect.getsource() fails in this exec() context, _make_function_key falls back to func.__code__.co_code, which does not include string constants — so
  structurally identical functions with different inline values produce the same key.

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.55.0
- Python version: 3.14.3
- Operating System: macOS Tahoe Docker Desktop `FROM ghcr.io/astral-sh/uv:python3.14-trixie-slim`
- Browser: Google Chrome 146.0.7680.178

### Additional Information

Related issue: https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/11157 (cache_data cannot detect difference in values of free variables). That issue covers a similar problem with closure variables, but the st.Page + exec() scenario is a distinct trigger.

Workaround: Give cached functions unique names per page (e.g., page_a_load_data, page_b_load_data).

title: Await a Components V2 initialization value without session-state residue
body:
### Checklist

### Summary

<details>
<summary>./docker-compose.yml</summary>

```yaml
services:
  main:
    build:
      context: .
      dockerfile_inline: |
        # syntax=docker.io/docker/dockerfile-upstream:1.20.0-labs
        # check=error=true
        FROM python:3.10-slim AS base
        RUN pip install "streamlit==1.55"
    init: true
    network_mode: "host"
    working_dir: /app
    volumes:
      - .:/app:ro
    entrypoint: ["/usr/bin/env", "streamlit", "run"]
    command: ["./streamlit_app.py"]
```

</details>
<details>
<summary>./comp.py</summary>

```python
# comp.py

import sys
from datetime import datetime
from pathlib import Path

import streamlit as st

st_comp_get_cookies = st.components.v2.component(
    "component_bidi_drop_bug.get_cookies",
    js="""
    export default function(component){
        const { data, setTriggerValue } = component;
        console.log("Comp Instantiated: " + data._);
        // More advanced logic here
        const retObj = document.cookie;
        console.log("cookie-getter:", retObj);
        if(retObj !== undefined) setTriggerValue("get_cookies", retObj);
    }
    """,
    isolate_styles=False,
)

def _frame_gen(frame, skip=0):
    while frame:
        if frame.f_code.co_filename.startswith("/app"):
            if skip <= 0:
                yield frame
            else:
                skip -= 1
        frame = frame.f_back

_cwd = Path.cwd()

def _rm_cwd(path):
    if _cwd in Path(path).parents:
        return str(Path(path).relative_to(_cwd))
    return path

def unique_key(suffix: str = "", skip: int = 0) -> str:
    return "".join(reversed([
        f"{_rm_cwd(f.f_code.co_filename)}-{f.f_code.co_name}-{f.f_lineno};"
        for f in _frame_gen(sys._getframe(), skip + 1)
    ])) + suffix

def unique_line_time(suffix: str = "", skip: int = 0) -> str:
    return unique_key(suffix, skip + 1) + f":{int(datetime.now().timestamp())}"
```

</details>

<details>
<summary>./streamlit_app.py</summary>

```python
# streamlit_app.py

import time

import streamlit as st
from comp import st_comp_get_cookies, unique_line_time

st.set_page_config(page_title="Component V2 Bidi Bug")
st.header("Hi")
st.write("This component passes a 'soft' key via data so that multiple instances of it can exist,")
st.write("that's LOC/time unique. So every app hard or soft refresh creates a new widget.")
st.write("Avoiding making a key, because intend to post-process the return value and populate")
st.write("session_state with refined data. Messy session_state is annoying.")
st.write("The base component only exists once, in the cached helper file.")

st.header("Problem")
st.write("Browser console logs: the widget is instantiated, then returns the value.")
st.write("Python logs: the returned value isn't always received.")
st.write("Because it's so inconsistently received, it's hard to depend on")

def get_raw_cookies() -> str:
    data = { "_": unique_line_time() }
    obj = st_comp_get_cookies(data=data)
    print(f"{obj=}")
    if not isinstance(obj, dict) or "get_cookies" not in obj:
        time.sleep(2)
        st.rerun() # Very first run, component mightn't be ready
    return obj["get_cookies"]

# Main

if "rerun_counter" not in st.session_state:
    st.session_state["rerun_counter"] = -1
st.session_state["rerun_counter"] = st.session_state["rerun_counter"] + 1
print(f'{st.session_state["rerun_counter"]} Refresh')

print(f"First: {get_raw_cookies()=}")
print(f"Second: {get_raw_cookies()=}")
st.header("Page finished loading!")
```

I'm trying to migrate our custom js widgets from v1 component api to the non-iframe v2 api.
It seems far more powerful, and seems like it'll cut boilerplate.
In our style, we have accumulated over the years a collection of js/client side running code, that doesn't particularly need/have an html or user-interfacing component.

I think I've noticed an issue, where values are getting returned from the js frontend (as seen by console.log msgs), but the streamlit backend logs see those msgs as dropped. I'm still getting the hang of the runtime behaviors of this new component api, to figure out how to update our v1 components, so I've been trying to test it. If this is not the expected or correct usage, I'm all ears, but I'm working my best from the online docs + repo src implementation. 

This is our current design / usage analysis of the v2 api:
- We declare/write a st.components.v2.component(...) object in a helper file, that will not be modified, with a unique name
- The js string includes all helper functions, and an `export default function(component: FrontendRendererArgs)`
- This default function is the per-widget-instantiation, and only run once (see below)
- It sets up callbacks or such on html elements
- If the component is called with a `key`, then all setTriggerValue and setStateValue items populate session_state
- Without an explicit `key`, setTriggerValue won't populate session_state, but the rest of the python arguments (data) are used to calculate a unique frontend key
- No two component instances therefore can have the exact same args (data)
- If the args to the component don't change, the widget object stays created, and is not re-instantiated
- If the rest of the args (data) to the component change, without a `key`, the old widget is discarded, and a new component is instantiated

Our goal is to have high-level code that uses caching & post processing of raw lower-level data call these low-level components as needed. But if the components are called, I expect them to behave consistently.

```

A couple of things I noticed while looking into this:

First, trigger values in the CCv2 API are only surfaced on the result object when you register a matching `on_<key>_change` callback ([docs](https://docs.streamlit.io/develop/concepts/custom-components/components-v2/state-and-triggers#callback-registration)). Did some more investigation around this issue. Short version: no messages are being lost in transit. Two separate by-design mechanisms produce what looks like dropping, and one genuine bug did fall out of the investigation, filed separately as #16732.

All measurements below are on 1.62.0:

### What reproduces

The reported symptom reproduces deterministically — the page never finishes loading, the second component never resolves, and the retry loop runs hot: **863 script runs in 15 seconds (~58 reruns/sec)**, with no error or warning surfaced.

### Why the original version never converges

`data` is hashed into the element id, so `unique_line_time()` builds a **different widget on almost every run**. The value the previous instance sent belongs to a widget that no longer exists. Measured: **0 of 1,271 runs** received a value, with 688 distinct element ids observed in 12 seconds. It works only when two runs happen to land in the same second — which is exactly the "about half the time" behaviour described above.

This is documented behaviour, in `component-v2-lib/src/types.ts`:

> If a component is mounted without a `key` parameter in Python, and one of the parameters in the mounting command changes, then this frontend key may change between app runs.

One consequence worth flagging, since avoiding `session_state` clutter was the stated reason for going unkeyed: the unkeyed version is the one that **accumulates** orphaned widget entries — registered ids grew 2 → 6 → 8 → 10 → 12 → 14 over six runs. Passing a `key` is what keeps state bounded.

### The trigger diagnosis in this thread was correct

The conclusion that trigger values are "resurfaced once, just... only resurfaced once", and the comparison to `if st.button("1") and st.button("2")`, is exactly right. `_reset_triggers()` in `runtime/state/session_state.py` nulls every trigger value at the end of each run. With stable `data` a component mounts once and sends once, so after that value is consumed there is nothing left to re-send — two sequential mount-time triggers deadlock. Measured: the second component received a value **0 times across 126 runs**.

### Three corrections to this thread

1. **Trigger values do not require an `on_<key>_change` callback.** Earlier in the thread we said the key wouldn't appear in the result without one; that isn't right. None of our repros registered a callback and values arrived normally — the pushback on that point was correct.
2. **The `st.stop()` approach doesn't work.** It loops forever exactly like `st.rerun()` — the second component still never resolves. Worth stating plainly since it was suggested here and looked promising.
3. **The automated triage comment above is only half right.** Async module loading does explain an empty result on the *first* run, but it predicts convergence on run 2 — which is what a stable-`data` component actually does. It doesn't explain the permanent failure.

### What works reliably

| Pattern | Result |
|---|---|
| `setStateValue` with a stable key | resolves in **2 runs** |
| Five `setStateValue` components at once | all resolve together in **2 runs** |
| `setStateValue` on mount, changing `data` | 21/21 delivered |
| `setTriggerValue` from an event handler | 40/40 delivered |
| Inside `@st.fragment` | works |
| Inside an `if st.button(...)` block | never resolves — matching the second report above |

### The one genuine bug

Separately from the above: `setTriggerValue` called **during mount** loses roughly a quarter of values when the component remounts on changed `data`, even with an explicit `key` and a verified-stable element id. Filed as #16732. Both alternatives above are unaffected, so the practical guidance is unchanged — use `setStateValue` for initialization values.

### What we're doing with this issue

Since the reported "result dropping" turns out to be documented behaviour plus the separately-filed bug, we're converting this issue to the enhancement underneath it — a supported way to await an initialization value without leaving permanent `session_state` entries — which is what's actually being asked for here.

@user @user — this is the part we'd need your input on to design it. At the point of the call, what needs to be guaranteed: that the value is *present*, or just a reliable way to distinguish "not ready yet" from "genuinely empty"? And what makes a persistent `session_state` entry unacceptable — the volume, the staleness, or key hygiene? The point that "supply a default" can't distinguish an expected value from cache invalidation is the crux, and knowing which of those matters would shape the answer.

title: Allow customizing generic uncaught exception message when client.showErrorDetails="none"
body:
### Checklist

### Summary

When `client.showErrorDetails = "none"` is configured, Streamlit correctly redacts uncaught exception details, but the browser still shows a hard-coded generic message:

> This app has encountered an error. The original error message is redacted to prevent data leaks. Full error details have been recorded in the logs (if you're on Streamlit Cloud, click on 'Manage app' in the lower right of your app).

It would be useful to have a supported way to customize this generic message.

### Why?

For production apps, the current hard-coded message is not always appropriate:

- Self-hosted apps may not use Streamlit Cloud, so the “Manage app” guidance is irrelevant.
- Some products need simpler user-facing copy, e.g. `This app has encountered an error.`
- Some deployments prefer a branded fallback page or a minimal status-code-style message.
- App developers can catch many errors manually, but import-time errors or framework-handled uncaught exceptions still fall back to Streamlit’s built-in error UI.

### How?

With:

```toml
[client]
showErrorDetails = "none"

### Additional Context

Streamlit redacts the original exception, type, and stack trace, but displays the hard-coded generic message above.

In Streamlit 1.56.0, this appears to be defined as _GENERIC_UNCAUGHT_EXCEPTION_TEXT in streamlit/elements/exception.py.

Desired behavior
Provide a supported configuration option for customizing the generic uncaught exception message shown when error details are hidden.

For example:

[client]
showErrorDetails = "none"
genericErrorMessage = "This app has encountered an error."
or:

[client]
showErrorDetails = "none"
uncaughtExceptionMessage = "This app has encountered an error."
Alternatives considered
App-level exception boundaries can catch runtime errors and render custom UI, but they cannot reliably cover all cases, especially errors that happen before the app’s main function runs.

Patching Streamlit internals is possible but brittle and not suitable for production deployments.

Additional context
This would make client.showErrorDetails = "none" more production-friendly for self-hosted and branded applications while preserving Streamlit’s current secure default behavior.

- App developers can catch many errors manually, but import-time errors or framework-handled uncaught exceptions still fall back to Streamlit’s built-in error UI.
sections.how?:
With:

```toml
[client]
showErrorDetails = "none"
sections.additional context:
Streamlit redacts the original exception, type, and stack trace, but displays the hard-coded generic message above.

In Streamlit 1.56.0, this appears to be defined as _GENERIC_UNCAUGHT_EXCEPTION_TEXT in streamlit/elements/exception.py.

Desired behavior
Provide a supported configuration option for customizing the generic uncaught exception message shown when error details are hidden.

For example:

[client]
showErrorDetails = "none"
genericErrorMessage = "This app has encountered an error."
or:

[client]
showErrorDetails = "none"
uncaughtExceptionMessage = "This app has encountered an error."
Alternatives considered
App-level exception boundaries can catch runtime errors and render custom UI, but they cannot reliably cover all cases, especially errors that happen before the app’s main function runs.

Patching Streamlit internals is possible but brittle and not suitable for production deployments.

Additional context
This would make client.showErrorDetails = "none" more production-friendly for self-hosted and branded applications while preserving Streamlit’s current secure default behavior.

comments.text: I'm also happy to open a PR with a proposed fix

We are working on allowing providing a custom script error handler in https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/14972, which would also allow showing custom error messages for uncaught exceptions. See the spec [here](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/blob/develop/specs/2026-04-20-exception-handler/product-spec.md).

## Update:

You can define a custom exception handler via `on_script_error ` in `st.App` which allows you to redact these error with a custom message.

title: `400 Bad Request: Request Header Or Cookie Too Large` after upgrading from 1.52.2 to 1.56.0 (i.e., >= 1.53.0) with Microsoft Entra ID auth
body:
### Checklist

### Summary

After upgrading from Streamlit 1.52.2 to 1.56.0, my deployed app on Streamlit Community Cloud returns `400 Bad Request: Request Header Or Cookie Too Large` (from nginx) immediately after Microsoft Entra ID login. 

The combined size of the auth-related cookies (`_streamlit_user`, `_streamlit_user_tokens_1`, `_streamlit_user_tokens_2`) plus the other cookies on `*.streamlit.app` pushes the request `Cookie:` header above 8 KB, which exceeds nginx's `large_client_header_buffers` limit on Community Cloud. The same app works locally on 1.56.0 and works on Community Cloud after downgrading to 1.52.2.

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python

```

### Steps To Reproduce

### Expected Behavior

The user should be logged in successfully and see the app, the same way the flow works on Streamlit 1.52.2.

### Current Behavior

The browser shows an nginx 400 page with "Request Header Or Cookie Too Large" after the OAuth callback redirect.

Cookie sizes after a successful login attempt (inspected via DevTools → Application → Cookies):

- `_streamlit_user_tokens_1`: 4034 bytes
- `_streamlit_user_tokens_2`: 1720 bytes
- `_streamlit_user`: 1396 bytes
- `_streamlit_user_tokens`: 150 bytes

Total `Cookie:` header on the failing request is over 8000 bytes.

Things I checked / tried that did not resolve the issue:

1. `groupMembershipClaims` is `null` in the app registration manifest, so no group claims are being emitted. Saw this in #12518
2. Token Configuration in the app registration is empty (no extra optional claims).
3. The authorize request scope is `openid email profile` only — no `offline_access`, so Microsoft is not issuing a refresh token.
4. Decoded the id_token via `st.user` — only standard OIDC claims (~16), ~1.5 KB.
5. Decoded the access_token via `expose_tokens = ["access"]` and jwt.ms. `User.Read` is granted (it's the standard delegated permission for OIDC sign-in; removing it blocks new users from signing in). The access_token contains the usual Microsoft internal claims (`xms_*`, `wids`, `puid`, etc.) and is ~3.5 KB. There is no Azure-side configuration to shrink this meaningfully.

The token bloat appears to be intrinsic to Microsoft Entra ID tokens, so trimming on the Azure side is not a viable fix. The issue seems specific to how >= 1.53.0 stores tokens in cookies (chunked across `_streamlit_user_tokens_1` / `_streamlit_user_tokens_2`) — 1.52.2's cookie handling fits under the nginx limit on Community Cloud.

### Is this a regression?

- [x] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: >=1.53.0 (broken), 1.52.2 (works)
- Python version: 3.13.3
- Operating System: Streamlit Community Cloud; localhost macOS
- Browser: Chrome, Edge

### Additional Information

Related issues:
- https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/12518
- https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/14290

Screenshot of error:
[image]

I'd like to take this on.

**Plan**
1. Trace where the intermittent Windows `OSError: [WinError 121]` from Uvicorn/`websockets` surfaces as the `data transfer failed` log (likely around the Starlette server / websocket path introduced in the Tornado → ASGI migration).
2. Suppress or downgrade this known-transient, non-user-visible error so it no longer pollutes logs (matching @user's note that it's noise worth hiding), without masking real connection failures.
3. Add a focused regression test for the filter/handler.
4. Keep the change scoped to logging/noise handling — no protocol or reconnect behavior changes unless needed.

Aiming for a draft PR within 48h. Happy to be assigned if that helps.

Fix ready on branch [`AJ-ing:fix/15022-hide-winerror-121-websocket-log`](https://github.com/AJ-ing/streamlit/tree/fix/15022-hide-winerror-121-websocket-log).

(Unit tests added in `lib/tests/streamlit/logger_test.py`.)

title: Auth cookies set by st.login() are session-scoped in 1.57.0 — Max-Age / Expires not emitted (regression from 1.56)
body:
### Checklist

### Summary

After upgrading from Streamlit 1.56.0 to 1.57.0, the cookies set by `st.login()` (`_streamlit_user`, `_streamlit_user_tokens`) are emitted with neither `Max-Age` nor `Expires`. Per RFC 6265 §5.3, browsers therefore treat them as non-persistent (session) cookies and discard them when the browser is closed. The [`st.login` docs](https://docs.streamlit.io/develop/api-reference/user/st.login) state the identity cookie should persist for 30 days, which was the behaviour in 1.56.0.

### Reproducible Code Example

```python
# app.py
import streamlit as st

if not st.user.is_logged_in:
    if st.button("Log in"):
        st.login(provider="auth0")
    st.stop()

st.success(f"Logged in as {st.user.email}")
st.button("Log out", on_click=st.logout)
```

`.streamlit/secrets.toml`:

```toml
[auth]
redirect_uri  = "http://localhost:8501/oauth2callback"
cookie_secret = "<a-random-32-byte-string>"

[auth.auth0]
client_id            = "YOUR_AUTH0_CLIENT_ID"
client_secret        = "YOUR_AUTH0_CLIENT_SECRET"
server_metadata_url  = "https://YOUR-TENANT.us.auth0.com/.well-known/openid-configuration"
```

Install with `pip install 'streamlit[auth]==1.57.0' httpx authlib`, run with `streamlit run app.py`.

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Run the app above against any Auth0 (or other OIDC) tenant.
2. Click **Log in**, complete the OAuth flow, land back on the app logged in.
3. Open DevTools → **Application** → **Cookies** → `http://localhost:8501`.
4. Look at the **Expires / Max-Age** column for `_streamlit_user` and `_streamlit_user_tokens`. On 1.57.0 the value is **`Session`**.
5. Close the browser entirely, reopen it, return to the app URL — you are logged out.

For a network-level trace, inspect the `Set-Cookie` response headers from `GET /oauth2callback`:

```
set-cookie: _streamlit_user=...;        HttpOnly; Path=/; SameSite=lax
            _streamlit_user_tokens=...; HttpOnly; Path=/; SameSite=lax
```

Compare to 1.56.0 on the same app — both cookies have `Expires=<~30 days out>`.

### Expected Behavior

`_streamlit_user` and `_streamlit_user_tokens` are emitted with a `Max-Age` (or `Expires`) of ~30 days, matching both the documented `st.login` behaviour and 1.56.0's behaviour. Closing the browser and reopening it should not log the user out.

### Current Behavior

Both cookies are emitted with no `Max-Age` and no `Expires`. Browsers treat them as session cookies; closing the browser logs the user out. The signed-payload server-side validation TTL of 31 days in `decode_signed_value(..., max_age_days=31)` is unchanged, suggesting the intent of the Starlette migration was to preserve ~30-day persistence and that the missing `max_age` argument is an oversight.

### Is this a regression?

- [x] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

The regression appears to originate in [PR #14553 "Make Starlette the default server and remove Tornado"](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/14553). The pre-1.57 code path went through Tornado's `set_signed_cookie(...)` / `set_secure_cookie(...)`, which defaults `expires_days=30` when the kwarg is omitted. The new path emits the cookie via Starlette's `Response.set_cookie(...)`, which has no implicit `max_age` default — so the attribute is simply absent unless passed explicitly.

Relevant code in `lib/streamlit/web/server/starlette/starlette_auth_routes.py`:

```python
def _set_single_cookie(
    response: Response, cookie_name: str, serialized_value: str
) -> None:
    cookie_secret = get_cookie_secret()
    signed_value = create_signed_value(cookie_secret, cookie_name, serialized_value)
    cookie_payload = signed_value.decode("utf-8")
    response.set_cookie(
        cookie_name,
        cookie_payload,
        httponly=True,
        samesite="lax",
        path=_get_cookie_path(),
        # max_age=... is missing here
    )
```

A community report of the same problem is open on the Streamlit forum: <https://discuss.streamlit.io/t/auth-cookie-persistence-broken-in-1-57-0-starlette-migration/121410>.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.57.0
- Python version: 3.13
- Operating System: Ubuntu 24.04 (WSL2)
- Browser: Chrome 141
- OS-level: Tornado removed; Starlette 1.0.0 / Uvicorn 0.47.0 / websockets 16.0 from the `streamlit[auth]==1.57.0` extra plus Authlib 1.7.2 and httpx 0.28.1.

I am happy to follow up with a PR adding `max_age` to `_set_single_cookie` (and a regression test asserting the `Set-Cookie` attributes), restoring the documented 30-day default, if that approach is acceptable.

title: st.App does not discover script-level .streamlit/config.toml
body:
### Checklist

### Summary

When using `st.App` with an external ASGI server and the working directory differs from the script directory,
script-level `.streamlit/config.toml` is silently ignored. The same config works with `streamlit run`.

I think there is a 1-line fix.

### Reproducible Code Example

Given a directory structure:

```
myproject/
├── myapp/
│   ├── .streamlit/
│   │   └── config.toml
│   ├── app.py
│   └── asgi.py
```

myapp/.streamlit/config.toml :
```
[theme]
primaryColor = "#ff0000"
```

myapp/app.py :
```
import streamlit as st
st.title("Config Discovery Test")
st.write(f"primaryColor = {st.get_option('theme.primaryColor')}")
```

myapp/asgi.py :
```
from streamlit.starlette import App
app = App("app.py")
```

### Steps To Reproduce

```bash
cd myproject
uvicorn myapp.asgi:app --port 8501
```

### Expected Behavior

`primaryColor` should be `#ff0000`, indicating that the config TOML was picked up.

This matches the behaviour of `streamlit run myapp/app.py`.

### Current Behavior

`primaryColor` is `None` (default). The script-level config.toml is silently ignored.

Note: if you `cd myapp` first, it works, because CWD-based discovery happens to find it, not because `st.App` wired it up.

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.57
- Python version: 3.11
- Operating System: Linux
- Browser: Chrome

### Additional Information

Suspected root cause: 

Config file discovery (`config.get_config_files`) only searches the script's directory if `config._main_script_path` is set. 

`streamlit run` sets this (`cli.py:296`), but `App.__init__` and its lifespan startup do not, despite already resolving the script path via `_resolve_script_path()`.

Proposed fixL in `App._combined_lifespan`, before calling `prepare_streamlit_environment`, add:

```python
config._main_script_path = str(script_path)
```
A workaround is to set the `_main_script_path` attribute manually, but this feels flaky as it's a private attribute:

```python
from streamlit import config
from streamlit.starlette import App

config._main_script_path = str(Path(__file__).parent / "app.py")
app = App("app.py")
```

sections.summary:
When using `st.App` with an external ASGI server and the working directory differs from the script directory,
script-level `.streamlit/config.toml` is silently ignored. The same config works with `streamlit run`.

I think there is a 1-line fix.
sections.reproducible code example:
Given a directory structure:

```
myproject/
├── myapp/
│   ├── .streamlit/
│   │   └── config.toml
│   ├── app.py
│   └── asgi.py
```

myapp/.streamlit/config.toml :
```
[theme]
primaryColor = "#ff0000"
```

myapp/app.py :
```
import streamlit as st
st.title("Config Discovery Test")
st.write(f"primaryColor = {st.get_option('theme.primaryColor')}")
```

myapp/asgi.py :
```
from streamlit.starlette import App
app = App("app.py")
```
sections.steps to reproduce:
```bash
cd myproject
uvicorn myapp.asgi:app --port 8501
```
sections.expected behavior:
`primaryColor` should be `#ff0000`, indicating that the config TOML was picked up.

This matches the behaviour of `streamlit run myapp/app.py`.
sections.current behavior:
`primaryColor` is `None` (default). The script-level config.toml is silently ignored.

Note: if you `cd myapp` first, it works, because CWD-based discovery happens to find it, not because `st.App` wired it up.
sections.is this a regression?: - [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.
sections.debug info:
- Streamlit version: 1.57
- Python version: 3.11
- Operating System: Linux
- Browser: Chrome
sections.additional information:
Suspected root cause: 

Config file discovery (`config.get_config_files`) only searches the script's directory if `config._main_script_path` is set. 

`streamlit run` sets this (`cli.py:296`), but `App.__init__` and its lifespan startup do not, despite already resolving the script path via `_resolve_script_path()`.

Proposed fixL in `App._combined_lifespan`, before calling `prepare_streamlit_environment`, add:

```python
config._main_script_path = str(script_path)
```
A workaround is to set the `_main_script_path` attribute manually, but this feels flaky as it's a private attribute:

```python
from streamlit import config
from streamlit.starlette import App

config._main_script_path = str(Path(__file__).parent / "app.py")
app = App("app.py")
```

title: runtime.txt completely ignored - forced Python 3.14.5 on Cloud
body:
### Checklist

### Summary

My Streamlit Cloud app ignores runtime.txt and forces Python 3.14.5 instead of the specified Python 3.9. This causes all data science packages (numpy, pandas, scikit-learn, pillow) to fail during installation because they are incompatible with Python 3.14.5. The deployment logs clearly show "Using Python 3.14.5 environment" despite having runtime.txt with "3.9" in the repository root.

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
import streamlit as st
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

st.title("Bank Churn Prediction")
st.write("Testing Python version compatibility")

# This fails on Streamlit Cloud due to Python 3.14.5

Plus these files in the repository:

runtime.txt:
3.9
requirements.txt:
streamlit==1.35.0
pandas==2.2.0
numpy==1.26.4
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Create a GitHub repository with runtime.txt (containing "3.9"), requirements.txt, and a simple streamlit_app.py
2. Deploy the app on Streamlit Community Cloud
3. Monitor the deployment logs
4. Observe that Python 3.14.5 is used instead of Python 3.9
5. See installation failures for numpy, pandas, and pillow due to Python version incompatibility

### Expected Behavior

The deployment should use Python 3.9 as specified in the runtime.txt file. The app should install dependencies successfully and run without Python version-related errors. The logs should show "Using Python 3.9.x environment".The deployment should use Python 3.9 as specified in the runtime.txt file. The app should install dependencies successfully and run without Python version-related errors. The logs should show "Using Python 3.9.x environment".

### Current Behavior

The deployment ignores runtime.txt and forces Python 3.14.5. The logs show:
"Using Python 3.14.5 environment at /home/<user>/venv"

This causes multiple failures:
- ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'distutils' (removed in Python 3.12+)
- Failed to build numpy/pandas/pillow
- Missing pkg_resources module
- Build errors: "RequiredDependencyException: jpeg"

The app fails to deploy with error: "installer returned a non-zero exit code"

Full log excerpt:
[19:20:31] Using uv pip install.
[19:20:31] Using Python 3.14.5 environment at /home/<user>/venv
[19:20:39] × Failed to download and build `scikit-learn==1.4.2`

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.35.0 (attempted)
- Python version (specified): 3.9 via runtime.txt
- Python version (actual): 3.14.5 (forced by platform)
- Operating System: Streamlit Community Cloud (Linux)
- Browser: microsoft edge (latest)
- Repository: https://github.com/Yasir2690/bank-churn-prediction

### Additional Information

This issue is blocking all data science deployments on Streamlit Cloud. The minimal test with just "streamlit" and runtime.txt still shows Python 3.14.5 being used, confirming it's a platform issue, not an app-specific problem.

Links:
- Repository: https://github.com/Yasir2690/bank-churn-prediction
- Logs show: "Using Python 3.14.5 environment" despite runtime.txt

Worked successfully on:
- Local machine with Python 3.9
- Minimal-test branch also fails with same Python 3.14.5 issue

This appears to be a platform-level bug where runtime.txt is completely ignored by the Streamlit Cloud build system.

title: FIPS friendliness
body:
### Checklist

### Summary

Streamlit should support [FIPS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federal_Information_Processing_Standards)  friendliness.

When a library or package is not FIPS friendly, it significantly limits your ability to use it commercially since you cant sell that software to the US gov or anyone that works with them.

### Why?

Streamlit is not officially [FIPS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federal_Information_Processing_Standards) compliant. Any current FIPS friendliness seems to be [maintained by the community](https://github.com/search?q=repo%3Astreamlit%2Fstreamlit+fips&type=issues). This means that sometimes new Streamlit features are developed that break FIPS requirements. 

The FIPS regressions seem to have been trivial, so it would be nice if they could be caught before release.

### How?

1. Streamlit should run it's pre-release CI suite on a FIPS compliant image and check for crashes. The suite should set up a FIPS environment (like the python-fips chainguard container) and executes a test script to see if unapproved paths are blocked. 
2. Streamlit should run a linter so that we pass `usedforsecurity=False` flag on non-cryptographic internal hashes; like cache key generation, file watchers, session IDs, or anything else we would use MD5 for. 

### Additional Context

title: TypeError: `_run_with_thread_state() takes 0 positional arguments but 1 was given` on websocket connect with `@st.fragment(run_every=...)` in 1.58.0
body:
### Checklist

### Summary

After Streamlit Cloud auto-installed **1.58.0** (released 2026-05-28), every websocket connect to a deployed app raises:

```
TypeError: add_script_run_ctx.<locals>._run_with_thread_state()
  takes 0 positional arguments but 1 was given
```

The error is raised inside the threading wrapper installed by `add_script_run_ctx` in `lib/streamlit/runtime/scriptrunner_utils/script_run_context.py`. The wrapper is defined as:

```python
def _run_with_thread_state() -> None:    # ← 0 positional args
    fields = getattr(thread, _FRAGMENT_THREAD_STATE_FIELDS_ATTR, None)
    if fields is not None:
        ThreadState.initialize(**fields)
    original_run()
thread.run = _run_with_thread_state
```

Something in the new threading path calls `_run_with_thread_state(arg)` with one positional argument, which the wrapper can't accept.

### Reproducible Code Example

```python
import streamlit as st

@st.fragment(run_every="5s")
def live_chart():
    st.write("tick")

live_chart()
```

Deploy to Streamlit Cloud (or run locally with Streamlit 1.58.0 on Python 3.13). The Sentry trace shows the error firing on every websocket connect even when no user-facing breakage is visible — the wrapped thread retries cleanly, so users don't crash, but Sentry floods.

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Deploy a Streamlit app with a `@st.fragment(run_every="5s")` (or any positive interval) somewhere in the render path.
2. Open the app in a browser.
3. Observe `TypeError: _run_with_thread_state() takes 0 positional arguments but 1 was given` on every websocket connect.

### Expected Behavior

The fragment thread runs without raising; the auto-refresh works as it did in 1.57.0.

### Current Behavior

`TypeError` fires on every websocket connect. 51 events in 4 hours on our production deploy (5-user friends-alpha) before we pinned to 1.57.0.

### Is this a regression?

- [x] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

Last known good: **1.57.0** (released 2026-04-28). Pinning to `streamlit==1.57.0` eliminates the error completely.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.58.0
- Python version: 3.13.13 (CPython)
- Operating System: Streamlit Cloud (Linux container) + reproduced on macOS 15.5
- Browser: Chrome 148 (also Firefox, Safari)

### Additional Information

Sentry trace excerpt:

```
TypeError: add_script_run_ctx.<locals>._run_with_thread_state()
  takes 0 positional arguments but 1 was given
mechanism: threading
transaction: ws://[app].streamlit.app/_stcore/stream
```

Workaround: pin `streamlit==1.57.0` until a fix lands.

Happy to add more detail or test a candidate fix.

comments.text: Thanks for reporting this @user, it looks like this error being triggered is specific to python 3.13 and also some other aspects of your environment -- I have not been able to reproduce it locally except in a unit test and our regression test for this path passes and is run in python 3.13. But, the fix is clear and I have made a PR. Once this is in a nightly maybe you can verify the fix?

Independently confirming this on production traffic + verifying [PR #15376](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/15376) resolves it.

**Production hit:** ~50 Sentry events in 4 hours on Streamlit Community Cloud after upgrading from 1.57.0 → 1.58.0. Same TypeError on websocket connect for a tab using `@st.fragment(run_every="30s")`. Pinned back to 1.57.0 as a hot-fix.

**Bug repros cleanly on 1.58.0 with this distilled version of [the maintainer's regression test](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/15376/commits/95a188951f):**

```python
import threading
from streamlit.runtime.scriptrunner_utils.script_run_context import (
    add_script_run_ctx, ThreadState,
)
from streamlit.runtime.scriptrunner_utils.script_requests import ScriptRequests
from streamlit.runtime.pages_manager import PagesManager
from streamlit.runtime.scriptrunner_utils.script_run_context import ScriptRunContext

pm = PagesManager("/main/script/path"); pm.set_pages({})
ctx = ScriptRunContext(
    session_id="test", _enqueue=lambda _m: None, query_string="",
    session_state=None, uploaded_file_mgr=None, main_script_path="/main/script/path",
    user_info={}, fragment_storage=None, pages_manager=pm,
    script_requests=ScriptRequests(),
)
ThreadState.initialize(fragment_id="test_fragment")

class T(threading.Thread):
    def run(self, *args): self.received = list(args)

t = T(); add_script_run_ctx(t, ctx)
t.run("test_arg")  # → TypeError on 1.58.0
```

Output on 1.58.0:
```
TypeError: add_script_run_ctx.<locals>._run_with_thread_state() takes 0 positional arguments but 1 was given
```

**Verified the fix:** applied PR #15376's 2-line patch (`def _run_with_thread_state(*args, **kwargs)` + `original_run(*args, **kwargs)`) to the installed 1.58.0 — repro now passes cleanly, `t.received == ["test_arg"]`.

Holding off on the unpin until a release lands (currently still 1.58.0 on PyPI). Any sense of timing on a 1.58.1?

@user 

I believe the root cause of the issue is not Windows itself (or not only Windows), but rather something related to authentication.

After my vacation, I decided to test the simple example I posted above using the latest version (1.60) to see if anything had changed. Initially, it worked properly. However, when I tried to run my "real" application - which uses st.login() - I encountered the same issue again. Following that, even the simple example stopped working. Therefore, my conclusion is that the problem is triggered by st.login() in my main application. It seems the cookie created by this function interferes with the simple example as well, even though no login or user context is defined there. (I suspect Streamlit reads session cookies regardless of whether st.login() is actively called at startup).

For st.login(), I have to configure specific proxy settings to get through our corporate network, using the following snippet:

}

os.environ['HTTPS_PROXY'] = proxies['https']

```

Without these proxy settings, authentication is not possible. However, I am fairly confident that this proxy setup is causing the malfunction, and it appears the behavior of this function changed starting with Streamlit 1.57.

I hope this details help isolate and fix the issue, as I would love to upgrade to the latest Streamlit version. If you have any suggestions for alternative startup procedures or further tests I can run, I would be happy to help!

### Checklist

### Summary

After upgrading from Streamlit **1.56.0 → 1.58.0**, `st.login()` fails on Streamlit Cloud with the following log messages:

```
Missing provider for OAuth callback; this often indicates a stale or replayed
callback (for example, from browser back/forward navigation).
```

The app works correctly on a local machine with identical code and secrets.

```Python
import streamlit as st

if not st.user.is_logged_in:

title: RuntimeError: reentrant call inside _io.BufferedWriter when stopping server via Ctrl+C on Windows
body:
## Bug: `RuntimeError: reentrant call inside <_io.BufferedWriter>` when stopping the server via Ctrl+C on Windows

### Summary

On Windows, when the Streamlit server is stopped via Ctrl+C (SIGINT), the signal handler calls `server.stop()` which tries to write a "Stopping..." message to the console via `click.secho` → colorama's `AnsiToWin32`. This can race with the asyncio event loop's `select.select()` → buffered write to the same console handle, causing a `RuntimeError: reentrant call inside <_io.BufferedWriter>`.

### Error

```
RuntimeError: reentrant call inside <_io.BufferedWriter>
```

### Full traceback

```
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "bootstrap.py", line 43, in signal_handler
    server.stop()
  File "server.py", line 529, in stop
    cli_util.print_to_cli("  Stopping...", fg="blue")
  File "cli_util.py", line 34, in print_to_cli
    click.secho(message, **kwargs)
  File "termui.py", line 690, in secho
    return echo(message, file=file, nl=nl, err=err, color=color)
  File "utils.py", line 321, in echo
    file.write(out)  # type: ignore
  File "_compat.py", line 543, in _safe_write
    return _write(s)
  File "ansitowin32.py", line 47, in write
    self.__convertor.write(text)
  File "ansitowin32.py", line 177, in write
    self.write_and_convert(text)
  File "ansitowin32.py", line 202, in write_and_convert
    self.write_plain_text(text, cursor, start)
  File "ansitowin32.py", line 211, in write_plain_text
    self.wrapped.flush()
  File "_winconsole.py", line 176, in write
    buf = get_buffer(b)
  File "_winconsole.py", line 112, in get_buffer
    out: Array[c_char] = buffer_type.from_address(buf.buf)
RuntimeError: reentrant call inside <_io.BufferedWriter>
```

Note: the signal handler at `bootstrap.py:43` is invoked *inside* the asyncio event loop's `_run_once` → `select.select()` call, so the reentrant write happens while the loop is already inside a buffered I/O operation.

### Environment

- OS: Windows 10/11 (10.0.26200)
- Python: 3.11.3
- Streamlit: latest (reproduced via `aider --gui` which launches Streamlit)
- Virtual environment: No

### Root cause

The signal handler (`signal_handler` in `bootstrap.py`) runs synchronously inside the asyncio event loop's `select.select()` call. It calls `server.stop()` → `cli_util.print_to_cli("  Stopping...", fg="blue")` → `click.secho` → colorama `AnsiToWin32.write` → `wrapped.flush()` → `_winconsole.py` `get_buffer`. This writes to the same `_io.BufferedWriter` that the event loop may already be writing to, triggering CPython's reentrancy guard: `RuntimeError: reentrant call inside <_io.BufferedWriter>`.

This is a race condition — it doesn't happen every time, only when the signal arrives while the event loop is mid-write to the console buffer.

### Suggested fix

Avoid writing to the console from inside the signal handler. Options:

1. **Set a flag in the signal handler and do the actual stop + console output from the event loop.** E.g.:
   ```python
   def signal_handler(signum, frame):
       # Don't do I/O inside the signal handler; schedule the stop
       loop.call_soon_threadsafe(server.stop)
   ```

2. **Wrap the `cli_util.print_to_cli` call in a try/except** to swallow `RuntimeError` during shutdown (less clean, but minimal change).

3. **Use `signal.signal()` with a coroutine-aware handler** that doesn't write to the console synchronously.

Option 1 is the cleanest — signal handlers should never do I/O.
